Name: Osteria Ime
Description En: In this pretty, welcoming restaurant, the female chef from Albania, who has adopted Italian culinary traditions over her many years in the country, serves a choice of tasting menus. Her dishes have distinct geographical names and are full of colour and prepared from top-quality ingredients which change with the passing seasons. There are only a few tables available, so booking ahead is always a good idea. You’ll be warmly welcomed with a friendly smile that sets the tone for what is sure to be a highly enjoyable evening.

Name: Alessandro Borghese - Il lusso della semplicità
Address: Calle Seconda del Cristo 2040, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description En: This restaurant is situated in the Casinò di Venezia, or to be more precise, Palazzo Ca’ Vendramin Calergi, a 16C building overlooking the Grand Canal which boasts a beautiful garden in which meals are served on warm summer evenings. Chef Alessandro Borghese serves modern and attractive cuisine which is full of enticing flavours. There are two tasting menus available, with the option of adding the chef’s signature dishes to either of these.

Name: Terraforte
Address: Via Bagnoli Terriccio 12, Castellina Marittima, 56040, Italy
Description En: In an elegant, country-house setting, Terraforte occupies an old hay barn on the beautiful, vast Il Terriccio estate, where 1 500 hectares of tranquil, bucolic Tuscan landscapes are home to horses, olive trees and the estate’s renowned vineyards (Lupicaia wines). The cuisine focuses on zero-mile ingredients, with an exclusive use of produce sourced from the estate, including beef, game, chicken, vegetables, aromatic herbs and excellent wine. The two menus (three or seven courses) showcase imaginative and well-balanced dishes which never lose the clean, decisive flavours of their top-quality ingredients. In fine weather, don’t miss the opportunity to enjoy the charming outdoor space and even, perhaps, spend a night on the estate by staying at the La Marrana villa.

Name: Pepe Nero
Description En: Overlooking the western shore of Lake Bolsena, Pepe Nero is an intimate restaurant that wins one over through its modern furnishings and a pleasing maritime character. The service, gentle and professional, discreetly accompanies a predominantly seafood gastronomic journey, conceived for an immersive and unhurried experience of flavour. Guests may opt for themed menus or entrust themselves to the carte, choosing at least two dishes. The wine list ranges across regional and national labels, while in the warmer months a small terrace at the water’s edge affords the pleasure of dining with a direct view over the lake shore.

Name: Caffè Grande - Osteria del Centro
Description En: Almost all the main dishes at this restaurant are grilled (mostly meat but there are also fish options), plus there’s a good choice of appetisers, including substantial options such as tripe and sweetbreads, with tasting menus that combine starters and main courses. The à la carte features a generous selection of classic, well-prepared dishes made from top-quality ingredients. The restaurant occupies the premises of a historic café that has experienced closures and problems in the past but has now been courageously reopened by three young business partners.

Name: Osteria FraSe
Address: Via Crociata 9, Piove di Sacco, 35028, Italy
Description En: In this restaurant, husband Francesco takes care of the wine, while his wife Serena is at the helm in the open-view kitchen, creating dishes with a focus on fish and seafood (including raw options), fresh pasta dishes and classic recipes with the occasional imaginative twist or the addition of exotic fruit. This is a modern and welcoming osteria with a simple decor, where the female staff provide excellent service with a friendly smile.

Name: Machettö
Address: Via Vittorio Veneto 23, Pietra Ligure, 17027, Italy
Description En: Situated amid the picturesque alleyways of the historic centre, this beautiful restaurant boasts an elegant decor and a warm, friendly welcome. Here, the young, talented chef (originally from Campania but now settled in Liguria) serves Mediterranean cuisine with a traditional regional influence cleverly added to each dish. Our favourite dishes included the excellent trenette pasta with octopus ragù and 24-month-aged parmesan fondue, and the timeless “brandacujun”, which is freshly prepared and served at your table by the chef himself.

Name: NUH Osteria Contemporanea
Description En: Situated in Tivoli’s historic centre, this restaurant has a young chef at the helm who skilfully pays tribute to the region’s gastronomic traditions. Although the menu also features a few fish dishes and the occasional ingredient from outside Lazio, it is the dishes made from local produce with their intense, delicious flavours that will linger long in the memory.

Name: Nunù Trattoria Moderna
Address: Corso Giuseppe Garibaldi 32, Torre del Greco, 80059, Italy
Description En: Just a stone’s throw from the seafront promenade, this friendly, colourful restaurant serves delicious, carefully prepared fish and meat dishes inspired by the traditions of Campania yet reinterpreted with a touch of imagination and character by skilful owner-chef Nunzio Spagnuolo. Our inspector’s favourite dish was the ravioli alla caprese with three types of tomato, provolone del Monaco cheese and basil-infused olive oil.

Name: Locanda Sant'Agata
Address: via del Brennero, SS 12 km 5,812, San Giuliano Terme, 55016, Italy
Description En: Not far from the village, this pleasant boutique hotel is home to a friendly, well-kept restaurant surrounded by a relaxing garden where guests can enjoy alfresco dining in summer. The menu features traditional meat and fish dishes with the occasional modern, personalised twist, such as “calamarotto” – squid (calamaro) stuffed with seafood pancotto, vegetables in dry vermouth and confit plum tomatoes.

Name: Il Sommelier
Description En: This small, intimate restaurant next to the elegant Palazzo Roccabruna in the historic centre is slightly off the beaten track despite its central location. Recently opened by the Poletti brothers (one in the kitchen, the other front of house), with an attractive dining room designed by the owners’ father, the restaurant serves top-quality ingredients (especially fish and seafood) in dishes which include modern influences (the mango cheesecake is delicious) and a pleasing classic appeal (raw fish dishes).

Name: Locanda Le Logge
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Classic Cuisine
Description En: Occupying a period building in the heart of this beautiful village, with an outdoor dining space laid out under the portico in summer, this restaurant serves typical cuisine from the Marche on its various tasting menus and à la carte supplemented by daily specials. Boasting a rustic and pleasantly informal atmosphere, the restaurant also offers six romantic guestrooms with wrought-iron beds, including a four-poster bed in the Sogno room.

Name: Exforo
Description En: Occupying old stables in the square where the town’s livestock market was once held, this restaurant boasts charming views of the Prato della Valle gardens. Also home to a bistro serving aperitif snacks and a cocktail bar for post-dinner drinks, the main restaurant is very much the focal point here, with its dark-coloured, contemporary decor and colourful, modern cuisine. In summer, don’t miss the summer terrace with its fine views.

Name: Il Ristorante Alain Ducasse Roma
Description En: A few steps from Piazza del Popolo, a 17th-century palazzo houses the Romeo hotel and, within it, the restaurant bearing the name of the world’s most-starred chef. The dining room – like the entire hotel, designed by Zaha Hadid – is a triumph of precious materials: ebony on the walls, marble for the open kitchen, an aesthetic that unites luxury, exclusivity and futuristic lines in every detail. Leading the kitchen is a young chef who honed his technique in the kitchens of Alain Ducasse, between Monaco and Paris. Here he selects ingredients of great quality and works them into compositions that are never complicated, characterised by clear, readable flavours, often punctuated by Mediterranean accents. Cooking that finds its most convincing expression in the elegance of the raw materials and the precision of the cooking, perfectly in harmony with the striking surroundings.

Name: La Ripadoro
Description En: Tucked away in the small medieval village of Rivalto, with stunning views of the surrounding Tuscan hills, the Ripadoro agriturismo is home to this rustic yet elegant farm-restaurant serving traditional Tuscan dishes made from produce grown on the property. There’s an authentic charcoal grill which is used to cook classic ribeye steak, as well as the superb “girarrosto” – boned pigeon and quail served with potato rosti, yellow carrots with ginger and Jerusalem artichokes in foil. Make sure you save space for one of the delicious desserts! In summer, it’s well worth booking one of the outdoor tables under the shade of large lime trees.

Name: Ego
Description En: The experience begins at the moment of reservation, when guests choose the number of courses and prepare to place themselves entirely in the hands of the chef’s creativity. Ego is a reflection of the personality of Lorenzo De Lio, a young Roman talent with an international journey that emerges clearly in his dishes. His cuisine is a voyage without borders, where Mexican influences, Southeast Asian references, and unexpected inspirations coexist, constructed to stimulate the palate with spices, contrasts, and intensity. The dining room counts just five tables – to be reserved well in advance – entrusted to the gracious and knowledgeable care of Beatrice, who also curates wine pairings by the glass with great sensitivity.

Name: Vico Astemio
Description En: Situated in the village centre surrounded by narrow alleyways, this attractive restaurant is housed in an old barrel warehouse. Here, self-taught chef Massimiliano Vasta serves colourful cuisine that is full of delicious flavours, showcased on two tasting menus and an impressive à la carte with an equal emphasis on meat and fish (despite the port being just a stone’s throw away). We focused on the main course and particularly enjoyed the Zuppa di Pietro, an updated version of the chef’s father’s favourite dish, as well as the tempting array of tasty welcome snacks. There’s an impressive wine list, while the family farm ensures that the extra-virgin olive oil is also of the highest quality.

Name: Ostaria
Address: Via Giovan Battista Perasso 10/12, Syracuse, 96100, Italy
Description En: This restaurant in the centre of the modern city, yet just a stone’s throw from Ortigia, focuses exclusively on meat (local and from further afield, much of it aged on the premises), which is sourced from non-intensive farming and cooked using contemporary methods such as the Josper oven. The excellent wine list focuses mainly on Sicilian labels but also includes bottles from elsewhere in Italy, as well as from other important wine-producing countries. A typical Sicilian ambience, soft lighting in the evening and friendly yet professional service complete the picture.

Name: Essenza
Description En: Essenza is housed within the Borghi dell'Eremo resort in a stunning setting surrounded by beautiful and tranquil natural landscapes. The spacious dining room, which is flooded with natural light thanks to the picture windows that look out at the Umbrian hills, provides the backdrop for a culinary experience that focuses on traditional cuisine. Our inspector particularly recommends the exquisite Borghi saffron tagliatelle served with a rabbit ragù (the rabbits are raised on the estate’s own farm).

Name: Locanda dell'Angelo
Description En: This stylish, elegant restaurant occupying a historic 17C building in an attractive medieval village serves contemporary cuisine which is influenced by recipes and ingredients from Liguria and Piedmont alike. Dishes include Ligurian-style rabbit terrine with a pine nut and gravy sauce, and Piedmontese white suckling pig tomahawk on sauerkraut with a spicy, sour apple sauce.

Name: À Putia - Enoteca e Cucina
Address: via Umberto I° 456, Giardini Naxos, 98035, Italy
Description En: This restaurant began life in 1946 as a grocery store (the name is the Sicilian word for shop) which, forty years later, was transformed into a very simple yet attractive trattoria-cum-wine bar (don’t be shocked by the paper tablecloths!). The cuisine focuses mainly on fish, seafood and fresh market produce, while the wines come from Sicily and further afield. Booking ahead is essential here, partly because there are only a few tables but also because the opening hours vary depending on the season. You may find it difficult to find somewhere to park between the main street and the seafront in the busy town centre, but it’s well worth the effort.

Name: Casa Camperio
Description En: Under the careful direction of Roberto Conti, here in the role of executive chef, this intimate address in the basement of an elegant central building, predominantly used for offices, presents cooking that reinterprets Milanese tradition with contemporary sensibility. The dishes speak a modern language, punctuated by refined Japanese influences that emerge decisively in the sharing snacks, raw dishes and sushi rolls. The establishment also functions as a cocktail bar, thanks to a list of twelve original drinks, created in-house and united by a constant Japanese-inspired thread.

Name: La Ristobottega
Address: Via Vittorio Veneto 46A, Reggio Calabria, 89121, Italy
Description En: As the name suggests, this restaurant is divided into two sections: a shop on one side, which sells local products such as tempting salumi and cheeses (they also serve informal lunches at midday); and on the other, in the evening, an attractive bistro with wooden tables and soft lighting, where you can enjoy delicious cuisine. Among the fish dishes (aged on site), we particularly recommend the grouper fillet with vegetable caponatina and raw scampi on a bed of mashed potato, while the meat options include top-quality cuts such as Wagyu beef. A small outdoor space on the pavement completes the picture.

Name: Al Pilèr
Description En: Situated in the town centre, this restaurant can be accessed by car despite its location perched above the town. It takes its name from an old boundary stone that is still partially visible and which once separated the Arab and Norman sections of town (the word comes from the curious Gallo-Italian dialect spoken in parts of Sicily, which has more in common with the Lombardy dialect than those of the island itself). Meat takes centre stage, including the aged meats on display, although the menu also features generous, colourful classic dishes with a creative twist. There’s also an outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Alloro
Description En: In the baroque heart of the city, this small restaurant – comprising two dining rooms, one overlooking the bell tower of the Basilica Collegiata dei Santi Apostoli Pietro e Paolo, the other more intimate – welcomes guests with a contemporary style and cozy atmosphere. The cooking takes a modern and bold approach, offered either à la carte or through two tasting menus that trace journeys of travel and inspiration by way of forthright and intriguing flavours. To then end the meal with a touch of lightness thanks to the playful ‘tiratisù’. Here, you are not simply clients, but guests.

Name: Osteria del Ponte
Address: Via Vittorio Veneto 22, Trezzano sul Naviglio, 20090, Italy
Description En: Housed in a majestic historic farmhouse, this small friendly restaurant boasts intimate dining rooms and attractive “shabby-chic” style furnishings. In summer, the delightful outdoor space in the internal courtyard offers an idyllic setting. Traditional Milanese cuisine is the star of the show here, including specialities such as risotto with roasted bone-marrow, mondeghili meatballs and delicious breaded veal cutlet, also available in an “imperial” version for sharing.

Name: Il Cairoli
Description En: As is suggested by the use of the definite article before its name, Il Cairoli is a modern hotel restaurant with its own entrance. The menu here features classic Milanese specialities such as mondeghili meatballs, ossobucco risotto and veal cutlets, as well as other delicious and colourful dishes that are contemporary in style and based on the use of seasonal ingredients. There are also a few vegetarian options, as well as daily specials at midday, when a quicker and cheaper lunch option is available. An attractive dining room with large picture windows boasting views (albeit partial) of the Sforza castle adds to the appeal.

Name: ConTanima
Description En: In the gardens of the Hotel Laurin, a refined glasshouse bathed in soft lighting and furnished with just a few tables creates an intimate and romantic candlelit atmosphere (booking recommended). In the kitchen, a Neapolitan chef delivers creative cuisine that blends local ingredients and Neapolitan influences, including vegetarian and meat dishes. The menu offers signature dishes and tasting menus of 3, 6 or 8 courses (the last being a surprise, chosen by the chef). Young and interactive waiting staff accompany the experience with elegance and warmth.

Name: Casa Rusticale dei Cavalieri Templari
Description En: This building, home to the San Bartolo Knights Templar “hospital” until the 13C, now houses an attractive restaurant which continues this old tradition of hospitality. Here, a friendly dining room with a pleasantly rustic yet elegant feel serves as a backdrop for generous, substantial cuisine with a hint of creativity. An outdoor space shaded by a vine-planted pergola completes the picture.

Name: La Sbornia a Verduno
Description En: This building, almost cube-like in shape with large floor-to-ceiling windows that offer breathtaking views of the beautiful surrounding countryside, is striking for its modern, contemporary design, with a delightful outdoor space that is perfect for alfresco dining. Originally from Puglia, talented owner-chef Carmela Straniero fell in love with the Langhe having spent time working in England and Italy. Her refined and highly personalised cuisine fully respects culinary traditions and is prepared using top-quality local ingredients.

Name: Stua Noa Fine Dining
Description En: Within the Hotel Concordia, the restaurant unfolds across two small and modern stube, reached by passing through the hotel’s main dining room. Here one may order à la carte or entrust oneself to one of the tasting menus – available also in a vegetarian version – for a contemporary cuisine that is measured and well-grounded in the flavours and produce of the territory.

Name: Enigma Restaurant
Address: Viale Leopoldo Nobili 2/c, Reggio Emilia, 42121, Italy
Description En: Housed within a hotel in a centrally located park, this attractive restaurant with its own private entrance boasts fine views of the surrounding greenery through its large windows. The cuisine is both regional and imaginative, often combining influences from Emilia and Campania (chef Ciro Sieno’s native region), as demonstrated by the tortello pasta filled with a Neapolitan ragù and the cappelletti filled with minestra maritata. Vegetarian options also feature alongside the meat and fish dishes on the menu.

Name: Waby
Address: Via Carlo De Cristoforis 2, Milan, 20124, Italy
Description En: Milan is becoming increasingly known in Italy for its impressive choice of ethnic cuisine, and one example among many is this excellent restaurant behind Corso Como and Piazza Gae Aumenti. With its contemporary design, including a counter with stools to the rear, and international ambience, the restaurant serves modern, attractive Japanese cuisine, including creative raw dishes (such as raw tuna noodles in dashi broth with a sprinkling of yuzu, topped with salmon roe marinated in sake), sushi and sashimi, uramaki and gozya, robata and much more, with a constant focus on top-quality ingredients. The excellent wine selection features labels from Italy and France (including a number of champagnes), as well as a good choice of sake, also available by the glass.

Name: Téa del Kosmo
Description En: Leaving one’s car in the car park, a lift carries guests directly to the third floor, where the restaurant Kosmo Taste the Mountain is situated; from here one is accompanied through to the Téa del Kosmo, its gourmet offshoot. ‘Téa’ means mountain chalet in the Valtellina dialect, and the atmosphere evokes precisely that of a modern alpine refuge, clad in reclaimed timbers, with a fireplace at its centre and just four tables arranged around it, for an intimate and quietly immersive experience. Booking online allows guests to choose between two or three tasting menus (depending on the season) all built upon alpine ingredients and the careful use of vegetables from the house kitchen garden, interpreted with creativity by chef Michele Talarico. Apulian by origin – as the excellent bread readily suggests – he is deeply enamoured of these mountains and brings to the table a cuisine that seeks to honour every part of the ingredient. Not to be missed is the spaghetti alla chitarra, made in-house with stale bread and dressed with a sauce of dill, garum and trout bottarga, both crafted by the chef himself. Equally unmissable are his vegetarian studies, such as the celeriac or the ‘100% carrot’: dishes that linger long in the memory.

Name: Soul Restaurant
Description En: Having spent a long period of time gaining experience abroad, the enthusiastic couple at the helm of this restaurant have returned to Italy where they delight their guests with imaginative and creative cuisine that focuses on top-quality ingredients and beautiful presentation. They serve three tasting menus, with the additional option of choosing courses à la carte style. Special mention should be made of the warm welcome, excellent service and skilful wine selection, all of which make the dining experience here even more enjoyable.

Name: Novanta
Description En: Situated in the Bassa Pavese region and easily accessible via the A21, Novanta is a classic, rustic-style restaurant with a warm and authentic feel. At lunchtime, the menu offers simple, genuine dishes, while in the evening and at the weekend the cuisine takes on a more gourmet and regional flavour. Duck takes pride of place on the menu, featuring in numerous dishes, and is an important ingredient in the delicious ragù served with fusilloni pasta. The extensive wine list features local and international labels, including an interesting 2012 Wollenweider Riesling Renano from Germany’s Moselle region. The lunchtime menu offers unbeatable value for money!

Name: Radici ristorante in vigna
Description En: The Relais Le Marne occupies the top floor of this building in a verdant setting overlooking the estate’s vineyards, while the ground floor is home to the restaurant. In the latter, a late-19C, brick-vaulted ceiling combines with clean lines and designer-style furniture to create a warm and attractive ambience. The cuisine is regional in flavour and finished with a light modern touch – there’s also a vegetarian tasting menu option. The excellent wine list includes the Mura Mura wines produced on the estate itself.

Name: Manna
Description En: Hidden away in a quiet district, this semi-pedestrianised area comes to life in the evening thanks to the restaurants nearby. The bar at Manna serves excellent cocktails, with a few tables outside on the street, while inside the new, elegant and minimalist-style dining room you’ll enjoy personalised cuisine that skilfully combines tradition and creativity. Perfect for a romantic dinner or a business lunch, with a faster menu available for the latter. Among the desserts, we highly recommend the delicious and not-to-be-missed Tarte Tatin.

Name: Izu
Description En: Recent refurbishment at this long-standing restaurant on the city’s main square has given it the feel of an elegant bistro. Although the owners and managers here are Chinese, the cuisine focuses on Japan and includes all the usual classic options (sushi, uramaki, sashimi etc), as well as a series of “Izu special creations” and various dishes influenced by Asia and the Mediterranean alike. There’s also a good wine list (including, as you might expect, a few sakes) overseen by an experienced and knowledgeable sommelier.

Name: A Mangiare
Address: viale Monte Grappa 3, Reggio Emilia, 42121, Italy
Description En: Situated at the entrance to the historic centre, this restaurant now has a new owner, who is nonetheless assisted by the old management team front of house. The cuisine here includes traditional and creative fare, both on the tasting menu and the à la carte, in dishes that are generously portioned and beautifully presented – you’ll also find a few fish options. Care and simplicity are the principles that guide the young female chef who arrived here with the new owners.

Name: Sunrise Restaurant
Description En: One of the most attractive restaurants in the city centre, Sunrise occupies the ground floor of an old Bourbon palazzo, extending right to the back of the building where you’ll find the delightful “literary veranda” and, beyond the large windows, a beautiful outdoor space surrounded by a garden planted with citrus trees. The menu has an exclusive focus on fish, with a combination of classic options and light, modern dishes, while an entire page is dedicated to raw fish and seafood. The wine list includes several champagnes.

Name: Mammà Isola di Capri
Description En: Situated within the multi-functional Sondo building (also home to a museum, offices and exhibition spaces), this large restaurant decorated in contemporary, post-industrial style provides the backdrop for chef Raffaele Amitrano’s Mediterranean cuisine which is strongly influenced by the flavours of Campania. His plin pasta dish pays tribute to the region and is particularly interesting thanks to ingredients such as cacio cheese, pepper and raw prawns. Make sure you arrive early if you want to visit the building and maybe even take advantage of the large sharing table.

Name: Al Pozzo
Description En: The cuisine at this restaurant is almost exclusively based on fish and seafood, with three main points of focus – an extensive array of raw dishes; ageing of almost all the fish to accentuate flavour and texture (as well as making the skin pleasantly crispy); and the grilling of some courses. Top-quality ingredients and delicious desserts complete the picture.

Name: Acqua & Sale
Description En: The enthusiastic owners of Acqua & Sale have transformed what was originally a simple fishmonger’s into a restaurant with the addition of an informal, well-appointed dining room on the side. Here, guests enjoy unfussy fresh fish dishes, including an array of raw options and Mediterranean recipes with the occasional personal touch. Recipes include grilled octopus with black broccoli and wine-fermented plums, and porchetta-style tuna with a green sauce, fried new potatoes and sweet and sour peppers. The perfect choice for fish-lovers!

Name: Gagini
Description En: In the vibrant heart of the city, between the Vucciria market and the Cala harbor, modern design and vivid colours bring a contemporary touch to the timeless charm of the ancient walls that house it: those of the 16th-century workshop of sculptor Antonello Gagini. In the kitchen, a new chef of Piedmontese origin weaves together the recipes of his native region and northern Italy with the freshness of the sea and the rich pleasures of Trinacria, drawing out their quality through original and well-considered pairings. Among the standout dishes are barbecued mussels with ‘nduja salmoriglio, Vietnamese bisque and crispy rapini, or tagliatelle made with 30 egg yolks, served with artichokes, citron and tuna bottarga: dishes that speak of a vibrant and contemporary gastronomic encounter.

Name: Gli Uffici
Address: Via Mario De Candia 3/5, Cagliari, 09124, Italy
Description En: Situated on the second floor of the 19C Palazzo Boyl facing the Bastioni di Saint Remy, this restaurant is home to chef Tommaso Sanguedolce from Puglia, who demonstrates techniques acquired throughout his period of training with skill and precision. Equally at ease with fish and meat, the chef creates recipes inspired by the Mediterranean and delicious traditional Italian cuisine, as demonstrated in his Italian-style brioche – a kind of sourdough maritozzo which is served warm with a creamy pistachio ice-cream, intensely flavoured saffron ricotta and red berry salad. There’s a delightful long and narrow outdoor dining area on the terrace with stunning views of the city framed by statues symbolising the four seasons.

Name: Terradimare
Description En: Overlooking a broad piazza that faces the evocative harbour basin of Trani, and a short distance from the magnificent cathedral, a masterpiece of Apulian Romanesque and enduring symbol of the city, this restaurant, modest in size yet possessed of considerable grace, has the talented Domenico Di Tondo in the kitchen. The gastronomic offering expresses clean, assured flavours and an elegant personality, favouring the catch of the day and a seafood-led kitchen that follows the arrivals closely, while not forgoing – in a nod to the restaurant’s name – some interesting meat alternatives. In the dining room, an entirely female front-of-house team, attentive and solicitous, completes what is a harmonious and carefully considered experience.

Name: Visteria
Description En: Situated in the Royal Victoria hotel on picturesque Varenna’s small central piazza, this restaurant has just a few tables overlooking one of the most spectacular sights on Lake Como, namely the Bellagio promontory flanked on either side by the two branches of the lake. Talented chef Francesco Sarno, originally from Salerno, is at the helm in the kitchen here – the colour and intense flavours of his native Campania are evident in some of his dishes.

Name: Taverna e' Mare
Address: Via Principal Marina, 16, Torre del Greco, 80059, Italy
Description En: In an elegant setting facing the harbour and the sea, the dining room at this restaurant is a terrace with large picture windows boasting beautiful views that also include Capri. The sea takes pride of place on the menu, which features fresh fish and plenty of local produce in the cuisine served here. Don’t miss the raw fish options, which include a selection of oysters, tartares and ceviche. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the roll of sea bass stuffed with spinach, fior di latte, beurre blanc sauce, parsley oil and onions.

Name: Silvestro
Description En: A cosy, welcoming restaurant with a contemporary feel situated on the edge of Monza’s park. Owner-chef Giuseppe Silvestro is young and talented, with excellent experience in renowned restaurants, and very precise ideas about the type of cuisine he wants to serve here, namely personalised and imaginative dishes inspired by the region and the Mediterranean. We particularly enjoyed the morone fish served with a Piennolo cherry tomato cream and the “mantecato” made with fish scraps.

Name: Nannini
Description En: This restaurant run by the young Nannini brothers (one front of house, the other in the kitchen) occupies one of Livorno’s most interesting buildings, situated in the district of Antignano with its period houses and typical atmosphere. The focus here is almost exclusively on fish, in dishes which are original yet at the same time respectful of their ingredients – matured fish is one of the specialities. A top-quality dining experience.

Name: Le Cantine
Address: via cantine cattaneo 1, Sestri Levante, 16039, Italy
Description En: A few management changes, but they are still in charge: Enrico in the kitchen and Nadia in the dining room. Already in a bucolic setting, but just a few steps from the centre and the sea, preceded by its own vegetable gardens, you dine within the restored 1590 walls of a former oil cellar, in a pleasantly rustic and romantic atmosphere overflowing with decorations. But the best comes with the cuisine, with no fish menu at all, with a strong focus on self-produced vegetables and succulent meat dishes, mostly barbecued with olive wood, along with a good selection of wines, mostly regional and high-quality.

Name: Franchino
Description En: Situated within the Onda Verda hotel on the road down to the delightful seaside town of Conca dei Marini, this attractive restaurant boasts a terrace overlooking the sea that is hard to resist. The menu here adds to the appeal, featuring traditional fresh fish dishes and local seafood recipes which combine to make this an exquisitely romantic experience. When you book, ask for one of the tables on the terrace or on the pedestrianised promenade.

Name: Il Salotto Atelier Gourmet
Description En: The small, classic Rosabianca hotel on the seafront in Rapallo has begun to improve its facilities, starting with its restaurant where large windows (which can be opened in summer) overlook the promenade, and its intimate, elegant interior with subtle lighting and a relaxing ambience. The cuisine focuses on fish and seafood which are skilfully prepared so that the quality of the superb ingredients shines through, while the service ensures that guests are looked after with discretion and professionalism.

Name: DaV by Da Vittorio Louis Vuitton
Description En: Situated in the heart of the central fashion district at the beginning of Via Montenapoleone, this new restaurant is the result of a collaboration between the renowned Cerea family and the equally prestigious fashion house Louis Vuitton, one of whose Milanese stores is located right behind it. The cuisine here is Italian to its core, albeit with a focus on dishes reinterpreted in a contemporary style that blends perfectly with the setting and the expectations of its guests. The decor is that of an elegant bistro, with the very busy dining room immediately after the entrance and reception, and a more intimate mezzanine accessible via stairs or a lift. The staff will quickly put you at ease and are on hand to offer recommendations from the à la carte or the chef’s tasting menu.

Name: Don Carlos
Description En: The tribute that the Grand Hotel dedicates to Giuseppe Verdi is accompanied, in the small historic rooms of the Don Carlos, by a tribute to Milanese and Italian cuisine, perhaps with a Mediterranean nuance introduced by multi-star Gennaro Esposito, here as a consultant, and carefully executed. In a succession of sketches, pictures and paintings dedicated to the world of opera, for music lovers the restaurant is a must-visit. Caruso Nuovo, on the other hand, with its bistro formula, can be an always inviting and less demanding alternative.

Name: Cascina Moro
Address: Strada Provinciale 8, Frazione Moro, Locate di Triulzi, 20085, Italy
Description En: This skilfully restored 18C farmhouse has all the authentic charm of the Milanese lowland region, with each corner telling a story, from the intimate lounges to the delightful room with a large stone fireplace. There’s also a bright, welcoming veranda-style space which is perfect at any time of year. The menu features an array of meat and fish dishes, including dishes that celebrate Mediterranean cuisine and Milanese traditions alike. The well-stocked wine cellar (which can be visited) will delight wine-enthusiasts thanks to its excellent selection of interesting labels.

Name: Come in Corte Aurora
Description En: At this restaurant, the two brothers (the owners) who work together front of house come from a family of farmers whose meat features on the menu, while two other brothers, originally from Rome but settled in the Veneto for many years, are at the helm in the kitchen. The original and colourful cuisine aims to please both the eyes and the palate, with dishes showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte – the quail served with a caponata of apricots, yucca and porcini mushroom mayonnaise was particularly memorable. Housed in the Villa Lussana, with its seven Art Nouveau-style guestrooms, the restaurant has been completely renovated by the new young owners. In summer, meals are served outdoors with views of the surrounding hills.

Name: Amandus
Address: via statale 125, Mandello del Lario, 23826, Italy
Description En: Situated in the Villa Lario Resort, this restaurant directly overlooks the lake and boasts fine views which extend as far as the promontory of Bellagio. The excellent cuisine features a few freshwater fish dishes, as well as plenty of meat and seafood options, on a menu that combines classic recipes with a few more creative specialities.

Name: Porta di Basso
Description En: Although the entrance is in one of the alleys of the historic center, the dining room opens entirely towards the sea, as it is perched on a cliff overlooking the water. Naturally, the most sought-after tables are on the terraces or near the windows, offering a stunning view. In Domenico Cilenti's kitchen, there's no à la carte option – only two tasting menus (one of which is vegetarian), showcasing many Gargano products from both sea and land.

Name: Isi Ivano Ricchebono Chef
Description En: In the heart of the Carignano quarter, the restaurant conceals itself along a quiet side street, revealing an atmosphere that is both intimate and elegant. Three tasting menus – Tradition and Innovation, Classic, and Vegetarian – guide the guest through a gastronomic journey rich in identity, with the option of dining à la carte should one prefer. The cooking unites boldness with refinement, interweaving classic references and modern impulses in dishes that impress through their balance and personality; the trofie al pesto genovese, presented here in a reinterpretation of decided character, are not to be missed. The business lunch proves a most welcome discovery: broad choice, excellent quality, and a value for money that is genuinely winning. The wine list is generous and well-structured, with a particularly interesting focus on Ligurian labels, while the competent and professional service contributes to making the experience pleasingly relaxed within surroundings that are both considered and comfortable.

Name: Arnaldo - Clinica Gastronomica
Description En: Crossing the threshold of this fifteenth-century palace next to Hotel Aquila d’Oro is like stepping into an Emilian tale of aromas, flavors, and memory. Rolling carts take center stage: antipasti featuring hand-carved prosciutto and erbazzone, desserts with zabaione to pour over pears in red wine, and the essential parade of roasts and boiled meats. The sfogline (pasta makers) prepare fresh pasta each morning, served in broth or with rich sauces. Arnaldo is a hymn to tradition: no frills, just authentic taste!

Name: Casa Vissani
Address: S.S. 448 Km 6,600, vocabolo Cannitello, Baschi, 05023, Italy
Description En: Upon arrival, welcomed by son Luca, weather permitting, treat yourself to a pause on the lawn facing the lake before entering and immersing yourself in the elegance of the dining rooms. You’ll begin in the rock room for the welcome, aperitif, and dish selection, then move to the refined service room, a masterful mix of diverse elements combined with open kitchens framed like paintings. Recently, a new à la carte selection method was introduced, allowing each diner to choose at least two dishes from the Departures and Arrivals sections (excluding Sweet Stops). Alternatively, you can opt for one of two tasting menus proposed by the chef: Volare in Piccolo (Flying Small), featuring 4 courses, or Volare in Grande (Flying Grand), with 7 courses. “TerritOri” is instead the new pop restaurant that, in another room of the same structure, complements Casa Vissani. More inclusive, this concept traces its storied past, offering cuisine that celebrates Italian territorial traditions with a more accessible and familiar formula.

Name: Oberraindlhof
Description En: The family that run this restaurant occupying an old farmhouse with origins dating back to the 16C has a relationship with the region that goes back decades. In later years, the farm became an inn and it has now been run by the same family for five generations, all motivated by a desire to introduce their guests to the best local recipes and ingredients. Dishes include excellent fresh ravioli stuffed with cheese produced in the nearby valley and served (in summer) with tomato and basil sauce. An excellent wine list and the hotel’s warm and friendly ambience add to the appeal.

Name: La Tradizione - Cucina Casalinga
Description En: A corner of traditional Apulia to be experienced in a trattoria in the centre, in a typical and pleasantly homely atmosphere. The dishes are listed verbatim, not to be missed are the series of starters, but also the characteristic fresh pastas.

Name: Sa Mandra
Description En: Located within the Sa Mandra farm holiday resort, this restaurant offers the opportunity to discover and appreciate one of the most iconic products of Sardinian culinary tradition: roast suckling pig. The single, fixed menu features it as the main course; guests are encouraged to arrive early to watch the cooking process (the owners are happy to explain each step in detail). Once seated, diners are served a succession of dishes and tastings, all prepared with ingredients grown directly on the farm. Rooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Antica Osteria
Description En: Situated in the centre of a beautiful little village in the Val di Sole, at the mouth of the Val di Peio and the foot of the Presanella mountains, this pleasant restaurant is divided into three small dining rooms with a charming mountain feel, plus a veranda with modern floor-to-ceiling windows. Every year, the food at this restaurant, prepared by one of the members of the family, improves in quality while retaining its focus on the region – the char (marinated in miso) and the venison loin are particularly good. The menu includes traditional recipes alongside more personalised dishes.

Name: Osteria Dalie e Fagioli
Address: via Campagnola 45, Manerba del Garda, 25080, Italy
Description En: One of the best restaurants in the region, where you’ll enjoy eclectic cuisine full of convincing flavours which is inspired by various regional traditions (especially those from Brescia, but also from elsewhere in Italy) which always hits the mark.

Name: Moi
Description En: It's worth heading off the tourist trail and making your way to the north of the city to find this small restaurant with its friendly staff and delicious cuisine. The chef here is Thomas Moi, whose dishes are influenced by various gastronomic traditions (including from outside Italy) and are definitely worth trying! Booking ahead is recommended.

Name: ChiaroScuro
Address: corso Vittorio Emanuele II 380, Cagliari, 09123, Italy
Description En: In this small neighbourhood restaurant, chef Marina pays homage to the iconic dishes of her island, such as Su Filindeu, a type of pasta in broth formed by very thin threads (the name means “threads of God”), stacked in three criss-crossed layers: it is a complex preparation that requires great skill. Originally from the Nuoro area, this talented cook's menu focuses mainly on inland dishes; nevertheless, two or three fish specialities are always on the menu.

Name: Podere 39
Description En: Just beyond Porta Romana, one finds an intimate dining room with few covers – advance booking is strongly advised – where the restaurant wins one over immediately through its style: a small space of considerable personality, made all the more appealing by rustic details set off by generous and carefully tended floral arrangements. A portion of the ingredients comes directly from their own farm, Podere 39, a guarantee of freshness and identity. The menu alternates between meat and fish, a well-judged balance that draws out the quality of the produce and a cooking of authentic and unaffected character.

Name: Accademia Ristorante
Description En: Over the years, the gastronomic quality of this excellent restaurant has been confirmed and even increased. The cuisine is basic Piedmontese (the ravioli del plin are excellent), with the addition of a few seafood dishes and some more technical courses (such as rabbit à la royale). In fact, solidity and growth are mainly due to the passion of the histrionic owner, Nicola Mecca, who is polite and passionate and also adept at providing pertinent suggestions on Monferrato wines and his beloved Champagnes. Naturally, we would also highlight the location itself, which offers some very fascinating insights: inside a late 18th-century aristocratic palace, you enter the first floor by climbing an imposing staircase, while with your nose to the sky you enjoy the all-Italian beauty of the frescoed ceilings.

Name: Aciniello
Description En: A simple family-run trattoria in operation since 1948, offering traditional cuisine in an informal and relaxed atmosphere. The dishes are relatively simple but full of flavor. Among the main courses, meat reigns supreme, with the exception of the baccalà.

Name: Vivilo
Address: via Nazario Sauro 15, Corte Franca, 25040, Italy
Description En: An old hay barn has been converted into this elegant restaurant offering impeccable service and delicious cuisine with a focus on classic dishes, including a vegetarian menu, an excellent cheese trolley and not-to-be-missed desserts. In other words, everything you need for a superb dining experience among the Franciacorta vineyards!

Name: I Lustri Lab
Description En: After years working in Michelin-starred restaurants in Lazio, owner-chef Kerim Jlali has achieved his dream of opening his own restaurant here, along with his life-partner Chiara. In an informal and colourful setting, the chef demonstrates his passion for fish and seafood, transforming his ingredients into contemporary recipes using skilful techniques (he refers to his restaurant as a “lab”) . The end results are visually striking and full of colour.

Name: Zamù
Description En: This restaurant’s name comes from the initial syllables of the two restaurants that once stood here, which were combined and refurbished a few years ago. Now in the style of a modern bistro, Zamù serves traditional and generously portioned cuisine, plus a reasonably priced business menu at lunchtime. There’s an equal emphasis on meat and fish on the menu, while the clearly displayed blackboard lists the daily specials available.

Name: Oasi
Description En: Over the years, the beach establishment has gradually developed: the beach and bar remain, but today's pride is the restaurant. The husband and wife divide their duties between the kitchen and dining area (including wine). They've built a good reputation thanks to classic seafood cuisine, highlighted by the chef's personal creative touches. A passionate and imaginative self-taught chef, his steamed oyster seasoned with lemon zest on tomato water is a particularly tasty shot that represents their style.

Name: Persika
Description En: Persika is a name that combines Italy and Sweden: in both languages, it means "peach." In the Chia district, an Italian restaurateur collaborates with a highly experienced Swedish chef to create a gastro-bistro with a relaxed and welcoming atmosphere. The surprise menu is often chosen, but there's also an interesting and accessible à la carte option. The cuisine is contemporary, with international influences and a strong focus on local ingredients.

Name: Osteria Forno Ercole
Description En: Hidden among the alleyways of Jesi, Osteria Forno Ercole is a former bakery (part of which can still be seen) which serves authentic cuisine in a warm, welcoming atmosphere. Local recipes and Mediterranean flavours come together on the traditional menu, with a focus on seasonal ingredients of the highest quality. Tagliatelle with porcini mushrooms, Marche-style fritto misto and steak with carrots, potatoes and radicchio are just some of the dishes on the menu here.

Name: Marino
Description En: As you drive along the scenic road from Pesaro, the sunset appears to the west, emerging from the greenery, while to the east the sea appears and disappears, finally settling as the backdrop to the pleasant outdoor area of this restaurant. This is the creation of the chef-owner, who, after traveling the world and working in Michelin-starred kitchens, has returned "home." He incorporates everything he has learned into modern and sometimes creative recipes, occasionally adding a light fusion touch, such as using fruit in dishes such as spaghetti with mussels and sea urchins enhanced by two well-balanced textures of peach.

Name: La Spigola
Address: Via Cristoforo Colombo 19, Golfo Aranci, 07020, Italy
Description En: You’ll immediately be charmed by this simple, Mediterranean-style restaurant which overlooks a white sandy beach and also has its own small private beach club. The views of the sea with its ever-changing shades of blue, the friendly service and, of course, the light, modern and delicious cuisine prepared by owner-chef Roberto Pisano from the best local fish, all add to the enjoyable experience here. Without forgetting the wine list which becomes truly extraordinary in its final three pages, where its “Orfanelli” wines showcase spectacular labels from across the globe in vintages from the 1970s, 80s and 90s.

Name: L'Aurum
Description En: Housed within L’Albereta, one of the most exclusive hotels in the Franciacorta region, this elegant restaurant provides the backdrop for Alberto Quadrio’s fine cuisine. On his various tasting menus and concise à la carte, this chef showcases local ingredients, from lake fish to Bergamo mutton, together with ingredients from further afield and produce grown in the estate’s own kitchen garden. The result is remarkable and elaborate cuisine of the highest quality.

Name: La Corte degli Dei
Description En: Relax amid the greenery on the patio terrace at this restaurant, which is housed in an old palazzo full of timeless charm and history. The interior is as charming as the exterior, boasting delightful dining rooms teeming with character. The cuisine skilfully encompasses traditional classic favourites alongside more innovative dishes, offering guests a culinary journey that combines past and present with elegance and flavour.

Name: Blu
Description En: Overlooking the delightful Piazzetta del Popolo, this restaurant delights guests with its views of the lake and the Rocca d’Angera, which can be enjoyed from the bright, relaxing dining rooms as well as from the shaded outdoor terrace. Chef Roberta, the soul of the restaurant, describes herself as a “home-style cook” who creates authentic dishes that are unfussy and full of flavour. Her “dal fondale alla superficie” fried fish recipe (literally, “from the depths to the surface”) is a triumph of flavours and includes zander, whitefish, trout, alborella and seasonal vegetables. Front of house, Carlo is at hand to recommend wines and pairings with style and elegance.

Name: Aquanova Hosteria
Description En: Housed in an old “water house” with origins dating back to the 17C and a large water wheel still visible in the dining room, this restaurant is home to a chef with Albanian origins (who grew up in Italy) who creates fresh, imaginative and seasonal cuisine in colourful dishes that are full of flavour. Sicilian traditions (inland as well as coastal) with a highly personalised twist take centre stage on the à la carte and tasting menus. There’s also a firm focus on vegetables thanks to the restaurant’s own on-site kitchen garden, which is well worth a visit. Also not to be missed is a visit to the delightful wine cellar – a real treasure trove which is home to more than 1 700 labels from across the globe.

Name: Sale
Address: Via dell'Amore 23, Licinella-Torre di Paestum, 84047, Italy
Description En: Housed within the Sogaris hotel, this restaurant boasts a spacious glass-fronted dining room overlooking a garden with swimming pool and furnished in a contemporary style that gives it an elegant yet relaxed look. The cuisine focuses on fish and seafood served in regional recipes reinterpreted with a light, modern touch. Don’t miss the daily raw seafood specials which are listed separately on the menu.

Name: Vita Pugliese
Description En: Situated a stone’s throw from the castle and the cathedral in the historic centre, this restaurant boasts an attractive outdoor space in an alleyway and traditional dining rooms with barrel-vaulted ceilings. Here, enjoy authentic dishes from Puglia with the occasional creative twist and careful attention to presentation.

Name: Saint Georges Premier
Description En: Standing in the king’s old pheasant grounds in Monza’s picturesque park just a stone’s throw from the famous racetrack, this restaurant has a refined and elegant feel. Here, the menu features Mediterranean fish recipes alongside regionally inspired dishes such as the excellent Milanese-style chop with mashed potatoes and sweet-and-sour shallots, as well as the occasional French-influenced recipe in a nod to the history of the park itself. The restaurant comes into its own in summer, when its attractive terrace looking out at the lush surroundings adds to the appeal.

Name: Fuori Rotta
Description En: In the "upper" part of the town, just steps from the public parking and already in the pedestrian area, the cuisine leans more towards Ligurian traditions than seafood. We enjoyed the "Scherpada": a savory vegetable tart with melted cheese, prepared and served by a young team passionate also about wine, as evidenced by the excellent wine list and recommendations from the owner-sommelier. Reservations are essential, especially for those wishing to sit at the panoramic outdoor tables.

Name: Casanova
Address: piazza San Benedetto 5, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
Description En: Occupying the first floor of the Palazzo del Suono del Mare in the historic centre of Polignano, this luxurious restaurant with its mosaic floors and Venetian chandeliers boasts views of the sea and the coast, as well as a panoramic terrace for alfresco dining in fine weather. The cuisine focuses on the gastronomic traditions of Puglia and Italy, which are reinterpreted with exciting results.

Name: Bluu il Mare Dentro
Address: Piazza Luigi Guerritore 11, Nocera Inferiore, 84014, Italy
Description En: The double “u” in this restaurant’s name is not a mistake but was added with the intention of evoking the flow and sound of water that can heard from afar. Here, chef Angelo Borghese demonstrates his passion for the sea through his delicious, precise and personalised recipes in which the highest quality fish takes centre stage. The escarole and anchovy pizza with colatura mayonnaise is excellent, as is the selection of raw and marinated fish dishes.

Name: Kircherhof
Description En: A 17th-century farmstead run by the same family for four generations, initially as a produce farm (fruit and vegetables) before the younger generation expanded into dining in the early 2000s. The offering, based entirely on organic, sustainably sourced ingredients, is compelling, particularly delicious, and rooted in local traditions while casting a savvy, curious eye toward the present. Dishes are colorful and very generous; the all-female service team is warm and happy to explain the house philosophy. There’s also a shop where you can stock up on treats before you leave.

Name: Capasanta
Description En: Just steps from the Shrine of Our Lady of the Rosary, young, talented chef Paolo Del Giudice delights with sea-driven, modern cooking. In a minimalist, marine-inspired space, he serves vibrant, flavorful dishes grounded in contemporary technique. Don’t miss his crudo selections and the irresistible scallops wrapped in lardo with spring pea purée and buffalo stracciatella. Excellent wines and a rich selection of house cocktails round out the experience.

Name: Vincenzo Degasperi
Description En: Situated in the busy heart of the town, the Zur Post hotel offers its guests a warm, homely welcome, discreet charm and Alpine elegance, while its contemporary-style wine-bar boasts a relaxed and friendly atmosphere. Here, Vincenzo Degasperi, the soul of the restaurant, oversees his guests’ experience with elegant professionalism and genuine hospitality, serving delicious Italian cuisine prepared from the best fresh ingredients. The superb wines are showcased on a skilfully chosen wine list, from which intriguing pairings are also available by the glass.

Name: UMA Roma
Description En: A restaurant with an innovative concept, placing at the heart of the experience three chefs working on two distinct tasting menus: one entirely plant-based and one that also includes animal proteins. The guiding idea is clear and well expressed in the dishes: a single ingredient becomes the absolute protagonist, explored through different techniques and showcased in all its parts. For those seeking creative cooking with an excellent quality-price ratio, this is the right place. The setting is pleasant, refined and defined by pared-back design; the majority of tables overlook the open kitchen directly, allowing guests to follow the crew’s work closely and experience the meal with an engaging extra touch.

Name: The View Milano
Description En: On the first floor, overlooking the piazza and set within surroundings of distinct historical character with glimpses of the Duomo and the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele, chef Valerio Braschi presents a culinary offering that sets recipes of the tradition alongside creations of a more contemporary spirit. The Contaminazioni menu traces a journey through Italian flavours and international influences, with South American and Asian forays conceived to intensify the taste. Worthy of particular note is the calamari salad, lifted by a well-judged chimichurri and tarragon, as is the costoletta alla milanese, reinterpreted with quiet grace in a pleasingly modern reading of the great Milanese classic. The spaces, elegant and formal in equal measure, are completed by the Terrazza Duomo, ideal for an aperitivo or after-dinner drink, with one of the most arresting views of the centre of Milan.

Name: Resilienza
Description En: Steps from the sea, just beyond the train tracks, a spot with an all-white decor welcomes guests in style, with outdoor spaces perfect for the warmer months. In the kitchen, his son reinterprets regional traditions, balancing seafood and land-based dishes, while his mother runs the dining room with warmth and professionalism. An authentic experience combining flavor, simplicity and a relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Il Paguro
Address: Via Cala Capra, Capo d'Orso, Palau, 07020, Italy
Description En: The small bay of Cala Capra is truly romantic and exclusive. Advance reservations are advised; without one, the barrier at the top of the road down to the marina won’t be raised. Hotel Capo d’Orso, which houses the Paguro restaurant, shares the same atmosphere: with a gorgeous Mediterranean-style terrace overlooking this little slice of paradise. The food suits the setting: classic, straightforward cooking built mostly around excellent local catch. A place that’s genuinely hard to leave.

Name: Ottavi Mare
Description En: In the heart of Bevagna, just steps from the picturesque Piazza Filippo Silvestri, this small, welcoming, and well-cared-for restaurant offers cuisine that blends seafood flavors with Umbrian tradition, serving balanced yet never predictable dishes. There are three tasting menus, each available in full or reduced versions, allowing for a personalized culinary journey.

Name: Osteria Giorgione da Masa
Address: Calle Larga dei Proverbi, 4582/A, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description En: Just steps from Campo Santi Apostoli, Chef Masa weaves together homestyle Japanese traditions with Venetian cicchetti, transcending the classic distinction between courses: here, dishes arrive all at once, without rules. For those who prefer to be guided, there’s a tasting menu offering a wide array of bites. Desserts are a true surprise, especially the yogurt, caramel, and matcha mousse, a favorite of our inspector.

Name: Mizuna Japanese Restaurant
Description En: Just outside the charming village center of San Pantaleo, this is easily one of Sardinia’s best Japanese restaurants. It’s the realized dream of an Italian chef who learned the craft while working around the world and who, in a minimalist, welcoming setting, deftly prepares an array of sushi and gyoza, plus mushi-pan (steamed cakes), soups, and more. Pristine flavors are assured by the kitchen’s reliance on mostly fresh Sardinian fish. To finish, creative Italian-inspired desserts appear alongside classic oriental mochi.

Name: Mia Ristorante
Address: via Borgotufi, Castel del Giudice, 86080, Italy
Description En: If you're not already in the area, plan some time to get there, traveling through a green, hilly landscape to reach Borgotufi, a "diffused hotel" spread among stone houses. In the former stables transformed into a restaurant, Marco Pasquarelli, a talented young chef, offers a modern take on various local ingredients, with a few seafood dishes as well.

Name: LeBolle
Description En: The “bubbles” promised in the name are five romantic private pods set in greenery, but you’ll also find beautiful comfort in the garden-side outdoor area and the more contemporary indoor dining room. After all, you’re inside the luxurious Boutique Hotel Stresa, and the same high standards are fully carried through. The kitchen took off with the arrival, in early 2025, of chef Salvatore Pacifico, who offers several tasting menus and an à la carte selection of modern dishes that at times reference the lake, the surrounding mountains, Campania, and also his native Puglia (especially apparent in the house-made breads). Expect balanced flavors and intentional lightness, along with harmonious presentations.

Name: Le Viste
Address: via del Falcone (spiaggia delle Viste), Portoferraio, 57037, Italy
Description En: Leaving the port area, you climb toward the historic area of the Medici fortresses and then descend again along the opposite side until you reach a small beach. Here you’ll find the restaurant, charmingly and characteristically simple, right in front of the water’s edge. The cuisine is pleasantly traditional and essentially offers classic Italian seafood dishes.

Name: Il Posticino
Description En: A tiny gem in the historic center, just steps from the San Michele towers. A very intimate setting, with a refined yet informal atmosphere. The cuisine? Seafood with a seasonal twist, including standouts such as the surprising Brandapolenta: creamy baccala, crispy polenta, taggiasca olive pâté. Reserving a table – especially for outdoor seating – is a must!

Name: Da Gianfranco
Address: via delle Orchidee 5, Alba Adriatica, 64011, Italy
Description En: Gianfranco Verdecchia, restaurateur and heir to a family of butchers, has always cooked the food that sustained his people. After running a restaurant in Sant’Omero – a hill town known for its festival dedicated to baccalà (salt cod), a staple in the area’s cuisine – he returned to his hometown of Giulianova. Here, in a stylish, secluded space away from the sea, he has kept baccalà as the sole seafood option, devoting an entire menu to it alongside a wide selection of dishes highlighting his first love: meat.

Name: Da Rinuccio
Description En: On the slopes of "a muntagna," one of the respectful nicknames for the volcano in the area, just outside the town with ample private parking, you'll find a family-oriented setting offering predominantly meat dishes, fresh pasta, and mushrooms. The dishes are carefully prepared, with generous portions, and meals are always enjoyed in a lovely glass-enclosed veranda. The wine list focuses mainly on Sicilian and particularly Catanese selections.

Name: Da Lorenzo – Al Giardino Segreto
Address: Fondamenta Madona de l'Orto, 3500, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description En: Hidden within the elegant walls of the NH Collection Palazzo dei Dogi, far from the bustling tourist crowds, Da Lorenzo – Al Giardino Segreto is an oasis of taste created by Paulo Airaudo, a multi-starred Spanish chef, who is assisted in the kitchen by the young Salvatore Paladino. Every dish at this restaurant is a refined combination of culinary technique, elegance and local flavours, enhanced by sophisticated Japanese accents. To immerse themselves in his gastronomic vision, guests can choose between two evocative tasting menus: Emozioni and Sensazioni – two experiences that convey the soul of this restaurant with style.

Name: Da iumén
Address: Via Vittorio Emanuele II 26, Castelnuovo Belbo, 14043, Italy
Description En: Since 1869, five generations have reinterpreted Piedmontese tradition through a modern lens. In an elegant, intimate setting, the restaurant serves dishes that fuse history and innovation – don’t miss the potato-and-hazelnut gnocchi with robiola cream. In the warmer months, reserve a table on the panoramic terrace: the view of the town hall and the hills of Castelnuovo Belbo is pure poetry.

Name: Club Morera
Description En: Nestled in Mediterranean scrub just beyond the hills overlooking the coast, this rustic farmhouse welcomes guests amid centuries-old olive trees and restorative quiet. Inside, exposed stone and beams frame a relaxed yet elegant setting, with a small garden terrace perfect for summer evenings. Chef-owner Vincenzo has realized his dream here: to offer genuine hospitality and regional cooking revisited with a contemporary taste. Don’t miss the candele pasta with knife-cut Cilento ragù and goat’s cacioricotta, or the tagliolini with four tomatoes, basil, and shrimp crudo. The cellar stocks 300-plus labels to pair thoughtfully with every dish.

Name: La Bursch
Description En: In the Valle Cervo lies a romantic retreat: La Bursch, a wonderful hamlet restored with great taste through the passion of an entire family and a vision of sustainable hospitality. Within it, the eponymous restaurant stands apart, among furnishings and fabrics gathered by the owners over a lifetime, soft lighting and a service of the warmest character, an atmosphere that is almost magical pervades the space. The dishes showcase the territory’s finest ingredients, enhanced in carefully prepared presentations (the precision of the beef Wellington is emblematic), well presented and lifted by a delicate contemporary touch.

Name: CASAeBOTTEGA
Description En: An attractive restaurant situated on the charming main square of the village of Dolceacqua, with a beautiful outdoor space and views of the old Doria castle. Inside, the dining room is decorated in “shabby chic” style which gives it a friendly, welcoming and colourful atmosphere. The regional, seasonal cuisine includes standout dishes such as “brandacujun mantecato alla ponentina” (creamed salted cod), “coniglio al rossese” (rabbit in red wine) and delicious desserts.

Name: Osteria Ophis
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Modern Cuisine
Description En: Situated in the beautiful historic pedestrianised centre of Offida, this restaurant with a brick-vaulted ceiling is housed in the former stables of an old palazzo with a modern, inviting and intimate feel. Here, owner-chef Daniele Citeroni Maurizi skilfully reinterprets regional cuisine to create precise, imaginative dishes that are full of flavour. The stuffed cannelloni cooked on the barbecue grill are delicious, as is the veal tartare served with a warm meat, herb and vegetable jus on the side. We should also highlight the “low cost” tasting menu available for guests aged under 25.

Name: Osteria Zanchetti
Description En: Situated at the top of a steep slope in Fossombrone’s beautiful historic centre, this osteria takes guests back to the 1920s thanks to its romantic decor. Here, having risen through the culinary ranks, the owner-chef makes full use of his expert techniques to create dishes that hover between tradition and a sense of fantasy using the best seasonal ingredients that the region has to offer. The concise wine list favours micro-producers and natural wines.

Name: Osteria La Solita Zuppa
Description En: In the heart of the historic centre of Chiusi, the authentic spirit of a true Tuscan trattoria pervades the air, between evocative barrel-vaulted ceilings and a cool terrace that invites one to linger. Here a love of regional cooking finds expression in the revival of ancient recipes, presented with the generous richness of flavour that characterises the local tradition. Among the dishes recommended by our Inspector, the fragrant artichoke and mint soup and the refined rabbit with ginger, inspired by an ancient medieval preparation, stand out.

Name: Durnwald
Address: via Nikolaus Amhof 6, località Durna in Selva, Gsies, 39030, Italy
Description En: A delicious plate of Schlutzkrapfen (ravioli stuffed with spinach and ricotta) is just what’s needed after a good day’s skiing or a hike through the woods. And that’s not all – Durnwald celebrates the Alto Adige in all its glory, both in terms of its landscapes, which can be admired from the dining room windows, and its cuisine, which keeps alive the region’s authentic traditions. The owner himself is at the helm front of house – a perfect host who guides guests in their choice of food and wine.

Name: 13 Comuni
Address: piazza della Vittoria 31, Velo Veronese, 37030, Italy
Description En: Situated in a pretty village square, this restaurant is reached by driving along picturesque mountain roads. Guests come to 13 Comuni to taste typical dishes from the Lessinia region, including lamb and Brogna mutton, as well as chicken, cheese and other delicious local specialities, all of which are rich and full of flavour.

Name: TuMa
Description En: Once home to the I Pupi restaurant, and run by the same team, this “new generation” osteria takes its name from chef Lo Coco’s children, Turi and Emma. The cuisine here is in the hands of the sous-chef, who pays tribute to Sicily and its glorious, colourful culinary traditions: caponata, aubergine balls, swordfish rolls and the catch of the day all feature on the menu. In summer, tables are laid out in the quiet alleyway behind the restaurant.

Name: Cile's Bistrot
Description En: A restaurant not to be missed if you are in the area. The moment you walk through the door, the rooms overflowing with decorations will surprise you, but then it will be time to sample the cuisine. The chef puts his own personal stamp on some of the classics of local and national seafood tradition. One dish after another, you won’t ever want to stop eating!

Name: Granaro del Monte
Description En: A return home for Granaro del Monte to the center of Norcia and inside Casa Bianconi, a charming hotel, overlooking the town’s main street. A series of intimate dining rooms includes one adorned with frescoes, originally part of the old local granaries. The cuisine is traditional and offers the classic cured meats, featuring a truly excellent 24‑month prosciutto, as well as traditional recipes revisited by the owners, such as the outstanding tagliatelle with ricotta and sausage. The grill is always fired up, turning out beef, lamb, and other specialties. With excellent value for money and service available every day, this address is truly unmissable!

Name: Estrò
Description En: A lively bistro with a youthful feel, set in the heart of the town centre and featuring a pleasant outdoor terrace overlooking the square. In the kitchen, chef-owner Della Croce presents a menu that strikes a pleasing balance between meat and fish, always guided by careful respect for the seasons. Among the dishes most appreciated by the Inspector is the excellent octopus alla marinara: expertly cooked in two stages and full of flavour, it is served with cherry tomatoes, garlic, olives and capers, bringing out the character of the ingredient with both simplicity and skill.

Name: Antica Trattoria Gianna
Description En: This delightful, long-established family trattoria, in business for over a century, has the motto “Chi mangium nustran” (“here we eat local”) in a demonstration of its commitment to cuisine from the Lower Po valley, although other Italian dishes also feature on the menu. At midday, choose from a selection of simple, delicious and reasonably priced homemade dishes, while in the evening just one single tasting menu, concluding with the dessert trolley, is served.

Name: Al Bersagliere
Description En: A classic, historic restaurant to which one returns time and again with great pleasure. No contrived or artificial creativity here, just traditional cooking that is reassuring and substantial. Among the must-try dishes: creamy whipped baccalà, pasta e fagioli, pastissada de caval, and, among the desserts, the diplomatico (prepared with pandoro and caramel).

Name: Ostaria Tyrol
Description En: Regional dishes including home-made pastries and desserts, as well as meat and salumi from the family’s own farm, are to the fore in this typical restaurant with beautiful wooden furnishings created by a local artist. Part of the Post Hotel situated in the centre of the village (in the traffic-limited zone), the restaurant is open non-stop from 11am-10pm and doesn’t take bookings.

Name: Krone
Description En: The past retains its fascinating appeal in this traditional restaurant situated in a small mountain village, where modern trends are ignored in favour of authentic dishes from the South Tyrol. Originally opened as an inn, the restaurant still offers a few simple and discreet rooms furnished in traditional style, as well as a new and modern sauna.

Name: Osteria La Torre
Description En: To get to this welcoming restaurant, it’s best to leave the car in one of the convenient car parks just outside the town walls a short walk from Cherasco’s quiet, picturesque historic centre with its two perpendicular streets. At Osteria La Torre, the friendly female staff will happily guide you through the menu, which features traditional dishes prepared in contemporary style – we particularly enjoyed the egg, cardoon and fondue dish, followed by breaded veal rump as our main course. If you’re a fan of snails, you really must try them here as Cherasco is renowned for this speciality. The extensive wine list demonstrates the same high quality as the cuisine.

Name: Contesto Alimentare
Description En: Situated on the central Via Accademia Albertina, this small, simple and unfussy restaurant with small tables set close together serves top-quality Piedmontese cuisine. Alongside its delicious regional specialities, the menu also features dishes from elsewhere in Italy, including Sicily. The tajarin pasta made from 40 egg yolks and served with a veal ragu is superb, as are the rabbit and pork belly dishes. There’s a focus on meat options, followed by some delicious desserts, which include specialities from Piedmont such as panna cotta and typical bacio di dama biscuits.

Name: Il Ciabot
Description En: Warmed by an open fire in winter, this welcoming family-run restaurant celebrates the cuisine of Piedmont, although a few fish dishes also feature on the menu. Traditional, time-honoured and overlooked dishes take pride of place, such as boiled meat terrine with a salsa verde, Fassone beef in a crust, plus an excellent giandujotto chocolate mousse. Booking ahead is recommended.

Name: Caffè Grande
Description En: Housed in a charming palazzo with an Art Nouveau façade overlooking the main square of the village, this restaurant has an unexpectedly modern and minimalist-style interior. The menu features an impressive selection of fine local charcuterie (including coppa, pancetta and salami), as well as anolini pasta in broth and ricotta and spinach tortelli. The quality of the meat is outstanding.

Name: Buatta Cucina Popolana
Description En: This simple yet lively and dynamic restaurant occupying the beautiful, historic rooms of an old shop is always busy with locals and tourists, so booking ahead is highly recommended. Dishes are traditionally Sicilian, such as the “sarde a scottadito” (sardines) and change regularly in line with the seasons. Meat, fish, offal and vegetarian options all feature on the menu.

Name: Andrea - Sapori Montani
Address: Via Padre Giacinto 20, Palazzolo Acreide, 96010, Italy
Description En: Recently relocated again within the historic centre, nothing has changed in substance in terms of both the direction of the cuisine and the tone of familiar hospitality and service. While Andrea is the cook, Sapori Montani already contains a foretaste of what you will find in the dishes: the homemade bread, pastas and desserts, the palazzolese sausage, the truffles – which have now made the locality famous throughout the island along with its Baroque churches and Greek theatre area – through trout, black piglet and excellent cheeses.

Name: L'Oste Dispensa
Description En: Along one of the two strips of land that join the mainland to the Argentario is this contemporary osteria, minimal but comfortable and equipped with a pleasant veranda that opens in summer, always projecting toward a splendid view of the sea (don't miss the sunset if you can). The cuisine is based on local products, especially sustainably caught fish: not surprisingly, in keeping with this, the wine list features several organic labels. Highly recommended tasting menus that can range from 35 to 45 Euro. Better make reservations because they are extremely popular!

Name: Roma
Description En: Over a century of history and several generations of the family make this restaurant a solid institution in inland Liguria. Generous seasonal cuisine linked to the local area and the produce of the family's vegetable garden and orchards is served in the airy, classically styled dining room. Homemade pesto, mushrooms and truffles, excellent meat tartare and steak, not to mention a section dedicated to fish. Highlights include chestnut lasagnette on a fondue made with local cheese, and the quintessential Ligurian vegetable soup. In addition to the menu, tempting specials arrive daily from the market. But the secret to this restaurant's enduring success is also its warm, family-style welcome, making it an essential stop when travelling through the Apennines.

Name: Antica Trattoria Cattivelli
Address: via Chiesa di Isola Serafini 2, Monticelli d'Ongina, 29010, Italy
Description En: Antica Trattoria Cattivelli remains a safe haven for those who want to savour authentic Piacenza cuisine. Traditional aromas fill the dining room, inviting guests to taste dishes that tell local stories: pisarei e fasò, , soft pasta smothered in rich sauce, and suckling pork fillet, glazed with honey and mustard, which releases a perfect balance of sweet and spicy notes. Authentic flavours that alone are worth the trip!

Name: Luna Rossa
Address: via Marconi 18, Terranova di Pollino, 85030, Italy
Description En: This rustic, convivial restaurant in the village centre boasts a panoramic terrace overlooking the valley. A constant search for recipes from Italy’s peasant tradition combines with the passion and talent of the chef to create specialities such as raviolo della memoria.

Name: Upepidde
Address: vico Sant'Agnese 2, angolo corso Cavour, Ruvo di Puglia, 70037, Italy
Description En: Quintessentially Apulian restaurant, beginning with its ambiance: a sequence of rooms excavated within the rock of ancient Aragonese walls.
