In summer, dine alfresco in the cool, shady garden.

Name: Da Nicolo
Description En: Located in an advantageous spot along the promenade, where there is a summer dining area, this restaurant is really patronized for the quality of its food. Serving seafood and Carlofortinian specialties.

Name: Forte del 48
Address: Via Carlo Vizzotto 1, San Donà di Piave, 30027, Italy
Description En: This pleasant restaurant started life in 1848 as a bastion used by the Habsburg army and was later transformed into an inn. Recognised as a “Locale Storico Veneto”, it’s now run by the third generation of the De Faveri family who serve traditional meat and fish dishes here. Comfortable guestrooms are also available for guests wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Bistrot 64
Description En: The classic-style dining room in this restaurant situated in the Flaminio district belies the gourmet discoveries that await here, with echoes of traditions from Lazio that act as inspiration for creative, top-quality dishes with the occasional Asian twist.

Name: Da Cesare
Description En: A restaurant with an ultra-classic character, founded as far back as 1921, offering a menu with the flavour of another era: one of those very long lists, rich in choice and able to range naturally between meat and seafood. The section devoted to grilled meats is extensive, as is that reserved for raw fish, which is always much in demand. In the evening, the offer widens further with the addition of the pizzeria.

Name: L'A Gourmet L'Accademia
Address: via Largo C. Colombo 6, Reggio Calabria, 89125, Italy
Description En: From the restaurant on the first floor (no lift) of this early 20C building, you’ll enjoy fine views of the sea and the Strait of Messina. Here, skilled chef Filippo Cogliardo prepares fish-based dishes which include classic recipes (raw seafood) as well as more modern options (amberjack, red turnip with honey, fennel mayonnaise and lime gel). A few meat dishes also feature on the menu.

Name: Bistrot
Description En: Overlooking a delightful, quiet little square, this romantic, welcoming restaurant serves traditional local specialities, often with an individual flavour. The menu includes some fish dishes, although the house speciality is the maltagliati pasta served with ‘Bistrot’ sauce.

Name: La Sponda
Description En: An elegant restaurant within Le Sirenuse, one of the most prestigious and glamorous hotels on the Amalfi coast, with an attractive outdoor terrace for summer dining with views of Positano’s colourful houses clinging to the cliff face. Whether you choose to eat inside or out, a romantic atmosphere is guaranteed thanks to the hundreds of candles lit every evening. At the helm, Neapolitan chef Gennaro Russo maintains the restaurant’s high standards with his Mediterranean dishes, often influenced by Campania and inspired by classic favourites. The flavours of southern Italy are showcased in delicious dishes such as lemon risotto with capers.

Name: Il Portolano
Address: via Molara 11, Porto San Paolo, 07020, Italy
Description En: Right on the seafront in front of Tavolara Island, a simple restaurant run by an experienced couple. The kitchen exalts the best fish in the area with a modern taste, offered with a wide selection including some raw (such as red tuna tartare with cucumber and raspberries) and the catch of the day grilled, baked or in salt. In the summer, reservations are highly recommended because the scenic outdoor seating area, although large, is extremely popular!

Name: La Chiocciola
Address: via Runco 94/f, Quartiere di Portomaggiore, 44015, Italy
Description En: A restaurant and an inn in a small country village, it’s the right place if you’re looking for hospitality and you appreciate the regional cuisine, made of snails and frogs, but also fish from the nearby sea. Something for every palate.

Name: Meltemi
Description En: This small restaurant boasts an enviable location on a small square, with an outdoor terrace which is perfect for summer evenings. Here, the talented chef focuses on fish in all its guises, including raw options and tartares, all served with delicious accompaniments that bring out the full flavour of the fish. Homemade pasta also features, such as pappardelle with raw and cooked prawns, as well as burrata, plus main courses that include a superb, delicate mullet dish. A choice of excellent Italian sparkling wines and champagnes, also available by the glass, completes the picture.

Name: Café Les Paillotes
Description En: This old acquaintance of the Michelin Guide now has a new chef at the helm! Although the decor and furnishings remain the same with a slightly old-fashioned feel, the cuisine is modern yet with no unnecessary frills and has a fresh and generous flavour. Highlights on the menu include the new raw fish options, which have an entire tasting menu to themselves. The well-stocked wine cellar is home to around 500 labels which offer good value for money.

Name: Osteria Numero Sette
Description En: There’s been a recent change in management at this informal, friendly restaurant which serves generously portioned, carefully prepared dishes from the region and elsewhere in Italy, all at highly competitive prices. Although the cuisine might not be particularly modern, this is good solid cuisine served in a welcoming atmosphere.

Name: Osteria del 36
Description En: The Osteria del 36 traces its roots to 1880 and owes its name to a curious tradition: wine was once sold here at 36 cents a litre. Today it presents a cuisine firmly anchored in the Emilian tradition, set alongside touches of a more contemporary flavour, as in the crispy loin of rabbit with Prosciutto di Parma, cream of onions, carrots and cardoncelli mushrooms. A deep affinity with the world of wine is reflected in a list that is well-constructed, carefully considered and of reliable quality, conceived to complement each dish to its best advantage.

Name: Boccadoro
Description En: Situated on the outskirts of Padova, this classically elegant restaurant is very popular with locals – and for good reason! The menu includes skilfully prepared dishes influenced by the traditions of the Veneto (from bigoli pasta to dried cod and liver Venetian-style) as well as a selection of grilled options.

Name: Derby Grill
Description En: Facing the Villa Reale, the dining room envelops guests in classic elegance with British undertones, reflecting the Hotel de la Ville that houses it, while select tables overlook a luminous, refined veranda. From the kitchen emerge two tasting journeys: Viaggio alle origini, which tells the story of the chef’s native Campania through Mediterranean aromas, and Il territorio… secondo me, where Lombard tradition meets creative touches. Dishes, which may be selected freely, showcase seasonal ingredients and fresh vegetables harvested from the restaurant’s own organic garden.

Name: Il Capestrano
Address: via Gian Francesco Pizzi 14, Milan, 20141, Italy
Description En: This restaurant takes its name from the warrior statue dating back to the 6C BC which was discovered in Capestrano (Aquila province) in 1934. The statue, carved from a single block of local stone, is one of the most mysterious finds in history. No such mystery surrounds the dishes served in this restaurant, which focuses on cuisine from the Abruzzo, including top-quality hams and cheeses produced by small-scale producers, as well as mutton, lamb, beef, barbecued lamb kebabs and other culinary delights.

Name: Ba Restaurant
Description En: This restaurant combines Chinese traditions with contemporary, fashionable design in a dining room where large red lamps and small lanterns on the tables create an intimate and relaxing feel, accompanied by lounge music as a backdrop. The modern twist added to the classic Chinese dishes gives the cuisine an interesting flavour, from the carefully chosen ingredients and quality of their Dim Sum to our inspector’s favourite dish, namely the scallops with XO sauce, asparagus, foie gras salsa and cured ham chips.

Name: Bon Wei
Description En: China on a plate! This attractive restaurant with an intriguing decor combining elegance, modern style and Asian influences serves a wide selection of Chinese specialities. Dishes include appetisers, dumplings, noodles and meat options, as well as a huge array of specialities from eight different regions, from the spicy dishes of Szechuan to the delicate flavours of Zhejiang.

Name: Hosteria Giusti
Description En: Hidden away in the back room of the historic Giusti delicatessen, which has been famous for over four centuries, is a small dining room with just four tables. Simple and pleasantly retro, this is th perfct place to soak up the authentic spirit of Modena’s culinary tradition. The menu is a sincere tribute to Emilian cuisine: it begins with charcuterie, mostly from Mora Romagnola pigs reared in the wild, accompanied by the ever-present gnocco fritto and fragrant pasta fritters.This is followed by fresh pasta, the star of iconic dishes such as tortellini in capon broth and tagliolini with cheese and walnuts, before moving on to slow-cooked meats, including the outstanding beef stew with mashed potatoes and the traditional recipe for fried cotechino with Sorbara zabaione, a precious tribute from the Morandi family. The desserts are simple yet delicious and include panna cotta with saba (grape syrup), a perfect blend of tradition and simplicity.All that’s left is to wish you “buon appetito”.

Name: La Taverna di Fra' Fiusch
Description En: Nestling in a charming hill town, this restaurant will delight visitors looking for traditional cuisine with an updated, contemporary flavour. Specialities include agnolotti (a type of ravioli) and Piedmontese fritto misto (fried seafood and vegetables).

Name: Il Chiosco di Bacco
Description En: This restaurant boasts a rural location in the Montefeltro region, to which half the menu is dedicated (fresh home-made pastas, salumi, porchetta-style rabbit etc). The other half focuses on meat dishes, with an interesting selection of steaks and ribs from Italian and Scottish breeds (including more expensive beef that has been left to age for a month). You’ll find the perfect wine pairing on the excellent wine list.

Name: La Cantinella
Description En: Nestling in the hills, this small country restaurant delights guests with its relaxed atmosphere and Tuscan cuisine reinterpreted with a light, contemporary flavour. The paccheri pasta with a sausage ragù and celeriac cream is particularly delicious. The warm welcome offered by the owner, who always greets guests with a smile, adds to the appeal.

Name: Il Melograno
Description En: In the village centre and therefore not right by the sea, this successful, well - established restaurant is decorated in elegant contemporary style. The menu focuses on fish dishes reinterpreted with a touch of imagination.

Name: Baracca - Storica Hostaria
Description En: A classic, attractively elegant restaurant which boasts an extensive choice of dishes on its menu. The varied options here range from meat to fish dishes, often prepared in regional recipes such as tagliatelle with duck ragù and toasted hazelnuts, chicken liver risotto, Vicenza-style baccalà and meat casserole.

Name: Pomiroeu
Description En: This restaurant, one of the finest in the region, is run by its owner Giancarlo Morelli and celebrated its 30th anniversary in 2023. Situated in the centre of Seregno, the restaurant is intimate and welcoming with walls adorned with beautiful works of contemporary art thanks to the restaurant’s partnership with a local art gallery. The cuisine here is modern yet unfussy and the chef is equally at ease with meat, fish and vegetable dishes. One of the few restaurants around Monza to still offer a cheese course!

Name: Lo Stornello
Description En: Offering quality and professionalism in a tourist setting, this small restaurant is popular with locals as well as visitors. The menu focuses on imaginatively presented Mediterranean cuisine.

Name: Corte Visconti
Description En: A classical, rustic style environment with walls in stone and brick vaulted or wood and stone ceilings. The cuisine is authentically local but with a pleasant touch of creativity.

Name: Mondschein
Description En: Surrounded by the lush greenery of the Dolomite valley of Sappada, Mondschein is one of the area's most refined and sought-after gourmet retreats. The Kratter family offers a warm welcome, wrapping guests in the authentic atmosphere of the Dolomites. The kitchen is filled with the aromas of the forest and local flavours, combined with the freshness of seasonal ingredients: don't miss the tender and juicy venison fillet, enhanced by a mountain pine sauce and the spicy sweetness of Williams pears with saffron. The wine list, which has been updated with new labels, invites you to make new discoveries thanks to KAVEAU, the spectacular wine cellar that's perfect for unforgettable tastings.

Name: I Savi
Address: via Spangaro 6, località Peseggia di Scorzè, Scorzè, 30037, Italy
Description En: Situated in a small rural hamlet, this restaurant is one of the best in the Venetian hinterland for top-quality fish. Served in welcoming dining rooms, the fish and seafood dishes here are traditional and unfussy in style, and full of natural flavour.

Name: Osteria La Sangiovesa
Address: piazza Beato Simone Balacchi 14, Santarcangelo di Romagna, 47822, Italy
Description En: History pervades this eighteenth-century palazzo, but above all it is the soul of Romagna that fills the air, its friendly welcome, through rooms that overflow with warmth and atmosphere. The cooking is, naturally, of the local area, with cured meats, pasta, meat dishes and excellent desserts holding uncontested sway.

Name: Terrazza Costantino
Description En: In just a few years, young owner-chef Giuseppe Costantino has turned what was once the family trattoria into an elegant restaurant serving delicious reinterpretations of local specialities. There is just one tasting menu which features either meat or fish (although this can be discussed when you make your booking, which is essential). Given the excellent quality of the food here, this menu offers exceptional value for money.

Name: Locanda Belvedere
Address: via San Giuseppe 736, frazione San Rocco, Saludecio, 47835, Italy
Description En: Using local ingredients, this restaurant offers regional cuisine with some creative touches. Pretty and inviting rooms, tastefully decorated and with period furniture. All overlooking the valley.

Name: Selvatico
Address: via Silvio Pellico 19, Rivanazzano Terme, 27055, Italy
Description En: Opened in 1912 and now run by the fourth generation of the same family, this is one of the best restaurants in the Oltrepò Pavese area. If you’re looking to sample the gastronomic delights of this region, you’ll find a whole host of delicious specialities on offer, from charcuterie and stews to boiled meats and excellent fresh pasta. Attractively furnished guestrooms with the same nostalgic feel as the restaurant are also available.

Name: Armando al Pantheon
Description En: This small restaurant just a few metres from the Pantheon has been run by the Gargioli family since 1961, with the third generation now at the helm. Popular with locals and visitors alike for its traditional cuisine, which includes Roman and Lazian dishes, meat and fish options, and specialities such as offal, veal intestines, spring lamb, fresh anchovies, and sour-cherry tart.

Name: Osteria Fernanda
Address: via Crescenzo Del Monte 18/24, Rome, 00153, Italy
Description En: In the district famous for its Porta Portese market, this restaurant run by two talented business partners is definitely worth a visit. Andrea oversees the minimalist-style dining room, while Luca demonstrates real passion in his creative cuisine made from locally sourced ingredients, as well as produce from further afield. Among the desserts, we highly recommended the Porter beer ice-cream with black garlic mousse, chocolate and tuber peelings.

Name: Antica Locanda dell'Orco
Description En: Fans of Piedmontese cuisine will find one of its best exponents in this restaurant located at the end of a beautiful porticoed street in the historic centre. Savour some of Italy’s most exciting regional cooking, such as snails, bagna caoda, agnolotti pasta, a few (mainly freshwater) fish dishes, braised and boiled meats, “finanziera” stew and some extraordinary desserts – all prepared in magnificent style.

Name: Il Piraña
Description En: A classic fish restaurant that opts for simply prepared dishes rather than fussy, inventive avant - garde cuisine. The perfect address for those in search of traditional fare.

Name: Antica Trattoria al Gallo 1909
Description En: It is an unavoidable reference point in the gastronomic panorama of Ravenna and, as a matter of fact, it is almost always full! An "Historical Establishment of Italy", and rightly so considering that it has been run by the same family for over 100 years, this restaurant is a trattoria only in its name, given the blaze of art nouveau decorations inside. As regards the cuisine, you can expect regional dishes: truffles, succulent meats and local fish. In the dining room everyone is involved, while the young owner will illustrate the wine selection with the typically delightful congeniality of Romagna.

Name: Rio Bistrot
Description En: Situated on the street that heads down to the port in charming Riomaggiore, this lovely, well-kept restaurant offers a small selection of dishes split between Ligurian specialities and more creative options. Dine in the rustic, elegant dining room or on the outdoor terrace.

Name: Osteria Il Granaio
Address: via dei Monaci, Rapolano Terme, 53040, Italy
Description En: Although it calls itself an osteria, Il Granaio is really a restaurant. It has elegant brick - arched dining rooms occupying a 17C palazzo in the historic centre of Rapolano. On the menu you will find Tuscan specialities such as pici pasta cooked with various sauces, peppery Tuscan beef stew and a selection of fish dishes.

Name: Ai Cadelach
Description En: Enjoy local cuisine in a rustic - style dining room or alongside the swimming pool in summer. The menu focuses on meat dishes (especially grilled meat), such as traditional Fiorentina steak and Alpago lamb. Wine lovers will appreciate the excellent wine cellar kept by Ezio, one of the restaurant owners.

Name: Hidalgo
Description En: Although fish dishes also feature on the menu, Hidalgo has long enjoyed a reputation for its excellent meat options thanks to its different cuts of steak and beef sourced from all around the world and cooked mainly (but not exclusively) on the barbecue grill. In a separate room(Aomi, a kind of restaurant within the restaurant), guests can choose from a menu dedicated uniquely (from antipasti to main courses) to Japanese Wagyubeef.

Name: Vite
Address: via Montepirolo 7, località Cerasolo, Coriano, 47853, Italy
Description En: Situated within the San Patrignano community, which grows its own crops, raises its own livestock and makes its own cheeses, Vite is now the setting for new, talented chef Giuseppe Biuso’s cuisine, which is made from top-quality ingredients using modern, creative techniques. His Mediterranean dishes are also inspired by his native Sicily, and include several vegetarian specialities. In summer, don’t miss the outdoor dining space which offers fine views of the surrounding countryside.

Name: La Martinatica
Description En: Housed in an old mill, this restaurant boasts a warm and welcoming dining room crowned by wood beams and elegant furnishings. The menu offers a selection of meat and fish dishes, although the latter are the main speciality of the owner-chef, who can usually be seen taking orders in the dining room. The raw seafood option demonstrates the skill and imagination of the chef, with its array of small bites which are both creative and delicious. The attractive outdoor space is perfect for summer dining.

Name: Kro
Address: via Tollarini 70/c, località Pontagna di Temù, Ponte di Legno, 25050, Italy
Description En: Old stables have been converted into this restaurant, which boasts a stylish decor of wood and stone and the sort of romantic atmosphere that you would expect from the mountains. Although a few fish options are included on the menu, the cuisine focuses mainly on Alpine cuisine, featuring ingredients such as mushrooms, meat and game.

Name: Perbacco
Description En: A rustic restaurant offering an authentic taste of the Cilento area, both in its setting amid lush Mediterranean vegetation and in its regional cuisine. Fish and seafood dominate the antipasti selection, while the main courses focus more on meat and vegetable dishes. Good choice of regional wines, plus the option of a few pleasant guestrooms.

Name: Giardinetto
Description En: Set on the shores of the lake within the elegant hotel of the same name – now approaching its centenary after careful renovations – this restaurant boasts splendid views that extend as far as the Island of San Giulio. The cuisine is Mediterranean (try the beef bavette with red and yellow pepper sauce), with the occasional imaginative flourish (such as Carnaroli risotto with basil, black lemon, and purple shrimp). For an aperitif or after-dinner drink, a stop at the Roof Top Bar is recommended. In addition to cocktails, the wine cellar is also well stocked.

Name: Parma Rotta
Description En: Here, where the Parma river once broke its banks, you’ll find an attractive trattoria with pleasant dining rooms and excellent cuisine cooked over a wood and herb fire, one of the oldest culinary techniques in the world. The main courses feature meat only, with an extensive number of dishes on the menu. Among the home-made desserts, we recommend the fior di latte ice-cream, which is served with a choice of delicious sauces.

Name: Lillotatini
Description En: Situated in the heart of a small medieval castle-hamlet, this traditional-style restaurant with an attractive terrace on the historic square provides the setting for local specialities such as freshwater fish and truffles in season. There’s also a wine boutique on the same piazza (reached as soon as you come into the historic centre), which sells typical local produce and a good selection of wine. The latter also features on the restaurant’s wine list, with the family on hand to offer recommendations.

Name: Al Fogher
Address: strada statale 117 bis, Piazza Armerina, 94015, Italy
Description En: This small, rustic-style restaurant just outside the centre of Piazza Armerina serves personalised cuisine in which local ingredients take pride of place. Influences from elsewhere in Italy are also evident, with dishes such as artichoke pansotti (stuffed pasta) with local tuma cheese and black truffles on the menu.

Name: Hanswirt
Description En: Occupying a former post-house, this restaurant boasts dining rooms decorated in Tyrolean style, as well as a large veranda-style room. Although the focus here is on local ingredients (especially vegetables and meat such as goat kid and lamb raised on the restaurant’s own farm in the Senales valley) and freshwater fish, the menu also features the occasional Mediterranean speciality, such as the excellent braised aubergine tartare with burrata, focaccia and basil-flavoured olive oil. There’s also a hotel of the same name, which is housed in an attractive old building to the rear of the restaurant.

Name: Il Rivale al Lago
Address: via Marconi 93, Padenghe sul Garda, 25080, Italy
Description En: Situated just a stone’s throw from the lake, this multi-faceted restaurant serves classic Italian dishes, often with a creative twist, alongside top-quality international ingredients such as Cantabrian anchovies and Japanese Wagyu beef. Grilled meats and vegetable dishes also make an appearance on the menu.

Name: Cielo
Description En: In the white city of limestone stairways, at the highest point of the village, a skillfully restored ancient residence houses a splendid relais that – fittingly – bears the name La Sommità. The gourmet restaurant Cielo welcomes guests with romantic summer dinners among the citrus trees of the small inner courtyard, or in the barrel-vaulted dining room, where the atmosphere is intimate and evocative. The menu offers a modern reinterpretation of Apulian cuisine: not to be missed are the stewed catalogna with grilled lamb offal and sweet-and-sour lampascioni, or the pasta cooked in spicy tomato water, served with raw red mullet and chervil. At aperitivo hour, it is worth ascending to the splendid terrace to take in the sunset, while at lunch the offering becomes simpler, designed for a lighter yet always refined experience.

Name: I Sette Consoli
Description En: In this simple restaurant boasting an attractive outdoor summer garden and splendid views of the Duomo, chef Anna Rita focuses on carefully selected ingredients from the region and beyond. Highlights include soft egg, pan-fried courgettes and spring onions, and pecorino crumble, as well as soft veal rump, Jerusalem artichoke sauce and home-made pickled vegetables. The wine and spirits selection is particularly appealing – as an example, the Orvieto Classico Superiore Doc “Vendemmia Tardiva” is the perfect pairing for your dessert.

Name: L'Archivolto - Osteria Nostrale
Description En: Situated on Ovada’s main square, this restaurant has the pleasant friendly ambience of an attractive trattoria, while its menu takes guests on a delicious culinary journey through the Piedmont region, including local specialities such as home-made tajarin pasta, braised beef in Ovada wine with mashed potato, and the local bunet dessert (finanziera stew also makes an occasional appearance). The restaurant is also a wine bar/boutique offering a selection of wines, including different Barolo labels (presented area by area) and aperitifs served both at lunchtime and dinner.

Name: Gino Sorbillo
Description En: In the heart of Spaccanapoli, on the famous “via della pizza”, an institution with an international feel welcomes guests into simple, rustic surroundings steeped in authentic Neapolitan energy. The choice of pizzas, enriched with excellent P.D.O. ingredients, is endless. You'll need to be patient during peak hours and, if you happen to find yourself sharing a table, embrace the magic of Neapolitan friendliness!

Name: Prato Gaio
Address: Località Versa, bivio per Volpara, Montecalvo Versiggia, 27047, Italy
Description En: The restaurant trade is in the family genes: already an inn in the 19C, the Prato Gaio takes inspiration from the cuisine of the Oltrepò region. A selection of traditional specialities alongside dishes reinterpreted with flair and imagination are served. An essential stop for anyone looking for local flavour.

Name: Boccon DiVino
Address: Via Traversa dei Monti 201, località Colombaio Tozzi, Montalcino, 53024, Italy
Description En: At the edge of the town, a skilfully restored farmhouse welcomes guests into an atmosphere of refined simplicity: from the carefully appointed rustic dining room to the bright glazed terrace, pleasant even in winter.The kitchen celebrates the flavours of the territory, reinterpreted in a measured contemporary key, without forgoing certain great classics such as peposo and onion soup.The wine list favours the local reds, with particular attention to Brunello and to labels of mature vintages. In the dining room, a warm welcome and assured knowledge of wine contribute to making the experience all the more rewarding.

Name: Trattoria di Coronate
Description En: Housed in a splendid 16C farmhouse just a few minutes from the beautiful Morimondo abbey, this restaurant has an elegant and friendly ambience. The wooden ceiling and furniture in the dining room gives it a warm and welcoming feel, while the cuisine, deeply rooted in the region, is reinterpreted with a contemporary twist. The delicious options on the menu include highlights such as quail breast with a thigh-meat “lollipop” and ravioli stuffed with braised beef.

Name: Alla Corte Lombarda
Description En: Housed in a restored hay barn on the edge of the village, this charming rustic restaurant offers traditional cuisine with a modern twist, a good selection of wine and an excellent choice of beer. Every week, the menu features five records which played a major role in the history of music or which represent an important moment in time for the restaurant owner.

Name: Aimo e Nadia BistRo
Description En: A small jewel of elegance and refinement, where the celebrated starred establishment has chosen to offer a simpler, more relaxed cuisine without sacrificing precision or identity. The menu gathers national classics reinterpreted through a contemporary lens – the signature saffron risotto with ossobuco reduction and warm zabaione served with cinnamon ladyfinger cookies are both essential – alongside a tempting selection of shareable dishes. Among these, the gnocco fritto with Colonnata lard and the celebrated mondeghili meatballs stand out, perfect for pairing with one of the cocktails from a list crafted specifically to complement the kitchen’s offerings.

Name: Il Giardino "Da Felicin"
Description En: A bastion of the most authentic Piedmontese tradition, the restaurant is located in a refined period building, enhanced by a panoramic terrace and a romantic garden that invites guests to dine al fresco in the summer months. The dining rooms reflect the same vocation for traditional, rich and welcoming elegance, which reaches its fullest expression in the dishes: impeccable interpretations of the region’s finest cuisine. The restaurant’s signature dish is the famous Tajarin di Felicin, handmade tagliatelle cut into very fine strands and served with a delicate Fassona beef sauce, a true declaration of love for local gastronomy. The property also comprises a scattered hotel, with rooms located both in the main building and in other parts of the village, including the charming Palazzo Boeri, which has a small spa accessible by reservation. The owners know the area intimately and are delighted to accompany guests on guided tours of the Langhe, organised by themselves or by local experts, making the stay a complete experience encompassing cuisine, hospitality and local culture.

Name: Le Vele
Address: via Litoranea Sud 71, Bagni 70, Misano Adriatico, 47843, Italy
Description En: This modern, minimalist - style restaurant is practically on the beach and almost within touching distance of the sea. It specialises in fish dishes with a contemporary flavour.

Name: Menegaldo
Address: via Pralongo 216, Monastier di Treviso, 31050, Italy
Description En: Menegaldo is a long-established favourite for anyone who loves authentic fish dishes made from top-quality ingredients. Although it feels as though time has stood still in the pleasantly old-fashioned dining room, with its outmoded decor and furnishings, the service here is attentive and enthusiastic. The dishes are traditional and typical of the area, making this an excellent choice for delicious seafood cuisine that is elaborate without being overly fussy.

Name: Locanda Perbellini
Description En: Highly renowned in his native Verona, Michelin - starred chef Giancarlo Perbellini has now opened a restaurant in Milan, where he continues to offer traditional Italian cuisine from the north and south of the country, with a nod to new techniques and contemporary trends. Situated in the central Brera district, his warm and welcoming restaurant is small, discreet and, of course, highly elegant.

Name: Marina del Nettuno
Address: viale della Libertà-Batteria Masotto, Messina, 98121, Italy
Description En: As its name suggests, this restaurant and lounge bar is situated right on the jetty of the Yachting Club Messina. Elegant and minimalist - style decor, as well as creative cuisine with a focus on fish dishes.

Name: Josè - Tenuta Villa Guerra
Address: via Nazionale 414, Torre del Greco, 80059, Italy
Description En: 2025 has seen a change at the helm in the kitchen at this restaurant, in line with the new approach introduced by its enthusiastic owners. The full focus now is on the flavours of Campania, served in lighter versions and reinterpretations of traditional recipes. This is the case with the legendary Santa Rosa dessert, which has been transformed into a millefeuille made with the same ingredients as the original dish, namely crispy puff pastry, custard and sour cherries in syrup. Situated in one of the extraordinary villas on Herculaneum’s “Golden Mile”, the restaurant boasts an elegant dining room within this 18C building, as well as a room overlooking the villa gardens where pizzas are served from mid spring to late summer. Wine-enthusiasts will be pleased to hear that the wine cellar continues to offer an extensive selection of superb labels.

Name: San Lorenzo
Description En: Situated within the Clitunno hotel, this well-managed family-run restaurant serves classic, seasonal meat and fish dishes, including generous portions of black truffles in some dishes. Recently refurbished, the intimate, elegant dining room also occasionally features live music at weekends, while the outdoor terrace on the small square offers pleasant alfresco dining. Guests are advised to park outside the ZTL (restricted traffic zone) and make their way on foot, via a short walk through the beautiful historic centre.

Name: Particolare di Siena
Description En: A fine-dining restaurant which changed tack in 2020, reducing its number of tables to just ten and embracing a sustainable approach to its cuisine. It now prioritises local suppliers and certified organic and environmentally friendly ingredients, while the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, featuring produce grown in line with biodynamic techniques, provides some of the best seasonal ingredients used in the dishes here.

Name: Alpes
Description En: A warm and welcoming setting, where hospitality stands out for its authenticity and attention to detail. The kitchen, under the direction of chef Matthias Kirchler, presents creative, refined dishes designed for those who love to experiment and be surprised. The gastronomic offering has been recently refreshed and now unfolds in two distinct journeys: “Alpes 1988” and “Alpes – Locanda” for culinary experiences that narrate the territory with contemporary flair.

Name: Il Favri
Address: via Borgo Meduna 12, San Giorgio della Richinvelda, 33095, Italy
Description En: This inn, which has been serving food since the early 19C, boasts a warm atmosphere with a rustic feel. The beautiful garden makes a delightful setting in fine weather, while the cuisine focuses on traditional dishes from Friuli, such as “frico” (potato, onion and cheese fritter) and cured ham.

Name: Trattoria Ceriati
Address: Località Cangelasio Ceriati 18, Salsomaggiore Terme, 43039, Italy
Description En: Situated in attractive countryside where the plains give way to rolling hills (a perfect destination for a Sunday outing), this simple yet well-kept trattoria serves all the usual traditional local specialities. The typical fresh pasta and the desserts are all home-made.

Name: Villa Arcadio
Address: via Palazzina 2, località Villa di Salò, Salò, 25087, Italy
Description En: The new chef at this restaurant prioritises beautiful presentation in his modern interpretations of Italian dishes, which are even more enjoyable in summer when meals are served outdoors, surrounded by greenery and with fine views of the southern part of Lake Garda and its shoreline.

Name: I Tigli
Description En: An iconic pizzeria which has brought Italy’s favourite street-food snack right up to date! With almost 30 years’ experience behind him, Simone Padoan knows how to make difficult things easy: he uses a mix of wholemeal flours and pays meticulous attention to natural leavening processes to create a dough which has a crispy crust yet soft interior. He also focuses on different types of toppings, including fish, meat and vegetables – whether your preference is for traditional or more imaginative pizzas, every option is of the highest quality. A choice of excellent desserts provides the perfect conclusion to your meal!

Name: Mater Terrae
Description En: Situated on the top floor of the Raphaël hotel just behind Piazza Navona, this restaurant serves some of the best vegetarian cuisine in Rome. Each of the elaborate dishes boasts numerous ingredients and every single course is a delightful surprise. Equally stunning is the panoramic terrace overlooking the city’s rooftops, where meals are served in fine weather.

Name: Il Tartufo
Description En: Housed in a small villa in the residential area of the village, this intimate and secluded restaurant serves delicious cuisine with distinctly regional roots. In season, locally sourced truffles take centre stage, while fish and seafood dominate the menu at other times of year.

Name: Osteria del Tempo Perso
Description En: Situated in a hidden corner of the historic centre, this small bistro-style restaurant has a friendly and welcoming atmosphere, with photos alternating with books, wine bottles and glasses on the walls (the wine list includes a few labels from elsewhere in Europe). Small tables set close together, warm, subtle lighting and an almost Parisian ambience make this a perfect choice for a romantic dinner or a meal with friends. There’s also a small outdoor space for fine weather but seats are limited, so it’s best to book ahead!

Name: L'Acciuga
Description En: A reliable city destination for seafood, the venue welcomes guests in nautical-themed surroundings that evoke the interiors of vintage ships. The ingredients are fresh and fragrant, interpreted through tradition and then elevated in personal recipes: raw scallops with cannellini beans, onion, and rosemary; anchovy spaghetti with crispy bread and lemon; monkfish ossobuco. The wine list is complemented by a playful selection of cocktails and kombucha offered at the Bar counter. A maritime atmosphere and warm Romagnolo hospitality round out an experience that delivers on every front.

Name: Acaja
Description En: Central, elegant and modern, the cuisine of Acaja winds along two lines: the traditional regional one, with ravioli del plin, cardi gobbi, Piedmont veal and hazelnuts to mention just a few that cannot be missed, but also various fish dishes that are truly remarkable, with a touch of contemporaneity, starting with excellent raw materials.

Name: Da Vincenzo
Description En: It's never easy to find the right balance between quality and quantity, especially in a town that is very much on the tourist trail. However, Da Vincenzo has succeeded in doing just this for years, ever since it was first opened by the family’s grandfather Vincenzo in 1958. Today, the founder’s grandson (who shares his grandfather’s name) is at the helm here, creating dishes which focus mainly on fish. Pleasant atmosphere, with a few small tables on the pavement of the street that runs through the centre of Positano. A choice of cocktails supplements the wine selection from lunchtime onwards.

Name: La Corte
Address: via San Pancrazio 41, Palazzolo sull'Oglio, 25036, Italy
Description En: Situated in a tranquil street that leads to the centre of Palazzolo sull’Oglio, this stylish restaurant in a 16C palazzo boasts classic elegance and authentic cuisine which is delicious and full of flavour. Here, Aldo and his wife offer guests a warm and informal welcome, always with a smile on their lips.

Name: Essenza Bistrot
Description En: A welcoming, original and well-cared for bistro-style restaurant with an intimate feel, where the stone walls are typical of the region’s architecture. Here, chef Massimiliano Villani is at the helm in the kitchen, where he creates contemporary cuisine with a focus on regional ingredients. His imaginative flair is also evident in his desserts, which include a liquorice cigar with cocoa nibs and rum. An interesting wine list and attractive outdoor space complete the picture.

Name: La Palomba
Description En: Boasting the attractive ambience of a typical Italian trattoria, La Palomba has been run by the Cinti family since 1965 and is now in the hands of the third generation. The menu features Umbrian specialities including delicious home-made umbrichelli pasta served with various sauces.

Name: Tola Rasa
Description En: This elegant, minimalist-style restaurant serves two tasting menus (Classici and Contemporanei – the names tell you all you need to know!) from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte style. When we ate there in late autumn, we particularly enjoyed the rabbit with saffron and porcini mushrooms prepared in the open-air kitchen. There are just a few beautifully laid tables, plus a wine list that includes a selection of labels from Italy and France.

Name: Da Miky
Address: via Fegina 104, Monterosso al Mare, 19016, Italy
Description En: Situated right on the seafront, Miky is one of the best restaurants for fish (including the famous Monterosso anchovies) in the region, serving cuisine which is more and more exciting and individual every year. There’s also a small shop selling local produce.

Name: Caruso Roof Garden
Description En: In a city already rich with rooftop restaurants, this address stands out as one of the most prestigious, both for its clientele and for its panoramic views: Castel dell’Ovo, Capri, the Sorrento Coast, and Vesuvius. Besides the sea! Chef Petrosino loves to express himself through several tasting menus; for those who prefer it, à la carte options are also available. Whatever the choice, Campanian products take center stage: abundant seafood, vegetables, and even some meat, all accompanied by the professionalism of excellent service and the breathtaking beauty of the Gulf of Naples as a backdrop.

Name: Osteria Il Maialetto
Address: via Della Repubblica 348, Monsummano Terme, 51015, Italy
Description En: Next to the historic family butcher’s shop lies the vibrant tavern, which is approaching its 100th anniversary without losing any of its surprisingly youthful spirit. People come here to enjoy authentic, straightforward Tuscan cuisine: from bruschetta and crostini to pappa al pomodoro and ribollita, via platters of charcuterie and Florentine steak – which, naturally, will bump up the bill a little.The warm hospitality that characterises the place makes the experience even more enjoyable.

Name: La Notizia 53
Description En: Although situated away from the tourist centre, Enzo Coccia’s pizzeria continues to be considered one of the best places for pizza in Campania. Featuring classic Neapolitan pizzas with soft, stringy dough, the menu offers traditional and creative toppings alike. The “'mpustarella”, a five-grain and wholemeal flour roll with different fillings, more than compensates for the lack of “fritti” on the menu. The first historic restaurant at number 53 has now been joined by a second address at number 94/a nearby.

Name: SaQua by Il Frantoio
Description En: This restaurant, previously known simply as “Il Frantoio”, now has new out-of-town premises but any regret you may have at leaving the town centre will soon disappear, thanks to the wide range of modern Tuscan dishes prepared by the chefs in the new, larger kitchen. A further attraction is the outdoor space which boasts beautiful sunset views in summer.

Name: Fattoria delle Torri
Description En: A slice of paradise in Modica’s historic center: delightful terrace service among the lemon trees and a professional legacy carried on by chef-patron Peppe Barone's daughters – Carla in the dining room and Francesca in the kitchen – who, with youthful energy, champion a highly original gastronomic offering that balances innovation with tradition. They draw freely from the island’s culinary history, enriching it with exotic touches often characterized by gently spiced flavors. The wine program is equally impressive: guests can confidently rely on their recommendations to discover something special from an excellent wine list.

Name: Zero Milano
Description En: “Zero” compromises when it comes to care and quality: the cuisine here is built on exceptional ingredients and rigorous Japanese technique. Under the guidance of Hide Shinohara, the crew presents pure Japanese gastronomy, centered on the highest quality products and the art of form. Beyond the à la carte, the Omakase tasting menu is highly recommended, where the chefs construct a blind journey of great interest and refinement. The dining room features white onyx panels, elegant minimalism, and soft lighting; at the traditional counter, in addition to observing the chefs’ dexterity up close, you can opt for a tasting prepared in the moment, further elevating the sensory experience.

Name: Dimora Ulmo
Description En: Three tasting journeys are on offer – Contaminazioni, Dimora Ulmo and A Mano Libera – conceived to accompany the guest in a continuous dialogue between modern cooking and local traditions; individual courses may also be selected à la carte from within the menus. All of this takes shape within an ancient palazzo sensitively restored, enriched by a summer terrace with a striking outlook over Sassi. Among the dishes tasted, the porchetta-style rabbit with Ligurian gravy and roasted pepper merits particular mention, a successful expression of technique and personality. The service, attentive and engaged, conveys both expertise and genuine passion, while the well-constructed wine selection does justice to the territory without forgoing an openness to the rest of Italy and to some interesting international labels.

Name: Trattoria Al Passo
Description En: Successive generations of the same family have run this pleasant restaurant just outside the city for over 70 years. Enjoy a selection of fish and seafood dishes (raw, grilled or fried with numerous condiments to accompany your starters) in a maritime themed dining room or on the light and airy veranda. There is a good selection of desserts to round off your meal.

Name: Osaka
Description En: A new home for this historic restaurant, with minimalist interiors that embrace a full‑on oriental aesthetic to showcase authentic Japanese cuisine. A set menu at lunch and à la carte at dinner from which we recommend the Makimoto rolls of amberjack with shiso leaves, sesame seeds and freshly marinated wasabi. Or the festive Sukiyaki, a Japanese take on a bourguignon where meat and vegetables are cooked in a simmering broth at the table and shared among guests. The menu is extensive and rich with other succulent offerings from the Land of the Rising Sun.

Name: Rovello
Description En: Although it has a new venue, this restaurant has retained its attractive friendly feel in a dining room that acts as a backdrop for substantial dishes that are full of flavour. The interesting classic menu is supplemented by a selection of daily specials, with meat, fish and vegetables (some grilled) prepared in front of guests seated at the counter. There are also traditional tables available and the lively atmosphere remains that of a friendly, welcoming bistro. Interesting wine list, including a selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Il Liberty
Description En: Nestled in an Art Nouveau palazzo just a short walk from the dynamic Porta Nuova district, the restaurant offers a warm and refined setting, comprising a bright main dining room, a romantic balcony, a small room with an open‑view kitchen and a convivial social table. Inspired by Mediterranean tradition, the menu weaves together seafood and meat dishes with fine balance: from the “cotto-crudo” veal and mortadella mondeghili with soft potato, light salsa verde and hazelnuts, to the sumptuous thick-cut veal cutlet Milanese, served with fresh potato crisps, homemade ketchup and a delicate honey mustard.

Name: Al Segnavento
Address: via Gatta 76/c, località Santa Lucia di Tarù, Zelarino, 30174, Italy
Description En: An elegant restaurant run by an entire family, whose philosophy could be summed up in the phrase “from farm to fork”. Fruit, vegetables, mutton, lamb, pork, plus a delicious breed of duck are all showcased in this zero-kilometre restaurant. If you’re looking for simpler fare and wine by the carafe, the restaurant also has a more informal bistro nearby. Charming guestrooms also available for visitors wanting to prolong their stay.

Name: La Cantina di Manuela
Description En: The dining room in this young, dynamic restaurant is surrounded by bottles of wine. Elaborate dishes feature on the menu, with antipasti available in the evening. At lunchtime these are replaced by various salads aimed at a business clientele in a hurry. Milanese-style cutlets are the house speciality.

Name: Terrazza Gallia
Description En: On the seventh floor of Hotel Gallia, with panoramic views of the square and Central Station, the restaurant’s limited seating is arranged in a room with modern furnishings and features a cuisine inspired by products and recipes from throughout Italy. A rewarding gastronomic destination in a refined setting.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Address: via Privata Fratelli Gabba 7/b, Milan, 20121, Italy
Description En: Housed within the Bulgari hotel, a secluded haven of elegance right in the heart of the most exclusive district in Milan, this restaurant alternates the trusted chefs at its helm, all of whom continue to serve light, contemporary Italian cuisine in dishes that focus more on substance than form. Choose between tasting menus and a generous à la carte selection featuring meat and fish dishes alike, including classic local favourites such as risotto and vitello alla Milanese (breaded veal cutlet).

Name: La Fugascina Ristorante
Description En: Situated on a small square with an attractive outdoor space, this restaurant offers a menu which features fish from the lake and other seasonal produce prepared with both modern and traditional techniques, but always with a contemporary flair. The focus is on locally sourced (zero-mile, wherever possible) produce.

Name: Darmagi
Description En: ‘Darmagi’ in dialect means ‘what a shame’, and it would indeed be a shame not to cross the threshold of this secluded little villa, enveloped in a warm and genuinely homey atmosphere, particularly evocative in the handsome dining room with its fireplace. The cooking celebrates with conviction the traditions of Piedmont and Canavese; on winter weekends, the fritto misto and bagna caoda are simply not to be foregone. In the warmer months, a pleasant terrace immersed in greenery, complemented by the convenience of ample parking.

Name: Oberwirt
Description En: The various Stube-style dining rooms in the Oberwirt hotel restaurant have a typical Tyrolean ambience, while the cuisine is decidedly traditional with its focus on seasonal and regional ingredients, although a few fish options also always feature on the menu. Wine-enthusiasts will be delighted with the excellent wine selection.

Name: Foresta
Address: via Litoranea 2, Marina di Pisa, 56128, Italy
Description En: Overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea, all the tables at this restaurant offer sea views, whether you’re sitting in the winter dining room or on the outdoor summer terrace. The menu here focuses on top-quality fish dishes, which are classic in style, as is the background music and wine list, although the desserts have a more imaginative flavour.

Name: Taverna Rovita
Description En: Situated just a few metres from the main square of old Maratea, this tavern is a historic and typical restaurant with a kitchen area that dates from the 18C and a decor featuring Vietri ceramics. The chef delights in introducing guests to local recipes, such as the “polpo murato” (stewed octopus), one of the house specialities. The wine list boasts around 400 labels, with a particular focus on France and small-scale producers from Italy and further afield. Small groups (a maximum of 6 people) can choose to dine in the wine cellar surrounded by old bottles, many of which are collector’s items.

Name: MikEle
Description En: An elegantly contemporary dining room punctuated by large portholes seems to herald the menu’s seafood focus: fish dishes arrive at the table, moderately creative yet firmly anchored to prime ingredients. The “nudo e crudo” is the essential selection of the day’s catch served simply, typically featuring at least six different varieties, while the tagliolini with langoustine is elevated with caviar and a creamy white cabbage purée finished with Martini. The heart of the experience, however, remains the quality of the ingredients, the absolute and memorable stars.

Name: Da Guido
Description En: The story of this restaurant began in 1967, when Guido and Giovanna Fasan, both of whom still work front of house, met in Germany. They then moved back to Italy, where they opened Da Guido in the early 1990s. White dominates in the elegant, contemporary-style dining room, while the cuisine features delicious seafood dishes with a focus on grilled specialities. In summer, there’s a welcoming bar in the garden, which boasts a romantic atmosphere. Together with other restaurant-owners from Venice, the Fasan family also have a kitchen garden on the Venetian island of Sant’Erasmo, where they focus on sustainable growing methods.

Name: Il Merlo
Address: Viale Sergio Bernardini 660, Lido di Camaiore, 55041, Italy
Description En: Situated right on the beach, Il Merlo boasts a welcoming dining room decorated in elegant, contemporary style. The owner is at the helm in the kitchen, where he creates dishes with a focus on fish and seafood, such as the raw seafood platter and the salt-baked catch of the day. A few delicious meat options, such as plin pasta and pigeon, are also available.

Name: Battipalo
Description En: An intimate and atmospheric venue, ideal for a romantic lakeside stop, where you can enjoy a relaxing break thanks to Italian and lake cuisine, sometimes reinterpreted with a more contemporary approach, but with little affectation and, instead, excellent substance. Enthusiasts will appreciate the snails with bread, butter, and parsley, accompanied by a garlic cream and seasonal mushrooms. Above all, the use of quality raw materials is fundamental.

Name: Del Fagioli
Description En: A historic city landmark, this rustic and sincere trattoria welcomes guests with a simple, warm atmosphere, where the open kitchen at the entrance serves as an immediate calling card. The distinctly familial ambiance makes it beloved by many, so much so that reservations well in advance are required. The table sees straightforward, fragrant recipes: excellent Florentine steaks, pici with aglione sauce, pappa al pomodoro, twice-cooked beef with sautéed green beans, and to finish, house-made cantucci. A stop that celebrates the most authentic Tuscan tradition with genuine spirit.

Name: Riso Amaro
Description En: Inspired by the famous film Bitter Rice, directed by Giuseppe De Santis, who was born in Fondi, this restaurant welcomes guests into elegant dining rooms and a lush courtyard which is perfect for summer evenings. The cuisine looks to the present with a well-balanced creative flair that is evident in dishes such as the cuttlefish lasagnetta, served with an intense creamy sauce made from cuttlefish ink and offal, or the intriguing sweet “pinzimonio”, a fresh and light dessert that combines sweet-and-sour vegetables with softer notes. The concise but thoughtfully curated wine list features labels from all over Italy, whilst the central location, just a stone’s throw from the castle, adds further charm to the experience.

Name: Trita Pepe
Address: via Gabriele D'Annunzio 4, Manoppello Scalo, 65024, Italy
Description En: Situated on the road that passes through Manoppello Scalo, this restaurant with a car park right in front of the building boasts a spacious, simple dining room and is our recommended choice in the region for anyone keen to try typical Abruzzo cuisine. Meat takes pride of place among the main courses (with an exception for salted cod), while menu highlights include excellent fried gnocchi with local salumi and cheese.

Name: Taverna dello Spuntino
Description En: This Roman trattoria has a particularly striking interior. From its old tufa passageways converted into a wine cellar in the basement, to its charming dining rooms with brick - vaulted arches where hams, flasks of wine, fruit and antipasti all form an attractive display.

Name: Le Cicale in Città
Description En: A classic-style dining room adorned with mirrors and silverware acts as the backdrop for fish and seafood dishes at this restaurant. The raw fish is particularly excellent, as are the mupa (a little-known fish that lives in the deep waters of the Mediterranean), prawns (in season) and home-made primi served with delicious sauces, such as the chicken plin with brown gravy. For special occasions, we recommend the table to the rear of the room near the arte povera-style dresser. Cheerful, friendly service adds to the appeal.

Name: Cacciani
Description En: Run by the Cacciani family for over 100 years, this is one of the most famous restaurants in the Castelli Romani region. Demonstrating a real passion for regional traditions and eschewing modern trends, the menu continues to offer a tempting selection of delicious classic dishes from Lazio, including a couple of fish and seafood options. The focaccia, which is served with the bread, is superb and well worth a mention. The dining room evokes the long history of the restaurant, while the panoramic terrace is a firm favourite with guests.

Name: Tana de 'l Ors
Address: via Roma 28, Forno di Zoldo, 32012, Italy
Description En: A favourite with food-lovers, this restaurant serves lighter meals at lunchtime which are nonetheless carefully and imaginatively prepared (don’t miss the orsoburger!). In the evening, the best daily ingredients are prepared with a lightly modern touch – meat is the undisputed start of the show, although a few fish dishes also feature. One-room and two-room apartments are also available.

Name: Trattoria 'petito
Description En: Located on the outskirts of Forlì’s charming historic centre, this simple, modern yet attractive restaurant serves eclectic and varied cuisine. More traditional fare on offer includes an excellent selection of hams and grilled meats, as well as delicious tagliatelle al ragù, while the menu also features a few more creative options including a few fish dishes.

Name: Villa Fiordaliso
Description En: Villa Fiordaliso is one of the beautiful early 20C villas that line the lake front. Surrounded by verdant grounds and extending out into the lake on a pontoon, the restaurant serves creative, modern cuisine. The chef is equally at ease with fish and meat dishes, while the extensive wine list suggests that you’ll have no problem finding your favourite wine here.

Name: Osteria Antico Brolo
Description En: Situated in the upper part of the town near the Vittoriale estate, this rustic 18C building is the setting for regional cuisine prepared using seasonal ingredients. The charming small courtyard offers shade for summer dining, while the interior dining room also includes a single table on a small balcony which needs to be booked well in advance.

Name: Cibrèo
Address: via A. Del Verrocchio 8r, Florence, 50122, Italy
Description En: A historic city institution and essential stop for anyone arriving in Florence, this establishment welcomes guests into an elegant dining room reminiscent of a private salon, where cordial, graciously measured service frames a cuisine of bold flavors. The menu features dishes that have become true house classics, capable of narrating the territory through recipes that time has rendered iconic: pork liver with lemon, tortellini timbale, squab stuffed with mostarda, rabbit roulade with sweet-and-sour borettane onions, and, to close, a cheese tart accompanied by marmalade.

Name: Locanda del Molino
Description En: This rustic yet charming restaurant occupies an old family mill. It has attractive guestrooms that reflect the elegant simplicity of the Tuscan countryside. In the kitchen, the female chef creates traditional specialities such as fried rabbit and nettle with ricotta cheese gnudi (ravioli filling without the pasta) in a fresh tomato sauce.

Name: Brindo
Description En: The service is characterized by a cohesive and friendly team in welcoming guests to their small home. Brindo is an informal reality, where the cuisine is fun, engaging and more than simply territorial: raw foods, tartar and fish of the day are at the top!

Name: Osteria della Chiocciola
Description En: Situated in the historic centre just a stone’s throw from the elegant Via Roma, this restaurant is decorated with paintings by renowned modern artists such as Pignatelli, Andy Warhol, and Valerio Berruti. The ground floor is home to a colourful wine bar, while the first-floor restaurant serves traditional cuisine made from local ingredients with a natural focus on Piedmont. There is also a fish alternative for non-meat-eaters.

Name: Pierre Alexis 1877
Description En: Situated in the historic heart of Courmayeur, this old house dating back over a century, once used as a stables and later as a carpenter’s workshop, is now home to a warm and welcoming restaurant. Here, traditional recipes are updated with creativity and enthusiasm, as demonstrated by the venison Rossini. The ingredients used are mainly local, including wild herbs for added flavour, while the wine list offers an impressive selection of labels.

Name: Osteria del Teatro
Description En: Enjoy traditional cuisine served in an elegant 16C dining room with a fireplace or in more informal trattoria-style rooms, all of which are decorated with the same theatrical theme. The recipes here focus on local traditions and seasonal ingredients, resulting in colourful, well-balanced and beautifully presented dishes that are full of flavour. There are just a few tables on the small terrace near the entrance overlooking the pedestrianised street, so if you want to sit outdoors make sure you book well in advance.

Name: Capuccina
Address: via Novara 19/b, località Capuccina, Cureggio, 28060, Italy
Description En: A new chef brings fresh energy and ideas to this excellent restaurant housed within a 16C farmhouse that is surrounded by countryside and which has been restored in elegant style. The chef focuses on top-quality ingredients (including vegetables from his own kitchen garden) and contemporary recipes with a classic flavour, as well as personalised recipes created with just a few ingredients for which he uses a mix of classic methods (“express” cooking) and modern techniques (such as whipping siphons) in order to achieve comforting, classic flavours. With the exception of a few champagnes, the wine selection showcases the region, especially the areas closest to Upper Piedmont, such as Ghemme, Gattinara, Boca and Sizzano – plus, of course, the wines produced on the restaurant’s own estate!

Name: Kandoo Nippon Restaurant
Description En: Contemporary spaces spread across two floors, plus a veranda terrace, make this solid restaurant a great choice for lovers of Japanese specialties – both cooked and raw preparations of meat and fish – executed with a light touch and clean, distinct flavors. At lunch (weekdays only), the kitchen also offers rice bowls and noodle dishes accompanied by various sides. Wine enthusiasts will appreciate the dedicated Champagne section on the wine list.

Name: La Casa degli Spiriti
Description En: The Chignola family has been welcoming guests in this beautiful, restored farmhouse – a luxurious residence with one of the best views of Lake Garda – for almost 30 years. The ground-floor restaurant occupies a veranda surrounded by greenery facing the lake, where young chef Filippo (following in his father’s footsteps), together with his brother, sommelier Lorenzo, offers his guests an enjoyable dining experience with its roots in the cuisine of the region. The first-floor terrace is home to the Osteria Spiritino, which is more informal in both its cuisine and atmosphere. The remarkable wine cellar is housed in a room adorned with 18C frescoes and boasts more than 1 300 labels, with a particular focus on champagnes.

Name: Rosita
Description En: Decorated in the same simple and rustic style as the Hotel Rosita in which it is housed, this restaurant boasts an attractive terrace overlooking the sea and the coast (call in advance to book one of the tables with the best view), which more than compensates for the narrow, winding road that you have to follow to get here. The delicious cuisine is regional in flavour, including seafood options such as the excellent stuffed baby squid in a sauce served with mashed potatoes, and meat dishes that include a tasty rabbit casserole.

Name: Trattoria Leoni
Description En: Nestled among the hills of Felino, amid the lush greenery of the Parma countryside, this trattoria in Barbiano has long been a point of reference for those in search of authenticity and the flavours of another age. The cooking of the Leoni family celebrates local tradition, drawing upon recipes handed down from grandmother Erminia and interpreted with care and deep respect. Among the most iconic dishes stands the delicious rabbit alla cacciatora: already boned, enveloped in a tomato sauce fragrant with aromatic herbs, it represents at its finest the substance and richness of Parma cuisine. Not to be missed either is a taste of the Felino salame, aged at length in the family cellar, which speaks with honesty and conviction of the soul of the territory.

Name: Tanzer
Description En: Located beneath the belltower in a small hamlet, this restaurant has two romantic 17C Stube-style dining rooms, where Melanie and her sommelier husband Michael delight guests with regional, modern and imaginative cuisine. Most of the ingredients are sourced locally, including from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden. The home-made syrups and jams are highly recommended.

Name: Al Vedel
Description En: A temple for the production of culatello ham, which features in the dishes served and is also matured on the premises for 16, 26 and 38 months (the maturing rooms are well worth a visit), Al Vedel also serves other regional specialities, as well as more imaginative fare. The menu features dishes such as gran lesso(boiled beef and chicken), delicious Bourguignon-style snails, tortel dols (tortelli pasta with a hint of sweetness), and specialities enhanced by the addition of Parmesan cheese and red butter. The wine list, which will delight Lambrusco enthusiasts, boasts a selection of French wines including newer wine-producing regions, while the cheese trolley offers a selection of regional and Italian cheeses, plus a few options from further afield such as the famous Brillat-Savarin with its natural, bloomy rind.

Name: Albergaccio di Castellina
Address: via Fiorentina 63, Castellina in Chianti, 53011, Italy
Description En: In the heart of one of Italy’s most iconic landscapes, Chianti Classico, with its harmonious hills and vineyards tracing picture-perfect panoramas, Albergaccio, considered Tuscany’s oldest historic restaurant, welcomes guests with a perfect balance of past and present. The interiors preserve the authentic charm of the setting, while the kitchen reinterprets traditional dishes with a contemporary touch, never betraying their essence. In the dining room, Francesco greets guests with grace and professionalism, guiding them in selecting the wine best suited to enhance the gastronomic experience. An establishment that celebrates history, terroir, and a timeless vision of hospitality.

Name: Il Verso del Ghiottone
Description En: This restaurant housed in an 18C building has a warm, rustic feel with terracotta, stone and brick decor and black tables with American-style place mats, resulting in a vibrant yet elegant atmosphere where the service is informal and yet also highly professional. The cuisine is inspired by regional recipes which are reinterpreted and given a lighter flavour. There’s no shortage of interesting fish dishes, including the exquisite red shrimp, which is half-cooked, half-raw and served with passion-fruit caramel.

Name: Da Orlando
Description En: Simply arriving in Cusago near Milan, where the imposing castle dominates the attractive centre, puts you in a good mood. At Da Orlando, the menu is equally balanced between top-quality fish dishes such as the “bollita di mare” and meat-based dishes that will delight food-lovers, such as snails with trumpet mushrooms and duck breast with ginger. Two elegant dining rooms are the perfect setting for a romantic evening, while the attractive outdoor space comes into its own in summer. A good restaurant with over 40 years of history.

Name: Da Ercole
Description En: Situated on Crotone’s seafront, Da Ercole is a culinary institution for anyone who loves fish, with the benefit of 40 years in the business behind it! The salty tang of the Ionian sea is celebrated on an extensive menu, although if you really want to enjoy yourself to the full, let owner-chef and old-school host Ercole guide you in your choice (including some excellent raw fish dishes).

Name: Quel Fantastico Giovedì
Description En: After forty years of experience, their consistency and care make this one of Ferrara’s most sought-after tables (best to book well in advance!). Guests enter intimate dining rooms of welcoming warmth, where service is gracious and precise. The menu is fragrant with the sea: fish dishes prepared with classic elegance and modern touches, such as the green bean and vegetable velouté crowned with raw scampi, fresh and glistening. Meat offerings are equally rewarding, rich and flavorful, with the celebrated potato sformato and gratinéed salama da sugo releasing intense aromas from the oven.

Name: Sichelburg
Description En: Treat yourself to a great meal in an idyllic setting in this village restaurant occupying the first floor of a castle dating back to the 13C. The romantic dining rooms are furnished with wood, while the creative cuisine focuses on typical mountain produce.

Name: Tavola di Guido
Address: Località Le Piazze 41, Castellina in Chianti, 53011, Italy
Description En: The menu crafted by Guido, a chef attentive to seasonality and estate products, is a tribute to the land. The extra virgin olive oil comes from Poggibonsi or Castellina, both from the same farm. Among the signature dishes is the beetroot risotto with pancetta, crème fraîche, and nasturtium – but only when in season! The wine cellar features Tuscan, Italian, and international labels, with a special treat to try: Amphoreum, a home-produced orange wine made from Trebbiano, known for its salinity and medium body.

Name: San Michele
Address: via Castello di Fagagna 33, Fagagna, 33034, Italy
Description En: Situated next to the ruins of the old castle and the small church of San Michele, this 13C building, thought to have once housed a guardroom, is now home to a small restaurant serving regional, seasonal cuisine with a modern twist. During the week, the restaurant offers a lunchtime menu of top-quality snacks (the Venetian “cicchetti”), as well as a few “primi” and desserts.

Name: Osteria de l'Umbreleèr
Description En: Situated in Cicognolo in the Lower Po valley, where early morning mists create an evocative atmosphere in autumn, this traditional restaurant with a rustic feel serves specialities from Lombardy with a focus on delicious starters and top-quality meat. Our inspector particularly recommends the white onion gratin soup and the Burgundy-style snails. A simpler menu is available at lunchtime and there’s a small garden for alfresco dining on summer evenings.

Name: Osteria dell'Oca Bianca
Description En: In the heart of a small town, right opposite the church, this typical village osteria run by a friendly family serves traditional cuisine from the Piedmont, including goose dishes. Highlights here include the rustic, welcoming ambience, an excellent wine list, a wine cellar that can be visited, and a charming glass-fronted veranda that is used throughout the year. There are also three beautiful guestrooms reserved exclusively for guests dining at the restaurant.

Name: Maré
Description En: An unexpected gourmet restaurant in a typical private beach club on the Romagna coast, with a dining room that opens on to the beach with its long line of beach umbrellas. The dishes here are carefully prepared and occasionally creative, and all of good quality. We particularly recommend the monfettini (fresh egg pasta) mantecati with cuttlefish, clams, mantis shrimp and ink, which looks like a risotto and is absolutely delicious. The restaurant also boasts a good wine list with an excellent choice of champagnes.

Name: Feel Como
Description En: Wild regional produce, game and freshwater fish take pride of place on the menu at this elegant restaurant which celebrates nature in all its glory, despite its town-centre location. The dishes prepared by chef Federico Beretta have a contemporary feel, while the tasting menu is dedicated to wild ingredients foraged from the woods.

Name: Doc
Address: via Vittorio Veneto 1, Borgio Verezzi, 17022, Italy
Description En: Quiet, well - kept restaurant located in an aristocratic, early twentieth - century villa surrounded by a pretty garden.

Name: Cascina Lautier
Description En: Situated outside the town on top of a small hill, this elegant restaurant serves modern country cuisine, with some personal interpretations.

Name: Antinè
Description En: Manuel Bouchard’s cuisine impressed our inspectors thanks to striking features such as his minimalist approach and the use of just a few well-chosen ingredients. Traditional recipes, such as plin pasta and Fassona beef, feature on the menu alongside more alternative, imaginative dishes (including fresh- and saltwater fish). This elegant restaurant is located on the first floor of a building in the old town, just a stone’s throw from the medieval tower. A warm welcome and an excellent wine list complete the picture.

Name: Il Giardino delle Esperidi
Description En: The ideal starting point for an exploration of the area. In summer one dines on the terrace located in the heart of the historic centre while drinks and cigars may be enjoyed in the lounge bar.

Name: Stube Ladina
Description En: The hotel owner is also the chef, serving carefully prepared and well - presented dishes made from regional produce in a quiet Stube - style dining room. An interesting wine list provides the icing on the cake.

Name: Marina Grande
Description En: Situated directly on the beach, this pleasant restaurant with a contemporary decor boasts splendid sea views and a small private beach club. Although the setting obviously has a tourist feel, the traditional cuisine served here is full of flavour. We particularly recommend the “gamberi in carrozza” (shrimp) with fior di latte and a variation on puttanesca sauce.

Name: Villa Baroni
Description En: This romantic restaurant on the lakeshore has a welcoming, elegant ambience and a delightful terrace for summer dining. The cuisine pays particular attention to top-quality, seasonal ingredients prepared in traditional recipes with a focus on fish. Cosy, Provençal-style guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Antica Osteria da Penacio
Description En: A family - run restaurant in a villa on the edge of a wood: inside two refined dining rooms and a small, but well stocked, wine bar; traditional cuisine.

Name: Il Pavone
Description En: Situated in the heart of Alghero and with a beautiful veranda overlooking the sea, this restaurant has been in business for almost 50 years. Fish and seafood take centre stage here, served in classic dishes which are full of flavour and prepared using top-quality local ingredients. Specialities include fresh pan-fried and grilled fish, delicious bavettine pasta with scampi and fried mussels, and the island’s famous “seadas” served with Sardinian eucalyptus honey or home-made ice-cream.

Name: Roof Garden
Description En: Make sure you ask for one of the tables next to the glass wall in this restaurant, which boasts romantic views of Bergamo’s Città Alta. The innovative, inventive cuisine is tempting and full of flavour.

Name: Opificio
Description En: A modern restaurant in the province of Padova which, over the past ten years, has grown and evolved from a gastro pub to the top-quality eatery that it is today. The cuisine is fairly eclectic, featuring meat and fish dishes alike, with the option of a lighter menu at lunchtime. The best dishes are showcased on the à la carte and are often made using luxury ingredients such as foie gras, scampi and Wagyu beef. The impressive wine list demonstrates a passion for international sparkling wines, while the excellent selection of wines by the glass is further enhanced by a choice of cocktails (also available at midday).

Name: Anticofurlo
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Country cooking
Description En: Situated in the Gola del Furlo nature reserve, this restaurant is run by the talented and enthusiastic Alberto and Roberta, whose focus is on typical Marche specialities such as fresh pasta, cured hams, fine cheese and regional dishes full of intense flavours. The picturesque grotto carved into the rock is perfect for an aperitif, while the inn also offers charming guestrooms.

Name: Il Carpaccio
Description En: This traditional family restaurant has been recently renovated to include an attractive veranda - style dining room overlooking the valley. Typical dishes from Calabria, fish specialities by prior arrangement, and a good wine list all add to the appeal.

Name: Da Peppe
Description En: Situated in the historic centre of a small village in the Parco del Pollino, this long-established restaurant serves traditional and copious local dishes that are always expertly prepared. Guestrooms are also available in the family B&B of the same name.

Name: Dogma
Description En: A small restaurant run by two young and passionate spouses, drawing on considerable previous experience: she in the dining room, he at the stove. Their cooking has a strongly defined personality and focuses above all on the sea, with dishes in which cooking over charcoal – or at least certain fundamental stages of it – takes centre stage, extending even into the desserts. The flavours are intense and convincing, with occasional foreign inflections, as in the Talo, a kind of Basque flatbread, made with white maize flour and filled with anchovies, broccoli and stracciatella: a preparation that showcases their mastery of this type of cooking. The setting is intimate and welcoming; booking is advisable, particularly in the evening, given the growing popularity of the venue.

Name: RistoFante
Description En: Run by the reliable and experienced “Titta” in the kitchen and Silvia front of house, this elegant, contemporary-style restaurant serves simple, modern dishes in which fresh, seasonal ingredients take centre stage. The focus here is on fish, with a menu that includes a fine selection of raw seafood options, as well as a simple yet tasty sea bass carpaccio which cooks quickly on a bed of hot porcini mushrooms.

Name: Ventuno.1
Description En: Major refurbishment at this renowned restaurant has given it the feel of an informal, welcoming contemporary bistro. Don’t miss the “Napule” tasting menu, which offers just four courses that include anchovies, cavatelli pasta and Neapolitan meatballs in a nod to the owner’s origins.
