Over time, the wine list has been extended and improved, with wines now stored in a new cellar. Some of the ingredients used in the dishes can also be purchased to take home.

Name: Hostaria dai Musi
Description En: Offering a limited à la carte that includes fish dishes (including raw options) which vary according to market availability, this restaurant serves what it describes as “typically modern cuisine”. The breaded and fried anchovies with a typical saor sauce and lemon gel are particularly good, plus the menu features a selection of typical regional specialities. The pleasant setting is enhanced by the backdrop of the large central square in a pedestrianised area on the edge of the old town. The drinks menu includes an excellent selection of wines, plus a good choice of local beers.

Name: Locanda del Marinaio
Description En: Delicious cuisine full of the flavours of the Mediterranean (prepared by the German owner - chef! ) in a delightful little restaurant in the bustling centre of Cefalù. Simple surroundings but excellent food!

Name: La Veranda
Description En: In summer, the terrace by the lake offers a splendid view and is the perfect setting for dishes that highlight Italian tradition but also satisfy the most cosmopolitan palates. The foie gras escalope served with parsnips, apple compote and pink grapefruit, for example, is excellent. If the weather's not so great, you'll be just as comfortable in the elegant indoor dining room overlooking the lake (the most popular) or the garden. The evening dress code is elegant (we are, after all, inside the luxurious Villa d'Este hotel).

Name: L'Argaj
Description En: In the Piedmontese dialect, “Argaj” translates as “satisfaction” and never has a restaurant name seemed more appropriate! In a simple, colourful and welcoming dining room with windows looking out at the hills, all the attention is on cuisine which is skilfully balanced between classic local dishes and more creative options. Choose between the à la carte and tasting menus, all accompanied by an excellent array of wines.

Name: Trattoria del Bivio
Description En: Situated in the Alta Langa region, this old restored farmhouse is now home to an elegant restaurant with a contemporary rural feel. The cuisine has strong regional roots, although the menu also offers a few fishes dishes. Excellent food, as well as attractive guestrooms and a warm, family welcome.

Name: Il Doretto
Description En: Housed in an attractive farmhouse, this restaurant serves seasonal cuisine that includes delicious fish and seafood (raw dishes as well as more elaborate options), alongside meat dishes, including some delicious game recipes.

Name: I Salotti
Address: Località Querce al Pino, SS 146, Chiusi, 53043, Italy
Description En: In summer, the outdoor spaces at this restaurant, such as the garden gazebo, are the perfect setting for a candlelit dinner in total harmony with nature, while in winter, the elegant dining room with just a few tables (book well in advance) really comes into its own. Creative cuisine prepared using produce from the restaurant’s own farm, plus a long-established wine cellar that has been extended over the years so that it now boasts over two thousand different labels from the region and elsewhere in Italy, many of them of the highest quality.

Name: Oste Scuro - Finsterwirt
Description En: Run by the capable Mayr family, this long-established restaurant has occupied a narrow alleyway in the centre of Bressanone (Brixen) since the late 19C. The dining rooms are decorated in historic style, plus there’s a charming terrace for alfresco dining in summer. Dishes are presented on different tasting menus with the option of choosing traditional or Mediterranean dishes à la carte style – we highly recommend the soup made with Sylvaner wine from the Isarco valley, as well as the Tirtl (fried pie) stuffed with ricotta, spinach and cinnamon. Guestrooms are available in the nearby and recently renovated Adler Historic Guesthouse, which is run by the same owners.

Name: Lanzani Bottega & Bistrot
Address: via Albertano da Brescia 41, Brescia, 25127, Italy
Description En: This modern restaurant (open from 7am to 11pm), once the family butcher’s, is also a delicatessen and wine boutique. It serves top-quality produce such as Pata Negra and other hams, anchovies from the Cantabrian sea, an excellent selection of cheeses and more elaborate dishes. At mealtimes, the venue transforms into a proper restaurant, with a smaller menu available at lunchtime.

Name: Clandestino Susci Bar
Description En: Built on stilts, the Clandestino is a unique restaurant with a simple yet trendy ambience, which overlooks a beautiful unspoilt beach with views of the sea from all the windows and a distinctly romantic feel at night. Here, Moreno Cedroni focuses on gourmet cuisine at lunchtime as well as in the evening. In addition to two tasting menus (Eros & Susci and Susci Memories), for lunch there’s a small à la carte.

Name: Gardenia
Description En: Even if you’re not a local, you’ll feel at home in this old property which offers a glimpse of the Piedmont of old. In this 19C building, with a typical balcony running along the inner courtyard, the atmosphere continues into the dining room and, of course, via the dishes on the menu. Here, regional cuisine is celebrated to the full, so you’ll find lots of meat (although some fish options are also available), accompanied by a carefully selected choice of vegetables, some grown in the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: Il Portico
Description En: Chef Lopriore returns to his native region with this new restaurant which offers an original format – the lunchtime menu focuses on single course options, while in the evening the tasting menus comprise an interesting combination of imaginative fish, meat and vegetable dishes which can be combined as you wish. Cuisine with an emphasis on seasonal market ingredients where locally sourced produce takes pride of place.

Name: Kürbishof
Description En: This romantic inn with guestrooms occupies an old farm with a hay barn. In two typical Stube-style rooms, one of which offers views of the Cembra valley, enjoy cuisine prepared by a mother-and-son team. They work side by side, preparing dishes from mainly regional ingredients (the menu often includes the names of producers) each in their own individual way, which is highlighted on the menu: to the left, you’ll find the traditional dishes made by the mother, Sara, while on the right you can choose from a selection of modern, creative options prepared by young chef Mathias. Our inspectors were delighted with their combination of choices from both lists!

Name: Phi Restaurant
Address: località Forte Cappellini, Baia Sardinia, 07021, Italy
Description En: Glamour and fashion are the hallmarks of this restaurant in Phi Beach, one of the most attractive nightclub-cum-lounge bars on the Costa Smeralda. Take a seat on the terrace right by the water and soak up the romantic sunsets and sea views as you enjoy Italian and Mediterranean dishes created by a famous chef from Lombardy who adds just the right touch of contemporary flavour. Also open for lunch, with some of the evening menu dishes available alongside an array of simpler options.

Name: La Conchiglia
Description En: This small restaurant with a vaulted ceiling provides the setting for dishes that have by now become classics thanks to their focus on top-quality ingredients. The cuisine is light and simple rather than bold and elaborate, with a focus on bringing out the full flavour of the fish (a few meat dishes are also available). If you’re keen to learn more about Ligurian gastronomic specialities, take time between courses to chat with the friendly owner, who has an impressive knowledge of the region.

Name: Granoturco Bistrot
Description En: Although the external façade of this restaurant recalls its former life as a pub, the building is now home to a restaurant run by a young chef whose experience working abroad has done nothing to dim his love of the Piedmont. Here, he serves some of the best regional cuisine in the area, with a few more creative options also featuring on the menu.

Name: All'Osteria Bottega
Description En: Beneath the porticoes of a somewhat hidden side street in the city centre lies a trattoria that celebrates authentic Emilian cooking, prepared according to tradition, without diversions or reinterpretations, but showcased in its most typical recipes. From the exceptional selection of cured meats and cheeses to the fresh pasta dishes, from the meat dishes to the wines – largely local – everything speaks the forthright and comforting language of this land. It is worth, therefore, leaving a little room for the zuppa inglese, served with alchermes ring cake and chocolate shavings: a great classic that concludes the meal in the most indulgent fashion. The setting is small and welcoming, and it comes as no surprise that the restaurant is fully booked every day: reserving a table is strongly advised.

Name: Enoclub
Description En: Under the arcades of a piazza named after Michele Ferrero, this restaurant has a simple, modern ambience with walls covered with wine bottles, as well as friendly, efficient female staff. The beautifully prepared Piedmontese cuisine is showcased on an à la carte and a tasting menu, accompanied by an impressive selection of quality wine.

Name: Maso Runch-Hof
Description En: Surrounded by woods, a trip to this restaurant housed in an 18C farmhouse is like taking a journey back in time. Take a seat in one of the wood-adorned Stube-style rooms and enjoy generous portions of delicious home-cooked Ladin specialities featured on a single tasting menu, including cajinci t’ega (spinach-filled ravioli), excellent pork ribs with polenta, and apple strudel. The small wine list has the same local focus, featuring labels from the Alto Adige region. A recent addition, the restaurant also now has a few spacious, welcoming chalets available for guests.

Name: Radimare
Address: via Beato Piergiorgio Frassati 5/a, Monopoli, 70043, Italy
Description En: There’s no tasting menu at this restaurant but instead a tempting à la carte featuring modern Mediterranean cuisine based on top-quality seasonal ingredients, with fish and seafood taking centre stage. Citrus fruit and a few spices, especially ginger, are used carefully and sparingly, as are aromatic herbs which add a touch of fresh flavour to the dishes. The contemporary decor, enhanced by plants and a profusion of wood, plus friendly service add to the appeal.

Name: Da Nilo
Description En: In the heart of Cetona's square, a well-tended outdoor area among hedges welcomes guests with warmth and smiles. The cuisine is authentically Tuscan and well-crafted. Don’t miss the selection of local cured meats and the classic pici all’aglione, a true must-try!

Name: Lou Ressignon
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Classic Cuisine
Description En: Founded in 1966 and now run by the fifth generation, the Lou Ressignon family trattoria (in local dialect the name translates as “the night snack”) serves authentic cuisine full of character which showcases the produce and traditions of the Aosta Valley. The dishes include a delicious Valpellinese soup and excellent tripe with borlotti beans and polentina. In addition to the first-floor dining room, there’s also a historic taverna, while four welcoming guestrooms are available for anyone wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Il Labirinto
Description En: Situated on the outskirts of Brescia, this long-established restaurant has an elegant retro atmosphere. The cuisine is varied with a balance of fish and meat dishes, as well as some excellent home-made salumi.

Name: La Porta Restaurant
Address: piazza Vieira de Mello 4, Bologna, 40128, Italy
Description En: "Housed in a futuristic building which extends like a bridge across Via Stalingrado, La Porta Restaurant is a highly versatile establishment. Set within a futuristic building that spans Via Stalingrado like a bridge, La Porta Restaurant is a versatile venue: the garage provides access to the café’s delicacies and, at lunchtime, the bistro opens with simple dishes, while gourmet diners can enjoy the evening menu in the restaurant with its elegant wooden decor. The menu features an array of fish, meat and vegetable options, while service comes courtesy of a mainly female team, all of whom are extremely friendly and welcoming. With some references to the culinary traditions of Emilia, the kitchen serves dishes featuring ingredients (both meat and fish) and recipes from various regions, complemented by the chef's creative touch. "

Name: Badessa
Description En: This restaurant has a surprising location in a 19C cheese factory which once produced parmesan. Although the purpose of the building has changed, the love of the region remains the same – the chef goes out of his way to source local ingredients and search out old recipes, serving traditional Emilian dishes often with a modern twist. The fresh pasta and other ingredients are produced by the restaurant, while the carefully chosen wine list focuses on natural labels in particular.

Name: Pescarino-Sapori di Terra e di Mare
Description En: Warm and inviting atmosphere with wooden walls and ceiling. The kitchen, recently renovated alongside the terrace, remains unchanged in offering: relatively simple in some concoctions, more creative in others, aiming primarily to highlight the product quality, predominantly seafood, with Ligurian nuances but extending to other regions. Considering the isolated location, seizing the opportunity to rest in the rooms may be worthwhile.

Name: Già Sotto l'Arco
Description En: A historic gourmet restaurant, with an equally historic setting on the first floor of a Baroque palazzo fronting an elegant piazza. A fine staircase leads up to the simple yet stylish dining room, which is skilfully run by a father and his offspring. In the kitchen, his wife Teresa prepares creative, regional cuisine, which is showcased on a surprise menu of four, six or eight courses and which features locally sourced meat and fish. If you’d like to book the delightful table on the small terrace for just two fortunate guests, make sure you do so well in advance!

Name: La Locanda del Cardinale
Description En: Situated right in the centre of Assisi, La Locanda del Cardinale occupies an old palazzo that is home to the perfectly preserved remains of a Roman villa dating back to 70 BC in a fascinating setting full of history. The menu features simple recipes such as crispy organic egg with asparagus and marjoram, as well as more elaborate, modern dishes including quail and Danubio brioche with barbecued artichoke. It’s not surprising that this delightful restaurant also boasts a superb wine cellar with an array of carefully chosen labels that will delight wine-enthusiasts.

Name: La Veranda del Color
Description En: This aptly named restaurant in the Color Hotel just a short distance from Lake Garda boasts a modern, colourful decor and cuisine worthy of its name. Dishes are inspired by Mediterranean traditions and are showcased on a number of different tasting menus.

Name: Piacentino
Description En: A short distance from the historic centre of the enchanting village of Bobbio, this restaurant presents a cuisine that speaks with coherence and respect of the traditions of the territory, drawing out authentic flavours and a faithful adherence to the seasonality of its produce. The menu is a homage to the local cuisine, and among its specialities stands out one of the emblematic dishes of the town: maccheroni alla bobbiese, prepared according to tradition and with consummate skill, a true expression of the gastronomic identity of the place.

Name: Trippini
Address: via Italia 14, Civitella del Lago, 05023, Italy
Description En: Just a few tables and spectacular views of Lake Corbara characterise this restaurant, which has been run by the same family since 1964. The delicious cuisine is regional in flavour, showcasing home-cooked recipes and typical Sunday favourites yet with a contemporary twist that incorporates plenty of intense flavours.

Name: La Terrazza
Description En: A salon en plein air overlooking Asolo’s historical center, this charming spot offers attentive service and Italian cuisine presented with a modern touch. The menu spans land and sea, with vegetarian options as well. A classic and welcoming atmosphere makes it an ideal setting for a romantic dinner.

Name: Il Focarile
Address: via Pontina al km 46,5, Aprilia, 04011, Italy
Description En: The sumptuous entrance gives an elegant tone to a large bright dining room with well spaced out tables; a touch of Tuscany with a cuisine rich in tradition and also imagination. Now offers new, elegant rooms.

Name: Loewengrube
Description En: This building has been home to a restaurant since the 16C, making it one of the oldest in Bolzano. Today, it houses an elegant restaurant that serves a combination of traditional Alpine cuisine and classic Italian dishes with a contemporary twist, such as carbonara tortelloni filled with parmesan cream and crispy bacon. The attractive wine cellar boasts a selection of approximately 1 000 wines from the region and elsewhere in Italy, as well as a choice of labels from further afield.

Name: Osteria Taviani
Address: Via del Monte Ovest 25, Bientina, 56031, Italy
Description En: Housed in a small Art Nouveau-style villa, this restaurant boasts an elegant yet warm and friendly ambience. The cuisine here is modern and full of flavour, with a focus on meat dishes (although a few fish options also feature) with their roots firmly anchored in Tuscan traditions (such as the fried steak). During the hunting season, the contemporary-style game dishes are particularly delicious. The wine list includes a few French labels, plus there’s a small, attractive outdoor space in the courtyard to the rear which overlooks a beautiful garden.

Name: La Fermata
Description En: Situated in the countryside around Alessandria, this 18C farmhouse has a modern, minimalist decor which serves as a backdrop for traditional Piedmontese cuisine with a clever modern twist. The chef offers just the right amount of creativity, with a focus on meat dishes and satisfying, memorable flavours that appeal to the emotions as well as the palate. Adding to the appeal, the elegant and exclusive ambience is the result of careful refurbishment, which has transformed the dining room into a triumph of art and design.

Name: In Riva a Numana
Description En: Riva is the Hotel Vista’s fine-dining restaurant, situated just behind Numana’s beach with fine panoramic views. The restaurant serves top-quality ingredients from the Adriatic and surrounding countryside in creative dishes full of flavour which are showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte.

Name: Januarius
Description En: Dedicated to San Gennaro, whose relics are kept in the nearby Duomo, this address pays homage not only to the city’s patron saint but also to the most authentic traditions of Campanian gastronomy. The table presents a procession of the specialities that have shaped the culinary history of Naples: from polpo alla Luciana to broken ziti with traditional ragù, through to the classic baccalà accompanied by Neapolitan-style escarole. Alongside these icons sit more contemporary offerings, described as ‘non-traditional special dishes’, born of the house’s own creative spirit. Guests are welcomed at the entrance by a well-stocked shop of excellent produce – salumi and cheeses above all – while to either side open two characterful dining rooms, authentic and full of personality.

Name: Delicato
Description En: Situated in a picturesque medieval hilltop village in the province of Rieti on the border with Umbria, this restaurant serves cuisine that is influenced by different regions and traditions. Choose between the minimalist-style dining rooms with exposed stone walls and, in fine weather, a charming outdoor space at the foot of Contigliano’s church. Here, chef Carlotta Delicato brings out the best of local ingredients in dishes that are kept deliberately simple and unfussy yet are full of flavour. We highly recommend the “spaghettone mare e lago” with a light brunoise of courgettes. As the restaurant is situated in Lazio, guests can enjoy good local wines made by small-scale producers, such as the Cabernet Sauvignon Masseria Baroni, which is of medium intensity with broad and pronounced aromas. .

Name: Scatto
Description En: From Turin’s beautiful Piazza San Carlo, you head through an inner courtyard to this restaurant’s modern dining room with its open-view kitchen. Whether you opt for the à la carte or tasting menu, you’ll find a balance of traditional Piedmontese and more creative dishes, all of remarkable quality, in keeping with the superb wine list.

Name: Osteria Ricanatti
Description En: This cozy little restaurant, backed by attentive and impeccably polished service, reveals a regional cuisine that is both flavorful and thoughtfully reinterpreted, available through several tasting menus as well as à la carte. Ingredient sourcing is exacting, with all vegetables harvested from the family’s garden just a few kilometers away – a guarantee of freshness and seasonality. Among the most representative dishes: the pecorino and potato tartare dressed with chimichurri, Argentina’s signature green sauce, or the perfectly al dente paccheri with a two-tomato coulis, raw bluefin tuna, and fried capers – a plate that strikes an ideal balance of intensity and harmony.

Name: Belvedere
Description En: Over the years, this family restaurant has become one of the most popular along this coastline. An informal dining room provides the backdrop for the decidedly Mediterranean cuisine served here, where the focus is the fish display cabinet that changes daily and from which guests can make their choice. The friendly and professional approach of the two brothers that run the restaurant has contributed to its success, while the brand-new terrace-lounge, with its stunning view, is the perfect spot for an aperitif or after-dinner drink.

Name: Millo Ristorante
Address: via Garibaldi 4, Santa Teresa Gallura, 07028, Italy
Description En: A charming restaurant with fair prices, Millo offers dishes infused with the flavors of the sea, sometimes with a creative twist (such as spaghetti with a garlic, oil, and chili emulsion, red prawn carpaccio, and a crispy bread crust), other times inspired by tradition (such as the seafood soup cooked in a jar). There are also a few meat options available. The lovely summer terrace is perfect for taking in the lively local scene.

Name: Nugolo
Description En: A restaurant with a convivial atmosphere, enlivened by chic, colourful furnishings, provides the setting for an open kitchen where a young and talented chef stages a contemporary, creative and deeply seasonal offering. The dishes reveal imagination and precision: seared octopus with mussels, potatoes, buffalo-milk panna cotta and parsley; duck breast with a red-fruit jus, chard, bao and shredded duck leg; Sorrento lemon sorbet with herb crumble and candied lemon. Completing the experience is cheerful, attentive service from a motivated and well-coordinated front-of-house team.

Name: Seta Sushi Restaurant
Description En: It was friendship and passion for Japanese cuisine that prompted two young business partners to open this quiet, welcoming restaurant in the heart of Bologna. Situated in a courtyard with medieval origins, Seta Sushi Restaurant has a modern bistro-style dining room, as well as plenty of outdoor space for summer dining. The menu features an impressive selection of traditional Japanese dishes with the occasional personalised touch, all made from top-quality ingredients. Don’t worry if you’re new to Japanese cuisine – Maurilio is front of house to offer guests friendly, expert advice on both food and beverage. The latter includes a choice of sake for those wishing to immerse themselves fully in the Japanese dining experience.

Name: Enotavola Pino
Description En: The entrance to this restaurant through a wine-bar can be misleading, as you are eventually led to simpler – yet still attractive – dining rooms. In this wine-themed setting, enjoy delicious fish and seafood dishes with the occasional creative twist, accompanied by a particularly extensive selection of wines by the glass. A highly recommended address for fish lovers, situated right in the historic centre of Padova.

Name: Al Petes
Description En: Situated amid the alleyways of the historic centre, Al Petes has a pleasant contemporary feel and is run by young, welcoming and friendly owners. Marko’s menu demonstrates an obvious preference for seafood, most of which comes from the Adriatic, and which is served with Mediterranean and even occasional Asian influences. The surprise tasting menu is highly recommended. Just around the corner, the restaurant’s small hotel (James Joyce) is the ideal choice for overnight accommodation.

Name: Futura
Description En: Situated in the heart of the historic centre overlooking the monumental Piazza San Giustino, this restaurant has a traditional feel in keeping with its location, enhanced by typical brick walls in dining rooms arranged on two floors. In contrast, the predominantly meat-based cuisine is contemporary in style, with some interesting technical and creative twists.

Name: Il Presidente
Description En: In the heart of the historic centre, just a short distance from the Cathedral of Lucera, this restaurant lies in an ancient alleyway where the stables of a noble palazzo once stood. Today the dining room is arranged across several interconnecting spaces, framed by elegant stone vaulting; at its centre, two glass panels allow a glimpse of the cellar, which houses over 300 labels. The cooking is Mediterranean, modern and vivid in colour: among the dishes, octopus with almonds, fusillone with pumpkin cream and scampi, and a fillet of fish – sea bream, sea bass or dentex according to the market – accompanied by seasonal vegetables, to give some sense of the style. The focaccia di mare is not to be missed. This is not so much cooking of technical virtuosity as a homage to the ingredient itself: flavour, here, remains the true protagonist.

Name: Osteria della Tana
Description En: Occupying the same red house as chef Alessandro Dal Degan’s gourmet restaurant, the Osteria is where this chef turns his attention to more traditional dishes (meat and fish alike), which are often typical of the Veneto. There’s one highly recommended exception, however, namely the carbonara dell’Osteria, prepared with top-quality ingredients from the region. Also popular are the baccalà alla vicentina (dried cod) and the tripe, both of which feature on a menu with a wide selection, including renowned dishes from the chef’s Michelin-starred restaurant. Full-bodied flavours that will delight the palate.

Name: Belé
Description En: The name says it all – in Milanese dialect, “belé” means beautiful and the word is an apt description of this restaurant. Belé is charmingly lit by an old-fashioned chandelier on which the pieces of crystal create a play of light resembling an intricate and shifting lace-like pattern. The dining rooms are decorated in attractive contemporary colours, with comfortable armchairs and acoustics perfect for conversation, while the cuisine is Italian with a modern twist.

Name: Kosmo Taste the Mountain
Description En: Just a stone’s throw from the centre and also accessible from the ski slopes in winter, this contemporary, Alpine-style restaurant boasts a spacious dining room and large picture windows. The cuisine reflects the traditions of the Valtellina mountains, with a dedicated space for the charcoal grill and an excellent selection of cheeses. The extensive wine list pays particular attention to mountain wines produced by wineries with a sustainable focus.

Name: Concezione Restaurant
Description En: This minimalist-style restaurant is home to one of the most interesting young chefs in Catania. In this historic building with beautiful ceilings, enjoy top-quality Sicilian cuisine created by Manuel Tropea, who focuses in particular on specialities from Catania which he interprets in a highly personalised way with a real focus on tradition. Dishes such as “L’Asina e la lattuga” and “Good morning in Catania” are good examples. The chef’s surprise menu takes guests on a culinary journey full of contrasts which is inspired by his own memories and experiences.

Name: Essentia
Address: piazza San Nicolò 2, Castrocaro Terme, 47011, Italy
Description En: Situated at the foot of the fortress in the historic centre of Castrocaro, this restaurant has an interesting young chef at the helm, Andrea Giacchini. The cuisine often (but not always) has a local influence and demonstrates remarkable technical expertise that is neither overly ostentatious nor an end in itself, but rather a way of skilfully showcasing the top-quality ingredients used.

Name: Frades La Terrazza
Address: SP94 - Località Abbiadori, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description En: Situated in a panoramic location on Cala di Volpe bay, this trendy restaurant serves excellent cuisine with a focus on Sardinian specialities and other Mediterranean dishes. There’s a beautiful terrace for an aperitif, plus tapas options to share and a good selection of sparkling wines. Young and enthusiastic staff.

Name: La Loggia Bistrò
Description En: Tucked into a slightly secluded courtyard yet still in the heart of the city, this venue offers alfresco service of discreet charm during the summer months. The interiors surprise with dramatic hot-air balloons descending from the ceiling, design details that help create a distinctive and welcoming atmosphere. The culinary offering moves between dishes rooted in local tradition and more creative forays, including some appealing fish options.

Name: Gennaro Di Pace
Address: vicolo della Chiesa 8, loc. Perno, Monforte d'Alba, 12065, Italy
Description En: The owner-chef’s Calabrian origins are evident on a menu that combines Mediterranean cuisine (including fish and seafood) with Piedmontese specialities and showcases beautifully presented dishes prepared using contemporary techniques. This small modern restaurant situated near Perno castle is also open at lunchtime (by prior reservation only).

Name: Regio Patio
Address: via San Francesco d'Assisi 23, Garda, 37016, Italy
Description En: Situated just a stone’s throw from the lakefront, this elegant gourmet restaurant in the Regina Adelaide hotel boasts an attractive English-style garden, as well as a beautiful outdoor patio and stylish dining room. The two tasting menus served here (one of which is vegetarian) showcase the traditions of Lake Garda and its surrounding region with a creative twist using vegetables from the property’s own kitchen garden and a focus on seasonal ingredients. There’s also an extensive wine list.

Name: Trattoria al Ponte
Address: via Bertolda 27, località Bornio, Lusia, 45020, Italy
Description En: Recognized as the only “Historic Establishment of Italy” in the province of Rovigo, this inviting, family-run trattoria offers traditional cooking with a strong emphasis on meat dishes, served in typically generous portions. The menu is enhanced by daily specials, shared verbally, which can be enjoyed in the warm, welcoming dining rooms or on the charming terrace at the entrance. A park with a natural pond and swimming pool provides an ideal setting also for events.

Name: Degli Angeli
Address: località Madonna degli Angeli, Magliano Sabina, 02046, Italy
Description En: The family that runs this excellent restaurant with views of the surrounding countryside has been doing so with passion and experience for over a century. The menu here focuses on the culinary traditions of Lazio, while the wine and extra-virgin olive oil are also sourced locally. The restaurant is part of a hotel and includes a shop (La Bottega delle Delizie) selling home-made produce.

Name: La Sosta di Ottone III
Description En: Ask for directions to this restaurant when you make your booking, as you’ll need to leave your vehicle in a private car park at the entrance to the village and then make your way uphill on foot. Situated in one of Liguria’s most typical and picturesque inland villages with views of the sea in the distance, the restaurant offers outdoor dining under a wisteria in fine weather. The menu features a small choice of regional dishes, with the same focus on Liguria evident on the wine list.

Name: Ristorante 1500
Address: via Pavicolo 43, funivia per raggiungere il ristorante in via Villa 3, San Vigilio, 39011, Italy
Description En: If you’re not a guest at the Vigilius Mountain Resort hotel where this restaurant is situated, leave your car in Lana and take the short cable-car ride to Monte San Vigilio where you’ll find the hotel at an altitude of 1 500m (remember to check the time of the last cable-car back down the mountain!). Decorated with a profusion of wood, the dining room has the same modern feel as the creative mountain cuisine prepared by the new chef who started here in 2023.

Name: Osteria del Guà
Description En: Housed in the “barchessa” of a Palladian villa dating from 1541, this restaurant boasts an elegant dining room with an open fireplace. The cuisine here is creative and of excellent quality, with many of the main meat courses cooked over the barbecue grill. All in all, a romantic setting and superb food that is not to be missed.

Name: da Omar
Address: via Dante Alighieri 21, Lido di Jesolo, 30016, Italy
Description En: Passion and enthusiasm overcome all obstacles and lead to the best results: this summarises the professional journey of the chef at this restaurant. He prepares fish dishes inspired by classic Italian cuisine, sometimes with a modern twist, but always using the best quality produce.

Name: Vino Buono
Address: via Castello 20, Grumello del Monte, 24064, Italy
Description En: In an atmospheric 17th-century barn, adjacent to the cathedral bell tower, takes shape a wine bar of considerable charm. Here to welcome guests is Roberto, patron and cellarman at once, discreet and warm, always ready to share the stories of wines and their local areas. In accompaniment, simple, straightforward cooking with a homely, traditional character, well executed and full of personality, with occasional forays into seafood. Not to be missed are the selection of cured meats and cheeses and the excellent primi piatti, genuine highlights of the offering.

Name: Osteria dai Mazzeri
Description En: Once the town hall of Follina, this building dating from 1704 is now home to a restaurant run by two brothers who serve delicious regional and seasonal cuisine here (in winter, don’t miss the spit-roasted chicken, veal or pork cooked according to local tradition). A beautiful mulberry tree, the old symbol of the village that was once involved in the silk industry, graces the outdoor dining space.

Name: Corsaro Nero
Address: Località Portu Maga, Marina di Arbus, 09031, Italy
Description En: A wide choice of fresh fish and a menu with a firm focus on fish and seafood served in a large dining room offering views of the spectacular sunsets.

Name: Crotto Valtellina
Address: via Fiume 11, località Valle, Malnate, 21046, Italy
Description En: For over fifty years, the Valbuzzi family has passionately maintained this enchanting crotto, now in its third generation. The atmosphere is elegant and refined while staying true to its origins: wooden tables, period furnishings, and floral touches. The summer veranda is particularly stunning, overlooking a lush garden and a sandstone wall. The menu balances traditional dishes – the pizzoccheri are unmissable – with more contemporary creations, such as the surprising saltimbocca of larded quail with fennel, escarole gel, pickled apricot, and zucchini flan.

Name: Vesta Versilia
Description En: Within Twiga beach establishment, in a setting where glamour reigns supreme, multifunctional and equipped with a fully-fledged cocktail bar, the cuisine favours classic recipes and cooking methods, but equally dedicates substantial attention to raw seafood and pizza. From our last visit, the seafood salad—boasting excellent varied citronette-dressed products—and the roast turbot with lemon potato cream and asparagus stand particularly memorable.

Name: Giglio
Description En: Housed in a beautiful 18C palazzo, Giglio boasts a superb location in one of the many squares in Lucca’s charming historic centre, as well as a delightful outdoor space. The meat and fish dishes on the menu here are inspired by traditional Italian recipes and reinterpreted with a light modern touch – a good example is the siphoned potato which is sprinkled with bottarga and served with a squid sauce, chanterelle mushrooms and spicy parsley cream. The bread is always excellent.

Name: La Rosina
Description En: With over 100 years of history behind it, La Rosina is still looking good, thanks to renovation work carried out a few years ago which has given the restaurant a new look. Situated in an attractive location in the hills around Marostica, this excellent restaurant is a sound choice for good food in the province of Vicenza, serving modern regional and Italian dishes which are full of flavour. Enjoy beautiful views of the surrounding hills from the guestrooms.

Name: Buca di Sant'Antonio
Description En: Just a stone’s throw from Piazza San Michele, in the heart of the beautiful historic centre of Lucca, the Buca di Sant'Antonio dates back over 200 years and is one of the city’s oldest restaurants. Here, the old copper pots and pans that hang from the ceiling add to the warm, romantic atmosphere, while the cuisine unsurprisingly showcases traditional Tuscan specialities including meat dishes and home-made pasta.

Name: Osteria Il Bagatto
Address: via XX Settembre 16, Limone Piemonte, 12015, Italy
Description En: Nestled amid the stone houses of Limone Piemonte, this charming gourmet restaurant is situated in a typical historic passageway. Influenced by the seasons and the chef’s creative skills, the menu includes interesting dishes such as char, gnocchi with blue goat’s cheese and delicious sweetbreads in butter with cannellini beans and cavolo nero. To accompany your meal, you might like to indulge in a bottle of vintage Barolo chosen from the concise yet carefully chosen wine list. The 2013 Michele Chiarlo Barolo Cerequio, produced in a cold and rainy year, has aged well thanks to its powerful tannins.

Name: Nicolin
Address: via Paisiello 4, località Maggianico, Lecco, 23900, Italy
Description En: Restaurant-hotel not far from the centre, but in a quiet, residential area, this is where you can find some of the best cuisine in town. The cook revisits some national dishes in a personal way, with a few seafood offerings as well.

Name: Duo Ristorante
Description En: This elegant, intimate restaurant with subdued lighting is the perfect choice for a romantic gourmet dinner. Showcased on tasting menus and a concise à la carte, the excellent cuisine focuses on typical recipes and specialities from Puglia, often with an added personalised and creative twist.

Name: La Tavola
Description En: Situated in the Il Porticciolo hotel, this restaurant will appeal to anyone who enjoys a lakeside setting. Leave your car in the car park, then take the lift down to the dining room with its windows overlooking the water and views of the opposite shore of Lake Maggiore. The lake also takes pride of place in some of the creative, elaborate and personalised dishes on the two tasting menus created by Riccardo Bassetti, many of which feature freshwater fish.

Name: Cavalluccio Marino
Description En: Imaginative cuisine in a long - established family restaurant, which is constantly updated by each generation. Situated away from the town centre, yet easily accessible, the restaurant boasts an enviable seafront location. Excellent selection of local and international wines.

Name: Ruris
Address: Via Spiaggie Rosse, località Mazzotta, Isola di Capo Rizzuto, 88841, Italy
Description En: Despite its rural setting inland, this restaurant is still situated within the Capo Rizzuto e Mar Ionio protected marine reserve, which helps to explain the focus on fish and seafood dishes demonstrated by owner-chef Natale Pallone on the menu. The wine cellar boasts over 200 different wines and more than 60 internationally renowned spirits.

Name: Antica Osteria Magenes
Description En: This fascinating restaurant occupying an old house renovated in modern style comes as a surprise given its location in a small village deep in the countryside. Enjoy traditional cuisine reinterpreted in a playful and original way in the well-tended garden, where six exclusive tables provide the perfect setting for an intimate and romantic alfresco dinner.

Name: Osteria Borgo Ronche
Description En: With only a handful of tables – all the more reason to reserve – and a contemporary, streamlined yet welcoming setting, this intimate spot showcases the chef-owner’s resolutely seafood-focused cuisine, though a couple of meat options round out the menu. Preparations and pairings remain largely classic, as seen in the gratinéed Breton scallops, while raw seafood also makes an appearance, sometimes unexpectedly atop pasta, as in the standout spaghettoni with cacio e pepe and red prawn tartare.

Name: Filippino
Description En: Opened in 1910, this historic restaurant with an attractive shaded outdoor pergola serves an extensive array of delicious local fish prepared in traditional recipes. Enjoy a selection of typical Sicilian specialities prepared by the Bernardi family, including the highly recommended “Nonno Filippino” fish soup.

Name: Bistrot Royal
Description En: Inside the refined Grand Hotel Royal e Golf, the Bistrot offers the opportunity to savor the delicious flavors of Valle d’Aosta in a refined and lighter interpretation. In recipes where the quality of the raw ingredients takes center stage, you’ll be pampered by excellent service while comfortably seated in spaces that interpret Alpine style with personal touches.

Name: Il Pescatore
Address: via Acqua Dolce 7, Cala Gonone, 08022, Italy
Description En: This Mediterranean-style restaurant has the evocative feel of a seaside village with its beautiful photos of the coast on the walls. It’s best to book ahead if you want one of the tables on the small terrace overlooking the sea. To avoid confusion, note that the Il Pescatore that we recommend is situated at 7, via Acqua Dolce.

Name: Botero
Description En: Close to the city centre and within walking distance of the Cathedral, the restaurant is located inside a beautiful historic building. The cuisine is fragrant, and the menu alternates between seafood offerings – depending on market availability – and a few more traditional recipes such as hand-pinched Cremasque sweet tortelli. The jovial welcome, streamlined service and interesting wine list (with a few "natural" offerings for enthusiasts) explain why there is a large turnout for both lunch and dinner. Better make reservations!

Name: Osteria dai Coghi
Address: via Alcide De Gasperi 9/13, Albarè di Costermano, 37010, Italy
Description En: This well-kept, welcoming restaurant with a colourful decor and wine bottles adorning the walls serves imaginative dishes with modern combinations – our inspector particularly enjoyed the guinea fowl supreme with smoked black tea, carrots and beluga lentils. The well-chosen wine list features labels from Italy and further afield.

Name: Osteria dalla Peppa
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Traditional Cuisine
Description En: A trattoria in the old town, with rooms filled with memories and nostalgia, offering an atmosphere that makes you feel at home, just like the traditional cuisine. The fresh-egg pasta rolled out with a rolling pin (also on sale in their nearby shop) is the main attraction here, with main courses featuring various types of meat, and fish dishes on Fridays.

Name: Ai Torchi
Description En: Occupying a 17C olive oil press in the heart of a charming medieval village, this restaurant has retained its old stone mill and wooden press in its vaulted dining room, which provides the backdrop for imaginative fish and seafood dishes prepared using top-quality local ingredients. The delicious Italian-style ceviche is made from the catch of the day, while the Mare Mare mixed fish dish is baked in a casserole with cherry tomatoes, courgettes and bay leaves. If you’re looking for a simpler option, try the I Torchiettibistro on the corner of the same street.

Name: L'Antico Giardino
Description En: A menu steeped in Ferrarese tradition, served in a welcoming and comfortable setting, energised by the friendly charm of the owner, who offers valuable advice on the best wine and food pairings. The menu features flavours that seduce the senses: passatelli drenched in a velvety cheese fondue, enriched with morel mushrooms and the intense aroma of autumn black truffle ; soft and juicy larded pheasant breast accompanied by a Castelmagno custard that caresses the palate; and to finish, a soft cheesecake with double white chocolate and pistachio mousse, topped with a blackberry sauce. And, season permitting, the king of the table: the white truffle, ready to enhance every dish.

Name: Aurora
Description En: Situated just a stone’s throw from the Concattedrale di San Pietro Apostolo, Aurora boasts a cheerful and contemporary-style dining room with colourful furnishings, soft lighting and plenty of wine bottles on display. The carefully prepared cuisine includes Italian and regional meat and fish specialities with a light, modern twist.

Name: Emilio
Address: via Girardi 1, loc. Casabianca, Fermo, 63900, Italy
Description En: With 60 years of history behind it, Emilio can definitely be described as a leading light on the region’s restaurant scene. The restaurant is renowned for its excellent fish, which is usually cooked in classic style (fish stew and mixed steamed fish served on steamed vegetables are prime examples) and often announced at your table, although a concise menu is also available. The elegant dining room is enhanced by a collection of striking works of art.

Name: Osteria Vecchio Borgo
Description En: Described as a “meeting point between Piedmont and Liguria”, this quiet, welcoming restaurant in the historic centre of Cuneo focuses on ingredients and recipes from these two regions – the family, all of whom are involved in the restaurant (the women in the kitchen and the men front of house), are from Liguria. The generous, top-quality cuisine is prepared using seasonal produce with a personalised touch and is accompanied by a good selection of wine, also available by the glass.

Name: 4 Ciance
Description En: Two bright rooms in the heart of the old town welcome guests with warmth and professionalism, courtesy of the all-female staff. A refined atmosphere, the scent of wood and meticulous attention to detail create the backdrop for the dishes created by the two chefs, conceived to delight both the eyes and the palate. The menu is based on solid traditional foundations, but with contemporary and creative touches. Choose from two tasting menus and an à la carte menu, featuring dishes made with seasonal ingredients. The focus is on meat, as is traditional in Piedmont, but there are also refined seafood alternatives for those looking for different flavours.

Name: La Meridiana
Description En: In business for over 50 years, this long-established, centrally located restaurant has changed its look over the years and is now a modern bistro with an attractive outdoor summer space overlooking the magical town centre. Here, the owner-chef serves fish prepared in two different ways, either in typical Italian tradition or in a style inspired by his native Spain – his paella is definitely worth sampling! The front of house is overseen by the owner’s friendly wife, who is also at hand to help with your wine choices.

Name: Cucina Bacilieri
Description En: A small restaurant in the heart of the city, refined and romantic, where soft spotlights cast a gentle glow over the tables, creating an intimate, comforting atmosphere. The flavors are entrusted to chef-owner Bacilieri, who crafts modern, harmonious dishes rooted in seasonality and the freshness of ingredients, spanning both meat and fish. Not to be missed: the dessert course, here it is a true indulgence for the palate. Service, led by a young, passionate team, attends to every detail of the experience with warmth and care.

Name: Menzaghi
Address: via San Giovanni 74, Fagnano Olona, 21054, Italy
Description En: In a small dining room decorated in traditional style, the Menzaghi Restaurant is now run by the fourth generation of the family, who passionately carry on its long-standing traditions. The owner is a great wine enthusiast, and the informal but professional service helps create a pleasant and welcoming atmosphere. The cuisine is hearty, with a strong focus on seasonal and locally sourced ingredients. It is also worth taking a look at the daily specials, which are often particularly interesting.

Name: Mirko's
Address: discesa Annunziata 1, Castellammare del Golfo, 91014, Italy
Description En: This small restaurant, located near the steps to Cala Piccola, is run by an entire family and is beginning to earn an excellent local reputation. The son is at the helm in the kitchen. Having gained experience elsewhere for many years, he decided to start his own venture, which shows every sign of having paid off. Enjoy excellent fish and seafood specialities cooked in Mediterranean and Sicilian style in a quiet, beautifully kept dining room.

Name: Entrà
Address: via Salde Entrà 60, località Entrà, Finale Emilia, 41034, Italy
Description En: Siblings Antonio and Elvira uphold a family tradition which, since the 1960s, has been part of a much longer history, that of the simple wine shop which occupied these premises immediately after the Great War. For generations, the Previdi family has been a benchmark for authentic, fragrant and delicious Emilian cuisine, prepared — as they like to recall — “without revisiting it, whenever possible”.Fresh, homemade pasta is a real highlight, starting with the legendary pumpkin tortelli – made famous in part by the restaurant’s proximity to the province of Mantua – served with a savoury meat sauce. The signature dish, however, is roast guinea fowl, served on a bed of seasonal salad and accompanied by tender roast potatoes, in the truest family tradition.The wine selection is also of the highest standard, comprising around 400 labels and reflecting a carefully considered choice that complements the dishes on the menu.

Name: Alla Lanterna
Description En: On the Adriatic coast road south of Fano, run by the same family since 1976, the year it opened, this restaurant is a must for seafood lovers. The dishes are essentially inspired by the seafaring traditions of the Marche region.

Name: Nni Lausta
Address: via Risorgimento 188, Santa Marina Salina, 98050, Italy
Description En: Fish plays the starring role here, where the authentic traditional flavours and ingredients of Aeolian cuisine are skilfully interpreted with a touch of imaginative flair. If it’s not too hot to sit outside, ask for a table on the pleasant, shaded terrace on the first floor.

Name: La Bottega del 30
Address: via Santa Caterina 2, località Villa a Sesta, Castelnuovo Berardenga, 53019, Italy
Description En: There’s a story behind the name of this restaurant: on the 30th day of every month a travelling salesman used to stop in this small, delightful village. In the meantime, a young French chef, Hélène, arrived here and fell in love with Chianti and its cuisine. She named her restaurant after the travelling salesman and the name has been kept in his memory. In a typical setting of stone walls and old rural objects from bygone days, Hélène is now front-of-house taking care of guests, while Nadia Mongiat has replaced her in the kitchen, where she continues with the restaurant’s tradition of creating simple Tuscan cuisine. The focus here is on preparing ingredients in traditional ways, such as pork liver (the thinnest part of the liver is used) cooked at a low temperature and then stored in lard with fennel for a few days before being re-heated sous-vide in a bain-marie. As a result, the liver (served lukewarm on a bed of Tuscan green beans) is soft and delicious.

Name: Il Galeone
Description En: In a bright, elegant and modern dining room inside the Elisabeth Due hotel, Galeone is one of the city's finest gastronomic destinations. The menu focuses on fish, with dishes that draw on local traditions, such as “brodetto alla fanese” fish soup (available by advance order), alongside more creative offerings.

Name: Locanda Gulfi
Description En: In an isolated but well‑marked location that doesn’t escape the notice of oil and wine enthusiasts, Locanda Gulfi produces both, as you can tell from the view of the wine cellar visible from the dining room. The cuisine offers revisited Sicilian dishes, with the possibility of overnight accommodation and, naturally, tastings of the estate’s products, accompanied by dedicated menus or simple snacks specially designed for the occasion.

Name: Lord Nelson
Description En: Set right on the seafront, with a delightful outdoor seating area, this historic restaurant – opened in 1969 and dedicated to the famous English admiral – boasts classic elegance with mahogany furnishings and light-coloured curtains reminiscent of unfurled sails. Mediterranean-inspired cuisine plays with modern and creative touches, such as slow-cooked amberjack served with baby spinach, pine nuts, marjoram and date tomato sauce.

Name: SaleGrosso
Address: viale II Giugno 15, Milano Marittima, 48015, Italy
Description En: One of the town’s authentic favourites, this fish restaurant has a pleasant, light - coloured decor inspired by the sea. The eclectic cuisine includes tapas and raw fish dishes.

Name: Ristorante Mas-cì
Description En: Situated in the charming historic centre, this hotel and restaurant are now run by the third generation of the same family. Welcoming dining rooms with a fireplace provide the setting for cuisine which makes the most of local produce while also including dishes from elsewhere in Italy. Don’t miss the black truffle specialities!

Name: Galileo
Address: via IV Novembre conc. 25, Civitanova Marche, 62012, Italy
Description En: Boasting a dining room overlooking the beach, Galileo is a typical Adriatic restaurant serving fish and seafood dishes that are popular with many Italians. Options include seafood salad, a selection of antipasti, fish and seafood pastas, assorted small fried fish, and grilled recipes. In other words, delicious, traditional and unfussy cuisine in which fish takes centre stage.

Name: Carlo Magno
Description En: This restaurant housed in a country house dating from the 19C offers elegant period dining rooms and a menu featuring Mediterranean-style meat and fish dishes.

Name: Pantagruele
Description En: Situated in the town centre just a stone’s throw from the port, this small, typical trattoria is renowned for its delicious fish and seafood, including an excellent antipasto buffet and fresh fish cooked mainly on the grill. The large outdoor area is perfect for summer dining. Informal service.

Name: La Porta Antica
Address: via Quarto dei Mille 16, Brescia, 25128, Italy
Description En: Contemporary interiors and a prime location in a quiet residential neighborhood provide the backdrop for a seafood-focused kitchen that balances measured creativity with precise flavors. The shellfish selection excels: from prized Sicilian red prawns to steamed jumbo shrimp, refined and elevated by a soft bean purée with crispy guanciale.

Name: Villa Tiboldi
Address: via Case Sparse 127, località Tiboldi, Canale, 12043, Italy
Description En: A delightful combination of good food and a romantic ambience in this old restored farmhouse surrounded by hills. Top - quality cuisine and a wine cellar that is well worth a visit.

Name: Alle Codole
Address: via XX Agosto 27, Canale d'Agordo, 32020, Italy
Description En: ‘Codole’ is the nickname of the family that runs this restaurant and whose ancestors once worked in the copper mines in the area. Today, the family has exchanged mining for cooking, offering guests specialities such as ricotta and black truffle ravioli with a lamb ragù, and loin of venison in a porcini mushroom crust.

Name: La Madia
Description En: This authentic rural trattoria overlooking the valley and Franciacorta specialises in regional produce and typical Italian cuisine. Each dish on the menu lists the origin of the ingredients used, plus the name and address of the producer. Specialities include tagliolini pasta sautéed in a walnut sauce with tuna. Top quality cuisine offering excellent value for money.

Name: La Bul
Description En: Here, in one of Bari’s most interesting restaurants, chef Antonio Scalera serves top-quality cuisine accompanied by intelligently chosen wines with fascinating stories behind them. The dishes often feature traditional recipes and ingredients from Puglia yet are creative and of the highest quality.

Name: Al Carroponte
Address: Via Edmondo De Amicis 4, Bergamo, 24127, Italy
Description En: This restaurant is renowned in Bergamo for its good choice of varied cuisine, as well as its lively, buzzing atmosphere. The excellent, tasty cuisine is typically Italian and contemporary in style, and includes luxury ingredients such as lobster and caviar, while the “classic” à la carte is enhanced by a selection of cured hams, cheeses and finger food. But the Carroponte’s beating heart is owner Oscar Mazzoleni’s passion for the world of wine, with an incredible selection of over 2 000 labels that puts many more famous Michelin-starred restaurants in the shade.

Name: Matteo Ristorante
Description En: In elegant and intimate spaces with soft, muted tones, guests enjoy the contemporary cuisine of Matteo Marra. Meat and fish feature equally on the menu, with a constant emphasis on meticulously crafted and spectacular presentations of dishes. A small outdoor area sits under a portico, with tables that must be reserved well in advance during the warmer months. Coffee and aperitif service is also available at the adjacent Laboratorio, at No. 10.

Name: Macelleria Motta
Address: strada Padana Superiore 90, Bellinzago Lombardo, 20060, Italy
Description En: Motta has established a reputation for quality, especially for its meat which is carefully sourced from farms in the Piedmont region. Some of the excellent options on the menu are aged in a large fridge near the entrance, along with different types of delicious salumi which are produced and cured by the restaurant. Various types of meat feature here – these are cured or cooked using classic methods with the occasional modern touch. Piedmontese beef is one of the highlights, with different cuts grilled on the barbecue or served boiled. Make sure you try the 300g hamburger with Aosta valley Toma cheese, BBQ sauce and caramelised onions served in a sesame-seed bun. Enjoy alfresco dining in a typical Lombardy courtyard in summer.

Name: I Carracci
Description En: "After leaving the lobby of the luxurious Grand Hotel Majestic, you come to the restaurant, adorned by a 17th century fresco from the Carracci school. This is the restaurant for grand occasions and, under the guidance of chef Agostino Schettino, also for outstanding cuisine. From Castellammare di Stabia in Campania, the chef presents a menu featuring a succession of references to the cuisines of Emilia and Naples: two of Italy's most renowned culinary traditions sit at the same table to create a truly extraordinary result. "

Name: Locanda San Michele
Address: SS 491 3, Contrada Camerale di Tossiccia, Montorio al Vomano, 64046, Italy
Description En: Practically on the slopes of Gran Sasso with views of the verdant landscapes of the Abruzzo, this restaurant is home to a local chef who has returned to his roots having spent time away gaining experience in Michelin-starred restaurants. Here, he serves regional cuisine with a modern, contemporary twist and a focus on meat and fish alike (examples include tuna tartare with strawberries finished in the dining room with lemon “snow”) in generous portions that are typical of the Abruzzo.

Name: Antica Trattoria Giovanelli
Description En: In an enchanting bucolic setting at the foot of the hills, this family-run trattoria – established in 1939 and now in its third generation – offers a cuisine deeply rooted in its territory.The menu celebrates the great classics of the tradition, from charcuterie to roasts and boiled meats, but it is above all the handmade fresh pasta and the almond cake served with zabaione that merit particular attention.In fine weather, the outdoor veranda provides a pleasant open-air space. For those wishing to extend the experience, the trattoria’s own-produced charcuterie is available to purchase.

Name: Barbieri
Description En: Enjoy your meal in the classic - style dining room or on the outdoor terrace in fine weather. The menu here is seasonal, with a focus on delicious Calabrian cuisine, while the wine list also features exclusively local options.

Name: Frosio
Description En: Housed in a 18C villa which was once a family inn, this restaurant is run by the dynamic and professional Frosio family who have over 30 years’ experience in the restaurant business. There’s nothing improvised about Frosio, where Camillo guarantees impeccable service front of house and Paolo is at the helm in the kitchen, creating carefully prepared dishes with a classic-modern feel and an equal emphasis on meat and fish, often made from traditionally “gourmet” ingredients such as scampi, lobster, foie gras, pigeon and caviar. The wine list continues to offer an excellent selection, with one section dedicated to Italy and another to the rest of the world. Decorated with austere elegance, the wine cellar in the 13C tower is home to more than 1,000 different labels. Attractive outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: 177 toledo
Description En: On the fifth floor of 177, via Toledo this restaurant exhibits works of art by contemporary artists in its elegant dining room. Delightful artisanal skills from Campania are also featured on the menu, which is made from handmade paper from Amalfi; the manner in which the menu is written recalls the game of Tombola (which originated in Naples), in original and creative reinterpretations of classic regional dishes.

Name: Agriturismo Ferdy
Address: Località Fienili, fraz. Scalvino, Lenna, 24010, Italy
Description En: Once you’ve left your car in the car park and crossed the Brembo river, you enter a fairytale setting of meadows and horses surrounded by the Orobic peaks. Here, the cuisine is a declaration of love for the mountains – although occasionally elaborate, the carefully prepared dishes are substantial and full of flavour, with the same solid character as the inhabitants of these valleys and with meat and dairy produce taking centre stage. The cheese trolley at the end of your meal is a real highlight – there’s something here for all tastes! The wine list is also full of character, featuring a personalised selection which showcases regional labels and natural wines. It’s worth noting that between 30 to 50 different labels are available by the glass at different times of year. Guestrooms and a shop selling typical local produce complete the picture at what is an extraordinary, high-end agriturismo.

Name: Crotasc
Address: via Don Primo Lucchinetti 63, Mese, 23020, Italy
Description En: Here one can choose between a smaller, typically mountain style dining room with stone paving and open fireplace and a larger room in contemporary rustic style. In summer one can dine on the terrace.

Name: Ai Do Campanili
Address: via Marco Polo 2, località Treporti, Cavallino, 30013, Italy
Description En: Both the building in which it is housed and the dining room of this restaurant are on the small side, but the quality of the food more than compensates for the lack of space. Run by young and enthusiastic staff, the restaurant specialises in fish and seafood with raw options and modern dishes featuring on the menu. Excellent selection of wine, also available to take away.

Name: La Nicchia
Description En: This tastefully decorated restaurant is housed in a late - 18C building, which is marked on an old map from the Napoleonic era. Here the best local ingredients are selected to create regional dishes with the occasional contemporary twist.

Name: Der Unterwirt
Description En: Occupying a private house, this restaurant boasts a couple of charming Stube-style dining rooms, one of which is highly romantic and dates back to the 13C – although the vintage wood looks as though it may have come from elsewhere, it has in fact been here for centuries. Owner-chef Thomas Haselwanter creates carefully thought-out dishes which combine precision and classic comfort with the occasional modern touch, harmoniously combining the flavours of the Alto Adige with Mediterranean influences, with a particular focus on fish. A welcoming outdoor terrace for summer dining and seven modern guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Coeur de Bois
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Classic Cuisine
Description En: The name of this elegant restaurant was inspired by its wooden ceiling. Surrounded by spruce decor dating from the 18C, antique furniture and paintings, enjoy interesting traditional cuisine in this excellent gourmet restaurant, which is all the more attractive thanks to its location in the Gran Paradiso national park.

Name: Osteria Cascina dei Fiori
Description En: This restaurant’s warm, elegant and rustic atmosphere with wooden furniture and exposed beams provides the setting for its seasonally inspired, regional cuisine. The experienced owners are welcoming and attentive, while the menu features specialities such as frogs’ leg and courgette flower risotto.

Name: Zur Kaiserkron
Description En: In the heart of Bolzano, on the ground floor of the refined Palazzo Pock which grandly overlooks the piazza, Zur Kaiserkron (The Imperial Crown) welcomes guests in elegant, contemporary surroundings enhanced by striking vaulted ceilings that lend a touch of theatricality to the experience. Since 2025, chef Sinisgalli’s vision unfolds along two distinct paths, designed to suit different guests and moments of the day. The first offers a light, dynamic cuisine firmly anchored to the territory, where traditional flavors are reinterpreted with contemporary spirit, ideal for a city in constant motion. The second, housed in a gilded dining room with an almost suspended charm, represents the chef’s deeper, more creative soul: a gastronomic journey that delves into research, technique, and imagination, delivering an immersive experience of great intensity.

Name: La Luge
Address: Perreres, loc. Varvoyes, Breuil Cervinia, 11021, Italy
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Italian
Description En: Situated in a tranquil, panoramic location on the road to Breuil-Cervinia (less than 4km away), this old farm has been transformed over the past decade into an intimate little hotel with a good restaurant decorated in attractive mountain style and enhanced by a fireplace that is always lit in winter. Here, you can enjoy simple, authentic cuisine prepared from top-quality ingredients with careful attention paid to seasonality. The owner himself oversees the well-stocked wine cellar.

Name: Wine & Dine
Description En: In the center of Canazei, this restaurant within the Croce Bianca hotel occupies wood-paneled rooms that foster a relaxed, informal atmosphere, with a few charming alcoves for more intimate seating. Meat reigns supreme, notably a dedicated selection of grilled main courses. A good assortment of wines by the glass.

Name: Extra
Description En: Situated slightly inland behind Marina di Carrara, Extra (the name refers to the quality of the region’s world-famous marble) is a bright, modern restaurant with a menu inspired by the area’s fish and seafood culinary traditions. The menu is slightly more elaborate and the ambience more elegant in the evening and on Saturday lunchtimes.

Name: Tenuta del Gallo
Description En: Whether you dine indoors in the charming, romantic dining room or outdoors with views of the surrounding countryside, you’ll enjoy traditional local cuisine and classic Italian favourites at this restaurant. Our inspectors particularly enjoyed the excellent beef carpaccio with truffles and the local guinea fowl with chickpeas. Comfortable guestrooms are also available.

Name: Antica Osteria dei Camelì
Description En: Within a sixteenth-century farmhouse of intact charm, where historic rooftops now coexist with modern solar panels in a clear gesture of sustainability, this establishment represents a successful encounter between classic elegance and contemporary design. The kitchen follows the same philosophy: tradition and innovation converse naturally in dishes that place great emphasis on nutritional balance and wholesome pairings, thanks in part to ingredients sourced from trusted local farmers. In the dining room, service maintains the professionalism and courtesy it has always been known for, affirming an approach that has lost neither rigor nor warmth over time.

Name: Paolo Teverini
Address: via del Popolo 2, Bagno di Romagna, 47021, Italy
Description En: Situated in the charming village of Bagno di Romagna and surrounded by beautiful rolling hills, Teverini is a culinary name full of history in this area. The cuisine here demonstrates different traditions – the local region is an obvious influence (especially its mushrooms), but fish and seafood also feature along with plenty of vegetables.

Name: Lu Pisantinu
Address: viale Giovanni Maria Orecchioni snc, loc. Liscia di Vacca, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description En: A terrace framed by granite columns overlooks the coast, the sea, and Porto Cervo (about 2 km away): both the culinary style and the overall décor of the welcoming spaces are classic. The menu features primarily seafood, though there are also dishes and flavors from the inland area, with nods to Gallura traditions, such as the strictly handmade chijusoni gnocchetti. Welcoming you is a local family that has been operating here for over 40 years.

Name: La Fiaschetteria
Description En: Enjoy excellent reinterpretations of Emilian classics in this large 18C farmhouse. It is lit with modern designer - style chandeliers and warmed by a large fireplace. The three splendid guestrooms combine elegance with typical regional decor.

Name: Pascalucci
Address: via Appia 1, San Nicola Manfredi, 82010, Italy
Description En: A traditional restaurant serving regional cuisine, as well as skilfully prepared fish dishes made from fresh produce. Specialities include Beneventano beef fillet and octopus in aspic jelly.

Name: Parco Gambrinus
Address: via Capitello 18, San Polo di Piave, 31020, Italy
Description En: A rustic and romantic setting provides the backdrop for the traditional and creative cuisine served here. It is made from typical local produce with an emphasis on ethical and sustainably produced ingredients (vegan and gluten - free options are also available). Exotic animals inhabit the park, where a stream is home to the house specialities of crayfish, eels and sturgeon. The restaurant also offers a few comfortable guestrooms nearby.

Name: Bistrot La Perla
Address: strada Col Alt 105, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description En: The venue unfolds around a large wooden bar, where the bartenders are constantly at work making excellent cocktails that complement an impressive wine list. We are in the bistro of the famous La Perla hotel: a tribute to mountain life, expressed through charming and cheerful décor that creates a lively and welcoming atmosphere. The menu invites you to indulge in mouth-watering dishes inspired by the classic flavours of Italian tradition, while live music plays in the background.The venue is open practically all day: a café in the morning, a bistro at lunchtime, a more informal menu from 2 pm to 4 pm, and then it’s time for aperitifs, with cocktails and snacks, before moving on to dinner.

Name: Babette
Description En: Situated just beyond the centre of Albenga in a beautiful location right on the beach (with only a small private beach club separating it from the sea), this restaurant has been in business for over 20 years (10 years on this site, and 10 in the town centre before that). It is renowned for its excellent, modern cuisine that focuses on top-quality, fresh and seasonal fish. A lighter (yet equally excellent) menu is also available at lunchtime.

Name: Il Baretto
Description En: Il Baretto on the outskirts of Padova is a must for anyone who loves classic, traditional fish and seafood, thanks to its menu which includes a number of typical Venetian dishes. The top-quality fish is skilfully prepared to bring out its full flavour and distinctive characteristics, providing a real treat for the tastebuds in this inland temple to the sea.

Name: Locanda dell'Arcimboldo
Description En: At the town gates, a friendly inn with a family atmosphere in a fine building, with a pleasant veranda. Fish dishes prevail on the menu, featuring an interesting selection of oysters. At midday there is also an easier set menu.

Name: Coltivare
Description En: The organic soul of the Brandini estate, which houses the restaurant, makes itself felt immediately upon arrival: from the vineyards managed with great respect for the environment to the small herb and spice garden, an invaluable support to the work of chef Zecchin in his continuous pursuit of new aromatic equilibria. A focused experimentation, serving to refine dishes of deeply Langhe character, underpinned by a solid grounding in the territory. Alongside the principal offering, a vegetarian menu is available for devotees of the kitchen garden, while from the carte particular attention is merited by the eel with an intense cream of pil and roasted lettuce, as well as the Fassona chuck, rendered all the more tender and harmonious by Pink Lady apple and a deep brown maize jus. The wine list reflects the same strong bond with Piedmont, without overlooking a carefully considered selection of Champagnes. By day, the spacious dining room affords a splendid view through the large windows that surround it, enriched by the dramatic presence of an imposing fireplace.

Name: Locanda di Nonna Ida
Address: Località Pontarola 12, Marano di Valpolicella, 37020, Italy
Description En: A welcoming inn nestled amid the last vineyards of Valpolicella and the first pasturelands of the lower Lessinia region, where a young chef serves cuisine with a focus on local ingredients and classic Italian recipes with a modern twist. In summer, the terrace offers a fresh, cool setting with extensive views. The barbecued meat is superb.

Name: Corte Federiciana
Description En: The dining room at this restaurant housed in the Palazzo Baronale’s old outbuildings in the historic centre of Apricena boasts an attractive brick-vaulted ceiling. The cuisine, which focuses mainly on fish and seafood (raw, cooked, baked in the oven or served with pasta), effortlessly combines traditional and modern flavours. A delightful welcome and friendly service complete the picture.

Name: Hostaria del Teatro
Address: via Ordanino 5b, Castiglione delle Stiviere, 46043, Italy
Description En: In the heart of the small town, within a rustic building enriched by refined interiors and an atmosphere that is at once warm and homey, the cooking distinguishes itself through a carefully considered and territorially inspired offering, with one dish that is most certainly worth tasting: the unmissable duck agnolini with their jus and black truffle, an authentic signature of the house.

Name: La Capanna di Eraclio
Address: Località per Le Venezie 21, Codigoro, 44021, Italy
Description En: Whenever we cross the threshold of Capanna di Eraclio, we are embraced by a rare and wonderful feeling, as if we were coming home. Opened in 1922 and now run by the fourth generation of the Soncini family, time seems to have stood still inn this restaurant, which offers the same authenticity that once transformed the inn into a kitchen. The atmosphere is nostalgic and familiar, understated but enhanced with touches of refined elegance. The aromas of the Po delta inspire a repertoire that celebrates water and land: delicate Goro sole, steamed and served with fresh mayonnaise; maltagliati pasta that captures the flavour of clams and savoy cabbage; and the obligatory “arost in umad” eel, golden and succulent, served with white polenta. A unique detail: the dining room is seven metres below sea level, offering guests a truly unique experience.

Name: Le Colonne
Description En: In a dining room with marble columns and flooring and enhanced by a beautiful grand piano, Rossana Marziale serves Mediterranean dishes that showcase the ingredients of Caserta and the Campania with a perfect balance of comforting classic flavours and creative modern ideas. Buffalo mozzarella takes pride of place here, presented in many different ways, including in some of the desserts.

Name: Carne & Spirito
Description En: On the outskirts of the city, meat lovers will find their paradise: the kitchen selects some of the finest breeds from around the world (almost exclusively beef), offered in a variety of cuts and cooked over a Josper charcoal oven: an authentic delight. Cured meats also feature among the starters, alongside fresh pasta and excellent desserts. The wine selection is equally noteworthy, as is the selection by the glass.

Name: San Marco
Description En: This long-established restaurant in the Asti region has been open for over 70 years and is still renowned for its regional cuisine served in a classic-style dining room. Dishes include cardoons with Raschera cheese fondue, the famous agnolottini del plin (a type of ravioli), and the Piedmontese bunet which is part of a trio of desserts that includes hazelnut tart and zabaglione with Canelli muscat wine.

Name: Trattoria del Cimino dal 1895
Description En: Situated on the hill leading to Palazzo Farnese, this restaurant occupies the oldest building in the village, which dates back to 1370. Since 1940, the Calistri family have been delighting their guests with delicious specialities from Lazio, including excellent cured hams, fresh pasta (the amatriciana is particularly renowned), grilled meats and an impressive selection of cheeses and desserts. Excellent wines and spirits complete the picture.

Name: L'Angolo d'Abruzzo
Description En: For almost 40 years, the Angolo d’Abruzzo restaurant has been home to the Centofanti family, who act as excellent ambassadors for the region by offering the best local, seasonal ingredients (for this reason, there’s no fish on the menu) in a host of traditional, regional recipes. Specialities such as cured meats, local ham, bruschetta and fresh home-made pasta (including “chitarra” spaghetti) take centre stage, while main courses include grilled dishes (porcini mushrooms in season, cuts of beef and veal at any time of year) and stews (mutton etc). When it comes to dessert, make sure you try the crème caramel with Navelli saffron. A misleading sign saying “sagrestia” (sacristy) actually indicates the well-stocked wine cellar.

Name: Il Ristorantino - Da Dino
