Address: via XXV Aprile 11, Anzola dell'Emilia, 40011, Italy
Description En: Hidden among the houses, Ristorantino da Dino is a gem with a family feel, loved by locals and discovered by passersby. The menu is broad and varied, featuring sea, land, and garden offerings. Don't miss the Zuppa Inglese – it's a dive into the authentic flavors of the past.

Name: La Locandiera
Description En: At the bottom of a steep valley, a rustic restaurant that offers fine cuisine, much appreciated in the area, with a great preference for local products. Old traditional recipes are revisited with a personal touch.

Name: Bacco
Description En: Nestled within the historic centre, you’ll find classic and charming Apulian stone environments of a fourteenth-century building, while the kitchen sends forth predominantly fish dishes, along with some meat offerings, in classic Italian tradition recipes with a few modern twists.

Name: SottoSopra
Description En: A pleasant and colourful restaurant in the village centre, divided into several dining rooms. The owner-chef prepares a range of eclectic dishes with passion and enthusiasm, offering a menu which includes meat dishes alongside fish options (salt- and freshwater), as well as a few regional specialities.

Name: Madama Vigna
Description En: This restuarant has a good wine list with a focus on local labels, as well as an excellent selection of regional specialities on the menu. Dishes include agnolotti (a type of stuffed pasta) with fondue, Piedmontese beef, Villanova chicken and the inevitable bunet dessert.

Name: Benedikto
Address: via Eremo delle Carceri 1/a, Assisi, 06081, Italy
Description En: On the edge of Assisi’s historic centre, within the refined setting of the Nun hotel, Benedikto offers a selection of classic Umbrian products, but the gastronomic proposal is principally creative and of a high order. In fine weather, dining on the terrace with its view over the Rocca di Assisi takes on a particularly romantic quality.

Name: Acqua Pazza
Description En: Although this restaurant is not in the centre, if you’re looking for excellent fish (mostly from the Mediterranean) personally selected by the owner - chef, then it’s well worth the few minutes it takes to find a parking space here. Beautifully cooked food, which is simply prepared using top - quality produce.

Name: Oltre.
Description En: This restaurant in the lively Mercato delle Erbe district has an entrance adorned with hundreds of stickers, giving it the appearance of a record shop rather than a contemporary-style eatery with a bar counter and a highly original surfboard table near the entrance. The modern cuisine has its roots in the region yet also includes skilfully prepared dishes from around the world (we highly recommend the Bolognese ramen, which includes tagliolino in a mushroom broth, with parmesan, quail eggs marinated in balsamic vinegar, and spinach). There’s also a choice of cocktails to start or round off your meal. Booking is highly recommended.

Name: Sale Grosso
Description En: This restaurant describes its cuisine as Mediterranean and it’s true that fish and seafood dominate the menu. However, other dishes also feature and during our visit we particularly enjoyed the carefully prepared fried artichoke heart accompanied by a fresh white Tuscan Montecarlo wine. Friendly, informal service in a simple dining room with a distinctive bistro feel.

Name: Osteria Al GiGianca
Description En: Although the out - of - town location is a slight drawback, this restaurant passionately run has a welcoming atmosphere. Seasonal, regional cuisine, plus a good choice of wine and beers.

Name: Serpillo
Address: via di Mezzo 1, località Torre del Colle, Bevagna, 06031, Italy
Description En: Situated in a charming medieval village which is also home to a couple of small hotels, this attractive, rustic restaurant in an old olive mill acts as the backdrop for regional and Italian cuisine. Dishes with a touch of modern flavour are presented on a menu which, although not extensive, offers good value for money.

Name: Trattoria Battibecco
Description En: Although it calls itself a trattoria, this restaurant situated in a narrow street in the city centre has an elegant ambience, welcoming guests with friendly service and serving an equal balance of meat and fish dishes. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the foie gras sautéed with Lambrusco blueberries and pan brioche, and the “finché c’è bottarga c’è speranza” (“while there’s bottarga, there’s hope”) spaghetti served with tuna tartare, mullet roe, lime and pistachios.

Name: Osteria dell'Arco
Description En: Enjoy a warm family welcome at this centrally located restaurant with an internal courtyard, where the menu features a good choice of traditional and authentic dishes full of flavour. The restaurant is run by the same friendly managers as the renowned and popular Boccondivino in Bra, where the Slow Food concept was born. Booking ahead is always a good option.

Name: Zest
Description En: Situated within the luxury Grand Hotel La Favorita in the centre of Sorrento, this restaurant has the traditional, opulent style of a grand hotel, while the outdoor terrace boasts the romantic charm that is typical of Sorrento. In the kitchen, the chef creates top-quality cuisine influenced by Campania and enhanced by his own creative touches, resulting in dishes such as marinated tuna with tonka beans, lemon gel and ginger mousse. There’s also a vegetarian tasting menu. A recently opened restaurant that is growing in popularity.

Name: Aubergine
Description En: Situated in a town famous for its thermal baths, this classically elegant restaurant serves meat and fish cuisine including specialities from the Veneto such as Berico ham, bigoli pasta with sardines, and veal liver with onions.

Name: Arca
Address: viale Rinascimento 143, San Benedetto del Tronto, 63074, Italy
Description En: After years of serving fine cuisine in Alba Adriatica, chef Massimiliano Capretta has moved around 15km away to the Hotel Smeraldo. Here, he pays careful attention to the use of organic produce, creating meat and fish dishes that are inspired by local traditions and prepared in a style that is a combination of classic and modern influences. Desserts remain in the capable hands of his sister Dalila, whose millefeuille is one of her standout dishes.

Name: Lalibera
Description En: In the heart of Alba, just a stone's throw from the cathedral, this refined and elegant restaurant offers guests a warm and simple welcome. The aromas of Langhe cuisine combine with the chefs' creativity to deliver dishes that reflect the region's flavours with taste and harmony. The wine list, lovingly curated by Flavia, offers a wide variety of labels, with Piedmontese wines taking centre stage.

Name: Due Pini
Address: via Spinale 37/bis, Madonna di Campiglio, 38086, Italy
Description En: Although recently restored, this restaurant has retained its strong Alpine character. The cuisine is regional in style and reinterpreted with an imaginative and contemporary twist.

Name: Alla Laguna - Vedova Raddi
Description En: Situated in a charming small town criss-crossed by canals, this restaurant serves traditionally inspired fish-based dishes. The restaurant stands on the port facing the fish market, so it’s no surprise that the fish served here is of the freshest quality.

Name: Amanõ
Description En: The tilde accent over the “o” in the name of this restaurant is a subtle allusion to the sea that lies between Campania (the chef’s native region) and Sardinia (his adopted home). With just a few tables and an open-view kitchen, the dining room here is adorned with hand-made decorations, hence the name of the restaurant (“a mano” means “by hand”). The chef makes full use of Sardinian ingredients in his elaborate and creative cuisine, so this is a good choice for anyone seeking a change from traditional fare.

Name: Luminist Cafè Bistrot
Description En: Situated on the ground floor of the splendid Banco di Napoli building that is also home to the Gallerie d'Italia museum, this restaurant also includes a bar and pasticceria. The varied restaurant menu features international dishes (for a quicker meal), fish based around recipes from around the world, alongside more creative dishes and regional specialities from Campania. The latter, from the aubergine parmigiana to the candele pasta served with a Neapolitan ragu, and the popular babà, are truly delicious and showcase all the colours and flavours of Neapolitan cuisine.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Description En: Situated on the fifth floor of the Hotel Bulgari with views of the Mausoleum of Augustus, this restaurant boasts a spacious terrace and an elegant, welcoming dining room with mahogany walls adorned with works of art. To reach the dining room, you pass through the lively bar, where we recommend starting your evening with an aperitif. Once at your table, the menu offers a concrete expression of three-Michelin-star chef Niko Romito’s culinary approach which focuses on lighter, elegant versions of traditional Italian dishes in a sequence of courses that take guests on a culinary tour around Italy. Spaghetti in tomato sauce, artichoke soup, saffron risotto and Piedmontese “bonet” dessert all feature on the menu.

Name: Quintogusto
Address: piazza Sandro Pertini 54 r, Savona, 17100, Italy
Description En: Recently opened in the renovated section of Corso Italia in central Savona, Quintogusto is a small, contemporary and minimalist-style restaurant occupying one side of the former hospital. Here, the owner-chef (once sous-chef at the excellent Michelin-starred Il Vescovado in Noli) cements his reputation with Ligurian-influenced cuisine to which he adds his own modern and imaginative touches.

Name: Forme Restaurant
Description En: Forme Restaurant is a modern, ever-evolving venue located outside the city center within the Atena educational complex, which also houses the Sottoforme bistrot. At the helm is Abruzzese chef Arianna Gatti: her cooking is a contemporary narrative, vivid in color and bold in flavor, rooted in Italian tradition yet reimagined with restraint and sensitivity. Her dishes evoke the comforts of home: the spice-scented ventricina, Navelli saffron butter that gently caresses the palate, and artisanal Abruzzese spaghettone celebrating authentic simplicity.

Name: N'uovo Vino e Cucina
Description En: Nestled in the refined Antico Borgo di Sutri resort, in the heart of the lush Tuscia Viterbese, this restaurant offers an intimate and modern atmosphere, characterised by soft lighting and large windows overlooking the surrounding greenery. The talented young chef Lezzerini offers cuisine inspired by the local area, revisiting traditional regional recipes with modern techniques and using local food excellences. The tasting menu offers various options, from 4 to 8 courses; among the à la carte dishes, we highly recommend the saffron raviolini with marinated young rabbit and a delicious sauce. Also not to be missed is the Carnaroli Riserva San Massimo risotto, served simply but finely, with smoked robiola, wild nettles and celery.

Name: Su Murruai
Address: via Giuseppe Garibaldi 36, Riola Sardo, 09070, Italy
Description En: In a small village overlooking the Sinis Peninsula, the restaurant has been established within an old mill and is dedicated to 'su murruai', Sardinian for the scent of aged Vernaccia. Contemporary Mediterranean cuisine is curated by young chef Ivan Matarese, who seeks quality regional ingredients—from both the mainland and the Gulf of Oristano—to reimagine modern recipes. Additionally, some Campania influences—being the chef's origin—are evident, especially in the desserts, half of which draw inspiration from renowned Campanian sweets (reimagined pastiera and babà).

Name: VeRo - Venetian Roots
Description En: Within the elegant Ca’ di Dio, in the beating heart of the Biennale, VeRo is an exclusive restaurant with contemporary flair. The cuisine reflects the chef’s soul: essential, personal, never predictable. Two tasting journeys, with freedom to choose between dishes and desserts, complete the experience.

Name: Autem*
Description En: The entrance opens onto the open kitchen where the charming chef Luca Natalini welcomes you, and who will also attend to your table with all his Tuscan flair. The selection centers on a limited list of handwritten dishes to accommodate daily arrivals. You dine in the soft lighting of elegantly atmospheric rooms, and the gastronomic experience is of the highest level. Among the most interesting offerings are the plin ravioli filled with duck and tomato seeds, Italian-style sauce and pepper leaf, as well as the grilled milk-fed lamb with bitter herb salad and chanterelles.

Name: Osteria de' Mercati
Description En: Slightly set back from the bustling streets of the historic centre yet still in the heart of the town, this delightful small restaurant is a recent addition to Sassari. It boasts a modern, elegant decor, friendly staff and a menu featuring carefully prepared fresh, seasonal dishes. Our inspector particularly recommends the seafood risotto. A choice of regional wines completes the picture.

Name: Alajmo Cortina
Description En: Situated in the restored premises of the historic El Toulà restaurant, Alajmo Cortina is home to a bar on the ground floor, with the restaurant occupying the two upper floors (no lift). Although traditional in feel with a profusion of wood, the restaurant is run by a young and enthusiastic team. The cuisine focuses mainly on the region, although the menu also features fish and other imaginative options on tasting menus and an à la carte.

Name: Io Osteria Personale
Description En: Well past its tenth year of operation, this contemporary bistrot has by now established itself as a solid point of reference in the San Frediano quarter – and more broadly across the city. The setting, spare yet considered, plays upon exposed beams, brick walls and a handful of wooden tables left deliberately in their natural state, arranged in two rows: a simplicity that is only apparent, behind which is felt a carefully attuned minimal sensitivity. The same attention is to be found in the kitchen, where a creative and personal offering takes shape, moving with balance between meat, fish and vegetarian options. Among the dishes tasted by our Inspector, the ravioli with peas and asparagus, accompanied by a camomile and pollen goat’s cheese foam, are particularly convincing: an original recipe, chromatically elegant and decidedly accomplished.

Name: La Refezione
Description En: An imaginative cuisine for the elegant "club - house" located inside a sports centre; managed by two great enthusiasts of the culinary art. You will receive a hearty welcome.

Name: Ora d'Aria
Description En: Behind the Uffizi, a restaurant that stands out for its originality: not so much for its impressively large open kitchen as for its deliberate desire to encourage direct interaction between guests and the kitchen team. The restaurant’s name reflects its proximity to the historic Florentine prison of Le Murate and its intention to offer customers a moment of genuine relaxation.A small but charming dining room adorned with a ceiling frescoed with gold leaf, houses Marco Stabile’s delightful restaurant, where he serves creative cuisine that is equally accomplished in both meat and fish dishes, all based on top-quality ingredients.

Name: La Filanda
Description En: Situated in the heart of the historic centre, this restaurant occupies an old spinning mill ("filanda") that has been completely restored without losing any of its original charm. Here, self-taught chef Barbara serves traditional dishes reinterpreted with real flair, such as the involtino di ciaffagnone filled with Maremma beef on a bed of melted pecorino cheese and crispy leek. The chef’s husband oversees the wine list, which includes a selection of Tuscan labels.

Name: Il Trillo
Description En: On the hills overlooking the town, an ancient residence transformed into a refined hospitality venue – and today home also to the estate’s own winery – receives its guests in surroundings of considerable elegance. A charm that reaches its apogee in the warmer months, when dinner is served in the evocative limonaia: a romantic panoramic terrace bathed in soft light and surrounded by lemon, orange, bergamot and mandarin trees. The kitchen engages in a dialogue with the territory, weaving together ingredients from sea and land along classical lines enriched by touches of imagination and careful presentation. Among the dishes that drew particular appreciation from our Inspector, the tortellini filled with pear and pecorino in a saffron and pistachio sauce, and the duck breast with mandarin accompanied by a celeriac tartlet.

Name: Stefano Paganini alla Corte degli Alfieri
Description En: Within the walls of Castello di Magliano Alfieri – a place suspended in time, with a magnificent frescoed hall and soaring ceilings overlooking the hills of Langhe and Roero – chef Paganini’s cuisine takes shape, deftly balancing local tradition and innovation. Two main offerings are available: the traditional menu, “Viaggio in Piemonte (Journey Through Piedmont),” and the “A Occhi Chiusi (Eyes Closed)” menu, customizable in three, four, or five courses according to guests’ preferences. It is in this latter menu that the chef gives full rein to his creativity, crafting bespoke dishes and personalized interpretations designed to make every experience unique.

Name: Osteria Boccolicchio
Description En: Having gained experience in various restaurants throughout Europe, Tespi has now returned home to open this delightful small osteria in the historic centre, just a stone’s throw from the sea. His huge passion for fish is evident from the menu, where fish dishes feature in numerous regionally influenced recipes. The excellent wine cellar includes a good choice of sparkling wines.

Name: Voltalacarta
Description En: A tiny doorway leads to this simple, friendly and intimate restaurant with just a few tables, where booking in advance is highly recommended given the restaurant’s excellent reputation in the city. Its renown stems from the owner-chef’s cuisine, which focuses mainly on top-quality fish prepared in imaginative and personalised recipes using classic techniques. If it’s on the menu, make sure you try the “cappon magro” (a type of seafood salad), which is so good that it even has its own identity card!

Name: Locanda del Falco
Address: Castello di Rivalta 4, Rivalta Trebbia, 29010, Italy
Description En: In the heart of a medieval village, an inn of authentic charm welcomes guests with the captivating aromas of Piacenza cuisine and imaginative creations that surprise the palate, accompanied by local wines and distinguished labels from beyond the region. Heritage dishes speak of time-honored flavors, revisited with modern touches, while the inspector’s favorite remains the grilled cardoncelli mushrooms: intense aroma and pure taste. In the dining room, Sabrina radiates energy and smiles, presenting each dish with infectious passion. On winter evenings, crackling fireplaces warm the atmosphere; in summer, a centuries-old wisteria drapes the courtyard tables in fragrant, romantic shade.

Name: Toe Drûe
Address: via Corsi 44 r, Sestri Ponente, 16154, Italy
Description En: Opened at the beginning of the 20th century to feed shipyard workers, this historic establishment still retains the authentic flavour of its origins. The name “Toe Drue”, which means “thick tables”, refers to the sturdy tables of the old inn. Today, the restaurant continues to celebrate Genoese tradition in an informal and welcoming atmosphere, with iconic dishes such as “cappon magro”, stockfish and other Ligurian specialities that tell a story of sincere and timeless cuisine.

Name: La Pineta
Address: via Gualco 82, località Struppa, Genoa, 16165, Italy
Description En: Now a gastronomic institution in the city, in a secluded setting immersed in nature, La Pineta occupies the ground floor of a nondescript building in which the simple, “dated” yet comfortable decor provides the backdrop. Although there is a menu (but no wine list), the dishes are usually announced in person at your table by the owners. Simple, traditional and abundant cuisine which is mainly cooked on the open grill in the centre of the room, including meat (its signature speciality) and fish.

Name: La Gallina
Description En: Villa Sparina is an elegant rural resort named after its winery. The Orangerie hosts guests, whereas fine dining unfolds at La Gallina restaurant: amid rustic and elegant settings, contemporary cuisine is presented, drawing ample inspiration from Piedmont, as well as nearby Liguria (the dessert "Good Morning Genoa" playfully mimics breakfast with cappuccino and focaccia), though Campania references, the chef's homeland, never falter. Personalised wine selection: exclusively Champagne, abundant Piedmont choices, with particular emphasis on Barbaresco and Barolo.

Name: La Leggenda dei Frati
Description En: After an uphill approach if you’re arriving here on foot, you come into the Villa Bardini museum complex and from there into this elegant and welcoming restaurant which provides the setting for delicious, creative and modern cuisine. Here, chef Filippo Saporito, never one to rest on his laurels, continues to experiment and perfect his cuisine, which focuses mainly on Italian culinary traditions and a scrupulous selection of top-quality ingredients, preferably from sustainable supply chains (various types of meat, bread and pasta), all showcased on different menus, including a vegetarian option. In summer, enjoy your meal on the romantic terrace surrounded by greenery and the scents of herbs, with a glimpse of Santa Croce church as a backdrop. Although the centre of Florence is not far away, it seems as though you’re already in the Tuscan hills, even with the occasional sound of cicadas in the background.

Name: Posillipo
Description En: Boasting a superb location above Gabicce Monte, this excellent restaurant run by the third generation of the same family offers breathtaking views of the Romagna coast. Posillipo’s superb fish dishes have made the restaurant a must in the region, with options ranging from raw fish to traditional pasta specialities and delicious main courses (fish fillets, catch of the day, fried options etc). There’s also a tempting dessert trolley and an excellent wine list.

Name: Da Bibe
Description En: At the gates of Florence, at the precise point where the city dissolves into the green of the countryside, Bibe welcomes guests beneath the leafy canopy of its summer terrace and within the warm interiors of a trattoria safeguarding over one hundred and fifty years of history, now in the hands of the sixth generation. Here, Tuscan cuisine remains the absolute protagonist: artisanal cured meats, traditional crostini, pici al ragù, and iconic dishes such as beef peposo. Not to be missed are the fried or grilled chicken and, for devotees, a fiorentina that interprets the classic canons in the most authentic manner.

Name: Trattoria del Vicolo
Description En: Overlooking the piazza for almost 50 years, this restaurant has been modernised but has nonetheless managed to retain its friendly ambience, especially in the outdoor space facing the narrow alleyway. The owner-chef serves regional specialities reinterpreted with his own individual twist, such as his famous swordfish rolls served in a type of pie.

Name: La Kuccagna
Address: via Milano 14, località Barbuzzera, Dovera, 26010, Italy
Description En: La Kuccagna's fresh, quality offerings are bolstered by management that is always full of energy; menus range between land (tripe with legumes, squash and mushrooms) and sea (amberjack with coconut sauce, sea urchin and herbs), while the grill is always ready to accommodate the most suitable cuts of meat. A fine selection of wines starting with labels from beyond the Alps. The location is exquisitely bucolic, while the interior is modern and comfortable.

Name: Sapereta
Address: via Provinciale Ovest 73, località Mola, Porto Azzurro, 57036, Italy
Description En: A working farm (producing wine and olive oil) that features charming interiors, though the real highlight is outdoor dining beneath a pergola draped with fragola grapes, overlooking a meadow. The menu features both meat and seafood, rooted in Tuscan tradition but often elevated with creative flair.

Name: Castel Toblino
Address: località Castel Toblino 1, Castel Toblino, 38076, Italy
Description En: Situated in a bucolic location in the Trentino where the excellent Vino Santo is produced (we recommend rounding off your meal with a glass of the equally superb grappa), this restaurant and adjacent bar occupy a fascinating medieval castle (tours of which can be arranged) jutting out into the lake of the same name. The generous, modern meat and fish dishes are featured on various tasting menus, along with an extensive à la carte. In summer, make sure you book a table on the charming terrace overlooking the lake.

Name: Da Poli alla Stazione
Address: viale della Repubblica 10, Castelnovo di Sotto, 42024, Italy
Description En: In the centre of a town known for its carnival and many allegorical floats, this family-run restaurant housed in an old railway station dating from the early 20C serves traditional regional dishes. The house speciality is charcoal-grilled cuisine, with an equal emphasis on meat and fish options.

Name: Locanda del Feudo
Address: via Trasversale 2, Castelvetro di Modena, 41014, Italy
Description En: In the upper and most ancient part of the picturesque village, this romantic retreat – which also offers six elegant suites – offers genuine and deeply satisfying cooking. The menu is split between dishes from the land, with numerous recipes that evoke the Emilian tradition, such as hand-rolled tagliatelle with ragù, tortelli in capon broth, or a selection of the finest local cured meats, and seafood offerings distinguished by a modern and lighter touch. In the warmer months, guests may take their place on the small and charming terrace overlooking the main street, ideally suited to savouring the village in its most relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Agorà
Description En: Michele Rizzo is the owner-chef of this interesting restaurant situated in a modern part of Rende. His menu focuses mainly on fish (although a few meat dishes are also available) which he prepares in light, modern dishes with an emphasis on local ingredients. There’s also an interesting wine list.

Name: Rosso di Sera
Address: via Pietro Nenni 2, Castelletto sopra Ticino, 28053, Italy
Description En: Situated closed to the motorway exit, this restaurant’s rustic exterior belies its young, colourful and contemporary interior. The dishes are as modern as the decor, yet they have their roots in strong local traditions. The owner has a real passion for French and sparkling wines, including around 160 different champagnes and a wide selection of Burgundies, plus a good choice of wines by the glass, craft beers and cocktails.

Name: Da Noemi
Description En: The mother of the current owner opened this busy restaurant in a medieval alleyway in the historic centre, giving it her own name. The historic dishes here reflect the culinary traditions of Ferrara, with specialities such as salama da sugo (pork sausage) and pasticcio di maccheroni (a baked pasta dish) on the menu. A must for anyone looking to sample local dishes already famous during the time of the Este family.

Name: Punta Lena
Address: via Monsignor Di Mattina 8, località Ficogrande, Stromboli, 98055, Italy
Description En: At this restaurant, dine under a pergola with superb views of the sea and Strombolicchio – the perfect setting for any occasion. The menu focuses on fish, including raw and dry-aged fish options. The first courses have a local flavour and are particularly delicious.

Name: Feva
Description En: Situated in the historic centre of Castelfranco Veneto, this restaurant has an intimate, elegant and contemporary-cum-minimalist feel despite its period courtyard setting and original wooden beams in the first-floor dining room. Nicola Dinato’s cuisine is showcased on two tasting menus, namely Anima and Corpo. The former offers a selection of new dishes created by the chef, who is constantly updating his cuisine, while the latter features his historic signature specialities (don’t miss the scampi “busara” risotto). A lighter, less expensive menu is also available at lunchtime. The wine list includes an interesting selection of French labels, as well as some superb Italian wines, such as the 1999 Case Basse Soldera Brunello di Montalcino.

Name: Casa D'Angelo
Address: via San Nicola 5, Fara Filiorum Petri, 66010, Italy
Description En: Housed in what was once an old family home, this elegant restaurant serves delicious regional cuisine. The menu includes dishes that have been skilfully and imaginatively enhanced by the chef, such as warm pheasant terrine with apple, alongside more traditional fare, from cured ham to charcoal-grilled local lamb and potato gnocchi with a duck sauce. The restaurant’s own extra-virgin olive oil often adds further flavour to the dishes. The 4-course tasting menu deserves a special mention for its excellent value for money.

Name: Antico Ristorante Pagnanelli
Description En: In business since 1882, yet constantly evolving, this restaurant boasts a superb location overlooking the lake. The menu features meat and fish dishes, enhanced by wild herbs. The extensive wine selection is presented on two wine lists. Don’t miss the famous wine cellars built into the rock, plus the small wine museum.

Name: Leone Felice
Description En: The new chef at this restaurant focuses on highlighting produce grown in the property’s own kitchen garden, as well as meat from the farm in the Grosseto area that is also run by the Andana estate. The classic-style cuisine on the à la carte features occasional personalised touches (for example, aubergines baked in fig leaf with oregano, and perch or sea bass fillet served with coloured beets and soft potato), while in the evening a tasting menu is served in a dedicated part of the restaurant. The expertly explained wine list focuses on the estate’s own labels and the Franciacorta region in general, yet at the same time includes a selection of wines from elsewhere in Italy and further afield.

Name: El Gato
Description En: Chioggia is famous as one of the more active fishing ports in the region and this restaurant takes full of advantage of the local catch. Situated on the central promenade of this picturesque town, the restaurant serves fish of truly exceptional quality served in traditional recipes from the Adriatic.

Name: Locanda dei Salinari
Description En: In the old village of Salinari, a young enterprising chef runs this simple restaurant. His creative cuisine is prepared with the best regional produce of Romagna.

Name: Miil
Description En: Housed in a converted 15C mill on the Kränzelhof wine estate, this smart, elegant restaurant provides the backdrop for excellent, contemporary-style cuisine prepared wherever possible using locally sourced (and always top-quality) ingredients.

Name: Pinocchio
Description En: This reliable restaurant is well run by a highly professional and experienced family. In the classic-style dining room, where the decor eschews fashionable trends, enjoy typical Piedmontese cuisine lightened by the occasional modern twist. The restaurant’s contemporary version of “paniscia” is a good example – a type of risotto with beans, salami and vegetables, in which the latter, instead of being cooked directly with the rice, are added on top of the mixture in the form of vegetable cream, giving the dish an attractive splash of colour. The menu always features a few fish-based recipes, including both salt- and freshwater species.

Name: Magiargè Osteria Contemporanea
Description En: The dining rooms in this lively, typical restaurant in the upper, historic part of Bordighera appear to be almost dug out of the rock. Here, a local chef with plenty of experience behind him creates predominantly Ligurian cuisine (and not just fish and seafood), accompanied by an excellent and extensive wine list, including labels from outside Italy and a good selection of champagnes. Attentive service completes the picture here.

Name: Romolo Mare
Description En: Situated in a private beach club facing the sea, this restaurant combines a relaxed atmosphere with an elegant feel thanks to its professional owners who have worked as restaurateurs for many years. Here, they serve excellent fish and seafood cuisine with a focus on raw dishes, plus a choice of daily fish specials. A selection of interesting local wines completes the picture.

Name: Alla Fassa
Address: via Nascimbeni 11, Castelletto di Brenzone, 37010, Italy
Description En: Although the beautiful views of the lake (with only a cycle path between the restaurant and the water) and mountains on the opposite shore can be admired from the dining room, in fine weather it’s a race for the outdoor tables just a few metres from the water. The cuisine is as impressive as the setting, with a fine balance of classic and modern dishes featuring fish from the lake (such as the “il lago in un piatto” – the lake in a dish – starter) and the sea. A few guestrooms with views of the lake are also available.

Name: Residenza del Lago
Description En: The name pays tribute to Lake Candia, and we are in a mid-18th century farmhouse which is located within the town. You will find a pleasantly regional, family atmosphere and the restaurant’s traditional cuisine includes popular dishes such as onion cooked three different ways with a faux “bagna caoda” sauce and smoked ricotta.

Name: Locanda Alpina
Description En: Along the enchanting Val di Non, amid rows of apple orchards and the silhouettes of ancient castles, this building of nineteenth-century origin is home to a dependable family-run establishment, in operation for nearly a century, since 1933 to be precise. The cooking interprets the flavours of the territory with quiet competence, drawing out its seasonal excellences – such as white asparagus and venison preparations – while not shying away from occasional forays into broader national influences. Emblematic in this regard is the excellent pistachio ice cream, singled out by our Inspectors as not to be missed.

Name: Enoteca di Canelli - Casa Crippa
Description En: Occupying a late-19C palazzo, in what was a historic wine cellar right up to the late 1960s, this family-run restaurant serves carefully presented, regional cuisine with a lightly creative and contemporary twist. A good example is the “carne cruda alla monferrina” (a kind of beef tartare) served with a Parmesan cream and hazelnuts.

Name: Nido del Picchio
Description En: This restaurant with a low-key, hushed atmosphere has the feel of a tastefully furnished private home, with an open fire to warm cold winter evenings while a cool, welcoming outdoor terrace becomes the ideal spot for al fresco dining in summer. The dining experience comprises four tasting menus and an extensive à la carte menu, offering a generous variety of dishes designed to delight every palate. The recipes range naturally between meat, fish and vegetarian options, offering a wide and well-balanced array of flavours. The desserts are all well worth trying and our favourites include Tribute to Gauguin, a tonka bean blancmange with passion fruit, mango, papaya and coconut ice cream for an exotic and refined finish. The chef’s wife, Lucy, manages the dining room service with the utmost courtesy and professionalism, contributing to a thoroughly enjoyable overall experience. The wine cellar is home to more than 700 of finest best Italian and international wines, with a curious and interesting emphasis on labels from cooler climes.

Name: Antica Locanda
Address: piazza della Seta, località San Leucio, Caserta, 81100, Italy
Description En: This establishment is practically a trattoria; one can dine in either of two characteristic rooms separated by a brick archway. The cuisine is typical of the Naples area and rice dishes are the specialty.

Name: Mistral
Description En: Situated at the tip of Bellagio’s promontory where the two branches of the lake meet, this villa occupies a superb panoramic location, with its restaurant housed in a covered veranda boasting delightful views of the opposite shore, its little villages and exclusive residences. The atmosphere here is reminiscent of a grand hotel, with background piano music in the evening and guests from all around the world. The moderately creative cuisine offers a choice of Italian dishes alongside more international options.

Name: Da Giovanni
Description En: The 18C ceramic stove, bright, colourful decor (both period and vintage), long family tradition and excellent cuisine all contribute to making this restaurant which opened half a century ago a bastion of fine cuisine in Piacenza and the wider Po valley. Meat and fish both feature on the menu, although it is the latter that has become renowned as the restaurant’s speciality over the years. The excellent service is friendly and informal yet highly professional, while the extensive wine list also includes a good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Pernambucco
Description En: This restaurant boasts a garden setting with a pleasant outdoor dining space, plus a long, narrow interior decorated in decidedly classic style. Fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, with a focus on local fish, including excellent tartare (usually either seabream or tuna, depending on the catch of the day) and shellfish (cooked in salt, baked or grilled). The vegetables are sourced from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden.

Name: Collina
Address: via Ca' Paler 5, Almenno San Bartolomeo, 24030, Italy
Description En: A family style trattoria has now been converted into these modern premises that, while jealously upholding their homely origin, offer dishes of contemporary inspiration. One small dining hall has an open fireplace and the other gives a panoramic view.

Name: Le Cicale
Description En: A grandparents’ home has evolved into a charming bistro-like restaurant, while outdoors, the owner-curated garden beckons a peek. The cuisine is simple and classic, comforting, with certain regional dishes alongside fish courses, while an entire menu page is dedicated to risottos.

Name: Bis Osteria Italiana Contemporanea
Address: Via 20 Settembre 50, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
Description En: In the glorious premises of the old Arnolfo restaurant in the old town, this restaurant is run by the same management as previously, although with a new young chef at the helm in the kitchen. The delicious yet concise menu features “Italian specialities” (the name given to all the main courses) with a focus on meat and fish, accompanied by excellent bread options (you can even order “scarpetta” dipping bread for mopping up the remains of a Cinta Senese pork sauce). The house speciality is a delicious pigeon dish. In fine weather, guests can dine on the beautiful, tranquil terrace.

Name: Locanda La Posta
Description En: A traditional setting reflecting the style of the early 20th century, with photos and documents telling the restaurant’s story, and numerous small dining rooms characterised by wooden ceilings. The restaurant’s traditional-style cuisine features excellent home-made pastas and a typical boiled meat trolley (“carrello dei bolliti”). One of the signature dishes here is rabbit stew served with a generous portion of Carmagnola peppers. In the summer, guests can sit in a welcoming outdoor area adorned with green plants and flowers.

Name: U' Vulesce
Description En: Born as a delicatessen over sixty years ago, and now enhanced by an offering of aperitifs accompanied by small plates, the Di Donna family has created a solid and well-structured restaurant dedicated to the finest products of this generous region. Spanning land and sea, cured meats and cheeses, it is above all patron Rosario who guides guests through their choices, enhancing each proposal with a carefully curated wine selection.

Name: Scola
Description En: Situated in the heart of the Ligurian hinterland, this country house is a real gem, surrounded by a garden that resembles a painting with an English-style lawn that ripples in the wind. Since 1926, the Scola family, now in the fourth generation, have offered guests a friendly welcome here, serving cuisine that is a delight for the tastebuds. In the warm dining room, where the wooden floor and exposed beams hint at the building’s history, guests enjoy traditional local dishes that have been reinterpreted with a modern twist, such as spaghetti with grapefruit, purple prawns and sea lettuce – an explosion of flavours!

Name: Al Camin
Description En: On the road to Misurina lake, this friendly restaurant with a modern Alpine style offers dishes of the regional tradition with imaginative touches and modern technique. So a great deal of practicality, then, as in the beef tenderloin wrapped in speck dry-cured pork with cep mushrooms and Ampezzo-style potatoes. The chef and sommelier Fabio Pompanin manages a wine list with approximately 200 labels. In the warmer season, take advantage of the open-air service.

Name: Malenco
Address: via Funivia 22, Chiesa in Valmalenco, 23023, Italy
Description En: This typical family-run restaurant serves typical mountain cuisine, although a few fish dishes also feature on the menu. Highlights include game, cheese and the delicious homemade pizzoccheri pasta. Ask the young son for recommendations from the wine list, which includes labels from Valtellina.

Name: La Lumira
Description En: In a town synonymous with tortellini, Lumira offers an authentically regional experience with a touch of modernity; contemporary interiors and warm service ensure a memorable visit. The menu draws on the generosity of Emilian and Romagnolo cuisines, a natural expression of the chef-owner, born right here. The house-made fresh pastas are essential: from tortellini in capon broth to pumpkin tortelli dressed with garlic, olive oil, chili, and broccoli. Special praise goes to the bollito misto, served with excellently crafted sauces.

Name: San Quintino Resort
Description En: Once you have crossed the plain and climbed up into the San Quintino hills, you come to this restored farmhouse surrounded by an attractive garden. The restaurant is divided into a brick - walled dining room and a winter garden, while the charming guestrooms make this a romantic place to stay. Creative dishes with a focus on local ingredients and a few fish specialities feature on the menu.

Name: Miseria e Nobiltà
Description En: The name of this restaurant occupying a late-18C palazzo with attractive flooring and Murano glass chandeliers alludes to the peasant traditions that influence its cuisine (miseria) and the creative, elegant dishes served here (nobiltà). The menu features excellent home-made pastas, vegetables and meat dishes, including boned rabbit with leeks and Annurca apples and white and black truffles from the Molise in season.

Name: Luigi Pomata
Description En: This famous classic restaurant in Cagliari serves top-quality cuisine in its modern dining rooms and on an outdoor terrace. The menu features interesting reinterpretations of Sardinian dishes among other options, including their own tuna (the house speciality), which is also available in tins to take away.

Name: Osteria Casale Ferrovia
Address: via Stazione 1, sulla SP 34, Carovigno, 72012, Italy
Description En: Housed in what was once the 20C dwelling of an old olive mill, this restaurant boasts elegant decor, including a few antique family pieces and Art Deco - style tables. The female owner - chef prepares light and modern dishes with a regional flavour, while the wine list also showcases the best of Puglia. As the name suggests, the railway lies to the rear of the property, although there’s very little noise and no disturbance at all.

Name: Da Tonino
Description En: The chef at this restaurant serves decidedly contemporary cuisine with its roots in traditional recipes. His creative flair results in modern dishes in which each detail is carefully curated, with bold combinations that come as a surprise yet always feature a perfect balance of flavours and textures. The restaurant, situated in a quiet residential area away from the hustle and bustle of the small town, is the perfect choice for anyone looking for a relaxed and yet elegant dining experience.

Name: Il Barolino
Description En: The Emilian authenticity of the Barolo brothers and their team fills the air with smiles and warmth, making every visit to this simple and welcoming restaurant a pleasure, the perfect place to enjoy the company of friends or colleagues. The menu is steeped in tradition: it is impossible to resist their pasta dishes, such as the creamy and satisfying “gramigna sporcafaccia” or tortellini covered in a velvety smooth Parmesan cream sauce. Desserts include a crunchy “sbrisolona” cake served with zabaglione made with passito wine, while the “zuppa inglese” trifle releases deliciously smooth notes to end the meal on a sweet note.

Name: Ginevra
Address: Rupi di via XXIX Settembre 12, Ancona, 60122, Italy
Description En: Situated on the fourth floor of the Seeport hotel, this restaurant boasts a summer roof garden offering stunning sea views. The chef, a native of Ancona who trained with Gualtiero Marchesi, serves traditional local dishes prepared using ingredients from the region, as well as remaining open to the rest of the world (just like his town and its port). Lighter fare is available at the Seeport Bistrò.

Name: Cravero - Osteria Contemporanea
Description En: Warm colours such as teal and ochre give this restaurant a cosy and welcoming ambience. The cuisine here is authentic and traditional in style, with dishes based on top-quality local ingredients accompanied by a choice of regional wines. There’s also an outdoor area for summer dining.

Name: Antica Cucina 1983
Description En: Overlooking a square in the city centre, customers are welcomed into elegant surroundings, where almost exclusively fish dishes are served, in classic and tasty preparations, without too many complications to enhance the catch.

Name: La Filanda
Description En: Housed on the first floor of an old silkworm factory, with a contemporary-style dining room that opens out on to a beautiful terrace in fine weather, this restaurant is one of the few in the province to serve top-quality fish and seafood, including a good selection of raw options. The cooked dishes on offer demonstrate a light modern touch and are prepared whenever possible using vegetables from the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: Caffè Meletti
Address: via del Trivio 56 (piazza del Popolo), Ascoli Piceno, 63100, Italy
Description En: Housed on the first floor of the historic café where the aniseed liqueur of the same name was created, this restaurant serves simple yet creative, regional and maritime - inspired cuisine. Don’t miss the terrace with views of Piazza del Popolo. Faster options available at lunchtime.

Name: Locanda Baggio
Address: via Bassane 1, località Casonetto, Asolo, 31011, Italy
Description En: A warm and welcoming dining room, together with professional yet pleasantly friendly and informal service, provide the perfect complement to the extraordinary cuisine: hearty, full of flavour, unsullied by unnecessary artifice. The pasta tubes with a rich sauce of baby cuttlefish, dried seaweed and sea urchins are unforgettable, as is the grilled fish with a sauce made from clams, leeks and seaweed oil.

Name: Duomo
Description En: Bright and inviting is the dining room of this small resource aspiring towards contemporary culinary offerings—grounded in seasonal products—and numerous homemade preparations. The two siblings at the helm also unveil intriguing regional recipes with apt personal touches. For the wine lovers, an appropriate label awaits every need, whilst the setting further enhances the enjoyment: located in the town’s alleyways, just steps from the Cathedral.

Name: Opera|02
Description En: An oasis of taste to the east of Modena: here, the farm estate, also known for its production of balsamic vinegar, welcomes guests with rooms, a small spa and a restaurant immersed in the quiet of the countryside. The cooking tells the story of the Modenese territory through recipes that showcase local ingredients, alternating dishes faithful to tradition – such as tortelli in capon broth or the indulgent zuppa inglese – with others in which the chef allows himself greater creative freedom. The result is an honest yet carefully crafted offering, capable of uniting gastronomic memory with more personal interpretations, always in keeping with the seasons.

Name: Laurin
Description En: In the magnificent setting of the exclusive Parkhotel Laurin, this restaurant is one of the best in Bolzano, boasting a Liberty-style dining room and tree-shaded tables in the garden for summer dining. The traditional cuisine also includes a few modern touches with ingredients and techniques from all over Italy and beyond, such as the grilled trout and leek terrine wrapped in nori algae in the shape of a flower. The menu features meat and fish dishes, with a small section dedicated to traditional local specialities.

Name: Baita Fraina
Description En: Warm little bar rooms, reminiscent of the German wine bars or "Stube", a summer terrace and well - prepared regional dishes: for those who want to escape the mundane life of Cortina for the silence of an isolated "baita" [mountain hut]. Delightful rooms, colourfully furnished in warm tones so you can better enjoy the silence and scents of the mountains.

Name: Sa Cardiga e Su Schironi
Address: strada statale 195 rotonda per Capoterra, Capoterra, 09012, Italy
Description En: Since 1967, this small restaurant has been delighting locals and visitors alike with its vast array of fish and seafood dishes, including grilled and skewered specialities. The fresh fish display cabinet at the restaurant entrance is one of the highlights here, as is the extensive selection of antipasti which includes tuna and mullet bottarga, “agliata alla bosana” (blue shark with tomatoes in a light sweet and sour sauce) and “burrida alla cagliaritana” (with dogfish). Other dishes include fresh and pasta with various seafood sauces, fried fish, soup, lobster, barbecued fish and even eel.

Name: Fiamma Cremisi
Address: via De Gasperi 37, località Viadana, Calvisano, 25012, Italy
Description En: Italian cuisine that strikes a balance on several fronts: while the chef’s dishes include nods to Brescia’s culinary tradition, they are also enlivened with creative touches. In summer, service extends outdoors beneath a gazebo; in the colder months, the main dining room is warmed by a fireplace. At lunchtime the menu is shorter, more affordable, and there is a business menu.

Name: I 5 Campanili
Address: via Luigi Maino 18, Busto Arsizio, 21052, Italy
Description En: Contemporary cooking with an emphasis on Mediterranean fare in tune with the seasons is to the fore in this elegant restaurant occupying a 20C building with an attractive veranda to the rear. Fish takes pride of place on the menu, with a particular focus on raw dishes and shellfish, but the splendid desserts are also worthy of note, such as cherries in sour cherry juice with fior di latte ice cream.

Name: Marsupino 1901
Description En: Once the village bakery and now a landmark for those in search of authentic cooking, the trattoria Marsupino 1901 tells a family story spanning four generations. Here, tradition remains the anchor: solid, reassuring and sincere cuisine, yet capable of revisiting familiar flavours with contemporary sensitivity and a measured hand. Emblematic of this approach is the hazelnut semifreddo with Marsala zabaglione cooked in a bain-marie, an indulgent, beautifully judged dessert that brings the meal to an elegant close. In the dining room, the welcome finds its ideal interpreter in Luca: professional, warm and animated by a genuine passion for wine, he accompanies guests with competence and ease. His carefully chosen selection of labels, and his ability to describe them with clarity and engagement, enrich the experience, transforming the gastronomic journey into a harmonious voyage through memory, territory and conviviality.

Name: Vitis
Description En: A modern wine bar in the centre of Bressanone (Brixen), situated in the same building as the delightful family restaurant, the Oste Scuro. Here, small armchairs, benches and stools are dotted among low square tables and higher tables, all surrounded by walls completely lined with wine bottles. The contemporary cuisine features tempting, generous dishes such as cod with cauliflower, cavolo nero and beurre blanc. Accommodation is available just two minutes’ away in the historic Adler Historic Guesthouse run by the same owners.

Name: Elephant
Description En: Situated in the famous Elephant hotel (with which it shares a name), this restaurant has a unique, historic ambience thanks to its decor of antique wood panelling. The cuisine here is regional with a modern twist, featuring dishes such as char with cream of celery and green apple on a bed of fragrant elderflowers. The interesting wine list boasts a selection of almost a thousand different labels.

Name: Castello Malvezzi
Address: via Colle San Giuseppe 1, Brescia, 25133, Italy
Description En: This elegant 16C hunting lodge offers a modern menu of fish dishes and regional specialities. Particular attention is paid to the excellent Calvisano caviar, with a dedicated menu. There’s an attractive outdoor dining area facing the gardens with views of the city of Brescia.

Name: Osteria da Nando
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Traditional Cuisine
Description En: Operating since 1957 in the heart of the historic center, Nando is a go-to spot for those wanting to experience Valdostan cuisine: excellent cured meats (usually served with the famous fontina), polenta and fondue, fondue bourguignonne, rustic polenta tart with goat milk gelato... all prepared with top-quality ingredients and served in a simple yet atmospheric setting. The wine selection is excellent, focusing mainly on the Aosta Valley, with over 100 different labels, many of which are available by the glass. Among the desserts, the rothia is a must-try: white wine custard, spiced bread, and a sprinkle of cinnamon – intense, rich, and delicious.

Name: Il Riccio
Description En: Situated just a few metres from the Blue Grotto and perched right above the water, Il Riccio is the quintessential Mediterranean fine-dining restaurant thanks to its tasteful and elegant decor. Undoubtedly one of Capri’s iconic addresses, it focuses uniquely on fish and seafood dishes. Whether you have a sweet tooth or not, a visit to the tempting dessert buffet to admire its array of delicacies is a must!

Name: Momento al 25
Description En: A late 19th century building houses this simple but welcoming restaurant, which moves its service outdoors during the summer months, creating a pleasant and informal atmosphere. The menu alternates traditional local specialities with Italian dishes, featuring a significant selection of seafood options. Raw seafood is always on the menu: served plain or in slightly more elaborate versions, it is one of the most popular choices among diners.

Name: Tosca
Description En: Set within the ancient Castello di Casole, Tosca establishes itself as a venue of great character, where warm and refined atmospheres take shape among exposed stone, sumptuous fabrics, and elegantly crafted furnishings. In the kitchen, the tasting menus reinterpret the Mediterranean tradition with a contemporary sensitivity, celebrating the seasonality and quality of the ingredients. Complementing this vision is the Territori project, which expresses a deep connection with the property’s agricultural surroundings: the Orti del Castello kitchen gardens, expanded with fruit trees and plants, nourish a cuisine ever more rooted in the land and in the concept of local sourcing. All of this unfolds within an estate of 1,300 hectares certified organic, where the farm-to-table approach finds its most authentic expression. In the warmer months, service moves to the open courtyard, offering an immersive experience in direct communion with the landscape.

Name: Il Credenziere
Address: via Quattro Strade 12, Annone Veneto, 30020, Italy
Description En: Situated in a small country hamlet, this restaurant is run by a chef from Puglia, whose origins can be glimpsed here and there in his dishes. The influence of the Veneto, where the chef has been working for some time, is also evident in the local dishes which appear alongside more creative options on the menu.

Name: Le Chiavi d'Oro
Description En: Situated in Arezzo’s historic centre, this restaurant boasts an original, minimalist ambience with an elegant wood decor. The main focus here is on the cuisine, which is among the best not only in the city but also in the region. Skilful interpretations of traditional dishes, with a focus on Tuscany, where the gastronomic pleasure increases with each course.

Name: Ca' 7
Address: via Cunizza da Romano 4, Bassano del Grappa, 36061, Italy
Description En: Housed in a charming 18C villa, this elegant restaurant overlooks its attractive garden in a magical setting which is typical of the Veneto. The cuisine also has a regional focus, with classic recipes featuring on the menu alongside more creative dishes (fish appears more often than meat).

Name: A' Paranza
Description En: For more than 30 years, this restaurant run by the Proto brothers has been a popular choice for visitors to the beautiful Atrani valley. Simple cuisine served in a simple and informal setting (dishes are nearly always announced at your table rather than listed on a menu), with a focus on Mediterranean and Campanian dishes.

Name: Regallo
Description En: An excellent restaurant situated less than five minutes from the town centre, Regallo has a contemporary decor with features that recall its former function as a factory. At the helm in the kitchen, skilful chef Claudio Ravinetto prepares dishes with an exclusive focus on fish, including interesting options such as cuttlefish tagliatelle with cream and diced winter roots such as celeriac, served at the table with an excellent hot vegetable broth.

Name: Rifugio Col Alt
Address: Stazione monte cabinovia col alto, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description En: During the day this restaurant can be reached in just a few minutes by cable car, providing you with breathtaking views of the Dolomites, while in the evening (when the service is more attentive – things are faster paced at lunchtime) you have to arrange transport via snowcat. The name “refuge” refers only to the location as the cuisine is definitely that of a restaurant: although the menu features hearty mountain fare, it also includes modern options and a few fish-based recipes, including oysters. Last but not least, there’s a good selection of wines.

Name: Lio Pellegrini
Description En: Despite its location in the town centre, the attractive outdoor terrace of this restaurant offers a peaceful atmosphere with its decor of light drapes. The red - coloured dining room makes a pleasant backdrop for the modern, Mediterranean cuisine served here. Elegant ambience.

Name: Posta
Description En: A corner of Tuscany in Bologna, where famous soups such as ribollita and pappa col pomodoro are followed by pappardelle pasta with wild boar, tripe, beef pepper stew and, of course, Fiorentina steak, although there’s also room on the menu for local specialities such as tagliatelle and tortellini. Many of the wines served also come from Tuscany.

Name: Baretto di San Vigilio
Address: via al Castello 1, San Vigilio, Bergamo, 24129, Italy
Description En: In the small piazza that welcomes the funicular’s arrival station – with a small public parking area right at the top of the climb – lies a venue of retro charm, with Anglo-Saxon touches and an authentic soul. It serves as both bar and restaurant, where tradition meets modern accents in generous, thoughtfully composed dishes. The undisputed stars are the meats, accompanied by bread and desserts made strictly in-house. In warmer months, service moves to the panoramic terrace, offering enchanting views over the city (and, for the more intrepid, even in winter when the sun permits). Inside, two rustic-elegant dining rooms are warmed by cordial, convivial service that completes the experience.

Name: Quintilio
Description En: For over a century, and from generation to generation, Quintilio has acted as a junction between two beautiful regions, Liguria and Piedmont – and not just in a geographical sense. These regions take pride of place on the wine list (overseen by the friendly and talented owner Lorena) as well as on the menu, which is created daily with dishes made from top-quality local ingredients full of flavour. Regional specialities such as plin, Ligurian-style rabbit tortelli, risottos, vitello tonnato (veal) and brain are all skilfully reinterpreted with a modern twist by owner-chef Luca Bazzano.

Name: Dispensa Franciacorta
Description En: The decor at this restaurant features bottles of wine on the walls (there are around 700 labels on the wine list, with an unsurprising focus on sparkling wines from the local Franciacorta region), while the menu celebrates some of Italy’s best produce, as well as ingredients from further afield, with a focus on Mediterranean flavours. There’s also an excellent cheese selection which will delight cheese-lovers.

Name: Visione Restaurant and Living
Address: Strada Nicolini Basso 34, loc. Tre Stelle, Barbaresco, 12050, Italy
Description En: Chef Samuele Di Murro presents a proposal structured around three tasting menus: one rooted in tradition, one more creative and contemporary, and a third – “a mano libera”, or freestyle – that gives full rein to the inspiration of the moment. The dishes are, however, also available à la carte for a more flexible experience.The restaurant is set within Casa Nicolini, an elegant hotel property nestled in a tranquil and panoramic position. Through the dining room’s broad picture windows, the gaze opens across the surrounding hills, while in the warmer months the terrace plays host to the bar and the more informal, accessible offer of the Bistrot, with its own dedicated area.

Name: Umami
Address: Via Ugo Secondo Partigiano 1, Badalucco, 18010, Italy
Description En: A young chef, strengthened by experience in important kitchens, has brought the village’s old nursery school back to life, carefully restoring it and transforming it into a restaurant that proposes contemporary cooking with more or less overt ties to the local area. The offering is structured around tasting menus, from which individual dishes may also be chosen à la carte. Among the dishes not to be missed is the marinated brown meagre fillet with seasonal vegetables: impeccable cooking, convincing pairings and a harmonious balance that leaves its mark. In summer, a wonderful outdoor space, almost overlooking the banks of the Argentina river – which gives its name to the entire valley – provides a particularly evocative setting, perfect for completing the gastronomic experience.

Name: Ristorante de LEN
Address: Via Cesare Battisti 66, Cortina d'Ampezzo, 32043, Italy
Description En: Just a stone’s throw from the central and very busy Corso Italia, this restaurant has an elegant Alpine feel. Here, subtle lighting, soft background music and larch wood cladding on the walls create an ambience with an attractive blend of the modern and traditional. The cuisine takes inspiration from the local region, with specialities interpreted with a contemporary twist, including a focus on vegetable- and cheese-based dishes such as the excellent “fonduta di Saporito d'alpeggio” (fondue).

Name: San Baylon
Description En: Just a short distance from Piazza del Popolo, within the elegant Palazzo Ripetta, San Baylon presents itself as a refined yet informal venue, perfectly at ease in the heart of Rome. The spaces marry the architectural charm of the historic building with a contemporary and measured atmosphere, giving rise to surroundings that are welcoming and equally suited to an unhurried lunch or a more elegant dinner. In the warmer months, service extends to the delightful internal garden, a kind of secluded green retreat that adds a note of tranquillity to the experience. The cooking is distinguished by precision and balance, with careful attention to seasonality and the selection of ingredients. It is the produce itself, of evident quality, that occupies centre stage, drawn out by a modern and restrained approach that keeps the flavours clean, recognisable and direct. Technique, never worn on its sleeve, and a measured creativity lend the dishes both finesse and coherence, giving shape to a style that is elegant and immediately legible. The service, attentive and discreet, accompanies the meal with natural and unhurried rhythm.

Name: Lo Scalco Grasso
Description En: A small, intimate restaurant with a welcoming ambience and simple yet lively feel, where the owner-chef at the helm in the kitchen also makes an appearance front of house. Mantuan traditions are evident in the generous portion sizes as well as in dishes such as the legendary pumpkin tortelli (served with butter or a tomato and sausage sauce), while other options are more creative in style – the Emilian lamb tartare delicately flavoured with its own cooking juices, and served with sautéed chard, savoury sbrisolona cake and black truffles from the lower Mantova region in season is particularly delicious.

Name: Ortica
Address: via Giovanni Migone 4, Pieve Ligure, 16031, Italy
Description En: You drive along 4.5km of winding, narrow (occasionally extremely narrow) roads to get to Ortica, the restaurant at the Tenuta Golfo Paradiso about 35min from Genoa. As is often the case, once at your destination the extensive views of the Tyrrhenian Sea from the restaurant more than compensate for the effort of getting here. Neither will you be disappointed by the cuisine, which is prepared using top-quality ingredients such as vegetables from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, local fish and carefully selected meat. Dishes are fresh and modern, and occasionally cooked over the barbecue grill.

Name: Marc Lanteri
Description En: Situated right next to the Fratelli Massucco winery, with which it shares its comfortable outdoor spaces as well as stunning views of the surrounding hills and vineyards, this restaurant is run by Marc Lanteri and Amy Bellotti, partners in life and work, who have chosen this setting for their new Piedmontese adventure. Their cuisine is full of individual character, with three tasting menus (including a vegetarian option featuring produce grown in their own garden) and dishes also available à la carte style. Local ingredients and recipes naturally take centre stage, always enhanced by small touches of colour and imagination. The wine list showcases the property’s own wines, as well as offering a choice of labels from elsewhere in Italy and further afield.

Name: Blum
Description En: A magnificent location directly in a gazebo where you can count the waves breaking on the beach, but in case of bad weather, there’s also an equally intimate and elegant indoor dining room available. Pampered by attentive and exceptionally kind service, follow the chef’s creations along tasting journeys, including vegetarian options, or à la carte dishes from both land and sea, always served with great aesthetic taste, often built on local products crafted with contemporary and colorful sensibility. In short, enjoy the complete experience that two hours in this exclusive corner of Sicily will offer you!

Name: Ladinia
Address: strada Pedercorvara 10, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description En: Both the Berghotel Ladinia and its restaurant of the same name boast a warm, vintage Alpine-style ambience, with wood decor that tells the story of this business which opened as a simple inn back in 1930. Little has changed since then and guests return here time after time thanks to the warm welcome and attention to detail offered by the Costa family. The traditional cuisine has the occasional modern twist, while the few Ladin-style guestrooms are decorated with a profusion of wood.

Name: Carusu
Description En: Along the road through the archaeological park, two small rooms on different floors host an elegant and refined restaurant, born from the Mangione family's passion – nomen omen. In the kitchen, young Alen, after significant experiences in renowned restaurants, offers his reinterpretation of Sicilian cuisine, with a strong focus on vegetables, many of which are grown on the farm tended by his uncle. At the entrance, you'll find father Francesco, while in the dining room, his equally young brother Dominique is available for conversations about wine.

Name: Kohaku
Description En: On a street running parallel to the celebrated Via Vittorio Veneto, Kohaku brings the elegance of Japanese kaiseki cuisine – the country’s haute gastronomy – to the capital. The menu offers a broad range of classic and traditional dishes, with quality at its heart: impeccable ingredients, precise knife work and carefully composed presentations. The freshness of the fish is evident in the many raw dishes, among which – according to the Inspector – the scallop and amberjack tartare stands out, mixed with cubes of avocado and dressed with a delicious ponzu sauce and sesame oil. The meats, too, are of notable quality. Depending on personal taste, guests may choose the celebrated gyoza dumplings, tempura, noodles or the many charcoal-grilled preparations, to name only part of the offering. For those seeking total immersion, the “Kohaku kaiseki” tasting menu is also available at dinner: an eight-course itinerary dedicated to lovers of great Japanese cuisine.

Name: Al Malò - Cucina e Miscelazione
Description En: The double entrance to this restaurant can be seen under the arcades in beautiful Piazza Cavour: the first door leads to the ground-floor cocktail bar (open in the evening) while, hidden to the left, there’s a lift which takes guests up to the restaurant itself on the first floor. Here, the contemporary-style dining room is enhanced by bright wallpaper that echoes the imaginative cuisine served by the owner-chef, which is modern, colourful and creatively and carefully presented. The chef is equally skilful with meat (his pigeon cooked “duck à l’orange”-style is superb) and fish, plus the menu features a few vegetarian options, as well as half portions. In the evening, the cocktail list adds to the enjoyment, alongside an impressive wine list which has an obvious emphasis on the Franciacorta region.

Name: Ca' Apollonio Gourmet
Description En: Ca’ Apollonio Gourmet offers a contemporary cuisine deeply rooted in the territory of the Venetian foothills, where nature, seasonality, and research coexist in refined equilibrium. Within a historic villa set in the landscape of Monte Grappa, executive chef Alessio Longhini constructs tasting menus that celebrate local and organic ingredients sourced from a carefully selected short supply chain, many of them grown in the property’s own kitchen gardens according to principles of regenerative agriculture.The proposal develops through menus that weave together gastronomic memory, technique, and contemporary sensitivity, following the rhythm of the seasons and offering an evolving reading of the territory. Completing the experience is a cellar of over a thousand labels – spanning small producers and great houses – with a particular focus on PIWI grape varieties, curated by sommelier Michele Griggio. In an intimate and elegant setting, animated by the masterful front-of-house direction of maître Lorenzo Palma, every detail is considered with a view to creating an experience that is harmonious and immersive.

Name: Nello
City: San Casciano in Val di Pesa
Address: Via IV Novembre 66, San Casciano in Val di Pesa, 50026, Italy
Description En: Federico at the stove and Chiara, pastry chef and the soul of the welcome, have brought new life to a long-established local restaurant, transforming it into a modern expression of Tuscan cooking. The menu, varied and stimulating, features dishes such as the raviolo filled with Parmigiano cream from Red Cows, served with chanterelles and onions – intense and technically accomplished – as well as their intriguing take on tiramisù, given an added dimension by a secret touch of tobacco. Over the years, the wine list has grown considerably, reflecting the deep passion of both proprietors; the bottles are kept in a captivating sixteenth-century space that is most certainly worth a look.

Name: Josef Stube
Address: Località Certosa 29, Madonna di Senales, 39020, Italy
Description En: Run with passion by the two owners who continue the long family tradition in this hotel-restaurant is one of the most picturesque sights in the Val Senales. Its beautifully kept dining room is romantic and typical of the region, providing a backdrop for just a few dishes which are prepared by the chef with a focus on local ingredients. A hint of Mediterranean influence adds to the appeal.

Name: Locanda San Martino
Address: via Don Ermolao Barattin 23, Chies d'Alpago, 32010, Italy
Description En: Founded in 1952, this inn has been run by the same family – and especially its female members – ever since. It now boasts the presence of a chef whose many years of experience are evident in his dishes. Much of the meat (especially lamb) is raised in the restaurant’s own farm nearby, while the dishes on the menu are seasonal and classic in style yet with a hint of modern flavour. When the weather allows, make the most of the large terrace boasting fine views of the sunset over the surrounding Alpago region.

Name: Ling's Ravioleria Migrante
Description En: A young couple (she was born in China; he’s half-French, half-Italian) have settled in this quiet residential district where they now run a tiny yet successful restaurant with around 20 seats in the dining room and a few small tables outdoors in summer – booking is essential! The menu includes various types of Chinese ravioli as well as dishes described by the couple as “migrant”, in other words “which draw inspiration from different cuisines from around the world, not only Asia but also the Mediterranean, France and Italy, with Emilia Romagna at its heart”. Examples include Peking-styleMora Romagnola coppa ham and pink Adriatic prawns marinated in mirin and soy sauce. The menu changes daily in line with market availability and the inspiration of the chef. Drinks include tea, beer and a small selection of wine.

Name: Il Gusto di Xinge
Description En: The dining room plays on warm brown tones reminiscent of a teapot, enlivened by touches of brilliant blue and modern leather chairs that lend a contemporary edge to the space. The Chinese chef presents authentic cuisine from her homeland – dim sum included – while drawing inspiration from Italian and French culinary traditions, all infused with a decidedly “pop” creative flair. To best begin the experience, consider an artisanal cocktail at nearby DrinX, the perfect prelude to dinner.

Name: ES Cantina&Ristorante
Description En: Situated within the Gianfranco Fino wine estate, this tuff building houses a restaurant on its first floor with large picture windows that look out at the vineyards and a spacious terrace offering views of the surrounding countryside. Here, chef Simone Profeta from Naples serves modern meat and fish dishes, often cooked using wines from the estate, such as in the deliciously tender braised veal cheeks served with a full-bodied ES reduction. There’s also a vegetarian menu that features organic vegetables grown in the estate’s own kitchen garden. The wine list showcases the winery’s own labels of different vintages.

Name: Osteria Grande
Description En: This restaurant overlooking the magnificent Piazza Grande and the Loggia Vasariana that takes up one whole side of the square was opened in the summer of 2022 by the enthusiastic Fatjon and Lorenzo (if you ask, they’ll happily share their knowledge of Arezzo’s history with you). The former is at the helm in the kitchen where he expresses his passion for cuisine in seasonal, contemporary-style dishes such as pigeon breast, leg and fillet (each cut is prepared in the appropriate way) served with sweet onion and cocoa nibs, while the latter oversees the wine selection and recommends suitable pairings to guests. For the chef’s pigeon speciality, he may, for example, suggest an original Maturato Tiberini 2018 (a white wine made from grapes that are left to ripen on the vine). Cocktail staff are also hand for guests keen to choose an aperitif or an after-dinner drink from the extensive cocktail list.

Name: La Casina
Description En: This large farmhouse with attractively renovated rooms overlooks the verdant landscapes of the Sarca valley from its wisteria-shaded summer pergola. Young chef Giada Miori prepares regional ingredients with skill and precision, serving specialities such as traditional potato fritters and “carne salada” (salted meat) preserved by the restaurant itself, as well as char, meat from the Trentino region and mushrooms. The Miori family also grow their own red berries, which often make an appearance in their desserts, along with their own sweet chestnuts.

Name: aldìVino
Description En: Shelves stacked with wine bottles line the walls at this smart bistro-style restaurant, which also boasts a quiet outdoor space for summer dining. The cuisine is contemporary and creative and is showcased on three tasting menus from which dishes can also be ordered à la carte. We highly recommend the pink shrimp, broad beans, lovage and almond dish – one of the chef’s iconic specialties. Courses here are divided into meat, fish and vegetable sections (Terra, Acqua and Vegetale).

Name: Quadri Bistrot
Description En: A modern bistrot with cocktail bar, fashionable furnishings, soft lighting and lounge music in the background, also featuring a small sidewalk terrace that requires advance booking. The cuisine, imaginative and creative, is guided by a talented chef who ensures personality and excellent seasonal products. Try the Mediterranean-style red mullet, while the tiramisu features a refined pairing with Sauternes. We also note a menu dedicated to caviar.

Name: InAlto Alfio Ghezzi Dolomites
Address: Passo San Pellegrino 32, stazione a monte della funivia Col Margherita, Moena, 38035, Italy
Description En: At Col Margherita, perched at 2,550 meters and accessible by cable car in winter (departing from Moena via Passo San Pellegrino), a new ski bar bears the signature of Alfio Ghezzi. The menu favors Alpine traditions, though a more elaborate, creative selection showcases several not-to-be-missed dishes from the chef. In warmer months, the venue is also reachable on foot or − for the more athletic − by bicycle (two charging stations available for e-bikes).

Name: Felter alle Rose
Address: via Gasparo Da Salò 33, Salò, 25087, Italy
Description En: A trattoria that tells stories of family and tradition, renewed under the guidance of those who have made hospitality and quality their vocation.
