The spaces open up into different atmospheres: the authentic warmth of the dining room, the closed veranda that filters the soft light of the seasons, and the cellar, where the scent of wine accompanies tastings and aperitifs. The kitchen serves Italian dishes, prepared with simplicity and good taste, using fresh, seasonal ingredients: genuine flavours intertwined with the pleasure of feeling at home.

Name: Savô
Description En: The reopening in 2022 of the Hotel Windsor with its romantic vintage decor, is a real bonus for Laigueglia, especially the hotel’s new gourmet restaurant Savô (which translates as “flavour” in Ligurian dialect). Here, a contemporary dining room and an outdoor space with views of the beach and the sea provide the setting for modern cuisine prepared from regional, seasonal ingredients with a focus on fish (there is also a meat option for each course). The impressive selection of wine and choice of cocktails from the elegant Windsor Bar adds to its appeal.

Name: Il Grottino
Address: piazza Beato Ugolino 5, Gualdo Cattaneo, 06035, Italy
Description En: Situated in the old medieval village of Gualdo Cattaneo, amid the gentle valleys not far from Foligno, Il Grottino is the perfect choice for anyone keen to sample the authentic flavours of Umbrian cuisine. Here, truffles and zero-km produce take pride of place on the menu, with a particular focus on meat which is carefully cooked on the open-view barbecue grill. Alongside locally sourced produce, you’ll also find a choice of carefully selected Prussian beef. Comfortable and welcoming guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Faraglioni Restaurant
Address: lungomare dei Ciclopi 115, loc. Aci Trezza, Aci Castello, 95021, Italy
Description En: Situated next to the hotel of the same name (a reference to the Faraglioni islands just off the coast here) but with its own entrance, this restaurant overlooks the beautiful Riviera dei Ciclopi. Sicilian ingredients take pride of place here in traditional and creative dishes with a focus on fish and seafood (vegetarian options are also available).

Name: Trattoria da Me
Description En: Lively and much frequented, this trattoria guided by the energetic Elisa owes its success to a well-judged balance between dishes of the tradition – with fresh pastas prepared by the sfogline and also available for purchase in the adjoining shop – and offerings that draw upon more contemporary techniques. Among the specialities not to be missed are the tagliolini with friggione and squacquerone cream: a thoroughly satisfying and well-balanced dish. For those drawn to the flavours of another age, Sunday is the day to seek out the classic lasagne alla bolognese on the menu, prepared according to time-honoured tradition. The terrace, available even in winter, lends a further note of pleasure to the experience.

Name: KELINA Fine Dine
Address: Strada Lech de Boà s.n., Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description En: From Corvara, take the ultra-modern Boè cable-car to this restaurant (accessible also on skis or by foot) which is one of the dining options at the Piz Boè Alpine Lounge (for access, turn right as you exit the cable-car). Open at lunchtime only, KELINA serves unexpectedly gourmet cuisine in a minimalist-style dining room which allows the stunning views of Sassongher, Santa Croce and La Varella to take centre stage through the restaurant’s large floor-to-ceiling windows. The dishes are always modern and creative, combining Alpine ingredients with fresh fish – the red prawns with scampi mayonnaise and sea asparagus sorbet is a good example.

Name: Terrazza Tiberio
Description En: Housed on the first floor of the Tiberio hotel, this elegant restaurant boasts a terrace overlooking the rooftops of Capri. The regional and island specialities on the menu leave a lasting memory, such as the “montanara” (fried pizza), “casatiello” (a savoury bread from Naples) and the caprese-style ravioli, although more creative options also feature, especially among the desserts. All in all, an elegant dining experience.

Name: Pellico 3
Description En: The Park Hyatt’s small gastronomic jewel enjoys one of the most privileged positions in the city: it may be reached directly from the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, or alternatively through the cocktail bar with its street entrance. The interiors, adorned with works of contemporary art, are complemented by elegant and precise service, creating the ideal context for the cuisine of young chef Guido Paternollo. The proposal is articulated across two tasting menus: “La mia città”, a personal homage to Milan, and a freer itinerary tied to seasonality and the inspiration of the moment. Both reveal a modern, intense, and well-calibrated cuisine, capable of exploring interesting pairings without ever losing balance, as in the wild garlic risotto with morels and sea snails, finished with a delicate smoked scamorza cream. The experience is completed by an outstanding wine service, guided by sommelier Lorenzo, who leads guests with expertise through a selection of around 700 labels, with particular attention also given to wines by the glass.

Name: Il Giardinetto
Address: Piazza Giuseppe Garibaldi 10, Mandello del Lario, 23826, Italy
Description En: Looking out over the calm blue water, this classic restaurant serves traditional cuisine with the occasional imaginative twist. Fish from the lake feature on the menu, as do meat and seafood options with something for everyone. There’s also a small outdoor terrace where guests can enjoy a pre- or post-dinner drink.

Name: Cucina
Address: Via Giano della Bella 3r, Florence, 50124, Italy
Description En: At this restaurant, local ingredients (mainly from the market) take pride of place on the daily menu which changes in accordance with whatever produce is available at the time. The rustic-style dishes are full of intense flavours, with meat and vegetables often cooked in the wood-fired oven. The pleasantly informal dining room with its many cookery books dotted here and there was designed by the owner-architects themselves.

Name: Campocori
Address: via di Santa Maria de' Calderari 49, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description En: Housed within the Chapter Hotel and designed by South African designer Tristan Du Plessis, this restaurant is conceived as a nighttime place with a dark atmosphere, “ferrying” into the capital a contemporary, cosmopolitan take on fine dining, blending Roman, Italian, and international references.

Name: Pentole e Provette
Description En: This restaurant run by Luca Trabalzini and his partner Rossella is a real gem in the small town of Fasano. Their story, which began in Australia, adds a fascinating touch to this gastronomic project. The atmosphere here is warm and lively, making this the perfect setting in which to enjoy the chef’s innovative cuisine, which he showcases on three distinct menus dedicated to meat, fish and vegetarian dishes respectively. Luca’s cuisine is modern and elegant, with particular attention paid to flavours and textures so that each and every dish offers a fully rounded sensorial experience.

Name: Locanda Sensi
Description En: A country retreat that captivates with simplicity and passion: modern, comfortable rooms open onto a landscape that embraces the hills of Piacenza, while outdoor dining offers glimpses of light and nature. The menu invites guests to enjoy a tasting menu in which the grill releases intense aromas, or à la carte dishes that range from land to sea to garden, in a balance of scents and colours. Two cosy suites, a holistic wellness centre scented with natural essences and, in fine weather, a Zen garden that invites you to relax, complete the experience.

Name: L'Agave
Description En: Be cautious not to be misled by any potential misdirections from satellite navigation systems. Head directly to the tourist marina of the quaint locality overlooking the sea—a place offering one of the most striking vistas in the area. Here, dishes crafted by a young chef and wines selected from remarkable regional highlights boldly declare a love for Liguria. From Albenga’s artichokes and asparagus to Pigna beans, pine nuts, 'prebugiun', olives, and of course, seafood—all elements here speak of this land. The concept encompasses tasting menus, with dishes available à la carte.

Name: Calvi Ristorante
Description En: This welcoming, contemporary-style restaurant with a large open-view kitchen serves two different types of cuisine – one regional and Mediterranean in style, the other more creative allowing the chef’s culinary skills to take centre stage. The black rice tacos with roasted eel, green beans, soya bean sprouts and spicy hummus mayo are truly delicious – definitely to be eaten with the hands!

Name: Masseria Moroseta
Description En: Chef Giorgia Eugenia Goggi offers a unique and authentic gastronomic experience that focuses on fresh ingredients (mostly vegetables), many of which are sourced from small organic gardens. The 90€ menu celebrates Mediterranean cuisine to the full, with colourful dishes that are full of flavour and in which the freshness of the ingredients is allowed to shine through. The beautifully kept, rustic dining room provides an ideal setting for an unforgettable dinner, while the selection of natural Italian wines offers the perfect accompaniment to the chef’s dishes, further enhancing your dining experience. There are six comfortable guestrooms available should you wish to extend your stay and immerse yourself in these peaceful rural surroundings. Booking in advance is highly recommended given the restaurant’s popularity and unique appeal.

Name: Stilla
Address: Località Casette 1, Colognola ai Colli, 37030, Italy
Description En: Run by an enthusiastic and committed young couple who left the big city to restore the family home and transform it into an elegant, welcoming restaurant, Stilla stands in a tranquil location surrounded by vineyards. Here, Silvia creates original, generous and colourful cuisine which is showcased on an à la carte with just a few dishes which change regularly. We particularly enjoyed the freshly seared bonito served with wild spinach, sour cherries and a cherry barbecue sauce. Meals are served on the outdoor terrace in summer. Accommodation is also available in five beautiful yet functional guestrooms. Well worth a visit.

Name: Remulass
Description En: They call it ‘Cucina con le radici’ (Cuisine with roots) and you only need to cross the threshold to understand why: a small, lively restaurant with warm colours, which gets very busy, especially in the evening, when booking is essential. The menu is simple, featuring just a few carefully planned dishes, mostly vegetarian, where seasonal freshness is paramount. Every recipe releases authentic aromas and genuine flavours, while leaving room for creativity: such as the variations on pumpkin, with oven-baked Mantovana and Hokkaido julienne in a sweet and sour sauce, caressed by tamarind cream and little cubes of blue goat's cheese. A combination of textures and aromas that tells the story of the land with elegance and creativity.

Name: Urubamba
Description En: Situated amid luxury boutiques and historic palazzi in one of Naples’ most exclusive districts, this restaurant boasts a chic and romantic dining room with soft lighting on the first floor, as well as an exclusive outdoor terrace for fine weather. The cuisine is totally in keeping with the trendy setting, featuring a successful combination of two different gastronomic cultures (namely Peruvian and Japanese) that blend together perfectly.

Name: John Restaurant
Address: via Santa Maria la Nova 35, Afragola, 80021, Italy
Description En: Follow the signs to Casamadre (the specialist food shop next door) to get to this gourmet restaurant, where the chef surprises guests with modern cuisine that is full of character. The dishes served here are inspired by classic recipes which are reinterpreted with creativity and a respect for local traditions, resulting in highly distinctive flavours. Each course reflects the region’s history, with a common thread running through the menu to create an authentic culinary experience. To accompany your meal, the wines are presented on a practical tablet which makes it easy to explore the different labels available. Among the different options, the excellent Costa D'Amalfi “Selva delle Monache” 2022 is particularly striking thanks to its fresh, earthy aromas.

Name: Indiniò
Description En: Located in a charming little village, Indiniò is an extraordinary place to discover Carnic cuisine. The ingredients tell the story of the local area, but chef Gloria Clama transforms them into refined creations that are sometimes bold and surprising. The dining rooms, furnished with wood and modern details, evoke tradition in an elegant way, creating a warm and romantic atmosphere.

Name: Oltremare
Description En: Situated on the fifth floor of the Due Torri hotel, the restaurant has recently been refurbished, giving it an even more charming and atmospheric feel than before. The cuisine is creative in style, almost always using ingredients and recipes from Campania as its inspiration – a good example is the many different ways tomato is used, including tomato water distilled in an alembic still. Chef Alfonso Crisci’s recipes are complex and always full of different ingredients and colours, with a selection of delicious and generous desserts to finish your meal.

Name: Cocun Cellar Restaurant
Address: strada Prè de Vì 31, San Cassiano, 39036, Italy
Description En: In the cellars of the Ciasa Salares hotel, you dine surrounded by bottles – after all, cocun in Ladin means cork, and not by chance the wine selection is vast. The chef creates dishes with ingredients and influences from every corner of the world and makes frequent use of the grill.

Name: Salvo
Description En: Situated opposite the Villa Comunale gardens, this restaurant serves some of the best pizzas in Naples (classic Neapolitan-style pizza which is soft and so big that it spills over the plate) as well as a selection of delicious appetisers, such as superb pasta fritters with various toppings. Welcoming ambience, with a more elegant feel than that of a typical pizzeria.

Name: Principe di Belludia
Description En: The Principe di Belludia is the gourmet restaurant at the Il San Corrado di Noto hotel, a luxurious resort in a secluded rural location with two enormous swimming pools. The new executive chef Martin Lazarov showcases his love for Sicily, with a particular attention to vegetables dishes.

Name: Essencia Restaurant
Address: piazza Santa Maria la Nova 9, Naples, 80134, Italy
Description En: Having spent many years living in Spain, the young chef at this quiet, elegant restaurant offers an appealing combination of Spanish and Italian dishes, resulting in his own interesting interpretations of Mediterranean cuisine. Situated in the heart of the historic centre, the restaurant has an open-view kitchen and chef’s table for four guests near the entrance, while the main dining room is on the first floor.

Name: DA MÓ
Description En: This new, restored restaurant in the upper part of the Sassi (yet still near the centre of Matera and its car parks) has a warm friendly ambience and boasts a small, charming outdoor space. Here, an entire family (father in the kitchen, mother and daughter front of house), who moved to Matera from Venosa (home of the Latin poet Horatio), serves regional cuisine with a contemporary twist and no little skill and professionalism. Various tasting menus are available, as well as an à la carte. An interesting wine list completes the picture.

Name: Dama
Address: Via Mulino 2, località San Gaudenzio, Cervesina, 27050, Italy
Description En: Situated just a few kilometres from Voghera in the Bassa Lomellina area, this gourmet restaurant run by a young chef occupies the old stables of the Castello di San Gaudenzio. Alongside local specialities such as baked onion and 24-month-old Grana Padano cheese, the menu also features more creative dishes based around authentic recipes. The wine list includes some particularly interesting labels from the Oltrepò region.

Name: Mogano
Address: via del Praticello Alto 7, Formello, 00060, Italy
Description En: Aiming to promote craft beers as a worthy pairing for gourmet cuisine, the Faenza family opened Mogano – a modern, elegant restaurant with a wood-inspired decor, soft lighting and just five tables, right next to their Ritual Lab brewery. One of the sons (Matteo, the chef here) greets guests before dinner with an aperitif served in the kitchen. With plenty of international culinary experience behind him, he combines Italian flavours with influences from all around the world. Despite the focus on beer, a wine list is also available.

Name: Impronta
Description En: An elegant restaurant that has the feel of a private home, with its beautiful light-wood tables. The Sicilian origins of talented chef Andrea Colombara are reflected in his dishes, which have a strong Mediterranean flavour. Highlights on the menu include delicious mullet with caponata which is served with onions, pine nuts, capers and small vegetables in a sweet and sour sauce.

Name: Cala Luna
Description En: Refined fine dining at the boutique hotel "Le Calette." In the summertime, Cala Luna is hosted in a splendid garden surrounded by plants and flowers, with breathtaking views of the bay, the Caldura sea stacks, and the Rocca. The dishes are a technical and creative expression of Chef Dario Pandolfo’s experiences, who applies what he has learned working in prestigious restaurants in Italy and abroad to Sicilian ingredients and traditions. The result is a vibrant and colorful cuisine, sometimes with strong flavors, always creative and deeply Mediterranean. "Green" notes are evident not only in the "Fiori di Luna" menu, dedicated to Sicilian vegetables, herbs, and flowers, but also in the sustainable approach to using raw materials, enhancing every part of them, and focusing on reducing waste without ever compromising quality.

Name: Cut
Description En: Situated right in the heart of the Bergamo plain in the small town of Caravaggio, famous for the painter of the same name and for a much-visited pilgrim shrine, this welcoming restaurant boasts a modern decor and vintage furnishings. At lunchtime, it serves a good, competitively priced business menu, while in the evening the more elaborate à la carte features contemporary-style meat and fish dishes (mostly the latter).

Name: Locanda Viola
Description En: A refined restaurant where the design plays with tables and seating of varied, original craftsmanship, yet it is the cuisine that captures attention, thanks to the talent of Filippo Moriggi. The starters are the calling card: an exotic-tinged journey that surprises with the fish bao, a soft steamed bun also available with BBQ sauce, or with the empanadas chilena, filled with white Sorrento scamorza, shrimp, and coriander-cumin mayonnaise. The journey continues toward more familiar flavors: well-executed pastas and risottos, fish dishes, and Bergamo lamb, leading to desserts that play on the freshness of gelato, served simply or affogato-style, for a light, flavorful finish.

Name: La Foresteria
Address: Contrada Passo di Gurra SP 79 km 91, Menfi, 92013, Italy
Description En: Planeta’s elegance is reflected in this property nestled among Sicilian vineyards. The rooms bear the signature of the celebrated winery, while the restaurant offers modern Sicilian cuisine, with an à la carte menu and two tasting journeys. Don’t miss “Casa Planeta”: five iconic courses inspired by the monsù, the chefs of ancient noble residences.

Name: Enoteca Meucci
Description En: Occupying a restored farmhouse at the foot of Cortona, this restaurant has two different dining areas: a wine bar on the ground floor where you can enjoy excellent aperitifs or buy local food produce, and a restaurant on the first floor that serves a traditional yet constantly evolving menu with a focus on seasonal ingredients. There’s also a beautiful outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Campo Cedro
Description En: Situated just a stone’s throw from the centre yet away from the tourist crowds, this restaurant is well worth the effort needed to find it! Here, Japanese chef Sugihara, who has more than 20 years’ experience working in Italy, creates modern and skilfully prepared Italian meat and fish dishes which are fresh and elaborate. You’ll nearly always find seafood risotto on the menu, which is made with fish, mussels and finely chopped shrimps all cooked together with rice and then sprinkled with crumbled seaweed and dotted with tomato paste. Excellent value for money!

Name: SOMS
Description En: In the heart of the seaside area, within a pedestrian zone, the historic *Società Operaia di Mutuo Soccorso* (SOMS) is now a delightful venue with a cozy, slightly contemporary dining room. It offers cuisine tied to Abruzzese traditions, both land and sea, executed with originality. The discreet and knowledgeable service, including the wine selection, along with an outdoor space to enjoy pleasant summer evenings, completes the experience.

Name: Qualia
Description En: Situated in a side street in the centre of this charming small town, this restaurant boasts a dining room with exposed brickwork and glimpses of the kitchen, plus a small outdoor space with a few tables for alfresco dining. The dishes here are full of flavour and focus on regional ingredients and fresh fish.

Name: Al Moro
Address: via Pietri 1277, Marina Di Campo, 57034, Italy
Description En: Situated away from the main tourist area, in a rustic building that is striking for its attractive outdoor space shaded by a wooden gazebo, this restaurant boasts an informal and relaxing atmosphere. The Mediterranean cuisine is full of character and prepared with top-quality ingredients, including a small selection of oysters.

Name: Portanova
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Italian Contemporary
Description En: A new restaurant in Urbino’s beautiful old town, where the designer-style decor blends harmoniously with the historic architecture. The modern, contemporary-style cuisine finds inspiration in ingredients from the Marche, as well as featuring flavours and traditions from other regions of Italy such as Sardinia, Campania and Lazio.

Name: Contrasto
Description En: Lucio Testa, chef-patron, has returned to his native village perched at an altitude of 937 metres, opening this restaurant in a former sheepfold on the outskirts of the village. The perfectly preserved stone façade, several small rooms spread over several levels, exposed beams and contemporary lamps give the ambience a modern touch. His is a creative cuisine, in which traditional Molise recipes are revisited, combining local and seasonal products (often from his own garden) with sauces, dressings and emulsions, learnt from working with French chefs; mulard duck is a favourite, several tasting menus guide the discovery of the territory, and finally, for those who prefer, a la carte choices. Among the wines, we suggest tasting a Tintillia del Molise Rutilia 2019 from Cantine Salvatore.

Name: FØRMA contemporary restaurant
Description En: Situated in a secluded residential district that is part of L’Aquila’s historic centre, this intimate restaurant with an elegantly minimalist ambience is home to skilful owner-chef Simone Ciuffetelli. Having gained experience working abroad, Ciuffetelli showcases local ingredients in his creative, contemporary dishes, with the occasional use of fermented products and a frequent focus on just three ingredients. A good example is his dessert featuring cream and crunchy toasted hazelnuts generously coated with a white-chocolate mousse that is “disguised” as an Italian-style meringue thanks to a sprinkling of liquorice powder.

Name: Bolle
Description En: We are in the Agnelli showroom, a well-known manufacturer of cookware for professional kitchens. The modern shop is located on the ground floor, while the first floor hosts the restaurant with its elegant tables in a refined minimalist and contemporary environment. On the menu, dishes with an impressive balance of ingredients, including occasionally exotic choices.

Name: Anastasia
Description En: This cocktail bar on the seafront is also a restaurant specialising in fresh fish served in a selection of classic dishes (such as tartare) and more elaborate recipes. The dining room is modern and spacious, plus there’s an outdoor terrace for alfresco dining in fine weather. Guestrooms and luxury apartments are also available (swimming pool on the roof).

Name: Cuculia
Description En: An establishment of measured elegance, with refined interiors that evoke the atmosphere of a contemporary French bistrot, enhanced by a small library displaying culinary volumes and beyond. Chef Oliver Betancourt, originally from Venezuela, built his training through notable kitchens in France, Spain, and Italy: a journey that today translates into a gastronomic approach rich in nuance, nourished by diverse traditions and constructed around seasonal local products, alongside more exotic ingredients such as kombu, soy sauce, and koji. Vegetarian options are clearly marked on the menu, together with several dishes suitable for vegans as well.

Name: Restaurant 700
Address: largo Michele Ayroldi Carissimo 14, Ostuni, 72017, Italy
Description En: Situated at the entrance to Ostuni’s historic centre, this restaurant is part of the luxury Paragon 700 hotel. The charming dining room combines historic features with a more modern decor, while the exclusive garden is perfect for dining alfresco in fine weather. The menu offers a concise selection of classic Italian dishes at lunchtime, while in the evening the chef conjures up more high-level and elaborate dishes showcasing strong technique.

Name: CiPASSO
Description En: A small restaurant which combines a contemporary feel with a hint of vintage style in its decor. The menu is inspired by Roman and regional traditions, with the occasional imaginative twist and other more Mediterranean-inspired dishes, all showing a strong focus on seasonal ingredients. The impressive wine list includes an excellent selection of regional wines, with a particular focus on wines by the glass. Friendly yet professional service from the young team completes the picture.

Name: Soul & Fish
Description En: From the centre of Sorrento, you follow a succession of roads downhill to Marina Grande, the town’s old, picturesque fishing village that is well worth a visit. Here, facing the water, you’ll find Soul & Fish, a seemingly traditional seaside restaurant that actually serves superb fish and seafood on a menu that combines traditional dishes with more creative options.

Name: Palazzo Utini
Description En: A historical palazzo in the town center has been given new life after its purchase by a local entrepreneurial family, who also bestowed their name upon it. Just steps from the heart of Italy’s famed food valley, it now serves as a refined hospitality venue: the ground floor hosts a bar and bistro, while upstairs are elegant spaces devoted to gourmet cuisine. Tasting menus are available, with dishes also offered à la carte, alongside an extensive and well-curated wine list. The upper floors feature intimate, stylish guest rooms, designed in the same reassuring style that runs throughout the building.

Name: Etra
Description En: Within the Palazzo Doria De Fornari, overlooking the celebrated piazza De Ferrari, one need only cross the threshold and venture into the heart of the building to discover Etra’s discreet entrance: a name that is an anagram of arte (art), evoked by the constantly evolving gallery that adorns the walls of the restaurant, enveloped in dark tones and studied minimalism. The cooking is distinguished by curiosity, verve and technical precision, structured around three tasting menus. Among the most accomplished offerings are the ray bottoni with red prawn tartare and a green vegetable jus, a dish that surprises with its freshness, aromatic character and refinement of execution.

Name: Duo
Address: via Cavour 7, San Felice del Benaco, 25010, Italy
Description En: Situated in the historic centre of the charming small village of San Felice del Benaco, Duo is the project of chefs Daniele Ghedini and Federico Pelizzari (the latter also oversees the front of house). Their personalised, modern cuisine is Mediterranean in style and features meat-based dishes, vegetarian options and fish recipes (salt- and freshwater), with a focus on matured fish which also has its own dedicated tasting menu. This colourful restaurant also boasts an outdoor space shaded by a pergola and surrounded by walnut trees.

Name: Ca' del Profeta
Description En: Situated in a beautiful location in the Asti countryside overlooking rolling hills and the estate’s own vineyards, Ca' del Profeta lies just a few kilometres from the provincial capital. A modern dining room and panoramic terrace provide the backdrop for decidedly innovative Piedmontese cuisine, which is inspired by traditional recipes and seasonal ingredients and then transformed by the chef into personalised dishes. Ingredients from further afield, such as root vegetables (black salsify, celeriac and beetroot) also make an appearance in three creative recipes inspired by the Orient. The service is friendly yet professional, plus a few modern guestrooms are also available. A panoramic swimming pool completes the picture.

Name: AlpiNN by Norbert Niederkofler
Address: Plan de Corones, alt. 2275, Brunico, 39031, Italy
Description En: Situated at an altitude of 2 000m in the Plan de Corones ski area, this restaurant is accessed via the cable-car from Riscone and then, in winter, by walking (or skiing) for around 150m through the snow. This impressive project by famous chef Norbert Niederkofler showcases his “Cook the Mountain” philosophy, where a modern approach and Alpine traditions combine to create perfect dishes full of flavour, all inspired by the seasons with a focus on using the whole ingredient with no food waste. The five tables with the best views are reserved for guests who choose the tasting menu, which has to be booked ahead of time. NB: the last cable-car leaves at 5pm!

Name: Carlo e Camillo
Description En: This intimate and elegant bistrot is the second restaurant of the Grand Hotel Sitea, a charming jewel box where you can enjoy Italian cuisine that gives ample space to Piedmontese tradition along with some other Italian regional dishes, as well as off-menu specialties that appear on the menu for brief periods.

Name: PS Ristorante
Address: via di Petriolo 7, Cerreto Guidi, 50050, Italy
Description En: This restaurant is an authentic surprise: the seemingly simple and unassuming names of the dishes conceal an extraordinary technique, designed to bring out the flavours of exceptional seafood; it is the creativity, at times sheer genius, that takes us by surprise. The sometimes overused concept of “cooking with produce”??????? reaches its fullest expression here: this is seafood as you have rarely tasted it, with aromas that waft through a refined dining room in shades of sea and sand. Gianfranco Pascucci is the architect of this emotional experience, while Vanessa Melis conveys his message and his love for fish in the dining room, with passion, expertise and a smile.

Name: Capriccio
Description En: Young chef Graziano Accolla has returned to his native city where he serves creative cuisine of the highest quality, while at the same time raising Augusta’s gastronomic profile. Thanks to his experience in Michelin-starred restaurants, he offers highly interesting dishes which focus on the use of top-quality ingredients.

Name: Meraviglioso Osteria Moderna
Address: largo Gelso 16, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
Description En: A few metres from Modugno’s statue and a breathtaking sea-facing balcony, with picturesque houses perched above Polignano, you’ll find exceptional cuisine, the creation of Andrea Vicario, whose hands craft predominantly seafood dishes with high effect and quality, showcasing a great passion—amongst mains—for charcoal cooking.

Name: Filia Ristorante
Description En: In Borgo Trento, an elegant residential quarter just steps from the historic center, Filia plays the card of a modern, minimalist setting, where just five tables find their place. Tasting menus are served, with dishes also available à la carte. The cuisine is modern and creative, at times revisiting classics of the Italian tradition.

Name: Casamare
Description En: Elegant and refined, this top-quality restaurant is the perfect choice for special occasions. Vietri ceramics, an open-view kitchen, fish on display and a successful mix of traditional and modern decor all combine to create an atmospheric setting in the dining room. As the restaurant’s name suggests, this is a good option for anyone who enjoys delicious classic fish and seafood dishes (mostly from Campania).

Name: Ca' Mia
Description En: This welcoming restaurant in the hills surrounding Lake Alserio makes guests feel completely at home. The two young chefs with plenty of experience behind them create modern dishes with a preference for quick cooking methods and a focus on a wood-fired oven and barbecue, as well as fermented ingredients.

Name: La RiMa
Description En: This restaurant in the heart of the town serves excellent contemporary cuisine (meat and fish, plus a few vegetarian options). The menu features dishes such as fregola sarda (a type of couscous) with tomato, buffalo mozzarella, friggitelli peppers and fried capers, with a personalised twist added by talented owner-chef Matteo Ridoni.

Name: Sücar Brüsc
Description En: A restaurant of young and contemporary character, with a lively entrance where a carefully considered display of wines – available for purchase – immediately signals the attention dedicated to the bottle. The offering focuses on a cuisine with a well-defined identity, built upon clean flavours and well-executed ideas. Among the most representative dishes, the tortelli duo deserves particular mention, half ‘sweet’ and half ‘bitter’, mantecati with artisan butter and sage, as does the Bove, a satisfying trio of beef that brings together braised stracotto, oven-roasted tongue and steamed cheek, served with soft potato and a fragrant salsa verde. Indulgent, satisfying and well-constructed dishes, perfectly suited to conveying the style of the house.

Name: Ménage
Description En: Situated in the heart of the city near the Teatro Bellini and Piazza Università, this restaurant occupies an Art Nouveau-style building. Here, a trio of experienced young chefs from Catania have brought new life to the old “Da Turi Finocchiaro” restaurant, which has always been very popular with the city’s high society. Offering a small outdoor space near the entrance, the quiet, intimate dining room on the ground floor provides the backdrop for reinterpreted, contemporary Sicilian cuisine with an exclusive focus on meat (especially barbecued dishes which are the restaurant’s trademark), while the first floor is home to a cocktail bar run with passion by one of the partners. Two frescoes painted by Giuseppe Barone in 1930 add to the appeal.

Name: 85 Bistrot
Address: piazza Martiri di Via Fani 85, Sesto San Giovanni, 20099, Italy
Description En: This simple, modern, family-run trattoria with a welcoming ambience is the kind of restaurant that everyone would love to have as their local. The owner-chef, who has plenty of experience working in Milanese restaurants, is a real culinary expert who creates traditional dishes from Milan but also from further afield. Here, the popular breaded cutlet is served thick so that the delicate flavour of the veal can be enjoyed to the full.

Name: La Botte
Description En: A modern and welcoming contemporary bistro situated in the heart of Stresa’s historic centre. Run by an entire family, the restaurant serves modern and imaginative fish and meat dishes where the focus is always on seasonal ingredients. The interesting wine list also includes a selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Strattoria
Description En: Situated in the foothills around Lake Maggiore, this welcoming restaurant has a pleasantly relaxed ambience. The chef is equally at ease with meat and fish, creating colourful modern dishes that demonstrate his individual take on contemporary Italian cuisine. Unsurprisingly, Piedmont takes centre stage, including desserts such as bonet with a traditional cake base which is then topped with dark chocolate and a crispy sphere filled with a kind of custard- cream mixture. Lighter options are also available at lunchtime.

Name: Gunè San Frediano
Address: via del Drago d'Oro 1r, Florence, 50124, Italy
Description En: The chef at this small gastronomic restaurant serves cuisine which acts as a bridge between Basilicata and Tuscany, the two most significant regions in his life, resulting in creative, delicate and beautifully presented dishes.

Name: I 5 Sensi
Description En: The whole family (mother and four children) is involved in the running of this restaurant, both front of house and in the kitchen. If you’re looking for top-quality cuisine which focuses on local ingredients yet is also creative and innovative, then this is the place for you! Classic-style dining room with the occasional modern decorative touch, plus a well-stocked wine cellar offering a selection of 700 labels.

Name: Mesadoria Restaurant
Address: Piazza De Honestis Cavallino, Sassari, 07100, Italy
Description En: This reliable restaurant has moved from the coast to simple, modern premises in the town of Sassari, where it has a new look and new chefs at the helm. The cuisine is as good as ever, with a focus on fish and seafood yet also including a few meat options, in dishes that are classic with a modern twist and cooked using predominantly Sardinian ingredients.

Name: Metodo
Description En: In a romantic setting of eighteenth-century farmhouses, you will find the same rustic atmosphere inside the restaurant as well, but combined with elements of modern elegance, starting with the solid wood tables left bare, with no tablecloth. Chef patron Stagi offers a single tasting menu (you can, however, choose between the full or abbreviated version, and the dishes are, in any case, also on the menu) with a creative and sometimes very elaborate character.

Name: Fàula
Description En: Fàula – “fairytale” in Piedmontese – represents the gourmet offering of Casa Langa, a property that opens like an elegant amphitheatre overlooking the valley. In the kitchen, Francesco Clerico presents a cuisine that weaves Piedmontese tradition and modern interpretations with natural ease, always with a personal touch. The tasting menu dedicated to vegetables from the estate garden speaks to a sincere attention to product, while the à la carte selection moves with balance among meat dishes, fish, and vegetable offerings. A well-curated wine selection and the gracious professionalism of the service complete a harmonious, thoughtfully constructed experience.

Name: Cosmo Restaurant
Description En: Although the menu here and there includes references to Campanian gastronomy and produce, Cosmo stands out as an excellent gastronomic destination for those seeking more elaborate and creative cuisine, the work of a young chef who produces complex dishes of a very high standard.

Name: Bottega Lucia
Description En: A charming bistro-style establishment, with exposed wood and brick creating a warm, informal atmosphere, offering immediate and flavorful Italian cuisine – the spaghetti alla chitarra cacio e pepe with black truffle is emblematic – alongside forays into the nearby Iberian Peninsula and playful international influences. Among these, the steamed bao with pulled pork and coleslaw and the celebrated Milanese-style gyoza stand out, the latter filled with ossobuco and served with saffron cream. Meat and fish appear in equal measure, in a menu designed to satisfy diverse tastes without losing coherence. Just steps away is Casa Lucia, a more informal iteration of the same establishment, ideal for simple dishes and good pizza.

Name: Il Cugnolo
Address: contrada Cugnolo 19, Torre di Palme, 63900, Italy
Description En: This gourmet restaurant housed in a restored period residence that once belonged to the counts of Adami is surrounded by the green maquis and hills of the Marche, with the sea visible in the distance just a few miles away. Here, the young Neapolitan chef creates cuisine that is surprising for its attractive, clean lines, providing a real explosion of flavours and a tribute to the region and the Mediterranean in general. The restaurant also owns a nearby agricultural estate which provides many of the wines and olive oils served during tastings.

Name: Gennaro Amitrano
Description En: The large picture windows at this restaurant offer fine views of the Tyrrhenian sea, where the blue of the sea blends with the elegance of the dining room. The view of the bay is truly spectacular, providing the perfect backdrop for a dining experience that is both traditional and innovative. The chef here serves classic dishes alongside Italian specialities reinterpreted with a modern twist, surprising guests with combinations that are bold yet always balanced. A good example is his elegant lemon tartlet served with a caper and pepper powder.

Name: Locanda Perbellini al Mare
Description En: The flavors of Sicily – and not just seafood – are reimagined in a modern way, with personal touches (such as the tuna cutlet cooked and raw with soy mayonnaise and mashed potatoes), as well as vegetarian recipes inspired by the multi-starred chef Perbellini, executed with good technique and a dedication to taste. This all takes place in a modern beach establishment, complete with loungers and umbrellas. In the summertime, the windows open, and you practically all dine on the terrace, surrounded by the scent of the sea.

Name: Altriménti
Description En: A bistro with a contemporary soul, where the informal atmosphere mingles with a subtle elegance that captivates without ostentation. The scents that waft out from the kitchen reveal the seasonality of the ingredients: fresh, carefully selected from small producers, transformed into dishes that speak Italian, with a harmony between sea and land. Every course is an invitation to discover something new, every detail a sign of attention. When it comes to wine, let the owner guide you: his enthusiasm will steer you towards pairings that enhance every nuance of flavour.

Name: Lupaia
Address: Località Lupaia 74, Torrita di Siena, 53049, Italy
Description En: An enchanting setting, a Tuscan hamlet nestled among the hills between Montepulciano and Montefollonico, from which breathtaking sunsets may be enjoyed; tables in the open air during the warmer months, while in the cooler season the dining room looks out onto a splendid open kitchen. The gastronomic offering is determined daily by the chef, whose tasting menu draws above all upon the produce of the estate. Booking is essential for those not staying in the hamlet, and the journey to reach it is thoroughly bucolic.

Name: Innesti
Address: via San Pietro 8, Pergine Valsugana, 38057, Italy
Description En: Daniele and Elisa are a couple of young restaurateurs who are familiar to us from their time at Blumenstube in Sant'Orsola. Having moved on, they have now opened their own restaurant in Pergine, where both the decor and the cuisine are contemporary-Alpine in style. As in currently in vogue, their dishes are showcased on three tasting menus (short, medium and long) from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte style. All the recipes have a creative feel, demonstrating the chef’s playful approach to his contemporary ingredients.

Name: Le Cementine
Description En: This rustic, vintage-style country restaurant run by the Alajmo brothers stands on the banks of the Sile river, just a few minutes from the Venetian lagoon, and overlooks a vegetable garden, vineyard and beautiful green meadows. The cuisine demonstrates a strong focus on seasonal, regional ingredients, featuring meat and fish alike, with vegetables taking centre stage in many of the dishes.

Name: Ichikawa
Description En: Ichikawa is one of the culinary masters who played a part in introducing Japanese cuisine to Italy. After decades in the country working in various restaurants, this chef has finally opened his own eatery, where he serves top-quality Japanese cuisine ranging from familiar favourites such as sushi and sashimi to other less-known family dishes and street food from the land of the Rising Sun. A good place to discover the joys of Japanese cuisine!

Name: Zàghara Restaurant
Description En: Housed in the elegant Relais Villa Flora, this restaurant occupies a natural terrace with breathtaking views of the Nissene hills. The dishes are predominantly regional in style yet reinterpreted with a modern twist. There’s also a good wine selection with a focus on Sicilian and Italian labels.

Name: Materia Prima
Address: Località Piana Santa Liberata, Castel di Sangro, 67031, Italy
Description En: A pleasant and intimate terrace overlooks the shores of an artificial lake dedicated to sports activities. The glass windows provide the same view from the modern, sleek, and minimalist interior rooms, just like the dishes: creative, yet reminiscent of local cuisine, such as the simple but tasty Pallotta Cacio e Ova, offered among the welcome bites. There are also various daily specials according to the market. The service is friendly and attentive, with a young and motivated team overall.

Name: La Società Milano
Description En: Situated near Porta Venezia and its lush gardens, Giulia and Andrea’s restaurant boasts a warm and original ambience. Three dining rooms adorned with tapestries and an entrance with a fine white marble fireplace act as the setting for Mediterranean cuisine with the occasional exotic twist. Don’t miss the amberjack caponata in which the ceviche flavours contrast with the sweetness of the fried breaded aubergine.

Name: Bites
Description En: The cuisine at this tiny, simply furnished restaurant includes barbecued dishes and fermented ingredients, all of which feature on a tasting menu. Guests can also choose à la carte: the small portions (as the restaurant name suggests) make it possible to taste several dishes at a reasonable cost. Booking is essential in the evening and also advisable at lunchtime.

Name: Le Macine
Address: via Lino Carlo del Favero 11, Vittorio Veneto, 31029, Italy
Description En: Housed in a recently renovated 18C mill on the banks of the Meschio river, this restaurant is run by brothers Giuseppe (front of house) and Adriano (in the kitchen), who serve top-quality cuisine with its roots in local traditions and the occasional imaginative twist with warmth and professionalism. It is even more appealing in summer, when meals are served on the beautiful outdoor terrace.

Name: Osteria del Posto
Address: via Calderini 15, loc. Chiugiana, Corciano, 06073, Italy
Description En: Housed within an ancient mill in the village of Chiugiana, a small hamlet of Corciano, the osteria offers contemporary cuisine deeply rooted in the local area. Ingredients are carefully selected, and the wine list tells the stories of small producers, both local and national, with a special focus on artisanal and natural wines.

Name: Cucina Rambaldi
Description En: Regional dishes and produce are reinterpreted with a personal and measured style, maintaining a constant equilibrium between territorial roots and creative impulse. Technique – from the precise control of temperatures to the accuracy of the knife work, through to the care taken in the selection and keeping of ingredients – is always placed at the service of flavour, and the result is one of great coherence and pleasure. Particularly tempting is the section dedicated to the ‘Lenitivi’: small tasting morsels conceived also for pairing with aperitifs, gathered in an introductory list that rewards careful exploration. For those seeking an even more tailored experience, there is the option of the social table, accommodating up to six guests. The service is professional and cordial, accompanying the meal with attentiveness and measure.

Name: Comi 107
Description En: Situated near the lake at the entrance to a narrow street dotted with various shops, this small contemporary-style restaurant boasts an equally tiny outdoor space for summer dining and is run with skill and professionalism by a young couple. The friendly, welcoming wife oversees the front of house, while her husband creates dishes full of character in the kitchen.

Name: Vecio Macello
Description En: A former early 20th-century slaughterhouse, today you’ll find a restaurant with a pleasantly classic atmosphere and a kitchen that, despite the building’s original purpose, serves predominantly seafood dishes, though with some meat classics.

Name: Antica Osteria il Ronchettino
Description En: An authentic Milanese trattoria in operation since the late 17th century as a post station, while the apartment buildings of Gratosoglio rose up all around it in the 1960s, the interiors still preserve their historic charm. The cuisine fortunately remains faithful to the spirit of the place, offering some Milanese classics, such as mondeghili (meatballs), risotto alla milanese (with or without ossobuco), and the “elephant ear” cutlet.

Name: Madama Piola
Description En: The aptly named Madama Piola (in Piedmontese dialect, “piola” is a village inn) has a simple yet attractive and friendly ambience that serves as a backdrop for typical Piedmontese dishes. Highlights include the memorable stuffed onion, as well as tonnato, braised cheeks and hot zabaglione. Regional wines take pride of place on the wine list, which includes a good selection by the glass.

Name: San Tommaso 10
Description En: It was here, in 1895, that Luigi Lavazza opened a grocer’s shop and immediately began blending coffee. Today, the same establishment is home to a modern restaurant serving excellent cuisine, led by a chef from Le Marche who offers one of the city’s most convincing interpretations of Piedmontese gastronomy, often revisited with a creative touch. Among the dishes, the carousel of starters is truly not to be missed, as is the white truffle (when in season). The wine list is also highly interesting, organised according to a chromatic system that identifies the various styles: from “voluptuous” to “purpureal”, from “luminous” to “veiled”. A refined game that invites guests to indulge in the choice of the perfect bottle for every palate and occasion.

Name: Zanze XVI
Address: fondamenta dei Tolentini, sestiere Santa Croce 231, Venice, 30135, Italy
Description En: Although the setting and convivial atmosphere in this restaurant recall that of a typical Venetian bàcaro , the cuisine is completely different in feel. The ingredients are sourced from the best markets and local producers, resulting in unique dishes that reflect the culinary traditions of the lagoon and its surrounding area. The few tables arranged outdoors with views of the tranquil canal add to the appeal, while the professional yet friendly service helps to put guests completely at ease.

Name: Quattro Sensi
Description En: Perched on a hill just a few kilometres from Torgiano, Quattro Sensi boasts a veranda with views of Perugia, which is perfect for a quick lunch, and an elegant dining room in which you can enjoy regional dishes such as pappardelle egg pasta with a Cinturello Orvietano pork ragù with orange and fennel.

Name: Trattoria Margherita
Description En: Don’t be fooled by the relatively simple ambience of this trattoria which is situated in the centre of a town with an interesting history linked to the reclamation of the marshes and the dairy industry. Dedicated to the owner’s two grandmothers, the restaurant serves some of Sardinia’s best-known meat and fish specialities.

Name: Radicì
Description En: The name of this restaurant alludes both to the chef’s origins in Isea (“radici” translates as “roots”) and his passion for vegetables, which make a strong appearance in his dishes. He offers three tasting menus, one dedicated to fish from the lake, a second which is more creative, and a third focusing on seasonal vegetables, with the option of choosing individual courses from each menu à la carte style. Whatever you choose, be prepared for complex, elaborate and surprising cuisine!

Name: Diana's Place
Description En: Facing the square in front of Termini station, this wine bar-cum-restaurant is striking for its fresh and creative approach to cuisine. Nearly all the top-quality ingredients are local and can be purchased from the food counter. The excellent staff are happy to help with your choice of wine, which is also available by the glass.

Name: Casa Rapisarda
Description En: This small welcoming restaurant on the famous Scalinata della Costarella in Numana, with a tiny terrace for summer dining and just a few tables, serves delicious cuisine with an imaginative twist. Originally from Sicily, the highly talented owner-chef has spent much of his life in the Marche and has plenty of experience in leading restaurants. Given the limited capacity here, booking is essential, especially in summer.

Name: Tano Passami l'Olio
Description En: In an elegant residential neighbourhood, Tano Simonato's restaurant welcomes guests with modern design and a refined atmosphere, a prelude to cuisine that tantalises the senses. Italian tradition is clothed in creativity in the dishes: the famous “tirami su” made with cuttlefish and potatoes releases marine aromas and velvety notes, while the honey-glazed pigeon, baked in salt, delights the palate with contrasting sweet and savoury flavours, accompanied by spinach and savoury cherries. Tano sees food as a source of pleasure and enjoyment: the chef comes to the table, tells stories and suggests pairings, with every glass of wine becoming part of an experience that seduces all the senses.

Name: Saur
Description En: An unexpected restaurant hidden among the fields of a small hamlet in the Bassa Bresciana region. Although the menu features a few regional dishes, the focus here is on creative cuisine with an emphasis on herbs and vegetables, some of which are grown in the restaurant’s own kitchen garden.

Name: Ensama Pesce
Address: via Aristide Dondarini 4, Sala Bolognese, 40010, Italy
Description En: A menu which focuses only on fish (from the daily market) which is prepared with a hint of Puglia, the chef’s native region. As soon as guests are seated at their table, they are brought a selection of homemade breads, including taralli bread rings and focaccia. Owner-chef Sabino is the heart and soul of this restaurant, where guests can be sure of a memorable culinary experience!

Name: Osteria alla Chiesa
Description En: Genuine warmth in the dining room and interiors that recall the inns of old: the building is historic, and the discreet creak of the wooden staircase contributes to a d’antan atmosphere. Among the most intriguing offerings is a raviolo accompanied by fried artichokes and a sweetbread “carpaccio,” completed by an almond sauce that rounds the dish with gentle, measured succulence.

Name: L'Ostì
Address: strada Sassongher 2, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description En: A minimalist-style restaurant featuring a wood decor, an extensive display of bottles, and some windows boasting partial yet splendid views of the Dolomites. The chef here prepares creative cuisine using local ingredients alongside produce sourced from other regions. The wine list includes a wide selection of natural wines.

Name: Antica Osteria Moirago
Description En: This old monastery in Moirago, overlooking the Naviglio Pavese canal, was founded in 1250 and converted into an inn as early as 1478. Centuries may have passed, but the tradition of hospitality continues in the building’s enclosed painted portico, as well as in its two warm and atmospheric dining rooms. The chef’s Puglian origins explain the abundant use of vegetables and raw fish dishes, while in winter the cuisine takes on a more northern Italian flavour. Good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Antiche Carampane
Address: rio Terà delle Carampane, sestiere San Polo 1911, Venice, 30125, Italy
Description En: From the typical floors to the wall decorations, everything here speaks to the heart to tell you about a historic trattoria where people joyfully return each time to enjoy local seafood specialities. Sarde in saor, baccalà mantecato, fried moeche (spring and autumn), cuttlefish in nero to name but a few. The recipes are crafted with skill and fidelity to tradition. In addition to the dishes listed on the menu, each day you will be verbally presented with off-menu specials. An excellent wine selection ranging from Italian to French labels with good value for money.

Name: Repubblica di Perno
Address: vicolo Cavour 5, loc. Perno, Monforte d'Alba, 12065, Italy
Description En: In the very heart of gastronomic Langa, where a reservation is an absolute necessity, lies a small and carefully restored restaurant brought to life by the passion of the couple who run it: she in the dining room, he at the stove. In the finest Piedmontese tradition, the entrance opens directly onto the open kitchen, a prelude to the intimate first floor, which accommodates just five tables. The offering takes the form of a daily menu that is rigorously regional, enriched by dishes that celebrate seasonality and local tradition. Among the most pleasing preparations, the cardoon tart with quail’s egg and fonduta stands out: harmonious and well-executed. The surroundings, neat and intimate, recall the atmosphere of a rustic family bistrot, where every detail contributes to a sense of warmth and authenticity. Completing the offering, three guest rooms are available, perfectly suited to those wishing to extend their stay and explore the Langa at an unhurried pace, between fine cooking, a domestic welcome and the spirit of the territory.

Name: Locale Firenze
Description En: Within a palazzo steeped in history, spanning from its medieval underground cellars to the Renaissance piano nobile housing the restaurant, guests enter through the ancient courtyard, now a refined lounge bar with a large counter dedicated to mixology and small tapas-style bites. From here you reach the splendid interior dining rooms, the ideal backdrop for an avowedly creative cuisine shaped by the chef’s international experiences across Australia, Japan, and France. The evocative medieval cellars also house “Labo-ttega,” an exclusive experience combining avant-garde cuisine and mixology, available by reservation for up to four guests. A vibrant destination brimming with energy and quality, interpreting contemporary gastronomy with distinct personality.

Name: Dulchemente
Description En: A contemporary-style restaurant which serves modern dishes alongside simpler, more classic options, with a notable focus on fish. A splendid outdoor terrace for alfresco dining and friendly, professional staff complete the picture.

Name: Osteria del Tasso
Address: via Bolgherese km 3,9, località San Walfredo, Bolgheri, 57020, Italy
Description En: Just a stone’s throw from the famous Viale dei Cipressi avenue in one of Italy’s best-known wine-producing areas, this restaurant occupies one of the region’s most famous wineries, namely Guado al Tasso, renowned for its excellent wines. In fine weather, guests can dine in the shade of plane trees looking out over the vineyards. Simple, delicious and well-prepared cuisine, mostly traditional in style, plus specialities such as cured hams and grilled dishes.

Name: Lofficina
Description En: This building with a minimalist, contemporary design is situated on the edge of the historic centre at the Sant'Erasmo belvedere, from where, in summer, panoramic views extend over Monte Conero and the sea (booking ahead is recommended). In the kitchen, owner-chef Davide Breccia conjures up creative dishes featuring original combinations and mainly inspired by the sea. There are two tasting menus, Iconico and Idee, for guests who like to be guided, plus an à la carte for those who prefer to choose their own courses.

Name: Gainn
Description En: A change of management in January 2026 brought with it a new hand in the kitchen, without however altering the identity of Gainn, open since 2007 and a long-standing and dependable ambassador of Korean gastronomic culture. The cooking is lively and flavoursome, composed of colourful dishes revolving around rice, restorative soups, meat and fish, with generous space given to vegetables, soya and a well-judged balance between sweet-sour and spicy notes. The approach is avowedly convivial: generous portions and preparations conceived to be shared at the centre of the table. A single dessert features on the menu: those with a sweet tooth would do well to bear this in mind.

Name: Milano
Description En: This is a historic establishment, the guardian of a family tradition stretching back almost a century – celebrated in its iconic dessert, zabaione. The elegant setting draws its charm from a veranda overlooking the lake, further enhanced by a private jetty. The cuisine interprets contemporary tastes without compromising on classic favourites, supported by excellent ingredients sourced from the land, freshwater and sea. A prime example are the refined ravioli del plin with 100% langoustines.

Name: Pescheria
Description En: The name of this restaurant between the historic centre and the seafront refers to the main item on its menu, which is dedicated almost exclusively to fish (fresh and not farmed). Fish and shellfish are displayed in a glass cabinet and aquarium respectively, both of which are situated to the rear of the long, narrow dining room near the open-view kitchen. Classic fish dishes full of flavour (served raw, baked, cooked in salt, in water or grilled) are to the fore here.

Name: Asina Luna
Address: via della Resistenza 23, Peschiera Borromeo, 20068, Italy
Description En: A restaurant with an attractive atmosphere, thanks to its profusion of wood, soft lighting and contemporary colour scheme. Meat aged for different periods takes pride of place on the menu. Sourced from different countries, it includes sweet Piedmontese Vicciola beef fed on hazelnuts and tender and delicately marbled Australian Scottona beef. Good selection of strongly flavoured and aged meat options.

Name: Al Persef
Description En: In the small, contemporary dining room of Hotel Sporting Family Hospitality, overlooking the Alps, diners can watch the kitchen staff as they work, creatively and paying close attention to locally sourced ingredients. Excellent wine list.

Name: Retrobottega
Description En: The fruit of a sweeping renovation by the celebrated architect Jean Nouvel, the building houses apartments and art galleries, while on the fifth floor the gastronomic soul comes to life: a single communal table, divided between an elegant interior dining room and a striking panoramic terrace offering uninterrupted views across the Palatine Hill. The cooking looks to the Mediterranean with particular attention to handmade pastas, the true hallmark of the offering. Among the iconic dishes, the tortelli with pork ribs, spring onion and cacao mass stand out with quiet authority. The same terrace is also home to a cocktail bar of enviable situation, ideally placed for raising a glass while contemplating the Roman sunset.

Name: MARdiVINO
Description En: Inside a recently renovated 1800s farmhouse, MARdiVINO's kitchen offers fresh seafood specialities inspired by Apulian tradition. Do not hesitate to try the barbecued rock octopus, marinated in scapece, accompanied by potato and speck mille-feuille.

Name: San Domenico
Description En: Perched high on the tufa cliffs overlooking the Costa degli Dei, this contemporary-style restaurant boasts superb views from its dining room and especially from its panoramic summer terrace. The cuisine served by the young owner-chef is as modern as the setting – dishes are light and almost exclusively focused on local fish.

Name: Feria
Description En: A modern restaurant with an Indonesian-style decor, plus an attractive open-view kitchen which creates a warm and welcoming ambience. Here, Marco Feltrin, an Italian chef with experience in Indonesian cuisine, serves typical dishes from this country with a contemporary twist. We particularly enjoyed the noodles, squid and leeks, and the charcoal-grilled snapper. The wine list includes a good selection of organic and biodynamic labels which are the perfect accompaniment to the Asian food served here. Feria has two distinct spaces – the bistro-cum-bar which serves cocktails and some street-food snacks and the gourmet restaurant.

Name: Veranda
Description En: Alberto Faccani, the chef at the Magnolia restaurant in the hills inland from Cesenatico, oversees the cuisine at this restaurant, which occupies an elegant veranda on the town’s main avenue – a busy promenade in summer. Fish takes centre stage here, in unfussy dishes that faithfully reflect the maritime traditions of the Adriatic. The menu, alongside daily specials announced at your table, features dishes that include raw fish and seafood, gratins, seafood salads, pasta and risotto, while the main courses feature a selection of grilled, baked and fried fish.

Name: Gallery Bistrot Contemporaneo
Description En: Modern cuisine, prepared with meticulous attention and enriched with carefully selected seasonal products. Tradition meets originality, as in the surprising risotto with clams, cauliflower and a dash of cocoa. Only twenty places in a spectacularly designed dining room: walls and ceilings clad in undulating light wood panels that weave together in a dynamic arch, creating an impression of movement that envelops the dining experience.

Name: Alla Locanda
Description En: A colourful, contemporary-style restaurant within the Locanda degli Artisti Art Hotel, a new address that is striking for its large art collection displayed throughout its various rooms. The cuisine here focuses on seasonal ingredients which are used to create personalised and imaginative dishes showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte. Interesting wine list, with a special emphasis on labels from the Trentino-Alto Adige region.

Name: GioEle
Description En: In the heart of the town, guests are received with professionalism and gracious warmth in a lively setting, carefully considered in its details and characterised by a measured elegance. The gastronomic offering moves within the tradition, reinterpreted with a contemporary sensitivity, alternating between dishes from the land and the sea. With the arrival of the warmer months, the experience is further enriched by tables set out in the pleasant internal courtyard or on the terrace, ideal for savouring the atmosphere to the full.

Name: Il Marchese - Osteria Mercato Liquori
Description En: Boasting a sumptuous Art Deco setting that contrasts pleasingly with the traditional cuisine served here, this restaurant is the Milanese sibling of Il Marchese in Rome which pays tribute to the famous Italian film “Il Marchese del Grillo” starring Alberto Sordi (it is also the first bar in Europe to offer more than 600 “amaro” liqueurs). The culinary philosophy here is based on traditional Roman cuisine with a contemporary flavour, including delicious specialities such as pasta with carbonara, matriciana and gricia sauces, veal saltimbocca, pork belly and much more besides!

Name: Azotea
Description En: In the very heart of the city, with a small terrace that sets the mood, the interior reveals deliberately aged walls in soft shades of green, enriched by climbing plants that evoke a corner of South American jungle. It is the ideal setting for Nikkei cooking that looks directly to Peru, the chef’s native land, and expresses itself through a range of beautifully fresh offerings available both à la carte and within carefully considered tasting menus. The philosophy is clear: to celebrate one of the most vibrant and contemporary gastronomic traditions, with a hand attuned to contrasts and the clarity of flavours. Among the distinctive features of the house, which also operates as a well-stocked cocktail bar, the sip pairing stands out: a sequence of small cocktail tastings crafted with ingredients typical of Nikkei cuisine, conceived to accompany the dishes without overpowering them. Not to be missed is the yuzu Americano, pleasingly citrus-forward, with a hint of sharpness that invites the next sip.

Name: Aria
Description En: The Villa Riviera resort home to this restaurant is situated slightly inland and uphill from the sea in a tranquil oasis of greenery. The modern, minimalist veranda-style dining room is welcoming and elegant, while the summer terrace has a romantic ambience with superb views of the coast, especially at sunset. The menu features modern, occasionally creative cuisine with Ligurian influences evident in dishes such as the “La mia Liguria” dessert which combines ingredients such as basil and olives with white chocolate, pine nuts and fiordilatte ice cream.

Name: Angiò-Macelleria di Mare
Description En: The phrase “macellaria di mare” translates as “fish and seafood butcher’s”, a reference to the cured and seasoned fish that features on the menu here. The restaurant has recently changed the way that guests order – you now make your way to your table in a simple yet attractive dining room with an open-view kitchen, where you choose from three tasting menus and à la carte. Our advice is to give young chef Alberto Angiolucci free rein!

Name: Musciora
Description En: ATTENTION: moved to number 77!The father-and-son team (chef and sommelier respectively) at this excellent restaurant not far from the town centre put heart and soul into their work, offering guests three tasting menus: one dedicated to fish and seafood; another to inland ingredients and meat; and the third, entitled “Completo”, simply offering a combination of the first two menus. The recipes are inspired by the island’s produce, which is prepared simply and with real skill. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the raw mullet tartare encased in a “fake” tomato made from tomato and raspberry jelly. The wine list also showcases Sardinia, with a focus on small-scale wineries, although bottles from elsewhere (including natural wines) also feature.

Name: MaMe Restaurant
Description En: Situated in central Viareggio near the town’s shipyards, MaMe occupies a long, narrow space that is reminiscent of Oriental restaurants with its long bench running alongside one wall and small bistro-style tables. This informal yet beautifully kept dining room is the backdrop for cuisine with interesting technical details such as the home-made mayonnaise served with the highly recommended steamed fish dish, and the delicious sourdough loaf which is freshly baked and served warm.

Name: ConTatto
Description En: Situated in a small town just a few kilometres from the capital, this restaurant run by two young food enthusiasts serves regional dishes with a modern touch, such as cuttlefish with asparagus and a Bernese sauce. Guests can visit the interesting tufa-rock cellar, where the chef experiments with old preserving techniques and special flavourings. In addition, the cellar is used as a venue for exhibitions by different art galleries every season.

Name: Soprattutto
Address: via Noalese 124, Santa Maria di Sala, 30036, Italy
Description En: This tiny, welcoming restaurant with a bright, simple decor has long since come of age, having been opened and run by the same family for years. The wife supervises the front of house, while the husband (whose past experience includes working as a metalworker as well as a chef) is at the helm in the kitchen, where he creates classic fish dishes which are full of flavour and simply prepared from top-quality ingredients. As the restaurant is very popular with its regular clientele, booking in advance is essential – you won’t be disappointed!

Name: La Pista
Address: Centro Commerciale Lingotto - via Nizza 262, Turin, 10126, Italy
Description En: The top floor of the Lingotto shopping center – a quintessential Turin landmark, once a Fiat factory whose rooftop test track has been transformed into a visitable botanical garden – is the site of an easily reached restaurant thanks to clear signage at the entrance. Once seated, guests may choose from four tasting menus (all available à la carte): the Piedmontese tradition of Radici, the contemporary restraint of Gli Essenziali, the vegetarian Botanic World and the creative Zero/100 km/h, as well as Trust, a ‘blind’ journey guided by the kitchen’s sensitivity. Whichever the choice, the experience turns out to be convincing: solid, harmonious dishes with clear, perfectly-calibrated flavors.

Name: Gallo Nero
Description En: Just a short distance from Campo, at the boundary of the Leocorno contrada, the restaurant settles at the foot of a medieval tower: a thirteenth-century structure that once served as an armoury and which today, following a careful restoration, receives its guests in surroundings enriched by design furnishings from the 1950s and 1970s. It is here that the gastronomic offering of the Gallo Nero takes shape, with a cuisine that celebrates the Sienese tradition through meat dishes firmly rooted in the territory, set alongside vegetable creations and forays towards the sea. The cellar, nestled within an evocative Etruscan grotto carved from tufa, holds some 300 labels: a treasure conceived to accompany the journey through flavour.

Name: Il Mirto
Description En: When you arrive at the luxury Botania hotel, you’ll be accompanied through 3ha grounds of lush Mediterranean vegetation to the restaurant. You couldn’t have a better introduction to the cuisine that awaits at Il Mirto, where you can choose between two long tasting menus or a shorter four-course option featuring dishes from these menus. One of the menus is vegetarian, the other vegan and almost all the vegetables are sourced from the property’s own kitchen garden or from other local growers from Ischia. A delightful experience in a beautiful natural setting, with excellent service provided by young, friendly staff.

Name: Hydra
Description En: Situated in the picturesque historic centre of Salerno, this is one of the city’s best restaurants. The dining room here is almost minimalist in style, yet thanks to the soft lighting and beautiful background music it has a pleasing atmosphere; in fine weather, tables are set out in a charming inner courtyard. The cuisine is Mediterranean and contemporary, with a selection of light and creative meat, fish and vegetable dishes featuring on the menu.

Name: iPalici
Address: via Antonello da Messina 3, Viagrande, 95029, Italy
Description En: Situated behind Acireale at the foot of Mount Etna National Park, this restaurant is located within the Relais San Giuliano. Deceptively uninteresting from the outside, this historic building and its inner courtyards boast a charm and grandeur that will take your breath away. A huge 16C wine press provides the backdrop for fine cuisine that is more than equal to its impressive setting. Here, the menu makes full use of vegetables and other Sicilian ingredients in dishes that are influenced by the island’s culinary traditions yet reinterpreted with a skilful contemporary twist by the chef.

Name: Donevandro
Description En: Up until a few years ago, the owner-chef at this restaurant was working as a painter – a fact that is evident from the artistic touch in his cuisine. His recipes are modern and personalised, with careful attention naturally paid to harmonious presentation, while the flavour of his dishes is brought out by ingredients that are skilfully chosen from the Abruzzo inland area. In 2024, the restaurant moved to new, centrally located premises which have an intimate feel and are elegant and minimalist in style.

Name: Dry Aged
Address: via Cesare Da Sesto 1/A, Milan, 20123, Italy
Description En: Two partners with significant experience opened this lively venue: the rooms combine modern and classic styles in an industrial-New York style decorated with works by major street artists. At the entrance, the glass counter shows off meats of different breeds to be enjoyed even charcoal grilled, but there are also other specialties: appealing dishes with a modern preparation and homemade pastas.

Name: Mirepuà Food Lab
Description En: Situated in a picturesque medieval village in the Monferrato hills, this restaurant serves classic Piedmontese cuisine with plenty of meat options, alongside a few specialties from the chef’s native Liguria, including fish and seafood dishes.

Name: Antica Farmacia
Description En: As its name suggests, this restaurant was used as a pharmacy until the late 1970s. In 2010, it was taken over by owner-chef Juri who now runs his own restaurant here, serving Tuscan-inspired cuisine made using local ingredients and recipes which he reinterprets with a light touch. Full of flavour, dishes include highlights such as baked marrow and Tuscan Chianti beef stew.

Name: Gimmi Restaurant
Address: via San Pietro in Lama 23, Lecce, 73100, Italy
Description En: The building is a former Dominican monastery dating back to 1442, which also houses a boutique hotel. The restaurant, on the other hand, is decidedly modern and furnished in a minimalist style: light-coloured floors, mighty stone columns, vaulted ceilings and a room with a view of the wine cabinet. The service is very efficient, attentive and friendly, and the cuisine reaches high levels. Among the most recommended specialities are palamita with fennel tarallo, burrata, salad, bell pepper extract, tarragon oil, and among the main courses the grilled snapper, its extract with saffron pistils, artichoke and provolone mousse.

Name: Caffè delle Rose Bistrot
Description En: Occupying an early 20C building in the heart of Pallanza’s picturesque historic centre, this authentic bistro now has a young and contemporary feel. Run by Massimiliano Celeste, a talented chef who is very well known in the region, the restaurant specialises in Mediterranean cuisine prepared with a touch of imagination. There’s a small chef’s table in front of the kitchen, plus an old ice-house (now a small wine cellar housing some excellent wines) which is well worth visiting.

Name: Artifex
Description En: This restaurant is situated within the Feuerstein Nature Family Resort, a 5-star property which continues to expand and which nestles in the verdant Val di Fleres, not far from Vipiteno and even closer to the Austrian border. In the small, elegant dining room here, the focus is on creative, regional cuisine, with dishes often accompanied by herbs and vegetables sourced from the property’s own kitchen garden where they are grown without the use of chemicals. Top-quality seasonal ingredients take pride of place in the cuisine here, while the well-stocked wine cellar features a good selection of labels decanted in the dining room by the talented sommelier.

Name: Specus
Description En: This charming restaurant’s name comes from the Latin and refers to the small grotto carved out of the tufa rock in the courtyard, which is home to just a few tables. The restaurant is run by a young couple, with Flavia front of house and Alessio at the helm in the kitchen.
