The café offers tables arranged outdoors in the extraordinary Galleria and is open seven days a week but does not take bookings.

Name: Luciano Cucina Italiana
Address: piazza del Teatro di Pompeo 18, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description En: It is said that one of the capital’s finest carbonaras is served here, and we can only agree: no small feat, given the dish’s sacred status in Rome. But the experience at Luciano Monosilio extends far beyond his famous signature; the menu offers other equally compelling preparations that strike a balance between deep Lazio roots and flashes of measured creativity, always delivering intense, well-defined flavors. In the basement, adjacent to the pasta laboratory, Veleno provides the ideal setting for an aperitivo or intriguing cocktail pairings. A new lounge area now also welcomes guests on the upper floor, rounding out a dining and mixology program designed for a fully immersive experience.

Name: Casa Perrotta Restaurant
Description En: This small, welcoming restaurant with a hint of minimalism and just a few tables serves personalised meat and fish dishes which aim to offer something a little different, with a choice of three tasting menus and an à la carte. Having previously gained experience outside the area, the young family team from Campania runs the restaurant with enthusiasm and a real love for the region’s cuisine.

Name: Evo Ristorante
Description En: This restaurant at the entrance to the historic centre boasts a delightful garden which leads to a porch where tables are set out in summer – an enchanting setting that feels as though you’re eating in the countryside despite the village location. The chefs’ imagination knows no bounds in complex and elaborate dishes that focus on ingredients from Puglia and are grouped into themed tasting menus.

The name of this restaurant refers to the year in which the hotel in which it is located (the Park Hotel Holzner) was opened, while the design is a nod to the Liberty style of the period. Despite this, both the ambience and the cuisine bear the modern and imaginative hallmark of Stephan Zippl. Paying careful attention to sustainability, this chef selects the best regional produce for his dishes – even the Wagyu beef is raised in the chef’s native Renon region. This strong connection with the Alto Adige is also evident on the excellent wine list, which features almost 400 labels from the region and provides perfect pairings for the chef’s tasting menu. Other options include non-alcoholic drinks such as apple juice and alcohol-free cocktails.

Name: Henri Restaurant
Description En: Having returned to his native Viareggio in 2021, Henri Prosperi, a gracious maître in the old-school tradition, will guide you with style and professionalism in choosing dishes that blend classic and modern approaches, with a penchant for some French influences. The menu, divided between meat and fish, always focuses on premium ingredients, the same character that distinguishes the wine cellar, rich with great national and international labels, from Sassicaia to Petrus, including the finest Italian and French sparkling wines. An open kitchen and outdoor seating!

Name: AceroRosso
Address: Via Ruvignan 1, Vodo di Cadore, 32040, Italy
Description En: This secluded mountain chalet immersed in verdant woodland boasts a welcoming dining room with a decidedly Alpine feel thanks to the profusion of wood and a warming open fire. The cuisine is also regional in style, featuring local recipes and ingredients albeit with a contemporary touch. Popular dishes include the rack of lamb cooked at low temperature and served with creamed sweetcorn, leek fondant and its own jus.

Name: Faletta 1881
Description En: Nestled among the hills of Monferrato and surrounded by its vineyards, this lovingly restored historic farmhouse offers an authentic welcome. The kitchen is dominated by Piedmontese tradition, with some modern touches and national flourishes. Be sure to try the trio of antipasti. The wine list is entirely house‑selected, featuring a Grignolino that deserves attention. Cozy rooms and a salt‑water pool complete the experience.

Name: Il Cavallo Scosso
Description En: A young and modern restaurant situated in a residential area about 2km from the centre, where owner-chef Enrico Pivieri offers a menu that is equally divided between traditional meat-based dishes from Piedmont (some, such as the plin pasta, are very traditional in style while others have a more reinterpreted feel) and more creative fish-based options. The chef gives full rein to his creativity in dishes such as the Mediterranean fish ceviche with avocado, passion fruit gel and sea-urchin mayonnaise.

Name: Teresita by Giardino di Mari
Description En: Among the finest seafood restaurants in the area, it enjoys a privileged position directly on the Viareggio promenade, a few steps from the sea, with an outdoor terrace particularly pleasant to enjoy during the warmer months. In the kitchen is a chef of undoubted talent, capable of ensuring raw materials of exceptional quality combined with sound, personal technique. Among the signature dishes stand out the octopus alla plancia with panissa and tomato chutney, as well as the salt cod in breadstick crust accompanied by chickpea cream and sautéed cavolo nero. In the dining room, courtesy and professionalism are very much in evidence, supported by an extensive and well-chosen wine list, rich in interesting labels.

Name: La Piemontese
Address: via San Martino 48, Mariano Comense, 22066, Italy
Description En: The focus at La Piemontese, a simple yet modern restaurant with a convenient car park, is mainly on meat dishes, although game and fresh truffles also feature in season, plus there’s a generous business menu at lunchtime. An enjoyable dining experience that offers good value for money.

Name: Shiroya
Description En: In the heart of the historic centre, this authentic Japanese restaurant well frequented by an Oriental clientele offers an intimate and carefully considered experience: covers are few, both inside and on the pleasant street terrace, which makes a reservation warmly advisable. A courteous welcome and professional service accompany an offering that traverses the great classics of the Japanese tradition: hand-made gyoza with various fillings, tempura and other fried preparations executed with precision, raw fish in the most canonical combinations, ramen, rice in various preparations and much more besides. To drink, alongside both craft and mainstream beers, saké, tea and Japanese spirits such as shōchū, a selection of wines is also available for those who prefer to remain on familiar ground.

Name: Vescovo Moro
Description En: Situated 50 metres from the basilica of San Zeno (the patron saint of Verona), this restaurant housed in a renovated workshop boasts plenty of outdoor space for summer dining. Here, enjoy eclectic cuisine with an equal balance of Mediterranean and traditional flavours, including an excellent array of raw fish dishes and a small selection of Italian caviar.

Name: Enoteca di Buttrio
Description En: Housed in a beautiful historic building, this business, originally a wine bar (hence the name “enoteca”), gradually developed into a restaurant over the years. The menu focuses uniquely on fish, almost all of which comes from the Adriatic, showcased in traditional dishes enhanced with a creative twist.

Name: Osteria 1861
Address: via Valentino Izzo 1, Santa Maria di Castellabate, 84048, Italy
Description En: Accessed via a narrow alleyway behind the beach, this restaurant housed in an old warehouse once used for smoking cured meats and drying Cilento figs boasts stone-vaulted ceilings, a romantic ambience and a small terrace embellished by beautiful plants. Chef Antoni Tafuri’s cuisine features on various tasting menus (including vegetarian and vegan) and an à la carte and demonstrates careful combinations that aim to showcase his regional ingredients to the full.

Name: Il Marchese - Osteria Mercato Liquori
Description En: Convivial and informal with a touch of elegance, this restaurant is perfect for a night out with friends – and indeed for anyone in the mood for delicious cuisine brimming with flavours which are predominantly Roman in style. The carbonara and amatriciana are superb, while the antipasti (especially the croquettes and artichoke in season) should not be missed. An impressive selection of cocktails completes the picture. Booking is recommended, as it’s often full!

Name: Voce Aimo e Nadia
Description En: Situated in the heart of Milan, this restaurant owned by the historic Aimo e Nadia in Via Montecuccoli is accessed via its bar-cum-pastry shop which includes a bistro serving a selection of simpler dishes. From here, you enter the main dining room with an open-view kitchen serving excellent Italian dishes reinterpreted in contemporary style. Voce in Giardino, the restaurant’s outdoor summer dining space adorned with interesting sculptures, is a green oasis in the heart of the city.

Name: Locanda Solagna
Description En: Although this restaurant has been in business since the 1950s, it feels much more modern thanks to its updated appearance. Renowned for its excellent regional cuisine served in the evening, the restaurant pays careful attention to seasonal ingredients. At lunchtime, the ”osteria”-style menu is much simpler. Excellent wine selection.

Name: Spoon
Description En: Located in the heart of the historic centre, just a stone’s throw from the beautiful 13C cathedral, this small, simple restaurant with an outdoor space is home to owner-chef Marco Cozzi, whose cuisine is the main attraction here. Having trained with Niko Romito, this chef creates dishes from seasonal, regional ingredients, reinterpreting traditional recipes to give them a contemporary flavour (for example, he transforms pancotto into a cream of bread and Navelli saffron, which he then crowns with Robiola cheese, cime di rapa and triangles of cured pork loin). His two tasting menus focus entirely on meat and feature an impressive selection of vegetables.

Name: Santamonica
Description En: Head down a small street along Corso Italia in the Albaro neighborhood toward the beach, where both the interior dining room and summer terrace offer sweeping sea views. The majority of the menu’s ingredients come directly from those waters (half a page is dedicated to raw preparations). The chef ventures into modern recipes with an emphasis on striking final presentations.

Name: Meta Ristorante
Address: via Generale Pescetto 5, Celle Ligure, 17015, Italy
Description En: Situated in the picturesque historic centre of Celle, this old boathouse with a typical brick ceiling is now home to an excellent gourmet restaurant, where a young chef creates some of the most interesting dishes in the region.

Name: Osteria il Moro
Description En: Boasting an attractive outdoor space on Trapani’s main street, Osteria il Moro focuses on dishes that are deeply rooted in Sicilian tradition yet enhanced by original and creative touches, resulting in cuisine that is full of flavour and personality thanks to owner-chef Nicola Bandi. The menu features plenty of fish dishes as well as meat, including beef fillet in a red sauce with spices and wild herbs, and Trapani-style mullet. The impressive wine list includes a good selection of regional labels.

Name: Hostaria da Franz
Address: salizada Sant'Antonin, sestiere Castello 3499, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description En: Founded in a different venue by an Austrian soldier in the late 19C, this historic Venetian restaurant is now run by owner Maurizio, who oversees the front of house in a courteous yet friendly manner. He introduces guests to its variety of dishes, which aim to please rather than surprise. Fish specialities are to the fore here.

Name: Cascina Vittoria
Description En: Situated in a rural setting surrounded by rice fields outside Milan, this restaurant specialises in home-made pasta and breads, vegetables grown in its own garden, and Piedmontese meat cooked in traditional fashion over a barbecue grill. Takeaway produce is also available for purchase.

Name: Cortile Pepe
Description En: Among the narrow streets of the historic center between the Cathedral and the sea, under ancient arches or in the pleasant outdoor area, the chef offers regional cuisine revisited with refined, modern technique, expressed in colorful, precise, and appealing presentations. Warmth and excellent hospitality form the foundation of impeccable service.

Name: Bianca sul Lago
Description En: In the elegant setting of Bianca Relais, the restaurant’s glass walls offer a romantic view of Lake Annone, with the sun setting behind it over the hills. In the kitchen, Andrea Cannalire creates elaborate and imaginative dishes; here and there, some ingredients from his Apulian origins peek through, and the result is remarkable. A restaurant not to be missed if you’re in the area.

Name: Mirabelle
Address: via di Porta Pinciana 14, Rome, 00187, Italy
Description En: From the penultimate floor of the Hotel Splendide Royal, guests enjoy an extraordinary view, among the most breathtaking in the capital at sunset, sweeping across Villa Medici, Trinità dei Monti, St. Peter’s, and the Janiculum Hill. For an even more dramatic setting, simply ascend one level to Adèle, a lounge bar welcoming guests for aperitifs and atmospheric after-dinner drinks. In the kitchen, a modern approach built on solid classical foundations, generous in its combinations and attuned to the seasons, with both meat and seafood offerings. A venue that has become iconic in Roman fine dining – in every sense of the word.

Name: Chat Qui Rit
Address: calle Tron, sestiere San Marco 1131, Venice, 30124, Italy
Description En: “Lagoon fusion” cuisine awaits you at this historic restaurant just a short walk from St. Mark's Square: generous, colourful dishes prepared with meticulous attention to detail and love for the local area, but without neglecting a few forays into the Orient, a passion of one of the two Venetian chefs. The menu features mainly seafood and, depending on the season, some really interesting locally caught fish with lots of personality. The excellent wine list includes some rare vintage and collectible wines.

Name: La Cucina de' Mibabbo
Description En: Exposed brickwork and lots of wood create a rustic, refined and welcoming atmosphere. Tuscan cuisine takes centre stage here, from the excellent charcuterie selection to the famous Florentine T-bone steak. When the weather warms up, a small covered terrace on the pavement offers the pleasure of al fresco dining.

Name: Tenuta Casa Virginia
Address: via Cascina Violo 1, Villa d'Almè, 24018, Italy
Description En: Surrounded by the property’s own vineyards, this restaurant nestlings at the bottom of a gentle hill features an elegant dining room and a beautiful terrace for outdoor dining in fine weather. The cuisine is contemporary (yet not excessively so), with a few freshwater fish also featuring on the menu, while the wine list showcases a good selection of wines. The property’s own wines are available for purchase in the shop.

Name: Il Molo
Address: via Aganor Pompili 9, Passignano sul Trasimeno, 06065, Italy
Description En: Situated in the historic centre of Passignano, where the village seems to jut out into Lake Trasimeno (some tables in the main dining room boast views of the lake – make sure you book in advance), Il Molo has been run by the Pellegrini family since 1978. The restaurant has become a popular choice for guests keen to try top-quality fish from the lake as well as excellent poultry dishes, with dishes showcased on an à la carte and three tasting menus. We highly recommend the herb bottoni pasta with sunfish and saffron butter. There’s also a good choice of sparkling wines and champagnes.

Name: Eggentaler
Description En: Just three kilometers from Bolzano and equally close to the highway exit, this restaurant boasts over a century of history and has been expertly run by the Schmieder family for more than forty years. Such longevity speaks for itself: the establishment is a benchmark for enthusiasts of charcoal-grilled meats, the true specialty of the house. But the menu does not end there: alongside the carnivore mainstays, a modern Italian cuisine offering finds its place, spanning land and sea, with simple yet well-executed dishes such as prawns in spicy garlic oil served with bruschette. The wine list is equally commendable, curated directly by a family member. Completing the offering is a small hotel equipped with sauna and pool.

Name: [bu:r]
Description En: Eugenio Boer offers a 100% Italian menu which focuses on local ingredients, with the aim of showcasing some of Italy’s favourite dishes while at the same time supporting small-scale producers. However, this philosophy is in no way limited to respecting traditions – on the contrary, it offers the chef the freedom to express his own creativity via a selection of dishes which combine past and present. As a result, guests can choose between a concise à la carte and two different tasting menus: “I Classici” (meat-based dishes) and “Le Aromatiche”, which changes perspective by placing aromatic plants centre stage. In short, a flexible approach which offers guests a culinary experience that will certainly make an impression!

Name: Osteria Il Cappello
Description En: The outdoor terrace at this restaurant overlooks a pleasant pedestrian piazza in the historic centre, while the welcoming dining rooms are decorated in a style typical of the Trentino. The cuisine – reliable, seasonal and full of flavour – is traditionally Italian, yet with a contemporary touch. The menu also features a few regional options as well as the occasional fish dish. The quail stuffed with acacia honey, pumpkin purée and stewed radicchio is superb.

Name: Osteria Europa
Description En: Despite its simple appearance, this restaurant housed in the hotel of the same name serves interesting, traditional cuisine which is well prepared and full of flavour.

Name: Casa Perbellini 12 Apostoli
Address: vicolo Corticella San Marco 3, Verona, 37121, Italy
Description En: Verona’s quintessential historic and elegant restaurant, this is where Chef Perbellini, already two-starred at a previous location, achieved the coveted three stars. Expect a sumptuous, refined setting, rich with color and historical references, paired with extraordinary cuisine expressed through three tasting menus, with dishes also available à la carte. “Io e Silvia” showcases the chef’s latest creations; choose “L’Essenza” for a vegetarian journey; while “Storie di Casa” presents the chef’s signature dishes in a contemporary key. But there is yet another option: the chef’s table, in effect a separate room with five intimate tables set amid the open kitchen, featuring a single menu and the exhilarating experience of dining among the cooks.

Name: Uliassi
Description En: From being the perfect star of summer holiday postcards, the Adriatic Riviera becomes a painting or, if you prefer, an artistic film, thanks to Mauro Uliassi's captivating interpretation. The restaurant seems to be almost hidden and camouflaged among the beach establishments that crowd the coast of Senigallia: one would never expect to find a 3-Michelin-starred restaurant tucked away between beach umbrellas and the waves that lap the shore. The strength and originality of this cuisine lies precisely in its consistency in offering only the very best, starting with locally-sourced ingredients, with the courage to draw on and engage with the best-known and most familiar gastronomic traditions, those that have made this coast so popular, while giving them a creative and personal interpretation. The restaurant, which has been in business since 1990, has put together a series of classics that form the backbone of the menu, such as smoked spaghetti, clams and roasted date tomatoes, Marchigiana-style wood pigeon and the Senigallia-Brest dessert. Those who prefer the chef's newest creations can choose the Lab tasting menu and, last but by no means least, fans of game can opt for the hunting menu.

Name: La Rei Natura by Michelangelo Mammoliti
Description En: This young yet already established Piedmontese chef, of part-Calabrian heritage, offers a creative and personal cuisine deeply anchored in its raw materials, particularly vegetables, the majority of which are sourced from his own kitchen gardens and greenhouses, managed according to biodynamic principles.Three tasting menus are available, from which individual dishes may also be chosen à la carte: De Rerum, comprising ten courses, presents the most complete and current expression of the chef’s vision; MAD 100% Natura places the plant world at the very centre, with animal protein in a discreet supporting role; and Voyage, which conveys bolder flavours reflecting the influences gathered during his international experiences. Among the dishes, the red mullet fillet in valenciana sauce stands out for its intensity and precision. The gastronomic offering finds its natural counterpoint in an outstanding wine list: in the heart of the Langhe, Barolo reigns supreme, presented in an extensive selection of crus and vintages. A young, dynamic, and efficient front-of-house team contributes to making the overall experience harmonious and engaging.

Name: Enrico Bartolini al Mudec
Description En: In his Milanese restaurant, the headquarters of the Bartolini international galaxy, the great chef – far from taking a break – continues to craft new dishes alongside resident chef Davide Boglioli, always focusing on fullness and intensity of flavors. There's nothing overly cerebral, though you can delve into the layers, references, and echoes if you wish. Or simply enjoy the perfect balance of the results. There are two tasting options: "Best Of" and "Mudec Experience," but dishes can also be selected à la carte. During our last visit, we were particularly struck by the creaminess and harmony of the beetroot risotto with “Evoluzione” gorgonzola sauce. And speaking of cheeses, we recommend trying (off-menu) "Our Tasting of 5 Creative Cheeses," with rare and intriguing pairings. All of this is set on the third floor of Mudec, the Museum of Cultures, in a refined and elegantly contemporary lounge space.

Name: Osteria Francescana
Description En: On arriving in Via Stella, one immediately senses how naturally this restaurant frees itself from frills and accolades, embracing instead a sober elegance, enhanced by major works of contemporary art that reflect Massimo Bottura’s personal passion. The same measured language returns in the kitchen, where greatness is expressed through control, balance and vision: a narrative that begins in Modena and Emilia before reaching towards the great international classics, reinterpreted by the chef with that playful lightness which reminds us that food should first and foremost be pleasure, memory and culture. The most innovative tasting menu of the moment, Miseria e Nobiltà, takes its inspiration from Eduardo De Filippo’s celebrated work and offers a journey that elevates essential ingredients and “humble” resources with surprising refinement. Among the emblematic dishes, Jazz Duck stands out: duck presented in several preparations to showcase every part of the bird, served alongside an unusual glazed panettone that perfectly completes its intensity. Alternatively, guests may choose from the à la carte menu, which features some of the chef’s great classics: “An eel swimming up the River Po”, Modenese tortellini in a silky 36-month Parmigiano Reggiano sauce, and hot-and-cold zuppa inglese, together with the finest dishes from tasting menus of years past. The wine list, exceptionally rich in outstanding labels, nevertheless also includes lesser-known bottles, the result of research into small producers capable of telling the stories of often unfamiliar places and terroirs, rounding off a gastronomic experience that unites local identity, curiosity and great culinary culture.

Name: Le Calandre
Address: via Liguria 1, località Sarmeola, Rubano, 35030, Italy
Description En: Leaving the provincial road and commercial zone behind, one enters the fabulous world of Le Calandre and the Alajmo family: soft lighting – achieved even by day – serves almost as a design element in the pared-back dining room, conceived by brothers Massimiliano and Raffaele, who also designed most of the porcelain used in service. The offering unfolds through three tasting menus: Classico, Max, and Raf, with the generous option to mix them freely or compose a meal as if ordering à la carte. Suspended between comforting flavors and whimsical touches, Max’s cuisine occasionally references itself through restaurant classics, such as the cuttlefish cappuccino in squid ink alongside the more modern Murrina version, an homage to the famed island of Murano and its colorful blown glass. The inspector recommends: Suono N'uovo, a tagliatella whose dough incorporates specially treated eggshell, adding an unexpected and delightful crunch.

Name: Quattro Passi
Description En: Temporarily closed.This restaurant’s 40-year-old history began with talented owner-chef Fabrizio Mellino’s grandfather, who ran a small business selling eggs from his own hens. From this, he decided to branch out and open a pizzeria “four steps” (“A Quattro Passi”) from the sea. Over time, his son Antonio transformed the pizzeria into a temple to Mediterranean cuisine, achieving two Michelin stars in the process. This compelling story continued with the arrival of Fabrizio, who had spent many years travelling (especially in France) and gaining valuable experience as a chef. The restaurant soon become legendary in southern Italy, becoming the first restaurant to achieve three Michelin stars in Campania for many years. A focus on flavour, skilful culinary techniques and top-quality ingredients results in sublime cuisine that is typical of Sorrento and Campania. A perfect example is the “squid flower”, which boasts spectacular presentation and exciting, well-balanced flavours using just a few carefully chosen ingredients – the squid is transformed into dozens of petals and served with raw scampi tartare and caviar. It’s not an easy journey to Marina del Cantone, but once here you’ll be warmly welcomed by the chef’s brother Raffaele, who oversees the wine cellar and front of house, and his team, after which you can sit back and enjoy a truly memorable dining experience.

Name: Villa Crespi
Address: via Fava 18, Orta San Giulio, 28016, Italy
Description En: A short walk from the fairytale village and its postcard-perfect view of the lake and the island of San Giulio, the setting of this three-star restaurant is no less dazzling: a late nineteenth-century villa in Moorish style, an aristocratic dwelling where the Crespi family life unfolded, as imposing in its exterior appearance as it is fascinating in its interior rooms. Here the veranda offers glimpses and plays of natural light, while the other three rooms are embellished with elaborate ceilings and marvelous parquet floors. Today the star of the villa is Antonino Cannavacciuolo, a brilliant chef at the head of a small empire of starred restaurants, who here in Orta San Giulio has his flagship: the most awarded and celebrated establishment! From Vico Equense in Campania, over the years his dishes have become the quintessence of Mediterranean and Italian taste. In all offerings you’ll find that passion, those colors and that intensity of flavors typical of his region of origin, which we are grateful he has never abandoned. In the two tasting menus, as well as in the extensive à la carte menu, an uninterrupted fil rouge of refinement and goodness flows generously through seafood, meat, and even vegetarian recipes. You’ll be pampered by service that runs like a metronome, supported in turn by a profound wine list, where two chapters of great importance dedicated to Krug and Domaine de la Romanée-Conti stand out.

Name: La Pergola
Description En: The new Pergola, following meticulous refurbishment, welcomes guests into surroundings that seem to breathe with the city: the hues of travertine, reflections of Roman red, soft light gliding across surfaces echo the soul of the capital and transform it into atmosphere. The terrace, too, has been renewed, yet the true spectacle remains unchanged: Rome, as evening falls, spreads silently at the foot of Monte Mario, a sea of rooftops and domes appearing suspended, as if holding its breath. At the stoves since 1994, Heinz Beck continues to drive his cooking towards new sensitivities, moving effortlessly between classic elegance and contemporary creativity. Many preparations are completed and finished directly at the table, releasing aromas and gestures that add theatre to the moment: vapours, textures, small details that come to life before the guest’s eyes, rendering the experience yet more immersive. In his pursuit of healthfulness and lightness, Beck deepens techniques and studies, selecting sustainable ingredients and transforming them with an almost scientific rigour, giving rise to dishes that are lucid, calibrated, vibrant in flavour yet delicate in structure. This is cooking that speaks to the palate but also to the mind, with intelligence and luminosity. Completing the journey, the extraordinary wine list finds in sommelier Marco Reitano a flawless interpreter: a master in the art of pairing, he welcomes guests with a smile and rare expertise, truly adding that finishing touch that renders the evening unforgettable.

Name: Dal Pescatore
Description En: Three-starred since 1996 – a record in Italy – and approaching its centenary, this restaurant is an unmissable landmark for understanding the history of Italian gastronomy. In Runate, a small hamlet in the countryside between Cremona and Mantua, a family osteria of long standing has been transformed into a place of rare elegance and genuine hospitality. In the dining room, Antonio Santini, flanked by his family, welcomes guests with warmth, while in the kitchen a tradition of rigour, sensitivity and continuity is lovingly perpetuated. The interiors, balanced between memory and contemporaneity, create a refined atmosphere in which space and light enhance every detail. The menu celebrates great dishes that have traversed the decades, evolving with quiet discretion and never yielding to fashion, in constant pursuit of pleasure at the table. Among the specialities, roasts and braises – using meats from the Cascina Runate – stand alongside emblematic preparations such as the Petit Gris snails of the plain with herb and sweet garlic sauce. The desserts merit particular mention: united by a measured indulgence, they strike a perfect balance between intensity and refinement, embodying the most accomplished meeting of pleasure and elegance. The meringues with pistachio and almond mousse and Marsala zabaione are irresistible, and display great harmony throughout.

Name: Da Vittorio
Description En: Now among the most celebrated restaurants in Italy, Da Vittorio has retained the warmth of its delightfully familial management. Both in the kitchen and in the dining room, members of the Cerea family are ever-present, and the dishes themselves speak to their talent for elevating top-quality ingredients into beautifully presented, deeply flavorful recipes, all in pursuit of a comforting, satisfying style of cooking. Generosity is another hallmark here, evident from the breadth of the offering! In addition to the à la carte menu, guests may choose from 4 tasting menus: “Gli esordi di papà Vittorio” (eight meat-based courses inspired by traditional recipes), “Dalla nostra campagna” (eight courses centered on vegetables from the estate garden and the Planet Farm), “Senza Confini” (twelve courses for a singular experience, guided by the chefs’ unfettered creative freedom), “Nella tradizione di Vittorio” (eight courses featuring fish and shellfish, prepared with the freshest market arrivals). The finale is elevated further by a superb cheese trolley and an array of sucreries to close the meal on a high note.

Name: Enoteca Pinchiorri
Description En: In the world of fine dining, Via Ghibellina is synonymous with Enoteca Pinchiorri: the magnificent seventeenth-century palazzo that houses it is home to one of the most iconic restaurants in Italy, a true legend of gastronomy. Opened in 1972 by Annie Féolde and Giorgio Pinchiorri, what began as a modest wine shop with a kitchen has over time become a great restaurant, in which Florentine history and elegance intertwine among paintings, frescoes and vivid arrangements of fresh flowers. At the stove, the cooking aspires to a refinement free of ostentation, eschewing fleeting fashions in favour of luxurious ingredients and a profound Italian identity, its flavours at once intense and rounded, destined to linger long in the memory. A fundamental role is played by the pastry kitchen, where Francesco Federici produces extraordinary desserts, among them the indispensable soufflé. In the dining room, an impeccable crew is led by the experienced Alessandro Tomberli, a historic figure at the Enoteca. And the wine cellar? A unique and quite simply mythological treasure, completing one of the most celebrated and cherished gastronomic experiences the country has to offer.

Name: Reale
Address: contrada Santa Liberata, località Casadonna, Castel di Sangro, 67031, Italy
Description En: On the first hilly slopes that embrace the village, amidst vineyards and silent gardens, the austere simplicity of the former 16th century monastery perfectly reflects the culinary language of one of the most recognisable fine dining experiences in Italy. Niko Romito continues to define - and refine - his vision here: a rigorous minimalism that never relinquishes sensory depth, expressed through dishes based on the measured use of just a few ingredients – be they vegetables or proteins – orchestrated with almost ascetic precision.The research continues relentlessly, as does the link with Abruzzo: products, recipes and culinary heritage come together in a constant drive towards evolution, keeping all the intensity of flavour and clarity on the palate intact.The bread and the entire range of baked goods are excellent, as always. The result of the almost maniacal selection of flours, long and carefully controlled proving times, and a bakery dedicated exclusively to doughs and breads of all kinds. The bread is so carefully crafted that it could almost be considered a course in its own right, capable of conveying the establishment’s methods and philosophy all on its own.

Name: Piazza Duomo
Address: vicolo dell'Arco 1, angolo piazza Risorgimento 4, Alba, 12051, Italy
Description En: The now famous red door ushers you into this temple of Italian cuisine. Once you cross the threshold, stairs lead up to the first floor, where pink walls and a fresco by Francesco Clemente welcome you, as do the friendly front-of-house staff. From here on, the focus is on chef Enrico Crippa's very personal cuisine, presented in three tasting menus (a fourth, shorter menu is available at lunchtime only): one linked closely to the vegetable gardens and the seasons, another intimately connected to the local area, and the last taking you on a journey through Italy and beyond. What emerges from every single delicious mouthful is the chef's passion for the plant world: vegetables, flowers and aromatic herbs, both cultivated and wild, are harvested daily and used to create memorable and aesthetically perfect dishes. The iconic appetiser, with its thousand and one delicious ingredients, continues to delight the eyes of the Inspectors. It goes without saying that we are in a land with a passionate love of wine, and indeed there are three whole volumes dedicated to it: Solopiemonte is a superb tribute to the region, while Tuttoilresto (divided into red and white wines) celebrates France. Simply put, the wine list is so extensive and varied that it alone is reason enough to visit the restaurant. And if you prefer to order by the glass, let yourself be intrigued by Sorsi: a small selection offering themed tastings, to be enjoyed according to personal preference or following a menu-based flight, with each glass telling a different story.

Name: Atelier Moessmer Norbert Niederkofler
Address: via Walther Von der Vogelweide 17, Brunico, 39031, Italy
Description En: Situated in a vast historic park near the centre of Brunico, this restaurant occupies a villa that was once part of the Moessmer textile factory – to illustrate the fact, an interesting fabric book dating from the early 20C is displayed on a large central table in the dining room. Here, the chef’s “Cook the Mountain” philosophy takes centre stage with a focus on top-quality produce sourced from the surrounding mountains, and a seasonal approach which ensures that flavours and ingredients are always at their best. Dinner starts with delicious appetisers served in the small lounge, perhaps accompanied by an aperitif. Having enjoyed this delicious prelude, you then move to the dining room or to the counter with its stools facing the kitchen. Wherever you choose to sit, you continue with the chef’s single tasting menu – a series of superb dishes that confirm this chef from the Ahrntal valley as one of the masters of contemporary Italian cuisine.

Name: Glam Enrico Bartolini
Address: calle Tron, sestiere Santa Croce 1961, Venice, 30135, Italy
Description En: Set between quiet, narrow streets, the gate opens onto Palazzo Venart, one of Venice's most exclusive residences. This hotel has two gardens, one at the entrance and the other overlooking the Grand Canal, where guests can enjoy coffee and little cakes at the tables on the main floor of the building as a very elegant alternative. Meals, on the other hand, are served in a room where the papered walls tell the story of the Silk Route. The gastronomic journey at Glam is in the skilled hands of Donato Ascani, resident chef at the multi-starred Bartolini. Ascani's talent shines brilliantly in two tasting menus (with the additional possibility of choosing dishes à la carte, without following either of them). He creates a gastronomic experience of the highest level, making the most of aromatic herbs and vegetables from the lagoon, together with his expertise in preparing grilled dishes.

Name: Acquolina
Description En: Just steps from Piazza del Popolo, the elegant First Roma welcomes guests with courteous, impeccable hospitality before leading them into a dining room of understated design, in keeping with contemporary taste, yet with tables still set with style and attentive service described as “dynamic” by its own team. At center stage is the cuisine of Daniele Lippi, who interprets the Mediterranean in its broadest sense, reaching well beyond national borders. Two tasting menus are offered: Periplo, dedicated to the aquatic world, and Anabasi Catabasi, which incorporates meat as well. Both conclude with a generous selection of desserts, the perfect finale to a gastronomic journey that is as intriguing as it is indulgent. Equally noteworthy is the wine offering, enhanced by an extensive list and the expertise of sommelier Francesco Aldieri.

Name: Seta by Antonio Guida
Address: via Monte di Pietà 18, Milan, 20121, Italy
Description En: Within the Mandarin Oriental, a symbol of Milanese luxury hospitality, Antonio Guida’s kitchen elegantly interprets the city’s cosmopolitan taste. Three tasting menus are offered: one dedicated to the chef’s classics, one to seasonality, and one to a single featured ingredient. In winter, dishes of great finesse come to the fore, from game to veal sweetbreads with cinnamon, through to a raspberry risotto, with desserts of a distinctly contemporary character. The wine list is of a high standard, available by the glass as well as by the bottle, and enhanced by magnums of notable vintages, alongside a thoughtful selection of non-alcoholic beverages for more moderate consumption. For after dinner, the Mandarin Garden next door to Seta confirms its place as one of Milan’s most exclusive late-night destinations, with signature cocktails and contemporary music setting the tone. The restaurant’s social engagement is worthy of note, with active involvement in education and inclusion projects.

Name: La Peca
Description En: 2027 will mark forty years of business: a story made up of aromas, flavours and traditions, the story of the Portinari family, who have carved their name among the pillars of Venice's restaurant scene and beyond. Chef Nicola Portinari welcomes guests to La Peca with one clear goal: to give them pleasure, letting them choose freely from an extensive and inviting menu (for those who prefer a guided experience, there are three tasting menus, including a vegetarian option). Leafing through it, it is easy to be seduced by dishes that speak to the palate and the mind. His creations are technical, but never ostentatious: harmonies rich in flavour, without ever being contrived. It's always hard to choose because there's so much to tempt you: the ravioli filled with venison, wrapped in a delicate jelly, accompanied by mushrooms and completed with a clear, fragrant consommé, are unforgettable; for those who love game, the mallard is a tribute to the season, with variations that enhance its nobility. And then there is the dessert, which ends the journey with one last embrace: creme brulée and ancient citrus ravioli are the historic signature dish, but there are also surprising reinterpretations of classics such as the Sachertorte, made intriguing by peanuts and Ghital cheese ice cream, and the Mont Blanc, enhanced by a delicate hint of green tea. A monumental wine cellar with around two thousand labels and a generous selection of natural wines completes the experience.

Name: La Madia
Address: corso Filippo Re Capriata 22, Licata, 92027, Italy
Description En: Park in one of the streets near this restaurant and prepare yourself for a delightful journey through Sicily and its culinary traditions! Chef Pino Cuttaia, who is demonstrably in love with his native island, highlights his ingredients in a simple and unfussy way, as demonstrated by the shellfish pasta minestra and the black Nebrodi suckling pig with a tomato-based “sugo della Domenica” (Sunday gravy). The two small dining rooms with a modern and minimalist feel offer an attractive setting for this enjoyable culinary experience, enhanced by the elegant service provided by the experienced Vincenzo and his team. Wine-enthusiasts will appreciate the interesting selection of labels (including large bottles popular with connoisseurs) which, like the cuisine, has a Sicilian focus. We recommend the 2019 Baglio Cristo di Campobello Adènzia, a red wine with earthy notes and delightful finesse.

Name: Il Piccolo Principe
Description En: This is the gourmet restaurant of the iconic Grand Hotel Principe di Piemonte, the undisputed emblem of hospitality in Versilia. On the ground floor, an elegant contemporary-styled dining area unfolds, extending into an exclusive wing adorned with bespoke art and furniture. Talented chef Giuseppe Mancino—of Campanian origin—melds traditions with Tuscan ingredients in his dishes, reinventing them with flair and creativity, along with options from other regions. The choices oscillate between three tasting menus: a vegetarian one, another devoted to the chef’s classics, and lastly, the longer and more elaborate ‘experience’. Among the intriguing recipes, the pizzaiola-style red mullet, bitter herb risotto with zimino sauce, and cuttlefish ink mayonnaise stand out, not forgetting the sea steak. A special mention for the exceptional farro and rye flour bread.

Name: Torre del Saracino
Description En: From the coast road you take a series of hairpin bends down to Marina di Equa, the beach at Vico, where you will see this old fortified tower standing just a few metres from the sea. In the tower itself, with music playing in the background, guests can savour an aperitif accompanied by an extraordinary selection of imaginative antipasti that offer an introduction to the excellent cuisine that awaits. From here, you move into one of two dining elegant dining rooms decorated in vintage 1970s style which look out at Vesuvius and the Bay of Naples – the setting for a meal that will linger long in the memory. Gennaro Esposito is one of the best chefs in Campania, creating beautifully presented dishes of meat and fish (often in the same dish) that are not only delicious but also full of the colour and vitality of his region.

Name: Agli Amici
Description En: Serving signature cuisine, Agli Amici is one of the leading restaurants in Friuli-Venezia Giulia, a border region of diverse cultural influences that is teeming with top-quality ingredients. Many of these are showcased on two tasting menus (one of which is vegetarian), as well as a small à la carte selection of “piatti del cuore” featuring the restaurant’s classic favourites. Owner-chef Emanuele Scarello makes full use of the array of ingredients from the region’s pastureland, mountains and vegetable gardens, which he transforms into culinary works of art. His interesting use of Godia potatoes involves a modern reinterpretation of a local butter and sage dish using roots, apple and fermented turnips. Front of house, Michela is responsible for a young, close-knit and professional team of staff who ensure that guests are made to feel completely at home.

Name: Harry's Piccolo
Description En: In the historical center of Trieste, the majestic former stock exchange building has become the new gourmet address of chefs Matteo Metullio and Davide De Pra. Already awarded two stars in the city, the duo have created a spectacular open kitchen here, transforming it into an exciting stage for the few fortunate tables set before it. Three tasting menus are offered: one focused on meat, another on fish, and a third showcasing the restaurant’s signature classics, including the celebrated Harrysotto. Whichever path you choose, the cuisine of Matteo and Davide ranks among the most thrilling in the region – and beyond!

Name: St. George by Heinz Beck
Description En: One of the most desirable and exclusive locations in Taormina, the St. George is situated in The Ashbee Hotel, an early-20C villa on the edge of Taormina’s historic centre which has retained all the charm of a private house with its elegant lounge and breathtaking terrace adorned with palm trees that frame the Straits of Messina. The cuisine comes courtesy of a partnership between Heinz Beck and resident chef Salvatore Iuliano. The three-starred Michelin chef’s instinctive elegance and gastronomic intuition combine with Calabrian-born Salvatore’s passionate and colourful take on Mediterranean cuisine. Together, the cuisine and setting guarantee an unforgettable dining experience.

Name: Il Pagliaccio
Address: via dei Banchi Vecchi 129/a, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description En: In the heart of Rome, a true gastronomic journey without boundaries begins, articulated through different menus according to the experience chosen: from Circus, “an itinerary that knows no limits”, to Scintille, centred on essential flavours and creative gestures, through to Parallels, an exclusive experience served in a private room of even greater intimacy.Guiding this narrative is Anthony Genovese, cosmopolitan chef-patron of personal vision and crystalline talent, capable of surprising even in moments closest to tradition, such as the Tortello, evocative of childhood memories, or the original green tomato, caviar, and crème fraîche dessert.The experience unfolds in an elegant and intimate setting, sustained by service of the highest order: sommelier Luca Belleggia curates a wine list of some 2,000 labels with great expertise, supported by Veronica Loachamin, consistently impeccable and welcoming. Together, they create a dining room of precision, warmth, and great distinction.

Name: Locanda Sant'Uffizio Enrico Bartolini
Description En: Nestled amid the picturesque hills of the Monferrato region, this restaurant overseen by multi-Michelin-starred Enrico Bartolini sees Gabriele Boffa at the helm in the kitchen, a chef who is young in years but already a real connoisseur of Piedmontese cuisine. With experience in some of the world’s best restaurants behind him, Boffa has accumulated expert knowledge and remarkable technical skills. His cuisine ranges from classic regional dishes interpreted in their purest form – such as his extraordinary agnolotti del plin – to more creative options, which demonstrate a connection with the region, whether in their ingredients or recipes. The setting here is that of an old monastery converted into a smart hotel, with meals served either in an elegant dining room or in the old limonaia (where lemon trees were once stored). The dishes on offer will linger long in the memory, from the generous amuses-bouches to the delicious bread and incredible focaccia, the top-quality meat and much more besides!

Name: Castel fine dining
Description En: Breathtaking 180° views of the Val Venosta provide the theatrical setting for Gerhard Wieser’s culinary talents at this restaurant. The chef’s cuisine is as precise as a Swiss clock yet full of international influences, with ingredients transformed into small masterpieces thanks to impeccable techniques and an elegant flair. His most memorable creations include red prawn tail cooked over a wood fire and served glazed, on top of a pea mixture (served plain, with cream or with olive oil) flavoured with chorizo sauce. To complete your dining experience, talented and attentive sommelier Ivana is on hand to help with wine choices, guiding you through the region’s wines and creating a bespoke wine pairing that is perfect for you.

Name: Enoteca La Torre
Description En: Within the captivating 1911 architecture of Villa Laetitia, the restaurant occupies a sumptuous dining room rich in stucco work and columns, enhanced by broad windows opening onto the exclusive garden: the ideal setting for an evening in grand style. The cooking, which does not forget the Campanian roots of the chef, returns to these echoes at several moments throughout the menu, alternating iconic recipes with more personal creations. Among the dishes that have become representative of the house, the egg, buffalo taleggio and black truffle of woodland character stands out, while the indulgent selection of desserts invites one to surrender to the pleasures of the final course, culminating in the characteristic trolley of petit fours. The experience is further enhanced by a skilled service, discreet and impeccable both in the management of the dining room and in the stewardship of the remarkable wine list, rich in prestigious labels and well-considered offerings by the glass. A refined destination, one that succeeds in uniting elegance, technique and hospitality of the highest order.

Name: Duomo
Description En: In the heart of Ibla, one of the most evocative historic districts not only of this wonderful island but of Italy itself, chef Ciccio Sultano embodies the very essence of Sicily, also through his latest “citrica” philosophy, about which he will – undoubtedly – tell you once you are seated in his classic, elegant venue just steps from the Duomo di San Giorgio (well worth a visit). You will be welcomed and served with refinement and expertise by a young, passionate team, including a carefully curated wine selection. Drawing on a profound knowledge of his land, the charismatic and friendly chef stages one of the most compelling shows of island gastronomy within the intimate, comfortable rooms of the restaurant. The offering is presented as two tasting menus, with the option to order à la carte as well. We were especially struck by the pasture‑raised lamb, Sicilian mole, fire‑cooked green beans, and a vegetable jus that blends sea and mountain flavors: a dish that unites technique, intensity, and originality, and alone justifies the journey. Among the many exclusive delicacies, each guest will find a memorable highlight to take home.

Name: Caino
Description En: Nestled in the heart of a charming Tuscan village, Caino is the gravitational centre of Maremma cuisine, with Valeria Piccini its finest interpreter: a skilful seeker of superior materials from a generous territory (which, along with a lovely vegetable garden, produces its own olive oil and some wines), later reimagining them without compromising an ounce of flavour—as in the delicious lamb ravioli or the pigeon stuffed with mashed potatoes and its entrails. For those craving a touch of the sea, there's an excellent risotto featuring cardoncelli mushrooms, lovage, and langoustines or amberjack with asparagus and almonds—always fresh fish cooked with Valeria's magical touch, paired with strictly seasonal ingredients. The dining area is ably supported by her son Andrea, keeper of a well-stocked wine cellar. In summer, Il Giardino di Caino opens on the terrace: a bistro where recipes are even more deeply rooted in ancient family traditions. Beautiful rooms upstairs ensure lingering enjoyment of Tuscan ambience.

Name: Krèsios
Description En: An ancient farmhouse serves as the laboratory home of ‘engineering-minded’ Chef Giuseppe Iannotti, who presents a single, long tasting menu that arrives at blind. An intriguing journey centring on flavour, featuring daring combinations paired with interesting techniques and experiments to entertain the guests. Throughout this gastronomic voyage, you'll find slight references to Campania, yet primarily the journey leads worldwide, through reinterpretations of familiar recipes reimagined with personal creativity, fermentations, macerations, extractions, and some nods to the chef's past. All accompanied by a selection of wines sourced from small producers, often natural, for after all, Krésios was none other than Bacchus.

Name: Madonnina del Pescatore
Description En: It’s now forty years since the Madonnina opened in 1984, yet chef Moreno Cedroni has not lost the creative touch that has resulted in him becoming one of the most influential chefs of his generation. Year after year, eating at La Madonnina remains a novelty: the menu succeeds like no other in reflecting past traditions and future culinary trends, especially in its fish and seafood dishes, and new dishes are added regularly, often having been researched in the laboratory next to the restaurant using specialised food technology. There are two tasting menus available: “Ricordi d'infanzia & Mariella 1984-2024” featuring chef Cedroni’s great classic dishes, and “Luca e Moreno... Il Viaggio di Marco Polo” which includes dishes with an Asian and Middle Eastern influence. The chef’s wife Mariella oversees the excellent service front of house, while this wonderful couple’s commitment to their cuisine is also demonstrated by their vegetable garden situated almost right on the beach, which provides vegetables infused with the salty sea air – a brilliant idea that represents their strong connection to the land. The wine list features a popular selection of French sparkling wines.

Name: Terra The Magic Place
Description En: Terra – The Magic Place begins to work its magic from the moment you begin the ascent along the road that climbs from Sarentino to an altitude of 1622 metres, winding through beech and fir woods. The restaurant is situated on a sunny alpine pasture with breathtaking views of the Dolomites, where the Schneider family has transformed the chalet built in 1940 by their grandfather Johann into a place that is truly unique. The gastronomic experience unfolds through à la carte dishes and an elaborate tasting menu, featuring little masterpieces of aesthetics and taste: the emulsion of brown trout with dill, chamomile and heather jelly is a revelation, as are the spaghetti made with beetroot, yeast flour and yarrow. The wine list – which also includes alcohol-free options – is lovingly curated by Gisela, the chef's sister. For those who wish to prolong the magic, the secluded resort completes a truly unforgettable experience.

Name: Campo del Drago
Address: Località Castiglion del Bosco, Montalcino, 53024, Italy
Description En: A certain amount of patience is required to get to this restaurant accessed via a dusty yet attractive dirt track that wends its way through typical Tuscan landscapes. On arrival, you’ll find an enchanting village of medieval origin with a tower and an old, frescoed church, where the Rosewood Castiglion del Bosco (awarded 3 Michelin keys) offers excellent service, splendid guestrooms and one of the best restaurants in the region. Here, chef Matteo Temperini serves some of the most interesting and creative dishes in Tuscany, many of which are prepared using vegetables from the hotel’s own kitchen garden, all showcased on three tasting menus and an à la carte from which a minimum of three courses must be chosen. Dishes are served in an elegant, contemporary-style dining room with a panoramic terrace, while the wine list features over 700 labels with a focus on the region – plenty of Brunellos, plus a particularly noteworthy 2016 Sasso al Sole, also available by the glass.

Name: San Domenico
Description En: In business since 1970, San Domenico is one of the flag-bearers of classic Italian dining. In the historic centre of Imola, inside you will find a succession of elegant rooms and an atmosphere that seems straight out of an English club. The menu alternates classic dishes accumulated over many years of activity with some more modern inventions from chef Massimiliano Mascia. An extraordinary wine list features more than two thousand labels.

Name: Arnolfo
Address: viale della Rimembranza 24, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
Description En: With sharp lines created by the use of iron and glass, this modern building is especially designed to allow guests to admire the views from wherever they’re sitting. To the rear of the dining room, the large open-view kitchen framed by a superb yellow Siena marble wall is home to chef Gaetano Trovato (Mentor Chef Award 2024) and his team. Although there are three tasting menus available, one of which is vegetarian, any of the courses can also be chosen à la carte style. We could say so much about Arnolfo’s cuisine, but we’ll limit ourselves to mentioning the bread (which has been central to this chef’s work from the very beginning), duck, Chianina beef, Valdarno chicken and the ice-cream which always features among the desserts. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the delightful amuse-bouche with which guests are welcomed, the caponata with Taggiasca olives and basil, and the mullet served with white asparagus, peas and mint. The wine list is impressive, both for its quality and for the extensive selection of wines not only from Italy and France but also from other countries around the world – 7,000 different labels in total.

Name: D'O
Address: piazza della Chiesa 14, loc. San Pietro all'Olmo, Cornaredo, 20007, Italy
Description En: On a charming piazza presided over by an elm tree and a seventeenth-century church, tables in two of the three dining rooms overlook the scene, while the contemporary elegance of D’O unfolds inside. Chef Davide Oldani, now a defining figure of Italian cuisine, crafts dishes that distill twenty years of work and formative experiences, including memorable stints with Marchesi and Ducasse. Creative ideas rooted in Italian taste, impeccable technique, and presentations that are both essential and playfully pop: as exemplified by the Cuttlefish in its ink with pickled porcini and dill. Among the tasting menus, Molteplicità and Leggerezza (10 courses) represent the fullest expression of his creative freedom, while Esattezza revisits signature classics. Completing the experience is the brilliant sommelier Manuele, who delights with playful and surprising pairings.

Name: L'Olivo
Description En: Upon arrival, guests are invited to begin with an aperitif in the refined bar area with its terrace, an ideal setting in which to savour a magnificent island sunset. We are in Anacapri, in its greener and more residential aspect, far from the more intense currents of Capri’s tourist flow. It is here that the Capri Palace, among the island’s most exclusive hotels, provides the introduction to its two-Michelin-starred restaurant, set within a spacious and elegant room that recalls a contemporary salon. In the kitchen, Andrea Migliaccio delivers a proposal that celebrates the Italian, and above all Campanian, tradition with great vitality, reinterpreted with a modern sensitivity yet always faithful to the generosity of its flavours and its vivid character. The dishes impress with intensity and precision, the first courses in particular, the true protagonists of the journey: from the pasta with reef fish to the richly constructed risotto al ragù napoletano. A deeply satisfying and joyful experience, which finds its natural complement in a stroll through the lanes of Anacapri or along the mule track leading to Villa Axel Munthe, perfect for immersing oneself in the island’s most authentic atmosphere.

Name: Andrea Aprea
Description En: Located on the top floor, with lift, of the Luigi Rovati Foundation, in a magnificent historic building renovated according to certified sustainability criteria and which also houses a very refined Art Museum, chef patron Andrea Aprea crowns the dream of a restaurant of his own: a space of great scenic impact, totally projected towards the open kitchen, with the walls of the central room covered in bucchero (the characteristic black ceramic used by the Etruscans to make their vases). It is here that you can admire the chef and his brigade intent on preparing the dishes of the three tasting menus: Contemporaneità, a 4-course creative itinerary dedicated to the relationship between memory and innovation (you will often find pigeon here); Partenope, a 6-course journey into the suggestions of Campania (how not to mention the tortello alla genovese di manzo with escarole, provolone del Monaco and black olives); Signature, a profound and prolonged experience into the philosophy and personal history of the chef in 8 courses identified by the vintage (it was 2016, for example, the first time he cooked the dessert strawberry with maraschino, mascarpone and nepetella). In the secret green courtyard of the building in Corso Venezia 52 is the Caffè Bistrot, where classic Italian flavours can be sampled from breakfast to dinner.

Name: Villa Feltrinelli
Description En: Within the eponymous villa, one of the most spectacular hotels on Lake Garda, the experience unfolds in a setting of extraordinary beauty: the lake before you, the mountains behind, and all around a park of absolute tranquillity. The interiors, finished to the last detail, express a refined elegance enriched by fine fabrics and floral arrangements. The evening begins with an aperitif in the garden, accompanied by an unforgettable view of the lake, before continuing in the refined inner rooms or on the terrace. The gastronomic offering takes the form of a single, elaborate surprise tasting menu, in which seafood, lake fish, and meat alternate seamlessly, with particular attention given to vegetables, the chef’s true hallmark, highlighted through a wide variety of aromatic herbs and occasionally exotic inflections.The wine selection favours Italy, with a significant representation of Champagne.

Name: Santa Elisabetta
Description En: Attention: Temporarily closed!In the heart of the historic centre, yet set apart on a quiet little piazza, the first thing to catch the eye is the Pagliazza Byzantine tower, the oldest in the city and the only one circular in form. Once through the entrance of the Hotel Brunelleschi, guests are accompanied to the first floor of the tower, where the restaurant is to be found: an intimate dining room adorned with a Murano chandelier and just six tables. The culinary offering reveals a strong Mediterranean inspiration, with marine echoes that surface throughout the combinations of flavours. The dishes are distinguished by creativity and refinement, the fruit of an approach that favours considered elaboration and an elegant construction of each course.

Name: Antica Corona Reale
Description En: Situated between the Langhe and Monviso, this historic restaurant was founded in 1815. Run by the Vivalda family for five generations, it started out as a dairy farm before gaining a well-earned reputation for its cuisine. Owner-chef Gian Piero Vivalda creates top-quality menus featuring expertly prepared, colourful and aromatic dishes. Popular with food-lovers from Italy and abroad, Antica Corona Reale is also a point of reference for many local businesses who supply it with capon, guinea fowl, veal, Carmagnola peppers, porcini mushrooms and much more besides. The menu offers an array of enticing flavours, with modern dishes featuring alongside classic favourites, including a delicate raviolo of bagna càuda served with the restaurant’s legendary bouillabaisse, which has made a reappearance on the menu after guests’ insistent requests. In summer, dine alfresco in the shade of a beautiful pergola, while two small private rooms are available for intimate dinners, one of which is in the wine cellar surrounded by legendary bottles of wine. There’s also a charming garden with an English-style rose garden and other beautiful flowers, which are often used in the delicious desserts, as demonstrated by the superb rose tart.

Name: Antica Osteria Cera
Description En: "Regarded as one of the most popular destinations for seafood lovers, the restaurant offers an extensive menu that combines classic dishes with modern creations, fine-tuned season after season. The atmosphere here is elegant, modern and minimalist, purposely distanced from the idea of a traditional “osteria”, with a section called “Solo Verde” dedicated specifically to vegetarians.The kitchen focuses on raw seafood and charcoal-grilled dishes, the restaurant’s real strengths. The highlight among the starters is the cold spaghettino with essence of molluscs, along with references to Venetian tradition, such as “cicchetti crudi” (raw fish or meat appetisersi) and, in season, fried “moeche” (green crabs). For those who love shellfish, “la catalana” is a classic plateau not to be missed, while the “risotto della laguna” precisely interprets the taste and identity of the territory. "

Name: Verso Capitaneo
Description En: From the entrance on Piazza Duomo, you take a lift to this restaurant on the second floor where three long tables are arranged in front of the open-view kitchen so that guests can watch the chefs at work (there are also more traditional tables away from the kitchen if you prefer something more conventional). The Capitaneo brothers from Puglia are at the helm here, serving creative cuisine with the occasional influence from their native region, as well as dishes that also embrace the gastronomic traditions of their adopted city of Milan.

Name: daní maison
Description En: This aptly named restaurant (At Nino’s house) is situated in chef Nino Di Costanzo’s own house in a residential district amid the hills of Ischia. Once over the threshold, you make your way through a garden planted with a variety of Mediterranean maquis shrubs and flowers, where aperitifs and post-dinner drinks are served in the evening. There are just a few tables in the dining room, which is crowned by a typical vaulted ceiling and where guests wishing to watch the chef at work can take a seat right in front of the kitchen. The dishes here are extremely elaborate, technical and sophisticated, perfect for anyone who loves concept-based cuisine with occasionally surprising results, including in presentation. If you’re coming here by car, take care on the last stretch of road which is particularly narrow.

Name: Piazzetta Milù
Address: corso Alcide De Gasperi 23, Castellammare di Stabia, 80053, Italy
Description En: It would be impossible to describe this venue without beginning with the welcome, the authentic hallmark of the Izzo family: a warmth and attentiveness that transforms every visit into a memorable experience. Leading the gastronomic proposal is Maicol, who expresses his vision through a seasonal and surprise tasting menu in constant evolution: the number and sequence of dishes remain unknown, leaving space for a free narrative constructed in the moment.The experience unfolds across several different rooms in a dynamic itinerary that may vary throughout the year: it often begins in the kitchen, before moving to the evocative historic cellar, surrounded by bottles from around the world, where each guest has their own private table, and concluding in the dining room, with possible further interludes beside the chef.The cuisine fuses technique and creativity to remarkable effect, as in the tagliolini with cardoncelli mushrooms, butter and aged Parmigiano, finished with white truffle and accompanied by a curious “fake crumb” fashioned from the same mushroom. The experience is orchestrated with precision by Emanuele and Valerio in the dining room, while the cellar – broad and carefully selected – helps make the experience even more immersive. The portions, well judged in size, allow guests to navigate the entire journey with ease, arriving at the close entirely satisfied.

Name: Taverna Estia
Address: via Guido De Ruggiero 108, Brusciano, 80031, Italy
Description En: An aromatic herb garden greets visitors to this restaurant, followed by jasmine-covered alcoves that provide the perfect setting for a romantic dinner in fine weather or, if you prefer to eat indoors, an elegant dining room with a wine cellar and open-view kitchen. The restaurant is run by brothers Mario and Francesco Sposito (the former front of house, the latter in the kitchen), who together keep alive the soul of the restaurant that they inherited from their parents. They have also improved the quality so that the restaurant’s reputation now extends well beyond the region. Choose from different tasting menus (from which dishes can be chosen à la carte if you prefer) featuring remarkable and exciting dishes influenced by the flavours of Campania. More than a thousand wines, including an impressive choice of French labels, complete the picture.

Name: Villa Elena
Description En: One must climb the steep, scenic Via San Vigilio, just steps from the beating heart of Città Alta, immersed in an exclusive hillside setting, to reach Villa Elena, one of the most majestic residences in the Bergamo hills. The garden terrace opens like a balcony suspended over the panorama, where on clear days lunch begins caressed by light and the fragrance of fresh air. Inside, amid stuccoes that resemble velvet, mirrors multiplying reflections, cool marbles, and frescoes that tell stories, the cuisine of Marco Galtarossa comes to life, the fruit of a creative dialog with Italy’s most decorated chef, Enrico Bartolini: a perfect harmony with the opulence of the surroundings. Complex, refined dishes, occasionally unfolding in multiple acts, elevated by aromatic herbs and vegetables that release intense fragrances; the close bond with local producers makes this venue an essential destination for memorable experiences, not only on grand occasions. The scampi with quince and hillside escarole is an extraordinary prelude, while the lemon spaghetto and sole with chanterelles and sea buckthorn continue the symphony of flavors. Recent additions to the dining room team confirm hospitality and service as further strengths, completing a picture of excellence.

Name: Magnolia
Address: via Pelliciano 35, loc. Montilgallo, Longiano, 47020, Italy
Description En: Situated in the elegant Relais Villa Margherita, an 18C villa converted into a stylish residence with just six guestrooms, verdant grounds and a swimming pool, Magnolia occupies a contemporary, veranda-style dining room with large picture windows boasting sweeping views of the Romagna hills as far as the mountainous “peak” of San Marino. Here, skilful chef Alberto Faccani serves a clever combination of the classic favourites that have marked his career, alongside other more unusual dishes that demonstrate a tireless search for experimentation. His contemporary style is elegant and balanced, as demonstrated by the delicate coconut milk sauce that provides the final flourish to his cuttlefish with caviar and peas.

Name: I Tenerumi
Description En: Arrive at the restaurant before sunset to admire a spectacular view of the Aeolian Islands: the setting is breathtaking, and the extraordinary “plant-based” cuisine, as defined by Chef Davide Guidara refusing the stereotypes of “vegetarian” or “vegan”, is sure to move you even further. From his open-view kitchen, a single surprise tasting menu is offered (price included), conceived as a journey through numerous often playful tastings. Guidara, previously awarded as a Young Chef, shows great skill in highlighting the winter produce from his garden through preservation techniques such as fermentation, maceration, and pickling, alternating with seasonal ingredients. His distinctive style is complemented by an automatic pairing of kombucha and herbal cordials. But fear not, wine enthusiasts: the cellar is at your full disposal. Making the evening even more special is the young service team: smiling, knowledgeable, and capable of creating a pleasant rapport with clients. An essential gastronomic stop!

Name: Famiglia Rana
Address: via Feniletto 2, località Vallese, Oppeano, 37050, Italy
Description En: Within the Feniletto nature reserve, the restaurant looks out over a tree-lined garden, an organic kitchen garden and an orchard that speak directly to the cooking. The warm and intimate interiors recall an elegant domestic drawing room, with wood, soft lighting and a welcome of homey character. At the stove is chef Francesco Sodano, who offers exclusively blind tasting menus: the guest chooses one of three journeys and the number of courses, while the dishes arrive as a surprise. The ‘Ricomincio da tre’ menu pays homage to Campania and gathers some of the chef’s signature dishes, among them a reinterpreted pastiera that preserves the aromas and identity of the traditional dessert while presenting it in a contemporary guise. ‘The Doors’ is the creativity menu, where technique and research shape a freer and more experimental cuisine. Those who prefer the freshness of the vegetable world may opt for ‘Vegetale’, dedicated to the produce of the kitchen garden, the protagonist of preparations that celebrate seasonality, fragrance and precise cooking. A young but well-prepared service accompanies the experience with quiet discretion, contributing to a journey that is harmonious and deeply pleasurable.

Name: George Restaurant
Description En: This roof-garden restaurant in one of Naples’ most luxurious hotels (Grand Hotel Parker’s) boasts an open-view kitchen facing a breathtaking panorama that takes in Vesuvius, the Bay of Naples and the city itself, which extends below the hotel in an evocative display of sparkling lights. It’s a challenge for the cuisine to compete with so much beauty but young chef Domenico Candela is more than equal to the task. His cuisine showcases the culinary specialities of the city and further afield with extraordinary skill, combining superb produce and recipes from Campania with techniques learnt in France to produce truly remarkable reinterpretations of regional dishes.

Name: Fradis Minoris
Description En: Fradis Minoris is a naturalistic and sustainable venture, inspired by the distant allure of the Nora Lagoon Natural Park. This captivating environment serves as a muse for creating a distinctive journey within the realm of fine dining. After parking, guests take a short walk of a few hundred metres along the isthmus, entering a protected marine area managed by the restaurant owners themselves. It seems almost inevitable that the culinary direction here embraces a fully circular approach. The menu features a single tasting option, deeply rooted in the seasonality of local ingredients: the catch is often sourced directly from the lagoon, or at most, the southern Sardinian sea. Additionally, wild herbs are gathered from the lagoon, and a variety of vegetables are sourced from nearby Campidano's small-scale producers. Creativity and the technical prowess of chef Francesco Stara shape exquisite and novel tasters. The wine list, with its profound focus on discovering small-scale producers scattered across the island, mirrors a strong attention to the region, complemented by an intriguing wine pairing suggested by the sommelier. Supporting this offering is their bistrot version, FradisLab.

Name: Romano
Description En: Celebrating its 60th anniversary in 2026, the timeless Romano continues to serve top-quality fish and seafood, occasionally updated yet always maintaining the traditions which have made it one of Versilia’s culinary institutions. Although this long-established restaurant’s philosophy has not changed over the years, current chef Nicola Gronchi should be applauded for adding a hint of contemporary flavour and technical expertise to the cuisine, bringing it in line with the times, while still retaining everything that this restaurant does best, namely serving fish of the highest quality (there are also a few meat dishes), including the occasional typical Versilian recipe. Front of house, talented Roberto and his team guarantee an enjoyable all-round dining experience, including wine recommendations.

Name: Locanda Mammì
Description En: In an evocative rural setting, among stone farmhouses, absolute tranquillity and a summer terrace that opens onto the surrounding hills, chef Stefania Di Pasquo presents an authentic cuisine, firmly rooted in the produce of her land and enhanced by a personal and unaffected touch. The variation of lamb is impeccable: a freshly cooked cutlet, a slow-braised preparation with onions, and alongside it a richly flavoured liver stew, together composing a coherent narrative of technique and memory. Equally remarkable is the dessert inspired by the traditional peasant breakfast, in which caramelised bread meets a surprising caciocavallo ice cream – a fitting homage to Agnone, not without reason known as the ‘city of cheese’ – finished with a delicate wine sauce. In the dining room, the chef’s husband, Tomas Torsiello, receives guests with grace and quiet assurance in a warm and romantic setting enriched by a fireplace and copper details. His is also the stewardship of the wine list, which reveals a marked predilection for Champagnes. The property also offers pleasant guest rooms, ideal for those wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Antica Osteria Nonna Rosa
Address: via Laudano 1, loc. Pietrapiana, Vico Equense, 80069, Italy
Description En: The dining room at this restaurant has the warm ambience of an old country house, where two small niches with their own tables are perfect for a more private and romantic dinner. The decor includes dove-coloured walls, an array of lamps and even a typical nativity scene in which the chef and his mother (“Nonna Rosa”) make an appearance. The cuisine is original and creative with its roots in local traditions, and is prepared using ingredients from Campania and the restaurant’s own kitchen garden. Some years ago, owner-chef Giuseppe Guida purchased a large garden where he now grows all the vegetables used in his dishes.
