The talented sommelier is his wife; together they worked in various gourmet restaurants along the Campanian coast before realizing their dream of ownership here, in Luigi Tramontano’s hometown.

Name: Grual
Address: via Alpe di Grual 16, Pinzolo, 38086, Italy
Description En: Housed within the Lefay Resort & Spa Dolomiti, an elegant hotel that dominates Pinzolo and is one of the best hotels in the Trentino region, this gourmet restaurant takes its name from the mountain behind the hotel (the Grual). Here, in the evening, chef Matteo Maezza serves his own reinterpretations of typical mountain cuisine inspired by the three different altitudes from which he sources his ingredients. For example, the bottom of the valley (“fondovalle”) is the inspiration for his marinated whitefish from Lake Garda, served with different types of turnip and Mugo pine milk; the Alpine pasture region (“alpeggio”) has inspired the delicious rib of beef with mustard and carrots; while the high mountain area (“alta montagna”) is behind the elaborate saddle of venison with cardoon gratin with a beef marrow and creamed rye crust. There’s also an impressive wine list featuring an impressive selection of champagnes.

Name: ARIA
Address: via Loggia dei Pisani 2, Naples, 80133, Italy
Description En: The ambience at this hushed and discreet restaurant couldn’t be more different from the hustle and bustle of the elegant district in which it is situated. The softly lit dining rooms are elegant and minimalist in style, with lamps creating pools of light illuminating the dishes conjured up by Paolo Barrale. Originally from Cefalù but now settled in Campania, the chef’s cuisine is inspired by the culinary traditions of both regions which he reinterprets with ease, occasionally creating more personalised dishes. Generous in every way, from the warm welcome to the cuisine right up to dessert, Paolo offers guests a top-quality dining experience ably assisted by his well-trained, professional staff.

Name: Gusto by Sadler
Address: via Tavolara, località Lu Fraili di Sotto, San Teodoro, 07052, Italy
Description En: To the north of San Teodoro, within the exclusive Baglioni Resort, the restaurant offers a Mediterranean-inspired cuisine that strikes a balance between more classical references and contemporary accents. On one side, dishes such as lobster salad with sweet-and-sour vegetables and yellow cherry tomato gazpacho, or a richly composed sauté of shellfish; on the other, more modern creations such as a dessert of rosehip jelly with raspberry, rhubarb, basil gel, and fior di latte ice cream. The offering is further complemented by a vegetarian tasting menu, designed to celebrate the seasonality and freshness of the ingredients. The setting provides a perfect frame: lunch and dinner are taken overlooking a beautifully kept garden with a swimming pool, immersed in a relaxed atmosphere that fully embodies the spirit of a holiday.

Name: Anima
Description En: Housed inside the prestigious Milano Verticale | UNA Esperienze hotel in the Corso Como and Piazza Gae Aulenti district of the city, this restaurant is run by multi-Michelin-starred chef Enrico Bartolini. Minimalist elegance and design are the key words to describe the stylish decor here, inspired by Gio Ponti’s city of the second half of the 20C. Resident chef Michele Cobuzzi prepares dishes with a modern flavour, prepared using top-quality ingredients which are mostly sourced from his native region of Puglia. Given his origins, it’s no surprise that this chef is highly skilful in his preparation of vegetables and bread-making. The wine list is enhanced by an interesting selection of cocktails, including original and exciting drinks from around the world alongside more classic options.

Name: Vineria Modì
Description En: Situated in the historic centre of Taormina, just a stone’s throw from Corso dello Struscio and the many brand-name boutiques that have sprung up here in recent years, this restaurant started out as a wine-bar. The passion for wine remains and is evident not only in the extensive, carefully selected wine list, but also in the enthusiasm of its staff. Nowadays, the wine accompanies fine cuisine prepared by the skilful Dalila Grillo, whose brother Ettore oversees the front of house. Guests have the option of two tasting menus or an à la carte (from which a minimum of three courses must be ordered) featuring creative and elaborate dishes with a Sicilian flavour (as well as influences from elsewhere), all served in an elegant dining room. In summer, the outdoor tables overlooking a pedestrianised street are particularly attractive.

Name: Casa Buono
Address: corso Cuneo 28, Località Trucco, Ventimiglia, 18039, Italy
Description En: This unexpected Ligurian gem is situated in Trucco, a small village in the Val Roia just inland from Ventimiglia. There’s no à la carte here, just the “Orto e Mare” tasting menu to which guests can also add a meat dish and a selection of cheeses from the well-stocked cheese trolley. Although the dishes are occasionally influenced by Ligurian traditions, they are for the most part creative, surprising and beautifully prepared. Given its success, the restaurant has recently been extended while at the same time retaining its simple, colourful and welcoming ambience. The high-quality service comes courtesy of the chef’s friendly wife, ably assisted by her professional and capable staff.

Name: Re Santi e Leoni
Description En: Just a few metres from the Duomo, within an elegant period building, a bright corridor leads guests from the entrance to the open-plan kitchen, crossing a minimalist, contemporary dining room. Quality reigns supreme in the kitchen: carefully selected ingredients, artisan breads with great character and desserts that leave a lasting impression. There are three tasting menus and a constantly evolving à la carte menu, based on the concept of gastronomic precision, distinct flavours and rigorous balance. The rich and well-structured wine cellar showcases some of Italy’s most prestigious labels, completing an experience of clear and conscious character.

Name: Cortile Spirito Santo
Description En: Situated near Castel Maniace at the southernmost point of Ortigia, this restaurant is part of the Palazzo Salomone Luxury Suites and is one of the most elegant places to eat in Siracusa, where it serves some of the best Sicilian cuisine on the island. Here, Giuseppe Torrisi prepares creative and technically expert dishes which are typical of Sicily’s Baroque soul and offer a real feast for the senses thanks to their exciting, intense and often unforgettable flavours. We particularly enjoyed the monkfish meunière with fennel and asparagus and the “Made in Sicily” almond tartlet designed in the shape of the island. The extensive wine list offers plenty of choice – you might like to try one of the local labels from Etna or the west coast of Sicily, or perhaps ask expert, knowledgeable sommelier Antonino to help you choose one of the top-quality international wines available.

Name: Sciabola
Address: via XX Settembre 28, Forte dei Marmi, 55042, Italy
Description En: Inside the elegant St. Mauritius hotel, chef Alessandro Ferrarini, supported by a trusted team, creates colorful, delicious, and balanced dishes using impeccable, often local ingredients. These are available in both tasting menus and à la carte. The focus is mainly on seafood (we especially remember the anchovy butter ravioli with bread and raisins, and the Mediterranean-style sea bass with cherry tomatoes, olives, and capers), but there are also various land-based options. Service is led by an experienced maître who coordinates a young and cheerful team.

Name: Cannavacciuolo Le Cattedrali Asti
Description En: Situated in the hills outside Asti, this modern inn with guestrooms is nestled in around 18 hectares of woodland and meadows. The interior decor here is contemporary and minimalist, while the cuisine is overseen by the famous three-Michelin-star chef Antonino Cannavacciuolo, with resident chef Gianluca Renzi, who has already earned his spurs at other top-quality restaurants, at the helm in the kitchen. Originally from Rome (his focaccia is excellent!) and having trained professionally in various locations, Renzi creates cuisine that combines personal imaginative touches with regional influences, including traditional flavours from the Piedmont. The young front-of-house team includes a number of excellent female staff. The superb wine list features more than 2 000 labels, while the cheese trolley focuses on local options.

Name: Linfa
Description En: Inside the walls, but easily accessible from the car parks outside, a small treasure chest of elegance, with contemporary artwork on the walls, and congeniality. Here chef Giovanni Cerroni, with a lengthy experience in fine dining, offers two tasting menus: Mimesis with the great classics and A mano libera, where his talent is best expressed according to the client's tastes as well. For wines, one quietly relies on the expertise of Cesario Delle Donne. Finally, the choice of using books as centrepieces is very much appreciated: the one on Tuscan proverbs illustrated by Renato Bellabarba is not to be missed. In short, a well-rounded experience in one of Tuscany's tourism gems

Name: Octavin
Description En: Housed in two small dining rooms connected by an arch on the ground floor of an old palazzo, this restaurant is decorated with materials that give it a minimalist feel – a combination of stone, wood and iron in the tables, glass in the mirrors and bottles on display, and paper in the books arranged in small niches, just like the lounge of a private home. There are just 20 seats in this warm, intimate and unfussy restaurant, as well as a large counter separated by an arch at the entrance which precedes the recently restructured kitchen. Observation of his own region has shown owner-chef Luca Fracassi that the varied geography of his province is an inexhaustible source of inspiration. As a result, he has embarked upon an impassioned search for ingredients that best showcase the region, combining these in dishes that not only respect the flavours of his produce but also revive traditional local techniques and include the occasional oriental influence. His cuisine is modern yet eschews modern trends, paying careful attention to integrity of flavour and zero waste. In this way, the kitchen becomes a place in which wild ingredients and forgotten flavours are rediscovered and brought back to life. This focus on lost traditions combines ingredients such as snails and game (often neglected in urban restaurants) with a skilful and updated use of contemporary culinary techniques.

Name: Mec Restaurant
Description En: In the heart of monumental Palermo, set in a 16th-century palazzo almost opposite the Cathedral (after your meal, ask to step out onto the balcony: a fitting finale to a special evening), this distinctive restaurant shares its space with an exhibition dedicated to Steve Jobs. Diners are welcomed into one of three elegant rooms, beneath frescoed ceilings and surrounded by photographs and memorabilia tracing the story of the computer pioneer. In the kitchen, chef Carmelo Trentacosti reinterprets Sicilian recipes and ingredients with a personal touch: his famous caponata, for example, becomes a velvety sauce enhanced with shavings of Modica chocolate – irresistible with house-made bread. Before dessert, a fine cheese trolley makes its appearance, all complemented by attentive, courteous service.

Name: Idylio by Apreda
Description En: An elegant dining room in shades of blue and orange is the backdrop for Francisco Apreda’s cuisine, in which this chef combines Italian cuisine with spicy and Asian-influenced flavours thanks to his time spent working in Asia. He offers various tasting menus: one dedicated to his classic favourites, a second featuring his new dishes, and a third for vegetarians. There’s also an excellent wine list, with an extensive selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Apostelstube
Description En: In beautiful Bressanone, the historic Hotel Elephant, housed in a building whose oldest section dates back to the late 15th century, is one of the city’s true icons. Managed by the same family since 1773, it is now in the hands of the eighth generation. In the intimate and exquisitely elegant dining room, with just four tables and the watchful eyes of the twelve apostles that, in the form of statuettes, observe you from the walls, Chef Mathias Bachmann presents a unique, extensive, and exclusive tasting menu. Drawing ingredients and techniques from around the world, with a special fondness for Japan, he reinterprets them with contemporary flair. Service is entrusted to Michael and Eleonora, whose expertise and innate warmth will also delight you with the incredible tale of the elephant that once passed through the city. In the warm season, aperitifs are served in the pleasant garden; during the colder months or inclement weather, they are offered in the elegant lounge, also on the first floor, just like the dining room.

Name: In Viaggio - Claudio Melis
Description En: The name of this restaurant gives a good indication of the experience you can expect here: a culinary voyage through the chef’s varied selection of recipes and ingredients, some from the Alps, others from countries across the globe. Dishes are served on tasting menus of five, seven or nine courses in a quiet dining room with just a few tables, where the chef himself explains his dishes to guests.

Name: Dissapore di Andrea Catalano
Description En: Don’t be put off by the maze of narrow streets leading to this restaurant in the historic town – once you reach your destination, you’ll enjoy delicious classic recipes from Puglia prepared using top-quality ingredients and full of unmistakeable flavours, all served in a charming dining room with lime and stone walls crowned by a domed ceiling. Among the highly recommended dishes, don’t miss the “purely instinctive” scampi with sweet pepper and saffron. Wines from Puglia, elsewhere in Italy and further afield accompany chef Andrea’s eclectic cuisine, while front of house, bubbly and friendly Franca oversees the excellent service. In summer, don’t miss the outdoor terrace overlooking the village rooftops with views of the sea in the distance!

Name: Unforgettable
Description En: Stefano Mancinelli and Sabrina Stravato are the two chefs who have taken over the reins in the kitchen at this original restaurant just a stone’s throw from the Santuario della Consolata. Although the format here remains the same (a blind tasting menu), the chefs are also making their mark on the creative cuisine, which combines typical dessert techniques and recipes with savoury elements (and vice versa) throughout the meal, as seen in the savoury potato crème caramel with onion. As previously, guests are greeted by the chefs in a small lounge and then served at a counter where they sit side by side (there are ten seats in total). Meanwhile, the volume of the background music (which is often quite loud) is adjusted to allow the staff to explain the different courses and wine pairings.

Name: Mater1apr1ma
Description En: This restaurant in the heart of the small town is run by a brilliant couple: Sara, who is extremely knowledgeable about her own wine list, offers guests an interesting selection of wines while also overseeing the precise and friendly service front of house; and Fabio, at the helm in the kitchen, prepares original cuisine that showcases the ingredients of the Agro Pontino. The chef shows real sensitivity in his lamb dish, which combines local ingredients with Indian influences, as if to encourage integration with the many Indian immigrants who have settled in this area. The “non-sweet desserts” served at the end of the meal are particularly interesting, including unusual ingredients such as olives, basil and artichokes.

Name: Sine by Di Pinto
Description En: Sine serves contemporary cuisine influenced by the chef’s native Naples, as well as the local region of Lombardy. The dishes are occasionally playful in style, as demonstrated by the shrimp ravioli served in various ways, including with an intensely flavoured fish stew. The chef’s speciality is his fried pizzetta with palamita fish and courgettes, while his new dishes are showcased on the exciting and creative “Sine Confini” menu, on which he demonstrates his culinary skills to the full. Attentive, courteous service and a constantly evolving wine list which includes some lesser-known labels complete the picture.

Name: Porcino
Description En: Inside the modern Badia Hill hotel, patron Marco Verginer offers two tasting menus: one focused on seasonality, the other inspired by his creativity, featuring ingredients such as Wagyu beef produced in Alto Adige. The pairings are flavorful and lively, with extensive use of vegetables, often from the home garden. The result is an excellent dining experience served in a contemporary setting surrounded by glass walls that offer splendid views of the surrounding landscape. The menu presents a succession of mountain territory references combined with Mediterranean and international touches in highly elaborate dishes.

Name: Acqua
Address: via Filippo Corridoni 1, Olgiate Olona, 21057, Italy
Description En: Family tradition is renewed with a contemporary spirit at this venue overlooking the historic Ma.Ri.Na. The philosophy here is clear: exceptional raw materials, carefully selected and showcased by chef Menoncin and patron Davide Possoni. The latter enjoys sitting down with guests at the start of the evening to guide them toward offerings best suited to personal tastes: fish, crustaceans, and mollusks interpreted in original recipes, occasionally with pleasing spicy accents, always generous and elegantly plated. The crudo selection is unmissable – notably the sumptuous crustacean trio of scampi, impressively sized caramote prawns, and red prawns – while among the hot dishes, we highlight the seared red mullet with Tuscan kale velouté and gorgonzola gelato, sampled on our last visit and truly memorable. The wine list favors Champagnes, with numerous labels available by the glass. In summer, the outdoor terrace adds an extra touch of pleasure.

Name: Vignamare
Address: strada Castello, 20 - Colla Micheri, Andora, 17051, Italy
Description En: At Vignamare, a new chapter unfolds: two chefs at the helm, a clearly recognisable local identity and a cuisine that weaves together agricultural production and contemporary sensitivity. From Andora, the road climbs the hill through a series of hairpin bends leading to the car park; from there, a few steps on foot bring guests to the restaurant entrance, while the landscape already sets the tone for the experience: vineyards overlooking the sea, olive groves and maritime pines sketch one of Liguria’s most luxuriant views. The project was born from the restoration of a 1970s cistern, unused for decades and now transformed into a fine-dining venue. When the weather allows, the panoramic terrace becomes the true stage; otherwise, a modern wood-clad dining room welcomes guests in a warm, contemporary atmosphere. The gastronomic offering is structured around two tasting menus, of seven and nine courses respectively, alongside an entirely “green” menu. The technique is clear and well defined, with a language rooted in the Mediterranean and showcasing regional produce of excellent quality, much of it from the gardens and livestock of PEQ Agri, the agricultural enterprise underpinning the project. On the upper levels there is also a more informal offering, ideal for a cocktail or a light stop, with an incomparable view and a particularly pleasant atmosphere on warm summer days.

Name: Grow Restaurant
Description En: Technique, creativity and a focus on and respect for the past are just some of the criteria that guide chef Matteo Vergine. His modern dishes aim to reflect the ancestral flavours of Brianza and Lombardy in bygone days when hunting, freshwater fishing, growing vegetables and gathering wild herbs were all part of everyday life. In the evening, choose between three tasting menus – in an effort to minimise food waste, guests are required to make their choice at the time of booking. We particularly enjoyed the quail served with its own broth and a brioche, and the gnocchi with stracchino cheese, caramel and venison bottarga. Lighter and less expensive options are available at lunchtime, as well as a convivial table for eight which can be shared with “strangers”. This love for the region extends to the whole of Italy when it comes to the wine list, which is concise yet personal and exclusively features natural Italian wines, all of which are served skilfully and with a wealth of information by sommelier Riccardo.

Name: Andrea Larossa
Description En: Across the Po from the city center, where ample, convenient parking invites a stress-free stop, a luminous dining room awaits, one that once hosted recreational gatherings and social events. Today it retains that same spirit of conviviality, marked by genuine smiles, attentive service, and measured professionalism. In the kitchen, Andrea Larossa demonstrates a deep command of Piedmontese ingredients and traditions, enriched by Southern Italian influences inherited from his family origins and a natural inclination toward contemporary creativity. Two tasting menus favor pleasure over ingredient rarity, free from the dogmas and rigidity of tradition. Both unfold in a generous sequence of small bites, almost a playful prelude that introduces the journey like a fan of appetizers.

Name: Atto di Vito Mollica
Description En: A few steps from the Duomo, within the Corte degli Imperatori of Palazzo Portinari, the historic former residence of the Salviati family, the restaurant occupies a setting of rare beauty, enriched by sixteenth-century frescoes by Alessandro Allori and the soothing sound of a fountain. An authentic Renaissance salon transformed into a refined dining room. The kitchen distinguishes itself through technical precision and elegance, bringing out the very best of the highest-quality produce in dishes that are creative yet always balanced and never contrived. Emblematic is the lightly seared langoustine, served over two mirror sauces – one sweet and aromatic with carrot and orange, the other more acidic and buttery with Champagne. Attentive and considered service accompanies the experience with expertise, from the wine pairing through to the final dedication to coffee.

Name: Da Lucio
Description En: This restaurant boasts an impressive setting on the end of a jetty surrounded by the sea in Rimini docks. The entrance stands next to the open-view kitchen (a spectacle in itself!), which then leads into the long dining room. Nearly all the fish here (which comes from the Adriatic) is aged to allow water to evaporate so that the flavours are concentrated; it is then grilled or baked in a wood-fired oven, as well as served raw, with surprising and remarkable results.

Name: Līmū
Description En: In a town renowned for its splendid villas built by the Palermo aristocracy, this restaurant occupies a small 16C tower on the edge of the historic centre. The name is a tribute to lemon, a fruit that grows in abundance in Bagheria. The restaurant has two elegant, contemporary-style floors, where dinner starts on the small terrace-cum-lounge – the setting for sampling a whole host of delicious appetisers. This is guests’ first encounter with a technical and creative cuisine that sensitively uses the finest local ingredients, while often following paths born from personal and imaginative ideas. The courteous and precise service is overseen by Giandomenico Gambino, a knowledgeable guide for pairings from the rich, well-stocked wine cellar.

Name: Quintessenza
Description En: What a fascinating historical context: the Swabian castle is right in front of the restaurant, the dining rooms, on two levels, are also within period walls, and finally there is the possibility, when the weather permits, to eat on a panoramic terrace from which you can also see the famous bell tower of Trani cathedral (as well as a table set up in a small room used as a wine cellar for dining among the bottles). No less than four brothers, between the dining room and the kitchen, share the restaurant's tasks; at the cooker, Stefano Di Gennaro, who creates a cuisine rich in substance and flavour, avoids unnecessary complications and virtuosity and aims firmly at satisfying the palate, in dishes that mostly reinterpret the classic Italian tradition using various Apulian products.

Name: Paca
Description En: This beautiful gastronomic establishment just steps from the historic center offers modern Italian cuisine that pays great attention to raw materials, selecting small local producers and, where possible, local ingredients. The exquisite Colonnata lard is often served with delicious bread offerings: from rice flour bread to chestnut bread. Excellent service completes this pleasant gourmet experience in the city of Prato.

Name: Abba
Description En: In the heart of Milan's Certosa District, Abba is set in a former brush factory and welcomes guests with Nordic elegance: an open kitchen, only eight well-spaced tables, minimalist furnishings, and natural light streaming through large windows. In the kitchen, Abbattista offers two paths that tell his vision: excellent ingredients and modern techniques merge into delicious and surprising dishes. Among the must-tries, the tomato water risotto with parsley oil and mantis shrimp cream, or the whitefish, elegantly served on black lentils and turmeric. To end beautifully, the hazelnut soufflé is an indulgence not to be missed. The wine list is essential but carefully curated, with some natural and organic options. At lunch, there’s also a business lunch with selections from the menus.

Name: Ancòra
Description En: A new adventure for skilful chef Agostino Iacobucci (his original restaurant of the same name is in Castel Maggiore), housed within a villa that food-enthusiasts will remember as the former home of the two-Michelin-star Magnolia. In this elegant and welcoming setting, resident chef Marco Garattoni demonstrates the precise culinary techniques acquired during his many years working in top-quality restaurants. His dishes are contemporary, always colourful, beautifully presented, pleasing and attractive, even mouthwatering at times, and mostly based on fish, with the addition of a few vegetarian and meat options. Don’t miss one of this Neapolitan chef’s most famous signature dishes, namely his “babà a tre lievitazioni”, which is light, delicious and perfect in every way!

Name: Abbruzzino Oltre
Address: Piazza Salvo d'Acquisto 16, Lamezia Terme, 88046, Italy
Description En: A historic palazzo that once served military and ecclesiastical functions now presides over the main promenade with understated grandeur. Inside, minimalist elegance converses with modern art objects perfectly integrated into the setting, creating a refined space of contemporary character. Here, Luca Abbruzzino explores his Calabria with a personal, engaging vision: a vibrant, modern cuisine that showcases technique and sensitivity through dry-aged fish, well-balanced contrasts, and masterful use of local ingredients. Bergamot takes the lead in the dessert course, while savory highlights include amberjack and grouper, prawns with sea urchin, and an oyster risotto that merits unequivocal recommendation. The menu, however, is a surprise: one entrusts the day’s selection to the chef, confident he will captivate with fresh, coherent intuitions. Intimate spaces, impeccable service, and a naturally romantic atmosphere complete an experience uniting history, elegance, and a cuisine that looks to the future without losing its bond to the land.

Name: Retroscena
Address: largo del Teatro 3, Porto San Giorgio, 63822, Italy
Description En: In the heart of Porto San Giorgio’s picturesque old town, among the exposed brick houses, is a dining room of refined minimalist elegance, with just a few tables and an intimate atmosphere. When guests are not captivated by the dishes, they will find themselves fascinated by the open kitchen, where the crew works with precision, creating courses that express the restaurant’s contemporary signature style, characterised by a deft use of acidity as a distinctive note. Although the team is young, the technical level is high and the cuisine, while retaining a few echoes of its Modenese training, develops above all through an inventiveness capable of stirring deep emotions. For a broad and creative overview, the ten-course Labor Limae tasting menu is the ideal choice, designed to capture nuances and ideas in constant evolution. The wine offering is excellent too: a cellar in continual expansion, with carefully curated selections and well-conceived by-the-glass options. Completing the picture is a convincing selection of cocktails, spirits and liqueurs, further enriching the overall experience.

Name: Casa Sgarra
Description En: A restaurant bearing the surname of three brothers who crafted this gourmet Trani address: two in the dining area, one in the kitchen. An atmosphere elegant and contemporary; the service cradles guests like family, whilst Felice Sgarra at the stove astonishes with dishes sometimes drawn from Apulian traditions, as well as those from other regions, all closely interpreted and elaborated personally. If cheese is your passion, don’t miss the remarkable trolley showcasing Piedmont and French offerings.

Name: Otto Geleng
Description En: The elegant atmosphere at this restaurant is typical of Taormina and of Sicily’s old villas, with just eight tables laid out on a terrace adorned with bougainvillea and overlooking Taormina, the Bay of Naxos and Etna. The decor here shows real attention to detail, with an emphasis on the splendour of a grand old residence, while chef Roberto Toro creates typical Sicilian dishes reinterpreted with his own personal twist. His cuisine is showcased on various tasting menus, including a vegetarian option, from which dishes can be chosen à la carte style. We particularly enjoyed the chef’s signature dish, a memorable spaghetti with roast peppers, prawn, sesame and lime which was recommended by the attentive and discreet serving staff, who skilfully manage to put guests at ease in this impressive setting. More than 400 different wines are available to accompany this gourmet journey, with a choice of regional, Italian and French labels, including several excellent wines from small local wineries.

Name: IYO Kaiseki
Description En: Kaiseki represents the most traditional and codified form of Japanese cuisine, structured as a succession of courses alternating raw preparations with cooked dishes, following techniques faithful to Japanese tradition and skillfully interpreted by the chef. In this modern structure at the foot of one of the Porta Nuova skyscrapers, a minimal, pared-back dining room, illuminated by natural light filtering through floor-to-ceiling windows, introduces guests to classic Japanese cuisine through a broad and distinctive menu. For a first encounter with Iyo Kaiseki, we suggest the chef’s menu: a sequence of sashimi, carpacci, and nigiri for the raw courses, complemented by traditional cooking methods – from steaming to preparations with bold, distinctly Asian flavors. Exemplary is the Iberian pork with leeks and sautéed mushrooms, draped in negimiso sauce and served on a hoba (magnolia) leaf: a dish as striking visually as it is on the palate. A recommended stop is in the back, where the open kitchens offer a captivating show. Not to be missed, by reservation, is Iyo Omakase: a completely independent journey at the sushi counter, in authentic omakase experience experience style.

Name: Casa Leali
Address: via Valle 1, Puegnago sul Garda, 25080, Italy
Description En: The eponymous restaurant of the Leali brothers has, over the course of a decade, become a solid gastronomic point of reference for the area. The cooking displays an increasingly signature style: the dishes are precise and technical, built upon original and carefully considered recipes, while a growing interest in the vegetable world emerges with ever greater clarity, even as sound offerings of fish and meat remain on the menu. Among these, the rainbow trout stands out, served with a mayonnaise drawn from its own roe, a parsley sauce and a kind of Brescian ceviche also based on trout: an emblematic example of their approach. In the dining room, the service is attentive and passionate, with a particular affection for sparkling wines and Champagne, alongside a solid grounding in still wines. The elegant dining room – created from the restoration of a fifteenth-century farmhouse – continues to improve with each visit, confirming the considered and welcoming character of this establishment. A venue of consistent and well-deserved growth.

Name: Iacobucci
Address: via Ronco 1, Villa Zarri, Castel Maggiore, 40013, Italy
Description En: Housed in Villa Zarri, a historic family residence where one of the most famous brandies in Italy was created, this restaurant is home to chef Agostino Iacobucci, who creates a culinary bridge between his native Campania and the Bologna region. His dishes include a delicious rabbit alla genovese, a type of Neapolitan stew, served with a scamorza cheese and herb cream and topped with shavings of local black truffle. The impressive wine list boasts a selection of vertical labels including prestigious wines such as Sassicaia and Tignanello, with over ten different vintages available. The villa also offers a convenient car park and a delightful garden which is perfect for a stroll either before or after your meal.

Name: Borgo Sant'Anna
Description En: Nestled among the vineyards and overlooking the gentle hills of the Langhe, this restaurant helmed by chef Pasquale Laera presents a cuisine of distinct identity, where Apulian roots dialog with Piedmontese terroir in a personal, measured balance. In the tasting menus and à la carte offerings, seafood, seasonal vegetables, and select meats coexist, always treated with precise technique and keen gustatory sensitivity. Among the most striking dishes, the hay-smoked buffalo mozzarella with buttermilk and Senise pepper remains a signature course, effectively encapsulating the chef’s philosophy.

Name: Cetaria
Description En: This charming restaurant in the Salerno hinterland is the creation of a passionate duo: Salvatore in the kitchen and Federica in the dining room. With just a few glass‑topped tables set beneath a lofty ceiling that recalls the historical character of the building, the atmosphere is intimate and enhanced by Federica’s attentive service (Service Award 2024) and her thoughtful storytelling of the wine list, which includes excellent selections by the glass. Salvatore presents a predominantly seafood‑based cuisine, offering contemporary interpretations of local ingredients and recipes. His technique is assured, the presentations playful and refined, and the raw materials of outstanding quality, supplemented by a nearby vegetable garden and a small family farm in Calabria, Federica’s homeland, from which she has also painted two of the canvases displayed in the dining room.

Name: Zia
Description En: A young chef of undisputed talent is the driving force behind this discreet restaurant, hidden away behind the busier, more touristy streets of Trastevere. We are speaking of Antonio Ziantoni and his cuisine: creative, yet always governed by rigour and restraint, and built on solid classic foundations. Through precise and delicate technical steps, ingredients of outstanding quality are transformed into dishes that are generous and well balanced, capable of delivering full, rounded and deeply satisfying flavours. A telling example? Quail with sage and carnation flowers. The cellar is equally accomplished, presented with passion, as is the service: knowledgeable and cordial, completing an experience of rare charm.

Name: Lunasia
Description En: One of the most imaginative and original chefs in Versilia, offering a showcase restaurant inside the luxurious Plaza e de Russie hotel. In a modern and bright dining room overlooking the famous Viareggio promenade, Luca Landi's menu features three tasting options: one dedicated to fish, another combining seafood and vegetables, and a third focused on meats, with the possibility to mix and match dishes à la carte. The courses are elegantly crafted, showcasing creativity that is substantial and not just for show, with presentations that truly impress. Supported by excellent ingredients, the chef honors the region, using local seafood and inland products, sourcing as much as possible from trusted small producers, and maintaining a focus on circular cooking to reduce waste. The wine list is a journey through around 800 labels, with a special emphasis on Piedmont, Tuscany, and Burgundy; prices are accessible, and the by-the-glass selection is notably unique.

Name: Impronte
Description En: A short distance from the Atalanta stadium, with the convenience of private parking, this Bergamasque venue defies easy categorisation: to call it simply a corner of Sicily would be to do it a disservice, as the proposal goes beyond any single regional identity. The island’s imprint nonetheless remains clear, reinterpreted with contemporary sensitivity through a series of dishes that range across land and sea, at times drawing on street food, as with the outstanding grilled stigghiola, served with escarole and a lively sweet-and-sour spiced extract. Among the main courses, a noteworthy variation on lamb is executed with precision and taste. The setting is a converted bus depot, today transformed into a modern space of faintly post-industrial charm, complemented by attentive and energetic service, with particular praise due for the wine offering.

Name: La Civetta
Description En: Deep in the Apennines, at the heart of a tiny village, you’ll find a cozy osteria run with passion by a young couple. The cuisine draws on Ligurian and Piedmontese traditions, honoring seasonality with both land and sea dishes: from fragrant fried anchovies with basil-lime mayonnaise to house-made ravioli filled with sea bream alla ligure. Lunch features a simple daily menu, but on request, an à la carte service is available by reservation.

Name: Osteria dal Moro
Description En: A lively fish and seafood restaurant on the seafront, which is always busy thanks to its excellent value for money – booking ahead is highly recommended! Fish-based dishes only, all of which are announced at your table and which change regularly depending on market availability. The dishes are simple, rustic but full of flavour, which is why it’s easy to forgive the rather restricted choice of wine.

Name: Il Sottomarino
Description En: A lively restaurant on the seafront, featuring a pleasant terrace with panoramic views, which is highly sought after during the season – so it's best to book it as early as possible. For over twenty years, the solid family management has focused on excellent seafood cuisine, mostly classic, with some personal touches, especially in the desserts. Be sure to try the dark chocolate and crunchy cannoli, served vertically and filled with gianduja semifreddo, topped and plated with a cold Moscato d’Asti zabaglione.

Name: Podere San Faustino
Address: via San Faustino 33 (SS Emilia Nord), Fidenza, 43036, Italy
Description En: Situated in the beautiful countryside outside Cerreto Guidi, Villa Petriolo is a magnificent Medici residence offering luxurious rooms in a setting of outstanding charm. In addition to the beauty of the villa and its garden, overlooked by the restaurant’s terrace, the location benefits from the property’s delicious home-produced ingredients, such as extra-virgin olive oil, wine, Cinta Senese pork, meat and chicken, produce from the kitchen garden and ancient grains. The kitchen reinterprets these rich ingredients with a modern twist, offering two tasting menus — one of which for vegetarians — with dishes also available à la carte. Alternatively, Osteria di Golpaja offers authentic and intense flavours, those that have made Tuscany a renowned destination for lovers of fine dining.

Name: La Cuccagna Giro di Vite
Description En: Founded in 1969 by Martino Marsella, the restaurant has its roots in the tradition of the Apulian butcher’s shop with grill, of which it became a natural gastronomic extension. To this day the management remains firmly in family hands and meat continues to occupy a central role on the menu, as the excellent breaded capocollo readily attests. Alongside these, freshly harvested vegetables, drawn in part from the family’s own kitchen gardens, find their place, together with a generous procession of antipasti and first courses frequently entrusted to fresh pasta, such as the riccioli sampled during our most recent visit. Considerable attention is also dedicated to wine, with a cellar of over 300 labels. For those wishing to prolong the pleasure of their stay, the family offers a bed and breakfast adjacent to the restaurant, the perfect conclusion to a generous dinner.

Name: Assonica
Address: via Don Santo Carminati 9, Sorisole, 24010, Italy
Description En: Situated in the hills just beyond Bergamo, this smart, elegant and well-run restaurant has the Manzoni brothers (Alex and Vittorio) at the helm in the kitchen, where they create some of the most interesting cuisine in the region, while the capable Giovanna Danzo oversees the excellent service in the dining room. Creative and surprising, the dishes here are striking for their complex and original flavours, which combine vegetables with a clever use of herbs and spices without overwhelming the palate. The chargrilled veal sweetbreads (slightly crunchy on the outside and soft inside) are delicious, served with a selection of mushrooms and a fir extract that provides a hint of bitterness. There’s a strong focus on sourcing local ingredients in order to create cuisine which is both contemporary and sustainable at the same time.

Name: Cinque Foglie
Address: Via SS 18 Tirrenia Inferiore, 54, Battipaglia, 84091, Italy
Description En: Cinque Foglie explores the roots of fine dining through the concept of “the evolution of ingredients”. Chef Roberto Allocca creates dishes that are regionally inspired, combing traditional flavours with an innovative touch. The ingredients, some of which come from the chef’s family farm in Piana del Sele, are showcased on three tasting menus, while the wine cellar is home to more than 1 000 labels, including some rare vintages.

Name: CR21
Description En: In the heart of the old town, among narrow streets steeped in history, lies a modern bistro that exudes energy with its bright colours and open kitchen. Here, chef Di Bartolo creates contemporary dishes that evoke Mediterranean flavours, interpreted with skill and imagination. Every creation is an invitation to discover authentic flavours with an innovative twist, in an atmosphere that combines elegance and friendliness. Highlights include the crispy cannolo, red prawns and burrata with red fruit coulis, as well as chive mayonnaise.

Name: Barlèsh
Description En: In the heart of Montevarchi, as cozy as a dining room at home, Barlèsh restaurant offers what the chef likes to call "spontaneous cuisine." This unconventional place will delight you with both traditional and contemporary recipes: a six-course tasting menu and an à la carte menu featuring shareable bites, main courses, and desserts.

Name: Terracotta
Description En: Situated in the old town, this small, cosy restaurant serves delicious cuisine, with dishes sometimes inspired by Italian and international recipes, but often revisited in a unique way. In summer, you can dine on the terrace under a beautiful wisteria tree.

Name: Osteria Erbaluce
Description En: Just steps from the Leonardo-designed canal harbor, this spot takes a bold stance: it serves only meat, with a strong focus on the grill. Quality ingredients, fresh pastas, and classic house-made spoon desserts. An excellent wine list, especially strong on reds, rounds out the offering. The dining room is bright and all white; the cool, tranquil outdoor terrace is very welcoming, ideal in the warmer months. At the helm is a young couple driven by passion and professionalism.

Name: Peculiare Restaurant
Description En: Just steps from the Arco dell’Annunziata, in a quiet side street off Via Roma, Peculiare is the reflection of a young chef’s talent. The menu blends creativity and tradition, with dishes such as sole Wellington, tagliolini with sea urchins, and a refined Rossini-style filet with velvety purée and foie gras. The sober, elegant setting unfolds in an 18th-century palace, where an ancient arch tells the story of the place. The warm welcome and genuine smiles round out the experience.

Name: Dabbanna
Address: Piazza Principe di Napoli 8/9, Modica, 97015, Italy
Description En: It all began with the Cabbanna rotisserie, opened by grandfather Carmelo in 1971 and still going strong today, on his return from a time spent living in Venezuela. Fifty years later, his grandchildren are running a restaurant right opposite, in the central area of lower Modica, in a charming establishment with tasteful, welcoming interiors and several outdoor tables used in the summer. The menu is based on the island's ingredients and recipes, but also includes exotic influences — such as ceviche, known locally as “Ciauru ri mari” — reinterpreted with a contemporary twist. This results in colourful, beautifully presented dishes, excellent ingredients and delicate, attentive service provided by a female team.

Name: I Mori
Description En: This is the classic spot to recommend to anyone who wants fish prepared simply and traditionally, with no frills, just top-quality seafood that the friendly owner personally sources. The menu is supplemented by spoken specials based on that day’s fish-market finds, but among the mains we suggest you don’t miss the charcoal-grilled dishes.

Name: Badalamenti Cucina e Bottega
Description En: A historic address, established in the 1950s as a delicatessen selling charcuterie, cheeses and wines, it is now in its third generation and has been given a contemporary makeover. It is still “the shop” where you can buy local delicacies, but it also offers a restaurant service: traditional dishes from land and sea, revisited with taste and personality. The inspector's favourite dish? Cuttlefish ink arancina with red prawn tartare, pea cream and cheese fondue.

Name: Casa Romano
Description En: "A long-standing family establishment overlooking the main square for over sixty years, and for much of its history devoted to banqueting, it has been redesigned by the younger generation – brothers and cousins – in a contemporary and elegant key. Today it presents itself as a bright and panoramic space, thanks to generous picture windows opening onto the surrounding landscape, where the kitchen is in the hands of Luca Adobati, a thirty-year-old with significant experience abroad. His proposal, vivid in colour and precise in flavour, follows the seasonality of the raw materials with rigour, and is articulated across a concise à la carte menu and a seven-course surprise tasting menu. Among the most convincing dishes, the amberjack accompanied by an aromatic mushroom trilogy, and the closing dessert: layered apple millefeuille, hay ice cream, and zabaione. At lunch during the week, a leaner business formula is also available. Summer evenings are further enhanced by a spectacular panoramic terrace from which the view stretches without limit. "

Name: Nero&Oro
Address: Via del Parco Regina Margherita 45, Naples, 80121, Italy
Description En: The dream of a young Neapolitan chef comes to life in an intimate, refined hideaway, tucked among the elegant streets connecting Vomero to the Chiaia waterfront. Here, dishes burst with vivid colors and Mediterranean aromas, accented by contemporary touches that reveal personality and culinary exploration. Two blind tasting menus invite discovery, or guests may opt for a well-balanced à la carte selection of land and sea, where each ingredient shines with clarity, lifted by subtle exotic nuances that awaken the senses. The wine cellar, dominated by Campanian labels, exudes tradition, yet upon request opens to selected wines by the glass, completing an experience that plays on harmony and curiosity.

Name: Coro
Description En: In the centre of Orvieto, Coro is set in the captivating deconsecrated church of San Giuseppe. The modern, refined style provides the backdrop for chef Ronald Bukri’s cuisine, which weaves together memory, innovation, and global influences into dishes with a distinctly contemporary character.

Name: The Tasting Room by Marcello Corrado
Description En: In Merano, within the elegant setting of Villa Eden, an intimate dining room with gilded accents and just four tables sets the stage for an exclusive gastronomic experience, woven around the discreet allure of candlelight. Here, chef Marcello Corrado presents a multisensory journey of singular identity: the eight-course tasting menu ‘OTTO ELEMENTI’ is a sincere expression of his culinary philosophy, his creativity, and a talent in constant dialogue with the territory and its extraordinary biodiversity. As an alternative, ‘EDEN ESSENCE’ offers a carefully curated selection of the most emblematic dishes from OTTO ELEMENTI, distilling their essence into a more concise yet equally evocative form. The cooking moves gracefully between lightness and satisfaction, with dishes crafted with an elegant hand and measured imagination, while the attentive and impeccable service completes a gastronomic visit of rare refinement.

Name: La Piazzetta Lake Como
Description En: Tucked among the picturesque streets of Cernobbio, this modern, inviting bistro blends retro charm with contemporary furnishings and personalized touches. At the entrance, a cozy lounge with a bar counter beckons guests to linger over aperitifs and signature cocktails, while in summer the outdoor terrace offers moments of pleasure amid the lake breeze. In the kitchen, a young, dynamic team reinterprets Mediterranean flavors through contemporary recipes that are both authentic and aromatic. Not to be missed: “Pappa e Gambero,” crusted shrimp atop tomato and basil pappa, and “Tagliolino ai tre pomodori,” a tribute to refined simplicity.

Name: Deschevaliers
Description En: Under the guidance of multi-starred chef Nino Di Costanzo, a fine dining destination takes shape along one of Italy’s most celebrated gourmet streets, set within the elegant spaces of an international hotel showcasing its most exclusive brand. The atmosphere exudes refined contemporary flair: soft lighting, minimalist décor, and works by local artists that engage with the space. At the table, Neapolitan identity is expressed through dishes bearing dialect names, dressed in a modern aesthetic: creations that evoke tradition yet come alive with contemporary details, in a harmony of colors and textures. The service, attentive and professional, discreetly guides an experience that bridges heritage and innovation, weaving together authentic flavors and signature inspirations.

Name: Trattoria del Bollito
Address: Via Don Giacomo Alberione 3/e, Alba, 12051, Italy
Description En: This trattoria in the heart of Alba welcomes guests into a warm, family atmosphere, where wood panelling and smiling staff create a sense of intimacy. The service is dynamic and polite, while aromas from the kitchen evoke Piedmontese tradition. The carefully curated wine list celebrates local labels from throughout the Langhe, inviting guests to discover authentic flavours. One of the most popular dishes is tajarin with rabbit and hazelnuts: thin strands of pasta paired with delicate meat and crunchy hazelnuts, creating a delicious and comforting balance.

Name: Il Frate
Description En: In 2025, this restaurant celebrates a century of existence, as a veritable treasure trove of history that has preserved its family soul intact. Today, the kitchen is run by Lorenza, heir to a tradition that smells of Emilia and Piacenza, the same tradition lovingly preserved by her mother. The dishes arrive at the table generous and steaming, with classic flavours that seduce the eye and the palate. The wine list, which is now digital, boasts around 350 labels: the treasures of Northern Italy prevail, but there are also international notes. For the perfect pairing, let yourself be guided by Giorgio, the fourth generation of the family in the dining room. With grace and expertise, he will transform every sip into a harmonious accompaniment to your dish.

Name: Gasthaus Lamm
Address: via del Villaggio 36, Saint Martin in Passeier, 39010, Italy
Description En: In the historic center of this small yet charming village, you’ll find a trattoria that has been in operation since 1777. Today, under the current family management, the wood-paneled dining rooms evoke the warm, traditional Tyrolean atmosphere, mirrored by a kitchen that turns out an enticing lineup of local specialties. Lamb, an homage to the restaurant’s name, goat, trout from Val Passiria, beef from Val Sarentino, and of course speck, strudel, and more, all executed at a high level.

Name: Bottega del Re
Address: Via Francesco Domenico Guerrazzi 66r, Genoa, 16146, Italy
Description En: In the tranquil heart of Albaro’s residential quarter, a cool summer courtyard welcomes guests with the scent of flowers and the gentle rustle of leaves. Inside, warm spaces blend rustic charm with elegant touches, creating a comforting, refined atmosphere. The cuisine is a journey between land and sea, where tradition meets seasonality: each dish reveals the authentic flavors of ingredients carefully sourced by young, talented Chef Orlandi. Not to be missed: the “quaglia della bottega,” quail stuffed with a giardiniera of crunchy, aromatic vegetables, releasing intense aromas with every bite. Our advice: save room for dessert, true masterpieces of sweetness that bring the meal to a close with velvety, surprising notes.

Name: Marino e Silvana
Address: via San Salvatore da Horta 7, Cagliari, 09124, Italy
Description En: Situated on the edge of the pedestrianised area near the Bastione di Saint Remy, this restaurant is named after its charismatic owner Marino, who helps guests with their choice of menu and is happy to tell them all about the history of the restaurant (the street in front of the restaurant, for example, has not always been there). At the helm in the kitchen, his wife Silvana prepares Mediterranean dishes with a Sardinian flavour – the fish and seafood options are particularly delicious.

Name: Cura Cucina Contemporanea
Address: Via Risorgimento 6/8, Marina di Davoli, 88060, Italy
Description En: A single tasting menu invites guests to explore the culinary vision of Chef Massimo: a journey through authentic flavors of land and sea, enhanced by creative, personal touches. Delightful contrasts unfold around the onion, enveloped in a velvety cheese cream, while the “sottobosco” dish evokes autumn with the earthy aroma of porcini and tart hints of red berries. All this is embraced by the warm atmosphere of a converted former stable, where dry stone walls whisper tales of times past.

Name: Sushi Matsu Omakase
Description En: Just 14 guests, seated in a horseshoe arrangement around two chefs, witness the preparation of each dish in real time. Fish, in all its variations, takes shape before your eyes, while conversation with those preparing it becomes an integral part of the ritual, essential for unlocking the secrets of the Japanese art of sushi. Eating with your hands is encouraged, as tradition dictates, and we recommend pairing the experience with one of the sakés offered by the glass, to complete the Japanese immersion. At lunch, the menu is more streamlined, but it’s worth taking the time to savor every detail. Among the creations that won over our inspectors: the Japanese scallop and squid tartare, enhanced by delicate notes of soy and yuzu in perfect balance, with wasabi applied with masterful restraint.

Name: Olio Fishbar
Address: Via Padre Luigi Monti 4, Saronno, 21047, Italy
Description En: A modern bistro in the heart of Saronno, where guests leave their cars in nearby parking areas to settle into well-appointed tables (reservations recommended, even for lunch) and savor generous dishes, primarily seafood, though not exclusively. Fresh aromas, clean flavors, an abundance of raw preparations, and a few meat options, curiously without any pasta courses. We particularly enjoyed the “fish and chips” featuring coalfish, crispy and golden, and the Sicilian cannolo “our way,” indulgent and fragrant. The wine list is concise but thoughtfully curated, while both ownership and kitchen bear the signature of the Michelin-starred restaurant Olio in Origgio.

Name: Le Fucine Gourmet
Description En: The modern Le Fucine hotel is home to two restaurants with almost identical names: Le Fucine Brasserie and, of course, Le Fucine Gourmet. The latter welcomes guests into an elegant dining room featuring contemporary, minimalist design: clean lines and spotlights that caress the tables, creating an intimate atmosphere. In the centre, like a live stage, is the open kitchen, where chef Andrea Fantini, from Friuli, moves with confident gestures amidst steam and aromas, sharing the experiences he has accumulated over time with every dish. Two tasting menus invite you on a sensory journey: the first reinvents local traditions, while the second is inspired by the chef's memories of his travels. For those who love balance, there is also a third, shorter menu that combines elements of both. To complete the experience, sommelier Nicholas Chiarossi will guide you through the wine cellar's labels, skilfully selecting the perfect wine pairing for each dish.

Name: Marconi
Description En: In the heart of the picturesque town that serves as a gateway to Val Formazza stands a welcoming establishment where familial warmth blends with a touch of contemporaneity. In the kitchen Denis, joined in the dining room by his wife Sabrina, knows how to pamper guests with a series of dishes that evoke tradition while being reinterpreted with imagination and modern sensitivity. Not to be missed is their signature “Walser Beef Filet,” a true house specialty, though the “venison ossobuco with cream of potato and blueberry compote” also merits a taste.

Name: Blanco Osteria da Fabio
Description En: Just steps from the waterfront, yet conveniently close to the city center, this venue captivates with its warm, welcoming atmosphere. The front-of-house is gracious and smiling, while the kitchen delivers a menu steeped in the sea and tradition: concise, yet brimming with authentic flavors. Our advice? Don’t miss the housemade fresh pasta: the scialatielli with shrimp and stracciatella is a celebration of indulgence, while the maccheroncini showcase simplicity elevated to excellence. Completing the experience, fragrant bread served with a light and rustic artisanal oil that speaks of authenticity.

Name: Altatto
Description En: A taste of the big city in Milan’s southwest inner periphery: Altatto brings a fully vegetarian cuisine built on contemporary ideas, modern techniques, and flavors that alternate between bright citrus accents and softer, more captivating tones. A prime example is the mascarpone risotto with celeriac base and walnuts, intense and perfectly balanced. The space, minimal and clean-lined, finds warmth in an informal, jovial service that makes the overall experience all the more welcoming.

Name: Gustificio
Address: Via Guglielmo Marconi 52, Carmignano di Brenta, 35010, Italy
Description En: An inn fragrant with freshly baked pastries, but above all a restaurant brimming with energy, where the glow of the charcoal grill caresses prime cuts of meat, the undisputed stars of the kitchen. Andrea Poli, chef-owner, celebrates product and season with playful dishes and authentic flavors, while embracing contemporary forays such as the irresistible “grilled radicchio gnocchetti, draped in béchamel, red wine sauce, and crispy hazelnuts.” On Wednesdays, a small selection of gourmet pizzas adds an unexpected twist to the experience.

Name: Inka
Description En: The name was not chosen at random: in the heart of the old town, you will find an excellent selection of Peruvian cuisine, rich in spices, colours and a variety of ingredients combined in often complex dishes. The chef is of Peruvian origin and, in addition to classic ceviche, he likes to add a Japanese touch to some dishes, creating Nikkei cuisine, the result of emigration to Peru by Japanese people who brought their own culinary traditions with them and blended them with the local cuisine.

Name: Casa Celesia
Address: Piazza Martiri della Libertà, 31, Oleggio, 28047, Italy
Description En: Nestled in the heart of Oleggio, beneath the portico that opens onto the charming main square with its historic bell tower, Chef Corrado Lombardo showcases his extensive expertise. The restaurant offers an understated entrance and a warm, inviting dining space, complete with intimate tables and a delightful ambiance. The menu masterfully blends culinary skill with traditional flavours, paying homage to seasonal produce and highlighting the finest ingredients with well-judged seasoning and subtle contrasts of aroma. This is all paired with impeccable yet approachable service, creating a refined and thoroughly enjoyable dining experience.

Name: Sakeya
Address: Via Cesare Da Sesto 1, Milan, 20123, Italy
Description En: A Kyoto-born chef, a yakitori grill on full display from the entrance, and pared-back interiors evoking Japanese bistros: the tone is set before you sit down. One wall is devoted entirely to sake – over 150 labels, with new arrivals each week. The kitchen takes an unmistakably Eastern approach in both ingredients and technique, ranging from creative forays such as Gindara 2.0, cod with ginger and yuzu, to classics such as wagyu fillet, cooked tableside over charcoal by the guest. The true specialty, however, remains the kushiyaki: skewers of various cuts grilled over the open flame near the entrance. Service is gracious and well-prepared; let the sommelier guide you through the list, he’s always eager to share the stories and craft behind each sake.

Name: Orso Grigio
Description En: In the center of Cavalese, within the hotel of the same name, a young chef presents an intelligent and delicious reinterpretation of Trentino gastronomic traditions without distorting their identity. A stop not to be missed, complemented by a solid wine selection featuring several organic, biodynamic, and amphora-aged bottles. Essential is the Schüttelbrot gelato with black bilberry, wild spinach, and thyme.

Name: Il Cigno
Description En: Adjacent to the historic center, this elegant and refined restaurant occupies an evocative sixteenth-century building that preserves a timeless charm. The talented and creative chef presents a contemporary cuisine that alternates meat and fish dishes with balance, playing with modern techniques and touches of imagination. The “amberjack sashimi with almond cream, raspberry, and puffed quinoa” is a small opening of pure finesse, while concluding with their excellent desserts is nearly obligatory. In fine weather, it is worth reserving a table on the evocative terrace, arranged around a captivating fifteenth-century well.

Name: Marchese
Description En: Located in a still-central area of the city, this restaurant is not a new opening but has recently reinvented its identity by entrusting the kitchen to a Roman chef with a solid background. The culinary offering maintains a classic structure, with a choice between a “surprise” tasting menu and an extensive à la carte selection. In the kitchen, local and national traditions intertwine, enriched by an international touch that translates into visually striking, colorful creations that above all deliver on the palate. The dishes, both meat and fish, follow the seasonality of ingredients, with particular attention to vegetable pairings. Among the standout offerings: the pumpkin risotto with blue prawn, red berry umami, and Caesar salad crisp, a successful balance of technique, flavor, and creativity.

Name: Nomos Ante
Address: Via di San Paolo alla Regola, 3, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description En: Within a newly opened hotel of clean, luxurious lines, a contemporary restaurant of well-defined personality takes shape, guided by a young and cosmopolitan chef. Deeply connected to the gastronomic culture of France, where he spent many formative years, yet also influenced by experiences in Japan and England, he delivers a refined and dynamic cuisine, capable of uniting technique with international sensitivity. The proposal moves along a modern line in which precision and immediacy of flavour are accompanied by careful attention to balance. The dishes tell a story that alternates elegance and character, never redundant, always centred on the essential quality of the ingredient. Among the most successful creations are the citrus spaghetti, conceived for those who appreciate fresh and vibrant profiles, and the charcoal-grilled lamb, elevated by a delicate accompaniment of rhubarb that adds a refined acidic note to the whole.

Name: Q.B. bistró
Description En: Q.B. Bistró is a small, welcoming venue in the heart of Cuneo’s historic centre, overlooking a quiet, secluded street. The kitchen looks to the contemporary with dishes that are essential yet thoughtful, built upon seasonal ingredients and carefully selected raw materials. The considered and well-structured wine list opens its gaze willingly to natural and organic bottles, with labels that tell stories of terroirs and independent producers. A youthful and pleasing establishment, ideal for those seeking simplicity, attention to detail and an authentic measure of passion.

Name: Sant’Agostino
Description En: Tucked beside the deconsecrated church of Sant’Agostino, a beautifully kept cloister ushers guests into the culinary world of chef Mauro Brina, a young talent with a stated preference for meat, yet one who truly comes into his own with seafood. Little wonder, then, that we recommend his marine preparations: the pisarei with shellfish or the fish soup brimming with tomato, crustaceans, mussels, cuttlefish, and the day’s catch. In fine weather, make a point of securing a table on the terrace, an evocative setting steeped in history and the timeless charm of the ancient convent.

Name: Osteria Dell'Unione
Description En: In the heart of the Langhe del Barbaresco, this osteria preserves the convivial spirit of traditional establishments from times past. The atmosphere is warm and familial, while aromas and flavors immediately evoke the home cooking of recipes handed down through generations, and prepared to order. The menu celebrates the cornerstones of authentic tradition: from free-range chicken cacciatore to the soft, celebrated spinach frittatas, dishes deceptively simple in appearance, yet revealing a precise hand respectful of Piedmontese culinary heritage. The wine list, well-structured and fairly priced, accompanies the meal in a natural manner. In warmer months, the vine-shaded pergola becomes the ideal setting for a meal of rustic, genuine charm.

Name: Insieme Dal Clandestino
Description En: A chef of Albanian origin, who in his restaurant’s name proudly acknowledges the complex journey that brought him to Italy, delivers a cuisine that seamlessly blends memory and modernity. Experience gained both in the region and in the city has shaped dishes that are anything but contrived, reinterpreting solid Piedmontese traditions through a contemporary lens, while making generous use of the territory’s iconic ingredients, from fresh pasta to chocolate, hazelnuts to truffles. The value is equally compelling: at lunch, a lighter selection is available from the menu, while the kitchen often extends the option to explore the more elaborate evening offerings as well.

Name: Enoteca Cavour 313
Description En: Reborn in late 2024 thanks to the enthusiasm of a young Frenchwoman raised among vineyard rows and harvests, this historic establishment has found new life without losing its soul as a rustic, welcoming wine shop. Just beyond the entrance, guests pause for an easy lunch, guided by a nimble offering written on the blackboard and enriched by a daily special – irresistible, during our visit, the saffron risoni with mantis shrimp. In the evening (reservations recommended), one moves into the more intimate spaces that open beyond the visible kitchen, where the young Roman chef, trained at the ALMA school, presents seasonal dishes interpreted with technique and creativity. The wine list is excellent, harmoniously divided between Italian labels and those from across the Alps.

Name: Barbagianni
Address: Via Gracco del Secco 86, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
Description En: Housed within an elegant stone building along the road leading into the heart of Colle, Barbagianni welcomes its guests into a warm and evocative setting: at the centre of the dining room stands a magnificent stabilised oak tree, illuminated by small lights that heighten its spectacular presence. Youthful and playful in its approach, the cuisine aims for a delightful balance between technique and flavour, featuring dishes that blend creativity with a sense of familiarity. The menu offers two tasting menus, alongside an à la carte option that encompasses meat, seafood and plant-based dishes, all designed to showcase the seasonality and quality of the ingredients. Completing the experience, a dynamic and good-humoured front-of-house team, attentive to the needs of each guest and always on hand to recommend the most fitting wine to accompany every creation.

Name: Darì
Address: vicolo Cieco San Pietro Incarnario 5, Verona, 37121, Italy
Description En: Overflowing with stuccoes, mirrors, ceramics, and Murano chandeliers, guests take their place in one of five dining rooms, each more refined and distinctive than the last, for an evening befitting a grand occasion. Everything draws inspiration from opulence within this sumptuous fifteenth-century palazzo, while the cuisine ranges from local to international, from creative to traditional. In fine weather, service moves to an enchanting garden, a rarity in the heart of Verona.

Name: Insieme
Description En: On a quiet, tucked-away street far from the well-trodden paths, a small neighborhood restaurant tells the story of a couple who, after experiences abroad, chose to return and put down roots here. The result is a venue of authentic character, where a familial warmth is immediately palpable and becomes an integral part of the experience. The nimble, ever-evolving menu reflects a cuisine that approaches flavors with contemporary sensitivity: from gentler notes, such as roasted squash with Parmigiano foam and almond crumble, to bolder tones, exemplified by an excellent Carnaroli saffron risotto enriched with tongue and a vibrant parsley sauce. Whatever the guest’s mood, simply trust the suggestions of owner Federica: young and knowledgeable, she guides with ease toward the ideal glass, in perfect harmony with chef Alessandro’s cuisine.

Name: La Nunziadêina
Description En: A landmark occasion: in 2026, the fourth generation celebrated one hundred years of history of this establishment, also with its inclusion in the Guide. The venture was first set in motion by Annunciata in Cittanova, before closing in 2002 and reopening four years later at its present address, directly opposite the magnificent Abbey of Nonantola, taking on the name that had long served as its founder’s nickname: Nunziadêina. Since then, the common thread has remained the same: the delicacies and indulgent treats of Emilia-Romagna.The dining rooms are homely, yet attentive to detail; fresh flowers on every table lend a pleasing touch, while a fire crackling at the back of the room offers a foretaste of one of the house’s specialities, charcoal grilled meat. Alongside this, there is always fresh pasta, outstanding charcuterie and a wealth of traditional recipes, all rounded off by the customary irresistible dessert trolley. An impressive wine list completes the offering. A truly deserving venue!

Name: Elementi
Description En: In this intimate, pared-back venue, with wooden tables and soft lighting, warmth and fine cookery reign supreme. Gentle chamber music sets the tone for a journey through the cuisine of Valentina and Saverio, whose cooking bears a distinctly personal stamp. The menu alternates between land and sea: house-marinated anchovies, caserecci from Abruzzo prepared in the classic cacio e pepe style with pink prawns, and an impeccably rendered duck breast among the main courses. A venue that will satisfy even the most discerning of palates: a truly gourmand experience.

Name: Ciccio Bistrot
Description En: In the evocative vaulted dining room that once housed the celebrated Cavallino, Ciccio Bistrot now brings to the table a forthright, deeply local cuisine, faithful to tradition and free of unnecessary digressions – except in the playful titles that punctuate the menu. Among the offerings, the whimsically named “no name” deserves a taste: agnolotti del plin served with the sauce of your choosing, a small ritual of personalization that wins over regulars. Each day brings a few off-menu delicacies, while wine maintains the role tradition assigns it: a discreet yet essential companion, supported by a well-curated selection and the expert guidance of the owner, always ready to steer guests toward the most fitting pairing.

Name: Zivieri
Description En: The produce of the hills come down into the city: this, in essence, is the restaurant. Within the mediaeval Torre Alberici, in the heart of the historic centre, the simple dining room furnished in a contemporary style showcases the produce that the Zivieri farm itself rears and cultivates in the Apennines. Regional cookery, therefore, of an excellent standard, with charcuterie and meats as the jewel in the crown, which moreover can also be purchased, along with cheeses and other foods, from their adjacent butcher’s shop.

Name: Sabaudia
Address: Viale Torino 11, loc. Stupinigi, Nichelino, 10042, Italy
Description En: Within the farms that once surrounded the Hunting Lodge of Stupinigi, in spaces formerly reserved for servants, springs to life a comfortable establishment characterised by a warm atmosphere steeped in history. The kitchen follows the regional tradition with consistency, enlivening it with touches of imagination and colour that lend freshness to time-honoured recipes. As an alternative, there is no shortage of seafood dishes, to which one of the two tasting menus is also dedicated. The cellar, too, prefers to champion local talent, with suggestions by the glass and bottle that change weekly, keeping the spirit of discovery alive.

Name: Pesceria San Martino
Description En: Born as a fishmonger’s and transformed over time into a small seafood delicatessen, this venue welcomes guests into a simple yet thoughtfully appointed setting, with an intimate front room and a colourful conservatory at the rear that opens to the outdoors in summer. Here Ivan manages front of house with courtesy and expertise, while in the kitchen Bartolo selects the freshest produce with great care. Among the more distinctive offerings, the original and well-executed “seafood charcuterie” stands out, alongside fried squid that is also available for takeaway. Not to be missed is the pan-cooked baby octopus, tender and flavourful, served with a datterini tomato sauce and a crispy bruschetta that practically begs you to mop up every last drop. Strong demand makes booking essential, particularly at weekends.

Name: San Genesio
Address: Via Francesco Viano 1, San Genesio, 10090, Italy
Description En: Commanding a dominant position in the heart of this small hamlet, this historic restaurant — lovingly maintained through the years — has found renewed vigour since 2017 under a passionate and accomplished stewardship (here, fittingly, sommelier Simone’s christening was once celebrated). From the dining room and expansive terrace, one’s gaze sweeps across the surrounding landscape, and on the clearest days the vista extends even further, offering a panorama of considerable enchantment.The kitchen remains faithful to tradition, yet interpreted with contemporary freshness in its presentations and through certain pairings that lend character to the offering. The wine list, too, is of excellent calibre, intelligently structured and rich in both breadth and depth, spanning Piedmont, Italy and beyond.

Name: Pirò
Description En: Just steps from Piazza Navona, which grows quieter and even more captivating come evening. this venue is devoted to classic seafood cookery, with a generous selection of crudo and an array of cooked preparations that let each day’s catch shine. The setting is modern and intimate, service attentive without being intrusive, and the management draws on lengthy experience in the Roman dining scene. A fine recommendation for those seeking understated elegance and a kitchen that brings the authentic scent of the sea to the table.

Name: Patrizia
Description En: Creative dynamism in the very heart of the city: this is Patrizia, a restaurant named after the chef’s mother. Here the journey is singular — available in either a complete or abbreviated form — and evolves with the turning of the seasons; alongside it, the lighting, music and dining room details transform as well, following precisely the vision of young chef Tommaso Zoboli. A continuous movement of ideas and exploration, designed to satisfy himself whilst delighting his guests.The progression of dishes reveals an exuberant kitchen, rich with references to diverse thoughts and cultures, unfettered by preconceptions in its pairings and consistently thoughtful in its presentation. The storytelling at the counter, led by the chef-patron and his young team, completes a dynamic and immersive experience.

Name: Mamma Orso
Description En: Situated in the lively Nomentano quarter, to the north-east of the city and behind Piazza Bologna — not a tourist area, but rather one of Rome’s student districts — this youthful operation offers fragrant and unfussy Italian regional cookery, reinterpreted with evident passion. The recipes traverse the Italian peninsula from north to south, before being reinterpreted with a personal touch: the traditional Mantuan pumpkin tortello, for example, becomes a slice of roasted pumpkin with sour butter, curry sauce, licorice, and amaretti.While many dishes retain an almost home-cooked feel, there is no shortage of imagination: the barley crème caramel, served with crushed salted peanuts, is excellent. All of this unfolds within a single, intimate and welcoming dining room, possessed of a charming vintage spirit.

Name: Ciambra
Description En: At the gates of the town and a few steps from the magnificent Cathedral of Monreale, this rustic yet elegant venue proves to be an intriguing destination for those wishing to explore refined seafood cookery, reinterpreted with a modern touch while never betraying the authenticity of the flavours. The Tonnarello fresco cacio e pepe con quenelle di gambero rosso (fresh tonnarello cacio e pepe with a red prawn quenelle) is a delightful pasta dish that well represents the chef’s hand, as do the impeccably fresh and expertly executed seafood crudo. Finally, the house desserts are not to be missed: the true stars of the end of the meal, leaving a deliciously lingering memory.

Name: Café Carducci
Description En: Those with a passion for retro and nostalgic atmospheres will find inspiration in this establishment opened in 1928. Since then, generations have succeeded one another, but always within the same family. Today, you enter through the bar before passing into the dining room, a space so enchanting with its books, paintings, and bottles that you’ll never want to leave. Alongside a vast selection of cured meats and cheeses (predominantly French), exquisite meat and fish dishes await, complemented by a legendary cellar boasting some two thousand labels.

Name: La Collina dei Ciliegi
Description En: Situated within the La Collina dei Ciliegi wine estate amid the verdant Valpantena hills, this first-floor restaurant (lift available) is home to two chefs – he is from Calabria, while she is from Puglia. Together they create exciting, modern Mediterranean cuisine using ingredients from their native regions, including their signature dish – homemade spaghetti served with a delicious, well-balanced 'nduja, smoked ricotta and tomato ristretto sauce. Top-quality local ingredients take pride of place, as demonstrated by the Brogna mutton, which is raised on site, barbecued and served with an exquisite caper sauce and seasonal mushroom pie. The concise wine list features labels from the Veneto alongside a few French options.
